# Caitanya Candramrta

## Introduction

Sripad Prabhodananda Sarasvati, the intimate associate of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu and a renowned Vaisnava poet, is the distinguished author of Sri Caitanya Candramrta - the Nectar Moon of Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

Caitanya Candramrta is a compendium of verses, grouped by the author into 12 chapters. The overall theme of the book is Lord Caitanya, the golden complexioned Personality of Godhead who inaugurated the Sankirtan movement and distributed the treasure of Vraja Bhakti. These two activities, chanting the Lord’s HolyName and following in the devotional mood of the Vrajabasis, are the essence of Lord Caitanya’s mission and are pure nectar.

The book is basically divided into two parts: the glorification of Lord Caitanya’s devotees and the glorification of Lord Caitanya. The poetry of the verses varies, but it is always sweet and always realized. Members of the Krsna Consciousness movement know and recite many of these verses, for they reveal the essential truths of Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada was particularly fond of verses 5 and 120 and would quote them often. Following in his footsteps, we should also be familiar with this short book and avail ourselves of the essential truths presented by the author.

In this edition of Caitanya Candramrta, His Grace Sarvabhavana Das has given commentaries on many verses. These commentaries are replete with references and are presented in a scholarly way. By studying this book one will understand Lord Caitanya’s teachings, which are the only shelter for those desiring to cross over the ocean of KaliYuga.

Hаге Krishna

Sivarama Swami

Vrindabап

8.4.2003

There are different versions of some of the original verses; some of the different readings are mentioned by Srila BhaktiSiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad in the anvaya (word-for-word) of the Sri Caitanya Vani Edition. The two editions used for keying in the original verses convey some of the different versions, making this a (partial) critical edition.

Roman transliterations (spellings) of some Sanskrit and Bengali words have adopted the original Sanskrit convention of sandhi. ‘euphonic combination of letters’.

Thus श्रीमन्महाप्रभ is written as SrimanMahaprabhu. In the DevaNagari, the ‘n’ and the ‘m’ have been combined into a single letter, or conjunct.

Prabhupada: “This is Sanskrit language. By combining words with the process of sandhi and samasa, one word can be as long as three miles. So for ordinary person it is very difficult to combine together. So it is for the learned scholars.”

## Biographical Sketch of the author - Sri Prabodhananda Sarasvatipada

In the beginning of 1433 Sakabda, Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu desired to go on a pilgrimage to South India, to distribute his mercy to the devotees there. Setting out from Niladri (JagannathPuri) in UtkalaDesh (Orissa), he first came to the GodavariRiver, where he met Ramananda Ray, and then eventually arrived in the land that is today known as the province of Madras (Chennai), having stopped at many holy places along the way.

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu entered Sri RangaKsetra on the Ekadasi of the bright fortnight in the month of Asarh (eleventh day of the waxing moon, June-July). Seeing that the period of CaturMasya was imminent, Bhagavan Sri CaitanyaCandra resolved to remain in the holy abode of Sri RangaNath for this four-month period, in pursuance of the codes of conduct regulating the lives of those initiated in the ten various orders of sannyasa.

Sri RangaKsetra is the principal seat of the Sri Sampradaya. The Vaisnavas belonging to the various sampradayas in the South were very strict followers of the codes of etiquette, proper procedure and behaviour. The villages in the South inhabited by these devout Vaisnavas were found to be unsuitable places of residence by the Smarta brahmanas, so at that time SriRangaNath was served by only the Sri Vaisnavas. For this reason, SrimanMahaprabhu felt inclined to pass the four months of the rainy season (CaturMasya) with these staunch adherents to the Vaisnava faith and thus impart instructions for their benefit, while going to have darsan of Sri RangaNath and while absorbed in transcendental talks on the topics of Bhagavan Sri Krsna.

At that time, three brothers from the province of Mahisur-Tirumalaya, Vyenkata, and GopalGuru - had also taken up residence in SrlRahga. In actuality, they originally hailed from either Andhra or UttarPradesh. SrimanMahaprabhu rfelt very kindly disposed towards this family of brahmanas and thus happily passed the period of CaturMasya while residing in their home. The middle brother, Vyenkata had a young son who eventually became the celebrated Sri GopalaBhatta, one of the six Gosvamis of Vrindaban.

The members of the Sri Sampradaya are most fond of the worship of Sri LaksmlNarayan. By the quality of SrlmanMahaprabhu’s heartfelt compassion, the Bhatta family became conversant in the mellows of love of Sri Krsna. Although we don’t have much information regarding Sri Tirumalaya, we can understand that he was very devoted to Sri CaitanyaDev. In the pages of Sri Caitanya Caritamrta, MadhyaLila, Chapter Nine, there is mention of some discussions that took place between Sri Vyenkata and Sri KrsnaCaitanyaDev. The affectionate attachment of Sri Prabodhananda towards Sri Caitanya was incomparable. By the influence of the honest instructions of Sri Prabodhananda to his nephew, the son of Sri Vyenkata, Sri GopalBhatta became an acarya among the Sri Gauriya Vaisnavas. Among the servants of Sri Caitanya, Sri Prabodhananda is one of the topmost. From the pages of Sri KaviKarnapur’s Sri GauraGanoddesaDipika, we learn that Sri Prabodhananda Sarasvati was present during Sri Krsna’s Lila as Tunga Vidya sakhi. In the beginning of Sri HariBhaktiVilasa, it is mentioned that the dearmost servant of Sri Bhagavan, the disciple of Srila Prabodhananda, Sri GopalBhatta, very much satisfied Sri Rupa, Sanatana and Sri RaghunathDas by composing Sri HariBhaktiVilas. Sri BhaktiRatnakar states - ‘Some say that Prabodhananda was so highly qualified that he became famous far and wide, receiving the appellation ‘Sarasvati’. He was most dear to Piurna Brahma Sri KrsnaCaitanya Bhagavan; no one should think differently, not even in their dreams. He was supremely indifferent to worldly affairs, the very form of affection, most pleasant and agreeable; a great poet, matchless in the fine arts of music, song and dance. Simply to hear his words was a source of satisfaction and happiness for all. The glories of Prabodhananda are interminable.’

When SrimanMahaprabhu returned to Nilacal, Sri Prabodhananda Sarasvati entered deeply into the worship of Sri KrsnaCaitanya, his inner being totally possessed. Within a few years he left SriRanga, setting out with a solemn vow to attain the most cherished object of his adoration. Without wasting any time, he came to MathuraMandala and took up residence at Kamyavan. Gradually, Sri GopalBhatta also became eager to take up residence at Sri BrajaDham. Later he also followed the footsteps of his uncle, arriving in Sri Vrindaban.

Many may question, that if Sri Prabodhananda Sarasvati was so dearly affectionate to Sri Gauranga, then why is it that Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj GosvamI hasn’t written anything of him to gratify the ears of the GauraBhaktas? In answer to this, Sri GhanaSyam Sri NarahariCakravarti comments in the pages of Sri BhaktiRatnakar - ‘In the accounts of Sri GopalBhatta, some authors have something to say, and some are silent. Those who are ignorant regarding these matters and instead engage in hair splitting arguments, only sow the seeds of offense within their own hearts. The poets of yore, highly competent in the matter of understanding the confidential mellows of devotion, refrained from composing any narrations on this subject, though they were more than qualified to do so. There is only a brief mention of Sri GopalBhatta in their writings. The reason is that Sri Gopal Bhatta himself very happily made this mandate, prohibiting any mention of his name in their writings. Who can understand why? He always considered himself very wretched and fallen. Therefore Kaviraj (Gosvami) was loathe to trespass his injunction.’

Some say that in the writings of Sri Prabodhananda there is an inclination towards svakiyavad (emphasis on Sri Krsna’s conjugal affairs with his wedded wives) and therefore the GauraBhaktas who are followers of Sri Rupa, addicted to the mellows of parakiyavad (the lawless love of the gopis for their paramour, the great gallant Sri Krsna), refrain from much discussion regarding Srila Sarasvati Gosvami. However, Sri Narahari has preferred to seek shelter within the boundaries of propriety, maintaining an unbiased approach, since anyone who has accepted shelter at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya should be understood to be the most fortunate soul in existence. Therefore, he reasons that it is better not to engage in tedious arguments, rather, one should try to see the immaculate faith and obedience of Sri Prabodhananda for Sri GauraSundar and thus relish the sweetness of (maid)-servitorship at the lotus feet of Sri Vrndavanesvari, the foremost mistress of Sri Krsna.

The moods and sentiments (bhavasamuha) of Sri Prabodhananda are quite distinct. His language is simultaneously filled with sobriety and sweetness. All the devotees who have accepted shelter at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya get pleasure beyond measure by regularly reciting Sri Prabodhananda’s Sri VrndavanSataka. His composition, Sri NavadvipSataka is similar to Sri VrndavanSataka. Sri Prabodhananda’s Sri RadhaRasaSudhaNidhi is without a doubt unparalleled in the world of poetry. Though the perusal of this book may not produce pleasure in the ears of those who have a taste for ordinary, mundane poetry, it is supremely dear to the sincere devotees who have a taste for the mellows of devotion to Sri Hari. Due to differences in taste, one’s attraction may either wane or wax. Therefore, according to the virtue of the reader, the transcendental moods and sentiments of Braja expressed in this literary work may or may not have the desired effect. He has composed another book by the name, VivekSataka, mentioned in a book by Professor Aufret, the Manuscript having been seen by a resident of Baharampur, RamdasSen.

Sri CaitanyaCandramrta has been widely published in Bengal. Even those who are inimical to Sri Gauranga will perceive the purity in their own hearts by reading this book. Thus it is superfluous to say that the followers of Sri Gauranga will naturally be plunged into an indescribable ocean of ecstatic bliss by going through this tome. The society of insignificant living entities definitely hopes to acquire even a morsel from the inexhaustible, imperishable storeroom of priceless treasures in the home of those who served the Lord of Goloka for four months and thus received the most rare gift in this world - Sri KrsnaPrema.

Some people attempt to establish that the Mayavadi resident of Kasi, Prakasananda is one and the same with that foremost of Vaisnavas, Sri Prabodhananda. We, however, do not accept this in any way, shape, or form. In the third chapter of MadhyaKanda, Sri CaitanyaBhagavat, we find the following discussion regarding Prakasananda, the Mayavadi resident of Kasi - ‘Thus did Prabhu Visvambhar float in the ocean of devotional delight, in the company of his companions in Navadvip. One day, having heard a description of his incarnation of Sri VarahaDev, he roared loudly as he entered Murari Gupta’s house. Pleased as he was by Murari’s recitation of prayers in praise of Sri VarahaDev, the SupremeDeity of VarahaDev himself replied in anger to the personified Vedas, “I am without hands, feet, mouth or eyes! Thus have I been rendered a deformed creature by these Vedas. That rascal Prakasananda teaches like this in Kasi, cutting my body into pieces. He explains that, according to the Vedas, I have no form. Even if he is afflicted by leprosy in all of his limbs, still he won’t understand. My body is supremely pure, the object of all sacrifices. The demigods headed by Brahma and Siva sing the praises of such a one as He. Simply by the touch of this transcendental body one can attain virtue and purity. How is it that this rascal has the impudence to say that such a transcendental body is false? unreal!’

This event occurred sometime between the years 1425 and 1430 Sakabda. SrimanMahaprabhu made his auspicious arrival in SriRahga in the year 1433 Sakabda, where he found Sri PrabodhanandaPada along with his two brothers. They were at that time Sri Vaisnavas, coming in the line of Sri RamanujAcarya; thus were they the eternal servants of Sri Narayan, following the doctrine of visistadvaitavada (qualified monism). Prakasananda was at that time chief among the followers of the doctrine of Mayavada as propounded by Sankaracarya. To suggest that these two personalities are one and the same is the attempt of a crazy fool.

Prakasananda was the leader of the single-staff sannyasis at Kasi, the followers of Sahkar Sampradaya; Sri Prabodhananda was a triple-staff Ramanujiya sannyasi, a jiyarsvami (those who can bring back life to the fallen, conditioned souls), a resident of RangaKsetra who hailed from Mahisur. Prakasananda: Mayavadi Kasi resident; Prabodhananda: Kamyavan Vaisnava. Prakasananda: nirvisesavadi; Prabodhananda: visistadvaita savisesavadi (acintyadvaitadvaita); Prakasananda: inimical to Lord Visnu and the Vaisnavas, only becoming a devotee after he was delivered by SrimanMahaprabhu; Prabodhananda: an eternal associate of Sri Gauranga, the guru of VaisnavAcarya Sri GopalBhatta. To insult and abuse the most worshipful uncle and guru of Sri GopalBhatta Gosvami, an eternally liberated soul, the crest jewel of a family of devotees, by calling him a Mayavadi, inimical to Lord Visnu and the Vaisnavas, a conditioned soul, bound by the hands and feet - is a most heinous offense, sufficient to send one to the most horrible regions of hell.

In Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta, MadhyaLila, twenty-fifth chapter, and AdiLila, seventh chapter, there is mention of the Mayavadi Prakasananda. It is beyond understanding how that person who was a Mayavadi from the year 1425 to 1430 Sakabda, travelled to Southlndia in the year 1433, to become a Sri Vaisnava of the Ramanuja Sampradaya and then in 1435 Sakabda, again became a Mayavadi. Consequently, the attempt to establish that Sri Prabodhananda was previously Prakasananda is the endeavour of an ignorant fool. In effect, this propensity to try to uproot the tradition is a matter of no small distress. Because Sripad Prabodhananda Sarasvati was conquered by his own humility and destitution, he forbade any mention of himself in the pages of Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta through his nephew Sri GopalBhatta, thus was Srila Kaviraj Gesvami unable to transgress this request and therefore this dangerous situation has developed in the present. If he had known that such an aberration would arise, in which some sentimental fools would try to include him within the ranks of those inimical to Lord Visnu and the Vaisnavas, Sri Prabodhananda would never have made this mandate to Sri KavirajGosvami through Sri BhattaGosvami. The readers of BhaktiRatnakar will be able to understand this - ‘The wealth of the life of these three brothers, Tirumalaya, Vyenkata and Prabodhananda, was none other than Sri GauraCandra. By the mercy of Mahaprabhu, these three worshippers of LaksmlNarayan became intoxicated with the mellows of devotion to RadhaKrsna. Then the brothers thought, “How will we remain in the absence of Prabhu? People will try to take us with them to bathe in the Kaveri, to sport and enjoy some fun, but we will only be able to cry in separation from Prabhu.” Thus when Prabhu was preparing to leave after his four months stay, the brothers sent up loud lamentations. Prabhu embraced them and consoled (prabodh) them in various ways. Some say that Prabodhananda became famous as the sannyasi (yati) Sarasvati, due to a superfluity of this quality of ecstasy obtained through solace. He was especially dear to PurnaBrahma Sri KrsnaCaitanya Bhagavan; no one should think otherwise, not even in their dreams.’

Professor Aufret has composed a list of Vaisnava literary works with their authors, attributing the composition of Sri SangitMadhav to Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati. We have managed to collect a copy of this book, subsequently published in full in Sri SajjanTosaniPatrika, from the tenth year, issue number five, up to the eighteenth year, issue number twelve.

When a householder of the Sri Sampradaya renounces his home, there is no provision for acceptance of the single-staff order of sannyasa (eka-danda). Rather, they accept initiation in the triple-staff order of sannyasa (tridandi) and are designated with a name of the order of Sri RamanujAcarya. While examining Srila Prabodhananda’s Sri CaitanyaCandramrta, some have determined that he was a ‘BrahmaSannyasi’; however, without any specific proof, we consider acceptance of this proposal to be a deviation, an evil course.

Sri Siddhanta Sarasvati

9. The result of attachment to Gaura is the servitorship of Sri Radha    306
10. The most pre-eminent position of excellence is shelter at the lotus feet of Gaura    308
11. The path for propagating GauraBhakti is simply to request everyone to abandon all varieties of religion and accept as their singular duty the culture of affectionate attachment to Gaura    311
12. The mercy of Gaura, the most secret, succulent taste of the nectar of PureLove, is rarely achieved even in Vaikuntha    313
13. Devotion to Caitanya is the origin of the most attractive qualities - sweet demeanor, compassion, tolerance - the greatest fortune of the taste of Prema    315
14. In the absence of singular shelter at the lotus feet of Gaura, it is impossible to cross over the ocean of material existence, to relish the mellows of Sahkirtan or to attain the great wealth of Prema    319
15. The topmost conclusion is that prema-bhakti and renunciation have pledged themselves to the service of the GauraBhaktas    321
16. For those who have no devotion to Sri Caitanya, there is nothing to look forward to other than repeated births and deaths in this material world    324
17. Even he who has but a drop of devotion for Sri CaitanyaCandra is able to engage Lord Indra and the other Devas as his servants    326
18. Those great souls absorbed in the adoration of Gaura, likened to a touchstone, have not a care in the world regarding their maintenance (food, clothing, etc.)    328
19. Other than the devotees of Gaura, who is there within this world, intoxicated by the mellows of Prema?    331
20. GauraBhaktas have not even a pinch of desire to go and live in Kasi, or to go to Gaya to offer oblations to the ancestors    334

## IX Eminence of Sri Caitanya

1. Description of the super-excellence of GauraHari, his beauty, qualities, sweetness, heroism and magnanimity    339
2. The superiority of Krsna’s beauty, pleasureful delight, loving affection, benevolence, sobriety, gravity and sweetness, decorated as he is with the mood and bodily lustre of Sri Radha    342
3. The super-excellent glories of Sri GauraHari that cause astonishment in Siva, Brahma and the other demigods, are personally revealed to his devotees    344

6. The lamp of Navadvip that burns forever bright    353
7. GauraHari, beautifully ornamented with the symptoms of ecstatic love    355
8. GauraCandra, that unblemished moon that has arisen from the milk ocean womb of Mother SacI, causing the rains of the nectar of love to inundate the land    358
9. Sri GauraHari, deeply absorbed in and overwhelmed by feelings of love in separation, in the mood of Srimati Radhika    360
10. Sri GauraHari, the combined form of RadhaMadhav    363

1. Glories of Gaura, who descended along with his HolyNames that melt hearts as hard as thunderbolts    365
2. In this incarnation, Gaura awards Prema not only to those who are inactive in terms of spiritual practices, but even to those addicted to forbidden activities    368

5. During this incarnation, even the most common man can attain to the mellows of love in conjugal attraction, secretly hidden within the Vedas    377

7. In this incarnation, even the ascetics and proud scholars addicted to the path of fruitive gain, attain Prema    383

13. Some of the motives for the incarnation of Gaura are to give the purport of SrimadBhagavat and to disseminate the loving mellows of Sri Radha    405

15. The difference between the ever-changing philosophies of the learned sages, concocted from the plane of mental speculation and the objective (demonstrable truth) of love in devotion preached by the devotees; prema-bhakti as propagated by Gaura is what is to be ascertained from every page of the Vedas, the topmost goal of mankind    412

## PART I - The Glories of Sri CaitanyaCandra Definition of the Subject Matter through the offering of Hymns of Praise MahgalaCaran

### Verse 1

*स्तुमस्तं चैतन्याकति मतिविम र्यादपरमा- द्भुतौदार्य वर्यं ब्रजपतिकुमारं रसयितम्। विशुद्ध स्वप्रेमोन्मदमधुर पीयूशलहरीं प्रदातुं चान्येभ्यः परपदनवद्वीपप्रकटम् ।। 1 ।।*

*stumastam caitanyakrti mativimaryyada parama-*  
*dbhutaudaryam varyam vrajapatikumaram rasayitum*  
*visuddha-sva-premonmada madhura piyusa laharim*  
*radatum canyebhyah parapada navadvipa prakatam*

**May that Supreme Personality of Godhead Sri KrsnaCaitanya be forever glorified. His munificence is astonishing, endowed with grace and dignity, offering preferential treatment to all who come within his domain. He has come to relish the Elixir of Love (rasa) by churning the Ocean of the Nectar of His previous exploits as VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna, thus drowning one and all in the waves produced therefrom. Having descended to the transcendental abode of Sri NavadvipDham, birthplace of the nine limbs of bhakti, He is superior to all other incarnations. He embodies unlimited wonder and generosity. He is the Supreme Personality of Compassion.**

**Rasikasvadini Tlka**  
**(Purports by Sri Anandi)**  
**Sri KrsnaCaitanyaCandraya Namah**

I, Anandi, a very insignificant jiva, offer my humble obeisances at the lotus feet of my guru, Sri Nrsimha. With an attitude of single-minded devotion, I begin this commentary to Sri CaitanyaCandramrta, entitled Rasikasvadini, that it might help rasika Vaisnavas to relish (asvadan) the rasa contained in this composition of Sri Prabodhananda Sarasvati Thakur.

Sri Mohini, an incarnation of the Supreme Lord, used Her MayaSakti to delude the demons and then gave the ambrosia (amrta) of immortality to Her favoured demigods. In the same manner, this commentary is intended to delude those with a demoniac, atheistic mentality and facilitate the devotees in drinking the nectar abounding in Sri CaitanyaCandramrta.

Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvatipada is the author of this most auspicious, devotional treatise. He has enlightened the hearts and consciousness of the learned with the esoteric conclusions of Veda, Vedanta, Sankhya, Vaisesika, Patanjala, Mimamsa, Agama, Nigama, MahaPurana, Purana, Itihasa, Kavya, Alankar, Natakand other scriptures. Foremost of sannyasis, the illustrious and erudite, Srila Prabodhananda has realized the paramount truth and conclusion of all scriptures, by the Divine grace of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu - the fountainhead of all incarnations. Sri Caitanya has appeared in the midst of KaliYuga, imbued with the transcendental sentiments of Srimatl Radhika, the embodiment of the Supreme Lord’s hladini-sakti(pleasure-giving potency). Sri Prabodhananda begins this treatise by first ascertaining who the supreme object of devotion and worship is, and then establishing Him as the worshipful Deity of his composition. He has saturated his compostion with glorification of his beloved Lord’s transcendental qualities and characteristics.

In the first seven verses, the respected author eulogizes Srlman Mahaprabhu. In the first verse beginning with stumah tam, he establishes the reason for the Lord’s advent in Navadvip. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Svayam Bhagavan Sri KrsnaCaitanya (caitanyakrtim) is the object of the author’s prayers. The use of the plural, stumah indicates that his prayers are directed towards the followers of Sri KrsnaCaitanya as well.

The word caitanyakrtim is an unequivocal address to Sri KrsnaCaitanya. In Sanskrit, a part of any name refers to the whole and to the person directly. Just as in SrimadBhagavatam, Satyabhama is referred to as Satya, or Bhimasena as Bhima, similarly, the name Caitanya addresses Sriman Mahaprabhu.

In SatanamaStotra, Sriman Mahaprabhu is addressed as -caitanya krsna-caitanya dandadhrk nyasta dandaka- ‘He whose consciousness is imbued with Krsna, who has accepted the renounced order of life (sannyasa), but who has laid down his staff’. (In this incarnation, Krsna only destroys the demonic mentality of the people, without directly accosting them with his rod of chastisement.)

In this verse the word akrti means ‘name’ - akarayati ahvayati anaya iti akrtih- ‘a word that is used to call or address someone is known as akrti or ‘name’. Thus the word caitanya means ‘consciousness’; or he whose original form or identity is suffused with consciousness - caitanyakrti - the Supreme Brahman, who has appeared with a golden complexion, the embodiment of eternality, absolute knowledge and infinite bliss (sat-cit-ananda-moy).

‘What are His inherent characteristics?’

This is answered with the words, parapada-navadvip prakatam. Para means ‘supreme’, above everyone and everything; pada means ‘place’ - Navadvlp, the supreme abode, where He revealed Himself. Parapada also means ‘the eternal abode where He eternally resides’, or, parapada can also mean ‘the place marked with the impressions of the Supreme Lord’s lotus feet’. His birthplace at SridhamMayapur, along the banks of MotherGanga, is surrounded by the nine islands of Navadvlp, which represent the nine limbs of pure devotional service (hearing, chanting, remembering, serving the Lotus Feet, worshiping, offering prayers, servitorship, becoming a friend of the Lord, and offering one’s very self (atma) to the Lord), thus did Sri KrsnaCaitanya choose this place for his advent.

One may ask, ‘Why did He appear in Navadvlp?’

His main purpose for doing so is answered by the words -vrajapati kumaram rasayitum- he desires to savour His identity as the son of NandaMaharaja, VrajendraNandana Sri Krsna (from the perspective, or, in the mood of Srimatl Radhika). The secondary purpose is denoted by the words beginning with anebhyah (to others); thus, he came to distribute Radharani’s love for Sri Krsna. Visuddha means ‘pure, unalloyed devotion, devoid of any other aspiration’. Prema (love) means ‘the living entities’ love for the Lord, arising out of such devotion’. The quality of this prema is unmada-madhura-piyusa. Unmada means ‘the source of ecstasy, invoking laughter, pride and so on, sublimely nectarean, fortified with immortality’. Thus the secondary purpose for His advent is to freely distribute unlimited waves of prema and encourage the jivas to taste it.

‘What is the quality of generosity in the distribution of this prema?‘

ati vimasyadi paramadbhutaudaryam - an unlimited, supreme and most wonderful magnanimity that He exhibited in his act of distributing prema. Later in this work (verse 77), this quality of unprecedented magnanimity will be described {patrapatra-vicaranam). While distributing prema, He does not take into consideration whether the receiver is worthy or not; or if the recipient is one of His own. Neither does He ponder over whether it is His duty to distribute prema to a particular person or not. He does not bide time, waiting for an auspicious moment to arrive, but bestows the rarest treasure of bhakti-rasa, unattainable even through the processes of hearing, darsan, offering obeisance, meditation, and the like. May that munificent Supreme Lord GauraHari be my supreme goal. He is superior to all other incarnations of Godhead.

Sri GauraCandra, nondifferent from VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna, advented for the express purpose of savouring Himself, the absolute marvel of His own sweetness. When NandaNandan saw His own reflection in the water, the greed to relish His own matchless beauty captivated His mind. The Supreme Lord’s wonderment at His own self is echoed in the words of Sri

Uddhava: yan martya lilaupayikam... - “Lord Krsna appeared in the mortal world by His internal potency (YogaMaya). He came in His eternal form of unparalleled beauty, perfectly suited for His human-like lila. These pastimes were wonderful for everyone, even for those proud of their own opulence, including the Lord Himself in His form as the Lord of Vaikuntha. Sri Krsna’s transcendental body is the ornament of all ornaments.’  
SrimadBhagavatam ([3.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.12))

The most magnanimous Srila Rupa Gosvami has also described Sri Krsna in the act of marvelling at His own beauty, in his drama, Sri LalitaMadhava (8.84) (aparikalitapurvah...) - Lord Krsna, seeing His own reflection, says, “Who is this person that I see? He is infinitely wonderful and has never been seen by Me before; the embodiment of exquisite beauty! He who dares to be more handsome and attractive than Me, is present here before Me! О dear Me! By seeing Him, greed has taken control of my heart, and, like Srimati Radhika, I desire to savour and enjoy Him.”

Similarly, Srila Raghunath DasGosvami writes in his Sri CaitanyAstaka; harir drstva gosthe... - ‘Lord Hari, Sri Krsna, while tending His calves, saw the reflection of His flawless form and immediately fell into a reverie - “What would it be like to savour such sweetness? as does My beloved Radhika.” Thus did he appear in GauraDesh. Aho! How astonishing! Will that same Supreme Personality Sri SaciNandan, who has borrowed His splendorous, golden bodily lustre from Srimati Radhika’s golden complexion, be again the object of my vision?’

In my own composition, Sri CaitanyAstaka - nijam madhurim...- ‘I worship Sri GauraHari, who upon seeing his reflection as Govinda, even while basking in the embrace of His beloved, became extremely greedy to appreciate his own beauty and thus appeared with a brilliant golden hue, as the son of Mother Sari.’

The revered author Sri Prabodhananda possesses profound understanding of all the revealed scriptures and is held in the highest esteem by mature, spiritual preceptors. He has ascertained that Sri Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is the supreme subject matter of everyone’s prayers, obeisance, meditation and worship - the final conclusion - that He alone is the sole object of worship in KaliYuga.

One may raise the question, ‘On what evidence is the author eulogizing Sri Caitanya as the Supreme Godhead?’

In reply, the author asserts that only by the Divine grace of the Supreme Lord is one impregnated with transcendental knowledge, which in turn reveals that same Supreme Lord. Having received Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s Divine mercy, the author has been able to recognize Him as the Supreme Person; hence he glorifies Him as his worshipful Lord. By applying mundane proofs, like anuman (inference), and so on, God’s existence as the creator of the universe can be proven. However, mundane proofs cannot help ascertain the Absolute Truth regarding the Supreme Person. The reason for this is that without the Supreme Lord’s grace, such knowledge remains encrypted. So there is no other pramana (evidence) by which the Absolute Truth can be known, other than His grace. This is substantiated in SrimadBhagavatam ([10.14.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.29)), wherein Lord Brahma says, athapi te deva - ‘My Lord, if one is favoured by even a slight trace of the mercy of Your lotus feet, he can understand the greatness of Your personality. But those who speculate are unable to know You, even though they study the Vedas tor many years.’

The Absolute Truths (eternal principles) regarding the Supreme Godhead are known only on the basis of transcendental evidence received from the Supreme Person by His causeless mercy. Moreover, in the pastimes of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, sabda pramana, evidence from the revealed scriptures is accepted as the principle ‘via medium’.

The crest jewel of all evidence {pramana), Srimad Bhagavatam mentions a question asked by Maharaja Nimi -“In what colours and forms does the Supreme Person appear in each of the different ages? By what names is He known and by what types of religious principles is He worshiped in human society?” ([11.5.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.19))

Sri Karabhajan replies ([11.5.20-34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.20)), “In each of the four yugas, the Supreme Lord Kesava appears in various complexions, with a multitude of names and forms, and is worshiped by different processes. In SatyaYuga He is white and four-armed, has matted hair and wears a garment made of tree bark. His possessions are a black deerskin, a sacred thread, prayer beads and a brahmacari’s rod and water pot. People in SatyaYuga are peaceloving and nonenvious, the equable well-wishers of all creatures. They worship the Supreme Personality through austere meditation and by internal and external sense control. He is glorified by the names Hamsa, Suparna, Vaikuntha, Dharma, Yogesvar, Amala, Isvar, Purusa, Avyakta and Paramatma.

“In TretaYuga the Supreme Lord incarnates with a red complexion, golden hair, has four arms and carries a triple belt, representing initiation into the three Vedas - Rg, Sama and Yajur. He embodies the knowledge of sacrificial worship and His symbols are sruk-sruva (ladle and spoon used to offer oblations of ghee into the sacrificial fire). Those fixed in religiosity aspire after the AbsoluteTruth by worshiping Sri Hari, the abode of all the demigods, according to the sacrifices recommended in the three Vedas. Lord Hari is thus glorified by the names Visnu, Yajna, Prsnigarbha, SarvaDeva, Urukrama, Vrsakapi, Jayanta and Urugaya.

“In DvaparYuga the Supreme Personality appears with a dark blue complexion, wearing yellow garments, His transcendental body decorated with the golden streak Srlvatsa and the KaustubhaMani, carrying in his hands His own distinctive weapons. My dear King, in this yuga, those who desire to know the Supreme Personality (the SupremeEnjoyer), worship Him in royal opulence, according to the injunctions of both the Vedas and the Tantras. The devotees glorify Him, offering the choicest of prayers, addressing his as Vasudeva, Sankarsana, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, NarayanaRsi, Purusa, Mahatman, Visvesvar, Visvarupa, and Sarvabhutatman. In this way, the devotees glorify the Lord of the universe, according to the regulations of the revealed scriptures.

“In the age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead, who constantly sings the names of Krsna. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Krsna Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons and confidential companions.

“My dear Lord, You are the Mahapurusa, the Supreme Personality, and I worship Your lotus feet, which are the only eternal object of meditation. Those feet destroy the embarrassing condition of material life and freely award the greatest desire of the soul - attainment of pure love of God. My dear Lord, Your lotus feet are the shelter of all holy places and of all saintly authorities in the line of devotional service, and are honoured by powerful demigods like Lord Siva and Lord Brahma. My Lord, You are so kind that You willingly protect all those who simply bow down to You with respect, thus You mercifully relieve the distress of Your servants. In conclusion, My Lord, Your lotus feet are actually the suitable boat for crossing over the ocean of birth and death, and therefore even Lord Brahma and Lord Siva seek shelter at Your lotus feet. О Mahapurusa, I worship Your lotus feet. You have given up the association of the goddess of fortune and all her opulences, most difficult to renounce and hankered after by even the great demigods. Being the most faithful follower of the path of religion, You thus left for the forest in obedience to a brahmana’s curse. Only due to Your absolute compassion do You chase after the fallen conditioned souls, who are always in pursuit of the false enjoyment of illusion, while simultaneously engaged in searching out Your own desired object, Sri SyamSundara.’ SrimadBhagavatam (11.5.32- 34))

In KaliYuga, persons endowed with proper intelligence thus worship the Supreme Lord by engaging in congregational chanting of His HolyNames.

‘Who is this Supreme Lord? What are His characteristics?’

He is krsna varnam - of blackish complexion; He who is always describing Krsna, or chanting the syllables of his HolyName. His tvisa (lustre), however, is that of Srlmati Radharani, the embodiment of hladini sakti. Hence, He is akrsnam, not blackish; rather, His bodily lustre is golden.

Srila Sridhar Svami (the original commentator on SrimadBhagavatam) remarks that the Lord’s bodily effulgence is akrsnam, shining with the brilliance of the IndraNila Mani (gem), placed in the midst of Campaka flowers. Just as this jewel {mani) acquires the hue of the Campaka flowers, similarly, due to intimate contact with Srimati Radhika, Lord Govinda has taken on Her hue. Lord Govinda, whose complexion is the colour of the IndraNila Mani, has become golden externally. Thus, Lord Gauranga is the combined form of SriSri RadhaMadhava. In verse thirteen of this book, we find: ekibhutam vapuravata vo radhaya madhavasya - ‘When Sri Madhava united with Srimati Radha, they became one as Sri Gauranga. May He protect us.’ radha krsna pranaya vikrtih.....

‘Srimati Radharani, who embodies the quintessence of KrsnaPrema, is His hladini sakti. Sakti and saktiman - Divine Energy and the Energetic Principle are non-different; hence, although they are One Entity, they eternally exist in two individual identities. Now these two transcendental identities have again united in the form of Sri Caitanya to relish rasa-madhurya. I bow down to Him, who has manifest Himself with the sentiment and complexion of Srimati Radhika, although He is Krsna Himself.’    Srlla Sanatan Gosvamipada

*antah krsnam bahir gauram darsitahgadi vaibhavam...*

**‘The Supreme Personality, though of a dark bluish hue within, externally manifests divine opulence through His golden effulgence.’    Srila Jiva Gosvamipada**

‘What are the hallmark features of this incarnation?’

sadngopangastra-parsadam

anga- the Lord’s bodily expansions (like Nityananda) are non-different from Him

upanga- His limbs or eternal associates (like Sri Advaita) astra- weapons (in this incarnation his own HolyNames) parsadam- eternal companions and servitors like Srila SrivasPandit

Srila Rupa Gosvamipada has presented the import of this verse ([11.5.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.33)) of SrimadBhagavatam in his StavaMala, Caitanyastak, Verse 2:

*kalau yam vidvamsah sphutam abhiyajante*  
*dyutibharad akrsnangam krsnam makhavidhirutklrtanamaih*  
*upasyanca prahuryam akhila caturtha asrama jusam*  
*sa devas caitanyakrtiratitaram nah krpayatu*

**‘The Supreme Personality Sri Caitanya is worshiped in KaliYuga by those endowed with good intelligence, by the process of SankirtanYajna. Though He is actually dark complexioned, He has now appeared with the golden bodily lustre of Srimati Radhika. He is glorified by erudite scholars as the supreme object of worship of even the Paramahamsa sannyasis. May He abundantly shower His mercy upon us.’**

The import of this verse is quite lucid; we need not elaborate any further. In the following verse (SrimadBhagavatam [11.5.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.34)), beginning with tyaktva... the Supreme Lord is referred to as Mahapurusa, the Supreme Personality endowed with Divine physical features: hands extending down to the knees; neck shaped like a conch shell; whose voice is as sweet and deep as the sound of a conch shell. He is addressed as dharmistha - perfectly fixed in religiosity - since He is the inaugurator and protector of the YugaDharma - religious principles prescribed for this particular age (HariNam Sankirtan). Moreover, He freely dispenses prema without considering the caste, creed or eligibility of the recipients. Gratifying everyone in this way, He is, hence, the best among all incarnations of Godhead. In this context, yat implies one who is immutable, imperishable. He renounced the company and opulence of the Goddess of Fortune Sri LaksmiDevi, desirables most difficult to give up, greedily sought after by even the demigods, simply as the result of the curse of a brahmana. He then entered the forest (aranya), meaning that He embraced the renounced order of life, sannyasa. The verbal root kr is accepted by all other verbs, so the verb anvadhavat (running after) means ‘to embrace’. The meaning of aranya is ‘to take shelter of Sri Krsna’s lotus feet’. The order of life that helps achieve this shelter is known as aranya, or vairagya - sannyasa.

sudustyaja- that which is very difficult to give up

surepsita- coveted by the demigods - the Goddess of Fortune, Sri LaksmiDevi, by whose grace unimaginable opulence is obtained (yet the Supreme Lord renounced her company)

dayitayepsitam- that which aides the Supreme Lord in obtaining His most desired object of love, Srlmati Radharani, the embodiment of prema-bhakti

maya-mrgarm- an illusory object; searching after illusion anvadhavat- He has dissipated the conditioned soul’s attraction for the illusory, material world

nic-pratyaya (causative affix)- implies another, esoteric meaning: the one who acts in this manner (the Supreme Lord), whose lotus feet are worthy of worship and eulogy

These two verses from SrimadBhagavatam ([11.5.33-34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.33)) are prayers that glorify the avatar of KaliYuga, Sri KrsnaCaitanya. These verses can also be interpreted in such a way that they glorify Lord RamCandra. This is because Sriman Mahaprabhu is a pracchanna-avatar, a covered incarnation. Since these verses fall in the context of describing KaliYuga, however, those who are discerning know their real import.

**“This boy Krsna has three other colours: white, red, and yellow, as He appears in different ages. Now, in this DvaparYuga, He has appeared in a transcendental blackish colour.” "    SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.8.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.13)**)**

The word asan in this verse is in the past tense; hence it refers to the KaliYuga of the past. In the prayers of Prahlad Maharaja:

**“O Mahapurusa, You appear in various incarnations, sometimes as a human being, sometimes as an animal, or a great saint, a demigod, a fish or a tortoise, thus maintaining the entire creation in different planetary systems while annhilating the demoniac forces. In every age You protect the religious principles prescribed for that particular age. In the age of Kali, however. You do not assert yourself as the Supreme Godhead, and therefore You are known as triyuga, the Lord who appears in three yugas."    SrimadBhagavatam(**[**7.9.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/9.38)**)**

pracchana avatar- covered because of a lack of aisvarya (divine opulence inspiring awe and reverence)

‘To deliver the pious and annihilate the miscreants, as well as to re-establish the principles of religion, I myself appear millennium after millennium.’    BhagavadGita([4.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.8)))

In the VisnuSahasraNam Stotram, SrimanMahaprabhu alone has been described in the verse: suvarna-varno hemango...-‘the SupremeLord Sri GauraSundar endowed with a golden complexion. Indeed, His entire body, so well-proportioned, is the colour of molten gold, with sandalwood paste adorning His limbs. He will embrace the fourth order of spiritual life (sannyasa), thus remaining self-controlled, peaceful and firmly fixed in devotional service. By propagating the chanting of His HolyNames, He will usher in an age of peace and harmony.’

*suddho gaurnh sudirghahga stri srotastlra sambhavah*  
*dayaluh kirtana-grahi bhavisyami kalau yuge*

**“I will appear in KaliYuga on the banks of holy MotherGanga, a tall figure with a golden bodily complexion. Demonstrating immoderate munificence, I will inaugurate the congregational chanting of the HolyNames to deliver the Conditioned souls.”**  
**VayuPurana**

*antah krsno bahir gaurah sangopastra parsadah*  
*sacigarbhe samapnuyat maya manusakarmakrt*

**“I will appear as a human being with a golden bodily complexion, though within, a darkish blue. I will take birth from the womb of Sri SaciDevi and will always be accompanied by My expansions, eternal associates, weapons and companions.”**  
**SkandaPurana**

*dvivija! bhuvi jayadhvam jayadhvam bhakta-rupinah*  
*kalau samkirtanarambhe bhavisyami sacisutah*

**“O demigods! You must take birth on the earth without delay, as devotees of the SupremeLord. I will also appear as the son of Sri SaciDevi, to inaugurate the sahkirtan yajha.”**  
**NaradiyaPurana**

*kalau ghora-tamas channan sarvanacara varjjitan*  
*saci-garbhe ca sambhuya tarayisyami narada*

**“People in KaliYuga will be bereft of all proper religious conduct, thus immersed in nescience. О Narada, I will take birth in the womb of Srimati SaciDevi and destroy their sorrow and suffering.” VamanaPurana**

*anandasrukala-romaharsa puirnam tapodhana*  
*sarve mam eva draksyanti kalau sannydsa-rupinam*

**“O Tapodhan, in KaliYuga people will see Me as a sannyasi, eyes brimming with tears, my body erupting in horripilation and other ecstatic symptoms.” BhavisyaPurana**

*kalau prathama sandyayam laksml-kanto bhavisyati*  
*daru-brahma samipasthah sannyasi gaura-vigrahah*

**“In the first part of KaliYuga, the beloved husband of Sri Laksmi will incarnate with a beautiful golden bodily complexion and after embracing the sannyasa order, He will reside close to Lord Jagannath, the SupremeBrahman who has accepted the form of a Deity made of wood (DaruBrahma).” GarudaPurana**

*aham eva dvija-srestha! nityam pracchana vigrahah*  
*bhagavad-bhakta-rupena lokam raksyami sarvada*

**“I will appear in my eternal form as the best of the brahmanas, covered in such a way, however, so that no one will recognize my true identity as the SupremePersonality. Accepting the form of a devotee of the SupremeLord, I will continue to protect and maintain this universe.” NaradiyaPurana**

In spite of so much evidence from the revealed scriptures, less intelligent people and those with a perverted intellect refuse to accept Sri KrsnaCaitanya as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. It is for this reason that SrimadBhagavatam states unequivocally that only those endowed with superior intelligence (sumedhasah) will recognize Sri Gauranga as the Supreme Lord and worship Him in devotion.

The case ending of the verb yajanti, qualifies the type of worship - the intelligent persons must worship and serve the SupremeLord, devoid of any desire other than pure devotion.

Karika (concise statement in verse):

*sviyam asvaditum premadatum cavatatara yah*  
*navadvlpe parapade stumastam gauram isvaram*

**“We worship that Supreme Personality, Sri GauraSundar, who advented in the transcendental abode, Sri Navadvip, to relish Love of Himself and to shower others with that ргеmа.”**

**Purport**  
**Compiled From Gauriya Vaisnava Commentaries**

*sri-krsna-caitanya-daya, karaha vicara vicara*  
*karile citte pabe camatkara*

**‘If you are indeed interested in logic and argument, kindly apply it to the mercy of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. If you do so, you will find it to be strikingly wonderful.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**8.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/8.15)**)**

*yo ’jnana-mattam bhuvanam dayalur*  
*ullaghayann apy akarot pramattam*  
*sva-prema-sampat-sudhayadbhuteha*  
*sri-krsna-caitanyam amum prapadye*

**‘We offer our respectful obeisances unto that most merciful Supreme Personality, who has converted all the three worlds, maddened by ignorance, and saved them from their diseased condition by making them mad with wealth from the treasurehouse of Love of God. Let us take full shelter of that SupremePersonality, Sri KrsnaCaitanya, whose activities are wonderful.’    Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.54**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.54)**)**

By inaugurating the easy and sublime method of chanting God’s HolyNames offenselessly, in an age characterised by strife and chaos, Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu proved that His unlimited mercy is causeless. Chanting God’s Names does not require any material qualification and can be performed by anyone. At the highest stage of chanting - chanting of the PureName - the chanter becomes eligible to taste the ambrosia of KrsnaPrema that Caitanya Mahaprabhu specifically came to distribute to the three worlds.

At present, Navadvip (SriDhamMayapur) is located on the banks of the BhagiratiGanga (MotherGanges) in Bengal. Centuries ago, Bengal’s ruling SenaDynasty erected its capital there. During Mahaprabhu’s time, the township now known as Navadvip was called KuliyaGram. BhagiratiGanga, having since changed her course many times, makes it difficult to locate the exact places of many of Mahaprabhu’s pastimes. However, some of the locations of His lila (pastimes) are intact and well known.

Navadvlp literally means (in Sanskrit) ‘nine islands’. This holy tract of land became the stage for Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s transcendental appearance and pastimes. These nine islands are glorified in the scriptures as the Supreme Lord’s eternal, transcendental abode of Svetadvip.

*bharatasyasya varsasya navabhedan nisamaya*  
*indradvipah kaseruman tamravarno gabhastiman*  
*agadvipas tatha saumyo gandharvas tvatha varunahas tesam dvipa sagara samvrtah*  
*yojananam sahasrantu dvlpo ’yam daksinottarat*

**‘This land of BharatVarsa has nine divisions: Indradvip, Kaseruman, Tamravarna, Gabhastiman, Nagadvip, Saumya, Gandharva, Varuna and the island surrounded by this ocean (Navadvip). This island from North to South is a thousand yojanas long.’    VisnuPuran (**[**2.3.5-7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/2.3.5)**))**

The names of the nine islands of Navadvip are mentioned in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta: Antardvip, Simantadvip, Godrumdvip, Madhyadvip, Koladvip, Rtudvip, Jahnudvip, Modadrumadvip and Rudradvip. This transcendental abode of the Lord is the best place to practice the nine-fold path of bhakti, beginning with hearing and chanting.

Sri Krsna appears in every KaliYuga. At the end of the seventh Manvantara, in the twenty-eighth DvaparYuga, Sri Svayam Krsna, son of Nanda Maharaja, the source of all incarnations (avatari) appears, followed by Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s appearance in KaliYuga. In this incarnation, as Sri KrsnaCaitanya, He appears with His full potencies as Svayam Bhagavan, the fountainhead of all expansions and incarnations.

Thus, Srila Narottam das Thakur sings, in his collection of prayers- Prarthana:

*brajendra-nandana jei, saci-suta haila sei, balaram haila nitai*

**‘Lord Krsna, the prince of Vraja has appeared as Sri Caitanya, the son of SaciDevi, and Lord Balaram has appeared as Sri Nityananda.’**

Just as the incarnation of Godhead, Sri KrsnaCaitanya is non-different in every aspect from the SupremeLord Sri Krsna, similarly, the transcendental place of his birth and activities is also non-different from Vrindaban.

*rasajnah sri vrndavanam iti yam ahur bahu vido*  
*yam etam golokam kati paya-janah prahurapare*  
*sitadvipam prahuh param api paravyoma jagadur*  
*navadvipah so ’yam jayati param ascaryamamahima*

**‘What the connoisseurs refer to as Vrindaban, those expert in the conclusions of the Vedic literature, call Goloka; some others call SitaDvip and still others call ParaVyoma. In any case, this place is now manifest as the most magnificent Navadvip, endowed with exalted majesty and charm. Sri NavadvipDham ki jaya!’    GauraGanoddesaDipika(18))**

### Verse 2

*धर्मास्पृष्टः सततं परमाविष्ट एवात्यधर्मे*  
*दृष्टिं प्राप्तो न हि खलु सतां सृष्टिषु क्वापिनो सन् ।*  
*यदत श्रीहरिरससुधास्वाद मत्तः प्रनृत्य-*  
*त्युच्चैर्गायत्यथ विलुठति स्तौमि तं कञ्चिदीशम् ।। 2 ।।*

*dharmasprstah satataparamavista evatyadharme*  
*drstim prapto na hi khalu satam srstisu kvapi no san*  
*yaddatta sriharirasasudhasvada mattah pranrtya-*  
*tyuccairgayatyatha viluthati staumi tam kancidisam*

**I offer my obeisances to that Supremely Powerful Personality whose wonderful characteristics are not possible to fully describe. Even the most sinful persons, devoid of even a hint of righteousness, steeped in the depths of iniquity, who shun the company of saintly souls, thus removing themselves from their merciful vision, and who never visit the holy places sanctified by the devotee’s presence - such reprobates, now reformed, dance, sing loudly and roll on the ground in ecstasy, overcome by the intoxicating effects of the mellows of KrsnaPrema, after having drunk from the hand of the Supreme Lord this nectarean ambrosia of transcendental loving devotion to SriSri RadhaKrsna.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri GauraHari is glorified in this verse, having exhibited such extraordinary magnanimity in bestowing prema upon the most wretched and least worthy - dharmasprstah (those untouched by dharma). Pranrtyati - even these most wretched rascals begin to dance ecstatically and sing loudly, sometimes rolling in the dust, when rewarded with the nectarean taste of rasa. The most merciful Personality who accomplished this is the object of our heartfelt worship.

‘What type of person is indicated by the word - dharmasprstah?’

Those who are fully disassociated from religious activities; bereft of any piety. Such persons are engaged in abominable sins like raping the wife of one’s guru or a brahmana. Steeped in vice, they do not find the time or the conscience to repent. One may say that such reprobates do not possess the conscience to practice repentance, but the mere sight of a saintly devotee or a moment’s association with him can sanctify such a person.

darsanad eva sadhavah - a saintly person can purify one by his mere presence or sight

drstim prapto na hi khalu - such sinful persons never come in sight of the saintly devotees

According to a Vedic axiom - ‘a person is sanctified simply by visiting a holy place where devotees assemble’. Yet here: satam srstisu - ‘they do not visit such places frequented by saints.’ The word no is a proscriptive preposition, indicating negation. Thus even these profligates, when receiving and relishing the nectar of bhakti rasa from that divine Personality, begin to dance and sing in ecstasy.

sri hari-rasa-suddha:

Sri - endowed with sublime charm - Srimati Radharani Hari - Nanda Maharaja’s son, Sri Krsna

The transcendental mellows of love that the Divine Couple share for each other constitute immortal nectar (suddha). Lord Caitanya has come to distribute this prema-rasamrta to even the most fallen, and having received the taste of such nectar, these scoundrels become intoxicated. Just as people become inebriated by drinking alcoholic beverages and begin to dance, sing, and so on, so also, by relishing the ambrosia of prema-rasa, ecstatic symptoms like dancing and loud singing are manifest.

The word isan, the Supreme Personality, indicates that other than Him, ‘who has the power to evoke such responses?’

Karika:

*atyadharmi dharma-varjji hari-sambandhi-varjjitah*  
*yena datta prema-matto’ bhuttam gauraharirh stumah*

**“We offer our choicest prayers and hymns to Lord Sri GauraHari. Even the most abominable rogues, bereft of all religiosity and piety, with not the slightest inclination towards the Supreme Lord Hari, receive prema directly from Him, becoming inebriated with bliss.”**

Rasa - sap or juice of plants; juice of fruit; any liquid or fluid; the best or finest or prime part of anything, essence, marrow, water, liquid, drink, juice of the sugarcane; syrup, draught, elixir, potion, milk, nectar, constituent fluid or essential juice of the body; serum, primary substance called chyle (formed from the food and changed by the bile into blood); mercury, quicksilver (sometimes regarded as a kind of quintessence of the human body, elsewhere as the seminal fluid of Lord Siva); semen.

virile, any mineral or metallic salt; a mineral or metal in a state of fusion; species of amaranth; taste, flavour (as the principal quality of fluids, of which there are six original kinds: madhura - sweet; amla - sour; lavana - salt; katuka - pungent; tikta - bitter; kashaya - astringent); any object of taste, condiment, sauce, spice, seasoning; the tongue (as the organ of taste); taste or inclination or fondness for; love, affection, desire, charm, pleasure, delight; the taste or character of a work; the feeling or sentiment prevailing in it: srngar - love; vira - heroism; bibhatsa - disgust; raudra - anger or fury; hasya - mirth; bhayanaka - terror; karuna - pity; adbhuta - wonder; santa - tranquillity or contentment; vatsalya - paternal fondness; prevailing sentiment of human character; disposition of the heart or mind; religious sentiment: santa - neutrality; dasya - servitorship; sakhya - friendship; vatsalya - parental affection; madhurya - conjugal love.

**Purport**

*raso vai sah rasam hy evayam labdhvanandi bhavati.*

**‘He Himself is rasa, the taste or mellow of a particular relationship. And certainly one who achieves this rasa becomes anandi, filled with bliss.’**  
**TaittiriyaUpanisad(**[**2.7.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/taittiriya/2.7.1)**)**

*aisvaryasa samagrasya*  
*viryasya yasasah sriyah*  
*jnana vairagyayos caiva*  
*sannam bhaga itingane*

**‘Full wealth, power, fame beauty, knowledge and renunciation: these are the six kinds of opulence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.’**  
**VisnuPurana (**[**6.5.47**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/6.5.47)**)**

*isavasyam idam sarvam yat kinca jagatyam jagat*

**‘Everything animate or inanimate that is within the universe is controlled and owned by the Lord.’**  
**Sri Isopanisad** [**Mantra 1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/iso/1)

*nа tasya karyam karanam ca vidyate*  
*na tat-samas cabhyadhikas ca drsyate*  
*parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate*  
*svabhaviki jnana-bala-kriya ca*

**‘The Supreme Lord has nothing to do. Nothing is equal to Him or greater than Him. He acts in different places by manifesting His parts and parcels, which are all differently situated by His unlimited, variegated potencies. Each potency acts quite naturally in sequence, providing Him full knowledge, power and pastimes.’**  
**SvetasvataraUpanisad(**[**6.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/6.8)**)**

*vyatitya bhavana-vartma yas camatkara-bhara-bhuh*  
*hrdi sattvojjvale badham svadate sa raso matah*

**‘That which is beyond imagination, heavy with wonder and relished in the heart shining with goodness—such is known as rasa.’**

The Supreme Personality Sri KrsnaCaitanya is the most powerful being, as substantiated by the scriptures. Nothing is impossible for Him to accomplish. With his limited mental capacity, man is unable to understand Krsna’s unlimited, absolute nature and characteristics, without the help of a self-realised guru. The guru is able to remove the darkness of ignorance and open the disciples’ spiritual vision to understand the AbsoluteTruth, through the eyes of the scriptures (sastra caksur).

*janma karma ca me divyam evam yo vetti tattvatah*  
*tyaktva deham punar janam naiti mam eti so ’rjuna*

**‘One who knows my transcendental nature of my appearance and activities, does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, О Arjuna.’**  
**BhagavadGita (**[**4.9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.9)**)**

Srila A.C.Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupad comments:

“One who can understand the truth of the appearance of the Personality of Godhead is already liberated from material bondage, and therefore he returns to the kingdom of God immediately after quitting this present material body.”

In the Nectar of Devotion, Srila Prabhupad explains:

‘In the BrhadVamanaPurana, the Lord says, “Although I have many fascinating pastimes, whenever I think of the RasLila that I perform with the gopis, I become eager to have it again.”

One devotee said, “I know about Narayan, the husband of the Goddess of Fortune, and I also know about many other incarnations of the Lord. Certainly all the pastimes of such incarnations are exciting to my mind, but still the pastimes of RasLila performed by Lord Krsna are wonderfully increasing my transcendental pleasure.”

The only way the conditioned soul can attain permanent release from his eternal bondage in the prison house of this mundane world is by associating with saintly persons.

*yat-pada-samsrayah suta munayah prasamayanah*  
*sadyah punanty upasprstah svardhuny-apo ’nusevaya*

**‘Oh Suta, those great sages, who have completely taken shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord, can at once sanctify those who come in touch with them, whereas the waters of the Ganges can sanctify only after prolonged use.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.1.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.15)**)**

Srila Prabhupad: “Pure devotees of the Lord are more powerful than the waters of the sacred river Ganges. One can derive spiritual benefit out of prolonged use of Ganges water, but one can be sanctified at once by the mercy of a pure devotee of the Lord. In the BhagavadGita it is said that any person, regardless of birth, as sudra or merchant or woman, can take shelter of the Lord, and by so doing can return to Godhead. Such devotees of the Lord are equally worshipped with the Lord, for they deliver the fallen souls from the material world unto the lotus feet of the Lord, who wants them to return home, back to Godhead.”

*bhavad-vidha bhagavatas tirtha-bhutah svayam vibho*  
*tirthi-kurvanti tirthani svantah-sthena gada-bhrta*

**‘Saints of your calibre are themselves places of pilgrimage. Because of their purity, they are constant companions of the Lord, and therefore they can purify even the places of pilgrimage. ’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila(**[**1.63**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.63)**)**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

‘...that pure devotees like him \[Vidura\] are personified holy places, because the Supreme Personality is always with them in their hearts. By their association, sinful persons are freed from sinful reactions, and therefore wherever a pure devotee goes, that place is a sacred place of pilgrimage. The importance of holy places is due to the presence of such pure devotees.’

*‘suddha-bhakti’ haite haya prema’ utpanna*

**‘When one is situated in pure devotional service, he develops love of Krsna.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.166**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.166)**)**

*sarvopadhi-vinirmuktarh tat-paratvena nirmalam*  
*hrsikena hrsikesa-sevanam bhaktir ucyate*

**‘Bhakti’ or devotional service means engaging all our senses in the service of the Lord, the Supreme Personality Hrsikesa, the master of all senses. When the spirit soul renders service unto the Supreme, there are two results: One is freed from all material designations, and simply by being employed in the service of the Lord, one’s senses are purified.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.170**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.170)**)**

Srila Prabhupad:

“Bhakti-yoga means that the Lord is there, the devotee is there, and the activity of exchange of love between the Lord and the devotee is there. Therefore, the individuality of two persons is present in the Supreme Personality and the individual person; otherwise, there is no meaning to bhakti-yoga. If one is not situated in a transcendental position with the Lord, one cannot serve the Supreme Lord.”  
BhagavadGita([14.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.26))

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“Pure devotional service or suddha-bhakti is transcendental to the three modes of material nature and is free from the contamination of fruitive activities and empirical speculations. It is causeless and self-manifest. By engaging in pure devotional service one easily overcomes the illusory potency maya and thus attains KrsnaPrema.”

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur cautions us,

‘... that Krsna Prema is not attained on the level of bhakti-abhasa (shadow bhakti); only on the level of suddha-bhakti (pure devotional service) is one able to attain KrsnaPrema.’

Attainment of pure devotional service (suddha-bhakti) is the only ambition and desire one may pursue to make progress on the spiritual path to perfection, in the matter of serving Sri Krsna. All other desires are detrimental and create obstacles on the path. No one other than Sri Krsna should be the object of one’s worship, including Brahma, Siva and Paramatma. Finally, neither the desire for fruitive results nor the knowledge of impersonal Brahman must be allowed to soil suddha-bhakti. Thus, suddha-bhakti means ‘to free one’s existence and sadhana from the dross influences of material nature, adopting only those practices which are favourable to bhakti, channelling and dovetailing one’s senses in serving Krsna’.

### Verse 3

*yannaptam karmmanisthairna ca samadhigatam yat tapodhyana yogair*  
*vairagyairstyaga tattvastutibhir api na yat tarkitancapi kaiscit*  
*govinda prema bhajam api na ca kalitam yad rahasyam svayam tan*  
*namnaiva pradurasid avatarati pare yatra tam naumi gauram*

**That which is unattainable through fruitive activities (karma-yoga); which is not to be known by practicing penance, meditation and AstangaYoga; which cannot be realised through the practice of penances and austerities, renunciation of the fruits of labour, philosophical analysis, or recitation of hymns and prayers; What more shall I say! That which eludes even those devotees who are very attached to serving Sri Govinda in loving devotion - that most mysterious pinnacle of esoteric love manifests itself through pure chanting of the HolyNames. I offer my respectful obeisances to Sri GauraSundar, who brought the chanting of Sri Hari’s HolyNames with Him when he descended to this world.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

This verse glorifies the SupremeLord Sri Gaurahga for revealing the most esoteric knowledge - details of the intimate loving relationships in Vraja. We worship Sri Caitanya since His advent in this world is accompanied by prema, held within the syllables of His HolyNames.

‘Who is this Divine Personality?’

He is para, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself.

‘What is the quality of this prema He has come to distribute?’

It is rahasyam - extremely confidential. Furthermore, this prema is beyond the reach of those dedicated to karmic or fruitive activities, performance of sacrifice {yajna), etc.

‘Does that mean that prema is unobtainable by performing tapasya (austerities and penances)?’

Neither severe austerities and penances, nor astahga-yoga (the eight-fold path of mystic perfection), nor even meditation on the form of the SupremeLord (dhyana ) can award prema, what to speak of vairagya (renunciation).

Vairagya actually implies yukta-vairagya, renunciation through specific attachment. The symptoms of yukta-vairagya are found in the following verse composed by Srila RupaGosvami:

*anasaktasya visayan yatharham upayunjatah*  
*nirbandha krsna-sambandha yuktam vairagyam ucyate*

**‘When one is not attached to anything, but at the same time accepts everything in relation to Krsna, one is rightly situated above possessiveness.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu(**[**1.2.255**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.255)**))**

Another sense of the word vairagya, is ‘specific attachment to the SupremeLord in the mood of devotion’, meaning attachment to anything that has a connection to devotional service.

The use of the plural tairapi, implies that even after long perseverance in one’s religious practices, prema remains elusive.

Tyaga - abandonment of the desire for fruitive work (karma), implies engagement in suddha-bhajan (pure devotional service).

Tattva indicates knowledge of bhagavat-tattva.

God-realisation.

Stuti - recitation of prayers and hymns in praise of the Supreme Personality. None of the above will help one obtain prema.

Kaiscit - even with the assistance and guidance of an extremely rare devotee, prema remains unattainable. What to speak of others, even the dear devotees of Sri Govinda are unable to trace out that rarest spiritual love found only in VrajaBhava - that was made to appear in the Divine process of congregational chanting of the HolyNames made available by Sri Gauraiiga. I offer my salutations at His lotus feet.

Karika:

*visesa sadhanair yattu praptam kairapi svayam*  
*tat pradurasid уad vyaktya naumi tarn gauram isvaram*

**“I sing the praises of the SupremeController Sri Gaura Sundar, who with His advent divulged to the world the location of that rarest spiritual gem, prema, previously unavailable through any particular spiritual practice.”**

**Purport**

*jnana-karma-yoga-dharme nahe krsna vasa krsna-vasa-hetu eka—prema-bhakti-rasa*

**‘By following the paths of speculative, philosophical knowledge, fruitive activity or mystic yoga to control the senses, one cannot satisfy Krsna, the Supreme Lord. Unalloyed devotional love for Krsna is the only cause for the Lord’s satisfaction.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila(**[**17.75**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/17.75)**))**

Sri Krsna tells Uddhava:

**“My dear Uddhava, neither through astanga-yoga, the mystic yoga system to control the senses, nor through impersonal monism or analytical study of the AbsoluteTruth, nor though study of the Vedas, nor through practice of austerities, nor thorough charity or through acceptance of sannyasa can one satisfy Me, as much as one can by developing unalloyed devotional service unto Me.”**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.14.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/14.20)**)**

Srila A.C.Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“Karmis, jnanis, yogis, tapasvis and students of Vedic literature, who are not Krsna conscious, simply beat around the bush and do not get any final profit because they have no clear knowledge of the Supreme Personality. Nor do they have faith in approaching Him by the execution of devotional service, although everywhere such service is repeatedly emphasized in the scriptures.”

*bhaktya mam abhijanati yavan yas casmi tattvatah*  
*tato mam tattvato jnatva visate tad-anantaram*

**‘One can understand the Supreme Personality as He is only by devotional service. When one is in full consciousness of the Supreme Lord by such devotion, he can enter into the kingdom of God.’**  
**BhagavadGita(**[**18.55**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)**))**

Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“When Krsna says, mam -‘unto Me’, He means His original Self as the fountainhead of all incarnations. This is revealed only to those jivas whose hearts have been cleansed with unalloyed devotion in pure goodness.”

Visate mam - does not indicate the suicidal tendency of a convoluted intellect, desiring to merge the self into the brahmajyoti effulgence. It factually means the liberation of the self from the incarceration of the illusory potency, thereafter becoming eternally situated in one’s original spiritual identity and engaging in spontaneous loving devotion to the Lord.

*ataeva madhura rasa kahi tara nama*  
*svakiya-parakiya-bhave dvi-vidha samsthana*

**‘Therefore it is called madhurya-rasa, with two further divisions - wedded and unwedded love.’**

*parakiya-bhave ati rasera ullasa*  
*vraja vina ihara anyatra nahi vasa*

**‘There is a great increase of mellow in the unwedded conjugal mood. Such love is found nowhere but in Vraja.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.46-47**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.46)**)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“Madhurya-rasa (conjugal humour) has two manifestations: svakiya and parakiya. When one’s love for Krsna conforms to the mood wherein one thinks herself His legally wedded wife, it is known as svakiya-madhur-rasa. When one loves Krsna as one’s paramour, that is called parakiya-rasa. The preceptors of rasa-tattva have concluded that the heights of ecstatic loving emotions experienced in parakiya-rasa are the loftiest. This is not manifest in any place other than Vraja. This fact has been supported in the writing of the Gosvamis of Sri Vrindaban.”

*maya-kalpita-tadrk-stri silanenanusuyubhih*  
*na jatu vraja-devinam patibhih saha sangamah*

**‘The gopis’ jealous husbands consorted not with their wives but with doubles manufactured by Maya. Thus these men never actually had any intimate contact with the Divine damsels of Vraja. ’**  
**UjjvalNilamani /Krsna2 Vallabha(19)**

The gopis are the internal energy of the Lord and can never belong to any other living being. Krsna arranged their apparent marriage to other men simply to create the excitement of parakiya-rasa, the love between a married woman and her paramour. These activities are absolutely pure because they are the Lord’s pastimes, and saintly persons since time immemorial have relished these supreme spiritual events.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments in his anvaya (word-for-word), that the intrinsic meaning of the statement: ‘That which eludes even those devotees who are very attached to serving Sri Govinda in loving devotion,’ should be understood as referring to those who are not eligible to comprehend the intricate nuances of spiritual emotions in parakiya-rasa. He has included therein the followers of NimbarkaSampradaya, who are generally attached to serving the Lord in the mood of svakiya-prema.

### Verse 4

*drstah sprstah kirttitah samsmrto va*  
*durasthairapyanato vadrto va*  
*premnah saram datumiso ya ekah*  
*sri caitanyam naumi devam dayalum*

**I sing panegyrics to the most merciful Lord Sri KrsnaCaitanya, who alone is able to reward one with bthe essence of all spiritual loving exchanges (prema), even to those who see, touch or glorify Him only once, or who simply remember Him, offer obeisance or think of Him affectionately from a remote distance.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The Supreme Lord Sri GauraCandra is eulogized in this verse as the crest jewel amongst munificent personalities, because He so readily bestows the most rare, spiritual gem, BhagavatPrema (Love of God), even to one who has simply seen Him.

Factually, He alone is the only worthy object of one’s vision - this is implied in the word drstah. The import is, that if He simply becomes the object of one’s vision, then He can easily reward one with prema, including such spiritual sentiments as sneha (affectionate attachment) and the like-hence, we offer our choicest hymns in His praise.

‘What are His characteristics?’

He is devam - the SupremePerson, whose DivinePlay {lila) is to savour the taste of prema unto Himself.

We accept that He is capable of dispensing prema, but why does He so easily distribute that which is so extremely confidential?’

He is dayalum - infinitely merciful; sprstah - although it is very difficult for anyone to touch Him, He Himself comes forward and forcibly embraces anyone and everyone. This is His compassion.

Kirtitah - chanting the names of Sri GauraHari:- “O SaciNandan (son of Mother Saci), О KrsnaCaitanya, О unlimited Ocean of Compassion. О Supreme Awarder of prema to the most wretched, О Ocean of Mercy, О Friend of the fallen, О Golden Incarnation... Kirtitah also indicates that we should make Him the object of our meditation, remembering His exquisite beauty and charm, especially for those who cannot see Him directly. Or, if someone affectionately considers in his heart (adrto va) that Sri KrsnaCaitanya is the Supreme Personality and thus must be honoured and shown respect - then Sri GauraCandra is ready to bestow that most rare, spiritual gem {prema) to such a person. The word va has been conjugated with a passive case-ending, implying the other devotional limbs like hearing, remembering, etc.

Karika:

*yo darsanadi matrena patita premado bhavet*  
*naumi tam krsna-caitanya devam karunya-baridhim*

**“We offer our choicest prayers to the Supreme Person Sri KrsnaCaitanya, who is an Ocean of Kindness, for He bestows prema even to the most wretched, simply by His darsan**

**Purport**

*dhyeyam sada paribhava-ghnam abhista-doham*  
*tirthaspadam siva-virinci-nutam saranyam*  
*bhrtyarti-ham pranata-pala bhavabdhi-potam*  
*vande maha-purusa te caranaravindam*

**“We offer our respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of He upon whom we should always meditate. He destroys insults to His devotees; He removes the distress of His devotees and satisfies their desires. The abode of all holy places and the shelter of all sages, He is worshipful by Lord Siva and Lord Brahma. He is the boat for crossing the ocean of birth and death.”**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.33)**)**

*seita govinda saksac caitanya gosai*  
*jiva nistarite aiche dayalu ara nai*

**‘The same Govinda personally appears as Caitanya Gosai. No other Lord is as merciful, in delivering the fallen souls.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**2.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/2.22)**)**

*tomara darsana ye paya sei bhagyavan*  
*tomake dekhiye,—yena saksat bhagavan*

**‘One who receives Your audience is fortunate indeed, for You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself.’**

*tomare ye smarana kare, se haya pavitra*  
*darsane pavitra habe,—ithe ki vicitra?*

**‘Since one who remembers You is purified, why should it be astonishing that one becomes purified by seeing You?’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**7.8-9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/7.8)**)**

*yesam samsmaranat pumsam sadyah sudhyanti vai grhah*  
*kim punar darsana-sparsa-pdda-saucasanadibhih*

**‘One can immediately purify his entire house simply by remembering exalted personalities, to say nothing of directly seeing them, touching their lotus feet, washing their feet or offering them places to sit.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**7.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/7.10)**)**

*nehabhikrama-naso ’sti pratyavayo na vidyate*  
*sv-alpam apy asya dharmasya trayate mahato bhayat*

**‘In this endeavour there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.’**  
**BhagavadGita(**[**2.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.40)**)**

Srila A.C.Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:“

Activity in Krsna consciousness, or acting for the benefit of Krsna without expectation of sense gratification, is the highest transcendental quality of work. Even a small beginning of such activity finds no impediment, nor can that small beginning be lost at any stage. Any work begun on the material plane has to be completed, otherwise the whole attempt becomes a failure; but any work begun in Krsna consciousness has a permanent effect, even though not finished. The performer of such work is therefore not at a loss even if his work in Krsna consciousness is incomplete. One percent done in Krsna consciousness bears permanent results, so that the next beginning is from the point of two percent; whereas, in material activity, without a hundred percent success, there is no profit. Ajamila performed his duty in some percentage of Krsna consciousness, but the result he enjoyed at the end was a hundred percent, by the grace of the Lord.
