“The underlying meaning in this verse is that the infinitely compassionate Supreme Lord is always eager to shower benedictions on the conditioned souls. However, the gloom of ignorance keeps the jiva in illusion and deprived of the Lord’s mercy. The Lord is willing to generously lavish good fortune on anyone who may perform, even unconsciously or inadvertently, the slightest act of devotion, what to speak of a devotee who is constantly engaged in serving Him - to such a devotee He willingly agrees to sell Himself.”

In his Bengali translation of this verse, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati has placed ( vipralambha / love-in-separation) in brackets after prema, as the essence of all spiritual loving exchanges.

### Verse 5

*kaivalyam narakayate tridasapurakasapuspayate*  
*durdantendriyakalasarpapatali protkhatadamstrayate*  
*visvam purnasukhayate vidhimahendradis ca kitayate*  
*yat karunyakataksa vaibhavavatam tam gauram eva stumah*

**Let us glorify Lord GauraSundar, whose devotees, enriched by the priceless treasure of the Lord’s merciful glance, consider mukti (liberation), as coveted by the yogis (kaivalya), or the liberation of merging into Brahman (sayujya), to be equivalent to residing in hell. To these devotees, the goal of fruitive workers (pleasures of paradise in the heavenly planets), is as ephemeral as castles in the air.**  
**The rapacious senses, like poisonous cobras for the conditioned souls, become tame and without fangs for the devotees; and the temporary, phenomenal world transforms itself into an abode of happiness by constant engagement in the service of the Supreme Lord. Even the lofty and powerful position of Lord Brahma or Lord Indra becomes as insignificant to the devotees as that of a tiny insect.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The devotees of the Supreme Lord, recipients of the mercy and grace of Sri KrsnaCaitanya, are glorified in this verse. These devotees, having received the fabulous wealth of Sri GauraSundara’s merciful glance, consider even mukti (liberation) as hellish suffering. We pray at the lotus feet of that Supreme Being, Sri GauraSundar. The use of the plural form, stumah, indicates an exultant mood brought about by realising the immense fortune of Sri GauraSundara’s causeless mercy on the recipient, something that must necessarily be shared with others; thus the use of the plural.

Yat karunya - the Supreme Lord’s merciful glance is the real vaibhava (treasure) or inherited opulence. To those devotees who possess this spiritual treasure, kaivalya (impersonal liberation) is worse than hell. Just as, for the residents of different hellish planets, the possibility of experiencing the bliss of bhagavad-bhajan (devotional service to the SupremeLord) does not exist, similarly in sayujya-mukti, or kaivalya, such bliss is absent. Therefore, the SupremeLord’s devotees consider impersonal liberation as worse than hell. Lord Siva tells his consort, Sri Parvati:

*narayana-parah sarve na kutascana bibhyati*  
*svargapavarga-narakesv api tulyartha-darsinah*

**“Devotees solely engaged in the devotional service of the Supreme Personality, Narayana, never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation and the hellish planets are all the same, for such devotees are interested only in the service of the Lord.”**  
**SrimadBhagavatam(**[**6.l7.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/17.28)**)**

Tridasa-pura - abode of the demigods or svargaloka. It is as illusory as a castle in the air. Thus for devotees, heavenly pleasure is a phantasm.

Durdanta - incorrigible, irrepressible; indriya - the senses; kala-sarpa - a deadly poisonous snake; patali - a row of. The import of this sentence is that those devotees who have received Sri GauraSundara’s merciful glance are not afflicted by the siege of the senses vying for gratification. They are as ineffectual as the strike of a fangless snake. On the other hand, the devotees become extremely proficient in rendering devotional service to Hrsikesa, Lord Govinda, the Lord of the senses. In fact, these devotees perceive the world around them (visvam) as purna-sukhayate, full of bliss. This happens by the Lord’s grace, since they are able to project their devotional mood externally and thus see the SupremeLord everywhere. They think, “I am experiencing immense happiness from serving the SupremeLord - all others must be experiencing it too.” To them, the exalted positions of Lord Indra, King of Heaven, or even Lord Brahma, Creator of the Universe, are as insignificant as that of worms. For the recipients of Sri GauraCandra’s Divine grace, the bliss they experience is millions of times greater than the insignificant pleasures of Brahma, Indra and the other residents of the higher heavenly planets.

*krsna-dasa-abhimane ye ananda-sindhu*  
*koti-brahma-sukha nahe tarn eka bindu*

**‘The conception of servitude to Sri Krsna generates such an ocean of joy in the soul that even the joy of oneness with the Absolute, if multiplied ten million times, could not compare to a drop of it.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**6.44**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/6.44)**)**

Karika:

*уat karunyavatam moksa prabhrtir narakadivat*  
*bhavettam naumi caitanyam karunavaridhim harim*

**“I offer my most choicest prayers to that Ocean of unlimited Mercy, Sri GauraHari, by whose compassionate glance the devotees consider moksa (liberation) and the other ordinary aims of mankind to be equivalent to hellish existence.”**

**Purport**

*sdlokya-sarsti-sarupya-samipyaikatvam apy uta*  
*diyamanam na grhnanti vina mat-sevanam janah,*

**‘My devotees do not accept salokya, sarsti, sarupya, samipya or oneness with Me - even if I offer these liberations, in preference to serving Me.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**3.189**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/3.189)**)**

*‘sayujya’ sunite bhaktera haya ghrna-bhaya*  
*naraka vanchaye, tabu sayujya na laya*

**‘A pure devotee does not like to even hear about sayujya mukti, which inspires him with fear and hatred. Indeed the pure devotee would rather go to hell than merge into the effulgence of the Lord.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**6.268**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/6.268)**)**

Srila Prabhupad:

“Kaivalyam narakayate - The impersonalist’s conception of becoming one with the effulgence of the Lord is exactly like hell. Therefore, of the five types of liberation, the first four {salokya, samipya, sarupya and sarsti) are not completely undesirable since they can be avenues of service to the Lord. Nonetheless, a pure devotee of Lord Krsna rejects even these four types of liberation; he only aspires to serve Krsna birth after birth. He is not very interested in stopping the repetition of birth, for he simply desires to serve the Lord, even in hellish circumstances. Consequently, the pure devotee hates and fears sayujya-mukti, merging into the effulgence of the Lord.”

*siddha-lokas tu tamasah pare yatra vasanti hi*  
*siddha brahma-sukhe magna daityas ca harina hatah*

**‘Beyond the region of ignorance \[the material cosmic manifestation\] lies the realm called SiddhaLoka. The Siddhas reside there, fully absorbed in the bliss of Brahman. Demons killed by the Lord also attain that realm.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila(**[**5.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/5.39)**)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“The words tamasah pare mean - ‘the place beyond the material world of trigunas, similar to BrahmaLoka, also known as SiddhaLoka (the planet of the siddha-yogis). In this planet reside the Mayavadi impersonalists and demons like Kamsa and Sisupala, who were killed by the Lord. Yogis strictly following Patanjali’s eight-fold yoga system to attain perfection of kaivalya also enter this planet. In conclusion, devotees dear to the Lord enter the spiritual planet of Vaikuntha and experience the ecstasy of transcendental variegatedness - whereas the Supreme Lord’s enemies (the atheists and agnostics) enter SiddhaLoka {kaivalya), devoid of any transcendental variegatedness.”

*bhukti-mukti-sprha yavat pisaci hrdi vartate*  
*tavad bhakti-sukhasyatra katham abhyudayo bhavet*

**‘Desires to enjoy the material world and desires to become liberated from material bondage are considered to be two witches that haunt one like ghosts. As long as these two witches remain within the heart, how can one feel transcendental bliss? As long as these two witches remain in the heart, there is no possibility of enjoying the transcendental bliss of devotional service.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.22)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.176**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.176)**)**

*dhyayato visayan pumsah sangas tesupajayate*  
*sangat sanjayate kamah kamat krodho ’bhijayate*

**‘While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment for them, and from such attachment lust develops, and from lust anger arises.’**

*krodhad bhavati sammohah sammohat smrti-vibhramah*  
*smrti-bhramsad buddhi-naso buddhi-nasat pranasyati*

**‘From anger, delusion arises, and from delusion bewilderment of memory. When memory is bewildered, intelligence is lost, and when intelligence is lost, one falls down again into the material pool.’**  
**BhagavadGita(**[**2.62-63**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.62)**)')**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“In reference to the negative results of false renunciation while executing very strict, regulative devotional service (vaidhi bhakti), it happens that as soon as the mind begins to meditate on matter, attachment to enjoy matter with our senses develops, giving rise to lust and anger.”

*iha yasya harer dasye karmana manasa gira*  
*nikhilasv apy avasthasu jivan-muktah sa ucyate*

**‘One who engages in the transcendental service of the Lord in body, mind and word, is to be considered liberated in all conditions of material existence, although engaged in many so-called material activities.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.187**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.187)**)**

Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur comments:

“As soon as one develops the strong desire to be an unalloyed servant of the Supreme Lord Hari, he becomes liberated even while living in this material world.”

According to SrimadBhagavatam - liberation means, ‘being situated in one’s original spiritual identity as an eternal servant of Krsna.’

*evam prasanna-manaso bhagavad-bhakti-yogatah*  
*bhagavat-tattva-vijnanam mukta-sahgasya jayate*

**‘Thus established in the mode of unalloyed goodness, the man whose mind has been enlivened by contact with devotional service to the Lord, gains positive scientific knowledge of the Personality of Godhead in the stage of liberation from all material association.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam(**[**1.2.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.20)**))**

*yas tu narayanam devam brahma-rudradi-daivataih*  
*samatvenaiva vikseta sa pasandi bhaved dhruvam*

**‘A person who considers the demigods like Brahma and Siva to be on an equal level with Narayana, is to be considered an offender and an atheist.’**  
**PadmaPurana(1.73)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur sings, in his Saranagati (11) prayers:

*kita janma hao yatha tuya dasa*  
*bahirmukha brahma janme nahi asa*

**‘As long as I can remain your servitor, my Lord, I do not care whether I am born again as a worm or an insect. However, I have no desire to be born as Lord Brahma, if he is averse to serving You.’**

In the anvaya (word-for-word) to this verse, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad explains tridasapuh - as the abode of thirty-three demigods: twelve Adityas (sons of Aditi); eleven Rudras; eight Vasus; and two AsviniKumars.

### Verse 6

*madyantah paripiya yasya caranambhojasravat projjvala*  
*premanandamayamrtadbhuta rasan sarvve suparveditah*  
*brahmadims ca hasanti natibahu-manyante mahavaisnavan*  
*dhikkurvanti ca brahmayoga vidusastam gauracandram numah*

**We offer hymns in praise of Sri GauraSundar, whose unalloyed devotees are glorified by all the demigods. These devotees, madly inebriated by drinking in full measure the wonderful nectar of the most brilliant prema (ecstatic love of Krsna) flowing from the lotus feet of Sri GauraSundar, laughingly address Lord Brahma and others, saying: “Hai! Hai! (Alas! Oh me oh my!) “You have been deprived of tasting the ambrosia from Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet.” These devotees are not in the least impressed even by great Vaisnavas who are devoid of devotion to Lord GauraSundar. As for the impersonal brahma-jnanis and mystic yogis (astanga-yogis), they deride them for their contaminated intelligence.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Drunken devotees in the ecstasy of prema, inebriated from drinking the honey from Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, lament for those who are not devotees of Srirnan Mahaprabhu. The devotees of Sri GauraCandra drink (paripiya) fully and deeply the sublime, super-excellent ambrosia emanating from His lotus feet. This ambrosia is the bliss of prema which intoxicates them, making them sometimes laugh at others, sometimes neglect to show respect to others and sometimes behave even reproachfully. All glories to Sri GauraSundar who evokes such diverse emotions in His devotee’s hearts. The quality of prema referred to here is projjvala - most exalted; the radiant love exhibited by the gopis of Vraja.

Here one must ask: ‘At whom are the devotees laughing?’ The response: Lord Brahma and others (brahmadin). “Alas! Lord Brahma and other demigods could not experience the divine and wondrous nectar emanating from Sri GauraCandra’s lotus feet,” hence they become the object of the devotee’s belittlement, not out of ridicule, but out of sympathy.

‘What is the author’s response to the fact that these devotees do not show respect to others?’

MahaVaisnavan - though there be great Vaisnavas, singleminded in their devotion to the SupremeLord, Sri Visnu, if they have not tasted the nectar emanating from Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet, then they are not accorded much respect.

‘What may be said about those who are reproached by the devotees?’

Those who desire to merge into the bodily effulgence of ParaBrahman (brahma-yoga-vidusah) are censured by Sri GauraHari’s devotees, since they have deprived themselves of the happiness that comes from rendering devotional service to the SupremeLord.’

*virajante yasya vraja-sisukulasteyavikala svayam-*  
*bhu-cudahrair lalita sikharah padanakharab*  
*ksanam yanalokya pradata paramananda vivasah*  
*sa devarsir muktanapi muniganan socati bhrsam*

**‘Sri Narada was submerged in supreme bliss upon seeing, for a fleeting moment, how young GopalKrsna’s restless toenail was shining by the friction from the tip of Lord Brahma’s crown, when he came to beg forgiveness for stealing the cowherd boys and their calves. Sri Narada felt great pity for the liberated sages who did not see this amazing sight.’    Hamsaduta**

This is an example of sympathy (karuna rasa) felt for some unfortunate soul, on the part of Sri Narada. In MahaBharat, Sahadeva’s lamentation is marked by reproach-

*matar madri gata kutas tvam adhuna ha kvasi pando pitah*  
*sandrananda sudhabdhiresa yuvayor masid drsam gocarah*  
*ity ucchair na kulanujo vilapati preksya pramodakulo*  
*govindasya padaravinda-yugala proddama kanticchatam*

**“My dear mother, Madri! Where are you at this moment? And where are you? my father, Pandu! Lord Govinda, in whose lotus feet the entire ocean of supreme bliss has been compressed, is at present visiting our home. Alas! You are not here to see Him.’’**

Thus did Sahadeva, his heart full with exultation from seeing the lustre of Sri Govinda’s lotus feet, began to lament, feeling the absence of his parents.

Lastly, one may demand to know - ‘are the devotees of Sri GauraSundar always condescending and neglectful of others?

The answer: suparveditah - these devotees are glorified by the demigods. If it was true that Sri GauraHari’s devotees are neglectful and disrespectful to everyone, then is it possible that the demigods would eulogize them?

Karika:

*уat padambhojamadhvika pana-mattah suradikan*  
*avajananti tam naumi gauracandram prabhum harim*

**“I glorify the SupremeLord Sri GauraCandra, whose devotees are so engrossed in drinking the nectar from His lotus feet that they sometimes reproach even the demigods.’’**

**Purport**

*acaryam mam vijaniyan navanmanyeta karhicit*  
*na martya-buddhyasuyeta sarva-deva-mayo guruh*

**‘One should know the асагуа as Myself and never disrespect him in any way. One should not think of him as an ordinary man, for he is the representative of all the demigods.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.17.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/17.27)**)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“When the Supreme Lord accepts the role of an instructor, desiring to eternally benedict the conditioned souls, he is known as an асаrуа."

The eternal associates of Sri KrsnaCaitanya are acaryas in the GauriyaVaisnava sampradaya who, like bumblebees, are engrossed in drinking the nectar of audarya-rasa from His lotus feet.

audarya - generosity (of spirit), nobility, liberality, munificence

Narottama das Thakur sings:

*gaurdngera sangi-gane nitya-siddha kari mane*  
*se yaya vrajendra-suta pasa*

**‘Simply by understanding that the associates of Lord Caitanya are eternally liberated, perfected beings, one can be promoted to the transcendental abode of the son of the King of Vraja. ’**  
**Prarthana (1)**

*sri-caitanya-paddmbhoja-madhupebhyo namo namah*  
*kathancid asrayad yesam svapi tad-gandha-bhag bhavet*

‘Let me repeatedly offer my respectful obeisances unto the beelike devotees who always taste the honey of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. If even a doggish nondevotee somehow takes shelter of such devotees, he enjoys the aroma of the lotus flower.’    Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila(10.1)

*prabhu kahe,— “ei ye dila krsnadharamrta*  
*brahmadi-durlabha ei nindaye ‘amrta ’*

‘Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu replied, “This prasadam, flavoured with the nectar of Sri Krsna’s lips, defeats the taste of heavenly ambrosia. Even demigods like Lord Brahma find it difficult to obtain.’    Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (16.97)

*nantam vidamy aham ami munayo ’grajas te*  
*maya-balasya purusasya kuto vara ye*  
*gayan gunan dasa-satanana adi-devah*  
*seso ’dhunapi samavasyati nasya param*

**‘If I, Lord Brahma, and your elder brothers, the great saints and sages, cannot understand the limits of the Supreme Personality of God, replete with various energies, who else can understand? Although constantly chanting His transcendental qualities, the thousand-hooded Lord Sesa has not yet reached the limit of the Lord’s activities.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**2.7.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.41)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta Madhya Lila (**[**21.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/21.13)**)**

The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri KrsnaCaitanya, reserves the exclusive right to reveal Himself as He is to whomever He so desires.

**‘The Supreme Lord, being pleased by devotional service, reveals Himself to His devotees.’**  
**PadmaPuran**

*atah sri-krsna-namadi na bhaved grdhyam indriyaih*  
*sevonmukhe hi jihvadau svayam eva sphuraty adau*

**‘With one’s materially contaminated senses one cannot understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead or His Name, Form, Qualities or Paraphernalia, but if one renders service unto Him, the Lord reveals Himself.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu(**[**1.2.234**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.234)**)**

*ye ’nye ’ravindaksa vimukta-maninas*  
*tvayy asta-bhavad avisuddha-buddhayah*  
*aruhya krcchrena param padam tatah*  
*patanty adho ‘nadrta-yusmad-ahghrayah*

**‘O lotus-eyed One, those who think they are liberated in this life, but who do not render devotional service unto You, must be of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penance and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realisation, they again fall down because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.’ SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.2.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.32)**)**

### Verse 7

*rakso daityakulam hatam kiyadidam yogadi vartmakriya*  
*margo va prakatikrtah kiyadidam srstyadikam va kiyat*  
*medinyuddharanadikam kiyadidam premojjvalaya maha*  
*bhaktair vartmakarim param bhagavatas caitanya murttim stumah*

**In His incarnations as Lord Rama, Narasimha and others, He exterminated the atheistic and demoniac forces, but to what degree were these acts highly beneficial and altruistic? How profoundly significant was the revelation by His incarnation, KapilaDeva, of the path of SankhyaYoga, its philosophy and practice? Is the work of creation, maintenance and annihilation of this cosmic manifestation, carried out by His GunaAvatar incarnations: Brahma, Visnu and Siva, really that grandiose and impressive? Furthermore, was it such a fortuitous act that the drowning earth was reinstated in its original position after being lifted out of the waters of the Causal Ocean by Sri VarahaDeva? In reality, how beneficial were these great acts? (We do not consider these actions to be of any great magnitude, for they fade into insignificance before Lord GauraSundara’s munificent act of freely distributing Love of Krsna to all.) We offer our choicest prayers to Sri KrsnaCaitanya, the crest jewel of all incarnations, who has illuminated the path to attainment of the highest ecstasy in loving devotional service to the Supreme Personality (erotic affection in the mood of conjugal love).**

**Rasikasvadini Tlka**

Sri Gaurariga is glorified in this verse as the best among all other incarnations of God, since it is He that has broadcast the science of the most confidential and radiant prema, saturated with Divine nectar.

The use of plural number in the clause: bhagavatah caitanya-murttim stumah - ‘we eulogize the SupremePersonality, who has appeared in the form of Sri Caitanya’ - indicates His followers and devotees as well.

One may question, ‘why must you ignore all other manifestations and forms of the SupremeLord and glorify only Sri Caitanya?’

The author responds by saying- premojjvalayah ...vartmakarirh - ‘Sri Caitanya is the preceptor and propagator of that most radiant spiritual truth, prema - pure devotion in conjugal affection. He is the embodiment of ujjvala-prema and mahabhakti - prema-rasa leading to mahabhava. He is its pathfinder and guide.’

‘What are the characteristics of MahaBhakti?’

It is the most rarified realm of pure devotion where prema shines with intense brilliance. Ujjvala-prema means: when samartha-rati, the VrajaGopis’ unalloyed and single-minded love, totally devoid of any mundane designation, attains the most exalted stage of brilliance, known as srngar-rati. In srngar-rasa, the VrajaGopis (alamban - support) and their beloved Sri Krsna (visaya - subject) are constantly drowning in an ocean of infinite ecstasy.

MahaBhakteh is an appositional compound word derived from - mahati casau bhaktih - meaning: bhakti’s greatness is due to its purity. This level of bhakti was never publicized before by any incarnation of God prior to Sri Caitanya. It is true that innumerable and immensely powerful demons were exterminated by Sri RamCandra, Lord Nrsimha, Sri Krsna and many others, but what was the great significance of that? Factually, if compared to Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s pastime of distributing prema-bhakti to one and all, the value of vanquishing demons and evil forces is trifle. How much worth is KapilaDeva’s propagation of the path of yoga? Compared to the science of prema-bhakti, it is trivial. Similarly, what is so remarkable about the act of creation, or Lord Varaha’s saving the earth planet?

Thus we see that by broadcasting MahaBhakti, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu is superior to all incarnations of God.

Karika:

*ati gudhojjjvala bhaktih kalau yena prakasita*  
*avataravararh naumi tam gauraharimisvaram*

**"I glorify the SupremePersonality Sri GauraHari, superior to all other incarnations of God. In KaliYuga He preaches the most confidential and radiant spiritual science of prema-bhakti (devotion in the mood of conjugal affection).”**

**Purport**

*ramadi-murtisu kala-niyamena tisthan*  
*nanavataram akarod bhuvanesu kintu*  
*krsnah svayam samabhavat paramah puman yo*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who personally manifests Himself as Krsna, and the different avatars in the world in the forms of Rama, Nrsimha, Vamana, etc., as His subjective portions.’**  
**BrahmaSamhita (**[**39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/39)**)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Gosvami Thakur comments:

“His subjective portions as the avatars, viz., Rama, etc., appear from Vaikuntha and His own form, Sri Krsna manifests Himself with Vraja in this world, from Goloka. The underlying sense is that KrsnaCaitanya, identical with Krsna Himself, also brings about, by His appearance, the direct manifestation of Godhead Himself.”

*srsti-sthiti-pralaya-sddhana-saktir eka*  
*chayeva yasya bhuvanani bibharti durga*  
*icchanurupam api yasya ca cestate sa*  
*govindam adi-purusan tam aham bhajami*

**‘The external potency, Maya, who is of the nature of the shadow of the cit potency, is worshipped by all people as Durga, the creating, preserving and destroying agency of this mundane world. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda in accordance with whose will Durga conducts herself.’**  
**BrahmaSamhita (**[**44**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/44)**)**

Lord Krsna tells Arjuna:

*ekamsena sthito jagat*

**‘With a single fragment of Myself, I pervade and support this entire universe.’**  
**BhagavadGita(**[**10.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.42)**)**

**“A learned scholar, who has studied the Vedas perfectly, who has information from authorities like Sri Caitanya, and who knows how to apply these teachings, can understand that Krsna is the origin of everything in both the material and spiritual worlds, and because he knows this perfectly, he becomes firmly fixed in the devotional service of the Supreme Lord. He can never be deviated by any amount of nonsensical commentaries or by fools. All Vedic literature agrees that Krsna is the source of Brahma, Siva and all the other demigods.”**  
**BhagavadGita (**[**10.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.8)**) Purport**

*matsyasva-kacchapa-nrsimha-varaha-hamsa-*  
*rajanya-vipra-vibudhesu krtavatarah*  
*tvam pasi nas tri-bhuvanam ca tathadhunesa*  
*bharam bhuvo hara yaduttama vandanam te*

**‘O Lord of the universe, best of the Yadu dynasty, we offer our prayers unto You, mainly to diminish the heavy burden of the universe. Indeed, You diminished this burden formerly by incarnating in the form of a fish, a horse \[Hayagrlva\], a tortoise, a lion \[Lord Nrsimha\], a boar \[Lord Varaha\], and a swan. You also incarnated as Lord RamCandra, Parasurama and Vamana, the dwarf. You have always protected the demigods and the universe in this way. Now please continue.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.2.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.40)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**20.299**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/20.299)**)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

‘Lord Krsna says in BhagavadGita - “the only reason for My appearance, is - ‘My own sweet will’. When I have the desire to descend, I come as an incarnation: ‘Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious principles, and an increase in irreligious activities, I appear by My own sweet will to establish the principles of VarnasramDharma (an integral part of SanatanDharma). I select from among My devotees, the powerful sages from amongst royalty (rajarsi), and brahman - realized (brahmarsi) souls, investing My Divine potency in them. Acting as saktyavesa-avatars, they easily accomplish the work of re-establishing the principles of VarnasramDharma. However, to save My dear devotees from persecution at the hands of demons and atheists, I personally send my different expansions as avatars. Therefore, as YugaAvatar, I protect the saintly devotees, vanquish the evil forces and preach the eternal religion for the jivas, namely bhakti, beginning with hearing and chanting the Lord’s HolyNames.”

*anarpita-carim cirat karunayavatirnah kalau*  
*samarpayitum unnatojjvala-rasam sva-bhakti-sriyam*  
*harih purata-sundara-dyuti-kadamba-sandipitah*  
*sada hrdaya-kandare sphuratu vah saci-nandanah*

**‘May that SupremeLord, known as the son of Srimati SaciDevi, be transcendentally situated in the innermost chambers of your heart. Resplendent with the radiance of molten gold, by His causeless mercy He has appeared in this age of Kali to bestow what no incarnation ever offered before - the most sublime and radiant spiritual knowledge of the mellow taste of His Service.’**  
**Sri Caitanya Caritamrta AdiLila(**[**1.4**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.4)**)**

## PART II - Salutations at the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra

### Verse 8

*namas caitanyacandraya*  
*koticandranana tvise*  
*premanandabdhi candraya*  
*caru candramsuhasine*

**He is like the full-moon rising from the ambrosial ocean of ecstatic bliss of Love for Krsna, his beatific face more radiant than millions of full moons. The enchanting beauty of the honey-sweet smile playing on His lotus lips is as luminescent as moonlight. We offer our respectful obeisance to Sri CaitanyaCandra.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The following five verses are offerings of obeisance by the revered author. In this verse he perceives the sublime influence of Sriman Mahaprabhu’s moonlike qualities that extirpate the darkness of ignorance in the hearts of the conditioned souls, illuminating their hearts with the transcendental bliss of prema. Thus the Lord is offered obeisance with the words namah caitanya candraya - salutations to the CaitanyaMoon (the dawning moon of consciousness) - Sri CaitanyaDeva.

One may desire to know, ‘what is this moon like?’

The author responds - koti candrаnаnа tvise - ‘the radiance of His face is as bright as billions of moons’; premanandabdhi candraya - ‘the moon rising from the ocean of ecstatic love floods the entire universe by its rays with the bliss of prema’; carucandramsu hasine - ‘His smile is infinitely more winsome than the pearly drops of the moon’s rays’. A fleeting touch of His smile inundates the universe with the ecstasy of prema.

‘What then will happen if one gazes upon this smiling face?’ kaimutya-nyaya - the obvious need not be stated.

The karika verse is absent here since this verse is composed in anustupa-chanda (eighteen syllables with four parts).

**Purport**

The SrimadBhagavatam states that even the greatest sages, including AnantaSesa with His thousands of mouths, cannot fully describe the transcendental beauty and excellencies of the SupremePersonality (Sri KrsnaCaitanya).

Srila Rupa Gosvami begs for forgiveness from the Lord for using analogies and comparisons from the mundane world to describe the Lord’s Divine attributes, thus stating that the Lord’s beauty has factually no equivalent in this mundane world. To appreciate the Lord’s bewitching charm and all-attractive personality one needs transcendental vision and a purified consciousness.

*nа tu mam sakyase drastum anenaiva sva-caksusa*  
*divyarh dadami te caksuh pasya me yogam aisvaram*

**‘You cannot see Me with your present eyes; therefore, I give you Divine eyes, by which you can behold My mystic opulence.’**  
**BhagavadGita (**[**11.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/11.8)**)**

*premanjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena*  
*santah sadaiva hrdayesu vilokayanti*  
*yam syamasundaram acintya-guna-svarupam*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**‘I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, Who is SyamSundara, Krsna Himself with inconceivable, innumerable attributes, whom the pure devotees see in their heart of hearts with the eye of devotion tinged with the salve of love.’**  
**BrahmaSamhita (**[**38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/38)**)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“True devotees see that form in their purified hearts under the influence of devotional trance. The form Syama is not the blue colour visible in this mundane world, but is the transcendental, variegated colour affording eternal bliss, invisible to the mortal eye.”

### Verse 9

*yasyaiva padambuja bhaktilabyah*  
*premabhidhanah paramah pumarthah*  
*tasmai jaganmangalamarigalaya*  
*caitanyacandraya namo namaste*

**Unalloyed devotional surrender at Your lotus feet can alone reward the highest goal of human life, KrsnaPrema - far more elevated than the other four goals enunciated in the Vedas (dharma- religion; artha- economic development; kama- sense gratification; moksa- liberation). You are the dBenediction Moon, the cause of all auspiciousness in the universe. We respectfully offer our repeated obeisances unto You again and again, О Sri CaitanyaCandra!**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

This verse emphasizes the esoteric principle that Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s devotees are the only ones eligible to attain prema, the highest aim of mankind enunciated in the Vedas (for the sake of the soul). Tasmai means Sri Caitanya, the dispenser of prema.

‘What kind of personality is He?’

Premabhidhanah- prema- the most precious spiritual gem, obtained solely by rendering loving devotional service to Sri CaitanyaCandra’s lotus feet. In the word yasyaiva (by whom), the syllable eva is used to stress that in KaliYuga Sri Caitanya is the only worshipful SupremePersonality. Only by one-pointed devotional service to His lotus feet can anyone attain prema, the supreme goal of life; not by any other means.

Rendering loving devotional service to Sri KrsnaCaitanya is therefore jagan mangala- all that is benedictory in the world; the most blessed attainment - prema. He who bestows this Divine spiritual treasure is Sri CaitanyaCandra, at whose lotus feet I offer my repeated obeisance. Comparing Sri CaitanyaCandra to the moon signifies that the rays emanating from Him destroy the pall of nescience in the jiva ’s hearts and motivate them to relish the nectar of prema.

**Purport**

Upon seeing Lord Caitanya in Prayag, Rupa Gosvami described Him as follows:

*namo maha-vadanyaya krsna-prema-pradaya te*  
*krsnaya krsna-caitanya-namne gaura-tvise namah*

**‘O most munificent incarnation! Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu - more magnanimous than any other avatar, even Krsna Himself. You are bestowing freely what no one else has ever given—pure love of Krsna. We offer our respectful obeisances unto You, who have assumed the radiant golden colour of Srimati Radharani’s bodily complexion.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.53**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.53)**)**

*ajanu lambita bhujau kanakavadatau*  
*sankirtanaika-pitarau kamalaya-taksau*  
*visvambharau dvijavarau yuga-dharma-palau*  
*vande jagat priyakarau karunavatarau*

**‘I worship Sri Visvambhar (Caitanya Mahaprabhu), whose arms extend down to His knees; whose beautiful complexion is as radiant as molten gold; whose elongated eyes are like red lotuses. Oh Best of the Brahmanas; Guardian of religious principles for this age; most Munificent Benefactor of all living entities; most Compassionate Incarnation of God, I offer homage unto You, the most dear Being in the universe, the father of sahkirtan (congregational chanting of the HolyNames of Sri Hari).’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaBhagavat (**[**1.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/1.1)**))**

**‘For a devotee who has actually developed prema (love of Krsna - the fifth goal of life), the pleasure derived from the other four aims of human life (dharma, artha, kama and moksa) appears as a mere drop in the presence of a vast ocean.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**7.85**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/7.85)**)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“Dharma, artha, kama and moksa are four aims of mankind prescribed in the Vedas, known as purusartha. KrsnaPrema (love of Krsna) is the fifth. The first symptom experienced in the state of liberation is the bliss of Brahman realisation. This is insignificant compared to the bliss of serving Krsna in loving surrender. These four Vedic goals are not the ripened fruit of chanting Krsna’s HolyNames. All the revealed scriptures unanimously endorse love of God, KrsnaPrema as the only result of chanting Krsna’s Names.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Gosvami Thakur comments:

“KrsnaPrema is indispensable in the jivas understanding of the highest human goal. It brings out in him (the jiva) the most sublime devotional feelings of love. When the four Vedic goals are compared to this most exalted fifth goal - KrsnaPrema, sense gratification and liberation become insignificant and fallible. Both sense gratification (kama) and liberation (moksa) are based on these mutable, gross and subtle bodies, whereas love of Krsna is the atma ’s eternal immutable religion (spiritual activity: dharma)."

*tvat-saksat-karanahlada-visuddhabdhi-sthitasya me*  
*sukhani gospadayante brahmany api jagad-guro*

**‘My dear Lord, О master of the universe, since I have directly seen You, transcendental bliss has taken the shape of a great ocean. Being situated in that ocean, I now realize all other so-called happiness to be like the water contained in the hoof print of a calf.’**  
**HariBhaktiSudhodaya (**[**14.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbs/14.36)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**7.98**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/7.98)**)**

Love of God (KrsnaPrema) cannot be attained by any process other than pure devotional service, devoid of any other aspiration. The process of pure devotional service begins with hearing and chanting Krsna’s transcendental Name, Beauty, Qualities, Pastimes, etc.

### Verse 10

*uccairasphalayantam karacaranam aho hema dandaprakandau*  
*bahu proddhrtya sattandava taralatanum pundarikayataksam*  
*visvasyamangalaghnam kimapi hari harityunmadanandanadair*  
*vande tam deva cudamanim atula rasavista caitanya candram*

**Aho! (How wonderful!) Imbued with the emotions of Srimati Radhika, He is possessed by the incomparable mellows (rasa) of intimate loving exchanges with Sri Krsna. His eyes like the blooming petals of a lotus, He is absorbed in dancing with His powerful golden arms raised high above his head. His hands and feet move with restless rhythm, impelled by the force of wild dancing (tandava-nrtya). His body and limbs move to and fro, ebbing and flowing with the waves of His moods, having offered themselves to the dance in ecstatic abandon. Erupting from His lotus mouth are the frenzied cries of ’Hari! Hari!’ this sublime vibration having uprooted inauspiciousness from the entire universe. I offer my obeisance to Sri KrsnaCaitanyaCandra, the crest jewel of all the Devas.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In this verse the respected author offers obeisance to Sri CaitanyaDeva, presenting before us an impressive picture of the Lord’s ecstatic dancing during sankirtan.

atula rasavista caitanya candram - atula- incomparable, without equal, unparalleled; rasa- transcendental humour, most confidential loving exchange between Srimati Radhika (asraya- the supreme shelter of rasa) and Sri Krsna (visaya- the supreme object of rasa); avista- totally immersed in this rasa, rapt, devoted, possessed, overwhelmed; caitanya candram- the Moon of Consciousness, Sri CaitanyaDeva.

‘What are His characteristics?’

He is deva-cudamanim- the crest jewel of all the Devas (Gods, Deities, demigods, etc.) All incarnations of Bhagavan (the supreme, most opulent Person) engage in lila (Divine play), either to satisfy His own sweet will, or for the transcendental pleasure of His devotees. Sri Caitanya is the most exalted of all avatars since He freely rewards everyone, even the most fallen, with ecstatic love of Krsna (prema). He presents the most amazing portrait of the Divine, totally absorbed in ecstatic dancing; His arms (hemadanda-prakandau - long, graceful, golden magic wands) move to and fro, raised high above His head, while His feet move restlessly, hither and thither. His body sways, surging with spiritual emotions. Such unprecedented beauty! - pundarikayataksam- His beatific countenance is adorned with eyes shaped like blooming lotus petals. By His loud, exultant chanting of ‘Hari! Hari! ’ (harityunmada nandanadair) everything inauspicious in the world is annihilated. In this verse, the revered author again uses the soubriquet, candram (the CaitanyaMoon), revealing the source of these cooling rays of transcendental pleasure.

Karika:

*uddhrtya bahu-yugalam nrtyantam karacalanaih*  
*harihriti tair visvasubhaghnam gauramanamam*

**“I offer my obeisance to Sri GauraHari, dancing in ecstasy, His two arms swaying to and fro above his head. By His loud cries, roaring with the Names of Sri Hari, all inauspiciousness in this world is destroyed.”**

**Purport**

In the Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta it is confirmed that the main purpose of the Supreme Personality Sri Krsna’s descent in KaliYuga, as Sri KrsnaCaitanya Avatar, is to fulfill three desires of His heart - to understand: 1) the glory of Srimati Radharani’s love, 2) the wonderful qualities in Him (Sri Krsna) that She alone relishes through Her love, and 3) the happiness she feels when she realises the sweetness of His love.

Srimati Radhika is Krsna’s original, internal potency, while Lord Sri Krsna is the possessor of this potency. By the verdict of all the scriptures, Radha and Krsna are one, but they have separated themselves eternally, taking two individual forms for the sole purpose of relishing the humour of their transcendental pastimes. Thus, to propagate prema-bhakti (pure devotional service), Sri Krsna appears as Sri KrsnaCaitanya, infused with the emotions and complexion of Srimati Radhika.

*evam-vratah sva-priya-nama-kirtya jatanurago druta-citta uccaih*  
*hasaty atho roditi rauti gayaty unmada-van nrtyati loka-bahyah*

**‘By chanting the HolyNames of the Supreme Lord one attains love of Krsna. Then the devotee identifies himself as an eternal servant of the Lord, gradually becoming attached to a particular Name and Form of the Supreme Personality. As his heart melts with ecstatic love, he laughs very loudly, cries or shouts. Sometimes he sings and dances like a madman, indifferent to public opinion.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**11.2.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.40)**))**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“Those advanced souls, undeviatingly fixed in service to Sri Krsna, become oblivious of this material world and mundane society. Attachment and attraction born out of chanting the HolyNames of the dearmost Lord of their heart, Sri Krsna, manifests in their bodies along with ecstatic symptoms like laughing, crying, singing, dancing, etc.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur elaborates on this point:

“Nondevotees, who have no attraction for Krsna, due to their uncontrolled senses and restless mind, exhibit symptoms of mundane emotions like laughing, crying, dancing and singing, etc. However, these mundane emotions are not beneficial for them. Such artificial symptoms manifest in the body through the senses are to be diligently shunned by those embracing the path of hearing, chanting and remembering Sri Krsna’s Names. When the soul’s original nature is awakened, spiritual emotions become manifest - ecstatic symptoms such as laughing, crying, dancing, singing and eagerness make their appearance. All these expressions are the soul’s natural proclivity, once attraction to the service of Sri Krsna awakens.”

The HolyNames of Sri Krsna are the all-purifying means, and, according to KaliSantaraUpanisad, to save oneself from the contamination of KaliYuga, there is no alternative to chanting the MahaMantra. This conclusion is arrived at only after researching all the Vedic scriptures.

Srila Rupa Gosvami writes in the third verse of Sri KrsnaNamastak, that anyone who chants or hears the HolyNames, in any frame of mind, is immediately enlightened with the knowledge of the science of devotional service to Krsna, even if such persons have not the slightest realisation on this topic.

### Verse 11

*ananda lilamaya vigrahaya*  
*hemabha divyacchavi sundaraya*  
*tasmai maha premarasa pradaya*  
*caitanya candraya namo namaste*

**We offer our repeated obeisances to Sri CaitanyaCandra, whose transcendental body is imbued with ecstatic pastimes (lila), presenting a most enchanting picture, radiant with the brilliance of molten gold. Your principle pastime is to distribute the liquid mellows of loving devotion to Sri Krsna; obeisances to you again and again.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya is portrayed in this verse as the embodiment of unlimited bliss; the source of Divine, unparalleled beauty. He is the dispenser of the loftiest form of love (madhur ujjvala prema), imbued with the erotic sentiments of conjugal attraction. Tasmai (unto You) namo namaste conveys the sense of offering repeated obeisance at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.

‘Who is this Sri Caitanya?’

Ananda lilamaya vigraha- the embodiment of transcendental bliss, always engaged in Divine play. He is hemabha- who captivates everyone with His golden bodily lustre; mahaprema rasa pradaya- the benefactor of the mellow taste of the most exalted loving spiritual exchanges, found only in Vraja. The moon represents the nectar of prema; ananda suggests that He is the embodiment of ecstatic bliss, and hemabha means an unprecedented and amazing golden radiance that destroys nescience.

Karika:

*tapta kancana gaurangam ananda rasa vigraham*  
*nigudha premadam srimac caitanyam pranamamyaham*

**“I offer my obeisance to Sri Caitanya, whose bodily lustre is like molten gold, who is the embodiment of the mellow taste of transcendental ecstasy, and who confers confidential, ecstatic prema."**

**Purport**

Srila Rupa Gosvami begins Sri BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu with the following words:

*akhila-rasamrta murtih*

Srila Jiva Gosvami gives an explanation of these words in his commentary, saying, “Sri Krsna is known as ‘the ocean of nectar’ because He is the embodiment of all the twelve spiritual humours {rasas), beginning with santa, dasya, etc. Thus, in the SrimadBhagavatam (10.41.28), Krsna is described as ananda-murtim-upaguhya- ‘embracing the personal form of ecstasy’.

The same Supreme Personality Sri Krsna has now appeared in KaliYuga as Sri KrsnaCaitanya. In this incarnation the Supreme Personality exhibits the unprecedented pastime called audarya - ‘distributing love of Krsna without discrimiination’.”

### Verse 12

*pravahairasrunam navajalada koti iva drsau*  
*dadhanam premarddhya paramapada koti prahasanam*  
*vamantam madhuryairamrta nidhi kotiriva tanu-*  
*cchatabhistam vande harimahaha sannyasa kapatam*

**Aho! (I say!) To He from whose eyes rain tears, giving the impression that myriad, monsoon-laden clouds have been trapped in them; whose unlimited treasure of love overshadows all, rendering billions of Vaikunthas as farcical comedies; the enchanting beauty and lustrous charm of His transcendental body agitates the waves of billions of oceans of nectar - to Sri GauraHari, who has disguised Himself as a sannyasi, I offer homage.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

This series of invocatory prayers offering obeisance to Sriman Mahaprabhu concludes with this verse, describing in great wonderment, the supremely amazing, Divine qualities and activities of Sri Caitanya. The term ahaha (Aho!) is an exclamatory expression denoting stupefaction.

‘Who is Lord Hari?’

He is sannyasa kapatam- pretending to be a sannyasi (renounced mendicant), He has become the object of everyone’s glorification and reverence. The general populace, by seeing and offering obeisance to a sannyasi, accrues ajnata sukrti (devotional acts executed unknowingly), conducive for KrsnaBhakti.

‘What are His characteristics?’

He is asrunam pravahaih- whose eyes, like fresh monsoon clouds pour incessant rain; premarddhya- who freely distributes an unlimited wealth of prema that mocks millions upon millions of Vaikuntha planets, portraying them as satirical comedies; tanucchatabhih- whose lustrous loveliness and captivating charm, vamantam- churn the waves of billions of oceans of ambrosia.

Karika:

*prema dhikkrta vaikuntham asrupura galaddrsam*  
*tanutottha sudhambhodhin yatindram pranamamy aham*

**“I bow before the king of sannyasis, Sri GauraHari, whose wealth of prema censures that of Vaikuntha; whose eyes appear as fountain springs of ecstatic tears and from whose transcendental body oceans of nectar have been distilled.”**

**Purport**

*goloka-namni nija-dhamni tale ca tasya*  
*devi mahesa-hari-dhamasu tesu tesu*  
*te te prabhava-nicaya vihitas ca yena*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**‘DeviDham (the mundane world) is the lowest of all. Next above is MahesaDham; above MahesaDham is placed HariDham (abode of Sri Hari) and above them all is located Krsna’s own realm named Goloka. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, who has allotted their respective authorities to the rulers of those graded realms.’**  
**(BrahmaSamhita (**[**43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/43)**))**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“The realm of Goloka stands highest above all others. Brahma, looking up to the higher position of Goloka, is speaking of the other realms from the point of his own realm: first in order is this mundane world called DeviDham consisting of fourteen worlds, viz., SatyaLoka etc., next above DeviDham is located SivaDham, one portion of which, called MahakalaDham, is enveloped in darkness; interpenetrating this portion of SivaDham there shines SadaSivaLoka, full of great light. Above the same, appears HariDham, or the transcendental VaikunthaLoka. The potency of DeviDham, in the form of the extension of Maya, and that of SivaLoka, consisting of time, space and matter, are the potency of the separated particles pervaded by the penumbra reflection of the subjective portion of the Divinity. But HariDham is over resplendent with transcendental majesty and the great splendour of all-sweetness predominates over all other majesties in Goloka. The Supreme Lord Govinda, by His own direct and indirect power, has constituted the respective potencies of those realms.”  
BrahmaSamhita ([43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/43)), Purport

“Those who are advocates of santa-rasa attain the region of Brahma-Paramatma, the seat of eternal peace; those of dasya-rasa get to Vaikuntha, the spiritual, majestic abode of Sri Narayana; those of sakhya, vatsalya and madhura-rasa (juvenile love) attain to GolokaDham, Krsna’s abode above Vaikuntha.”  
BrahmaSamhita ([36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/36))

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur:

‘In Paravyoma (the Vaikuntha planets), Lord Sri Krsna’s internal spiritual potency (YogaMaya) is of the nature of pure goodness. MahaMaya is not present. In order to exhibit YogaMaya’s most wonderful and super-excellent acting potencies, Sri GauraSundar manifests His eternal, very confidential and precious, jewellike form, manifest from His pastimes of Goloka.’  
(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (21.103))

*suvarna-varno hemango varangas candanangadi*  
*sannyasa-krc chamah santo nistha-santi-parayanah*

**‘In His early pastimes He appears as a householder with a golden complexion. Indeed, his entire body, which is very nicely constituted, is like molten gold, smeared with the pulp of sandalwood. In His later pastimes He accepts the sannyasa order, and will be thus self-controlled, equipoised and peaceful. He is the highest abode of peace and devotion, for He silences the impersonalist nondevotees.’**  
**VisnuSahasraNama Stotra / Chapter 189 DanaDharmaParva MahaBharat**

The fountainhead of all incarnations Sri GauraHari embraced the sannyasa order, not to prove that He was detached from this world, as is the general practice, but to teach austerity and detachment by personal example, and to benedict human society, as we learn from the following two slokas composed by Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya:

*vairagya-vidya-nija-bhakti-yoga-*  
*siksartham ekah purusah puranah*  
*sri-krsna-caitanya-sarira-dhari*  
*krpambudhir yas tam aham prapadye*

**‘Let me take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, who has descended in the form of Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu to teach us real knowledge, His devotional service and detachment from whatever does not foster Krsna consciousness. He has descended because He is an ocean of transcendental mercy. Let me surrender unto His lotus feet.’**

*kalan nastam bhakti-yogam nijam yah*  
*praduskartum krsna-caitanya-nama*  
*avirbhutas tasya padaravinde*  
*gadham gadham liyatam citta-bhrngah*

**‘Let my consciousness, like a honeybee, take shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has just now appeared as Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu to teach the ancient system of devotional service to Himself. This system had almost been lost due to the influence of time.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**6.254-255**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/6.254)**)**

*dhrta-koti dora kamandalu dandam divya*  
*kalevara mundite mundi durjana*  
*kalmasa-khandana-dandam tam*  
*pranamami ca sn-saci-tanayam*

**‘I offer my obeisances unto the son of Sri SaciDevi, who embraced the renounced order to nullify the sins of so many degenerate rascals. As a sannyasi with a shaved head, His transcendental form is adorned with a simple loincloth (kaupina), and in His hands are the sannyasa staff and kamandalu (waterpot).’**

## PART III - Propitious Prayers invoking Auspiciousness in the form of Benedictions and Blessings

### Verse 13

*simhaskandham madhura-madhura-smeraganda sthalantam*  
*durvjneyojjvalarasamayascarya nanavikaram*  
*vibhrat kantim vikacakanakambhoja garbhabhiramam*  
*ekibhutam vapuravatu vo radhaya madhavasya*

**His shoulders are raised like a lion’s; a sweet smile plays constantly on His lips, illuminating His cheeks on either side. Various astonishing and astounding ecstatic symptoms, beyond the ken of the common man, are manifest in His person due to superlative spiritual emotions caused by intense feelings of separation. His bodily effulgence is more luminous and enchanting than the whorl of a fully blossomed golden lotus. May the combined form of SriSri RadhaMadhava (Sri GauraHari) protect you.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu is the sole object of worship in KaliYuga. After establishing this Truth, the author explains how the devotees are always under His protection, and then continues in these five verses to shower blessings on all his listeners.

Radhaya Madhavasya- may the combined form of Srimati Radharani and Sri Madhava (Sri Krsna), protect you all. Madhava {madhur amsa)- born of sweet nectar. Drinking draught after draught of the Divine ambrosia of His wondrous, sweet beauty, the conditioned souls (jivas), burned by the flames of material existence, are refreshed, soothed.

‘What are His physical features?’

He has graceful, powerful shoulders, like a young lion (simha-skandha); madhura-madhuram smeraganda- a sweet smile sweeter than nectar, illuminating His charming cheeks; durvijneya-ujjvala-rasa- erotic pleasure (ujjvalarasa), unfathomable by even the Supreme Lord’s devotees; ascarya-nana-vikaram- extraordinary, ecstatic, emotional transformations (sattvik bhava). His bodily lustre is the same deep hue as the whorl of a golden lotus (kantim vikacakanakambhoja).

Srimati Radhika’s union with Sri Krsna is manifest as an eternal entity (Sri GauraSundar). On one occasion, Sri Krsna was sitting in solitude, pondering the following:

1. What is the nature of the Divine majesty of Srimati Radharani’s love? the love that tastes my extraordinary and sublime sweetness?
2. What is the wonder of the sweetness she relishes?
3. What is the glory of the ecstasy she experiences by loving Me?

The sweetness of Sri Madhava, reflected in the mirror of Sri Radhika’s love, shines with ever newer and fresher sweetness; her love is a transcendental tongue with which she tastes such sweetness. To whatever degree she agrees to benedict one with this love, through her compassion, to that degree someone may taste the sweetness of Sri Krsna. Thus did the desire awaken in Sri Madhava to realize the happiness that ensues from a full dose of His own sweetness. He tried in many ways to fulfill these three desires, but in vain.

He then considered: ‘Srimati Radhika is the supreme asraya (shelter of love, or lover of Sri Krsna (Me), so if I (Madhava) want to taste the glory of her love and her Divine exhilaration of love, then I must accept her transcendental mood. Thus must I unite My individual identity with Srimati Radhika’s individual identity and appear as one Divine Entity in another place (Sri Navadvip). In this unique incarnation I will teach the living entities the confidential process of devotion, that they might attain our eternal service.’ This prompted the Supreme Lord Madhava to appear as Sri Caitanya.

While Lord Madhava was deliberating in this manner, Srimati Radhika thought to herself, ‘I yearn to know the condition of the Lord of my heart, my most beloved SyamSundara, when He experiences the pangs of separation from my absence. But this cannot be accomplished unless I am in His body, or unless I am present in Him while covering my own identity. Hence I must unite with Him.’ At this moment, Sri Krsna united His identity with Srimati Radharani’s and Srimati Radharani’s identity with His and became One, Divine Entity. Thus did Sri Gauranga advent Himself. He is Krsna within (antah-krsna- of a darkish complexion within) and Gaura without (bahir-gaura- of golden complexion), the united form of SriSri RadhaGovinda.

When Lord GauraSundar chanted Radha Radha, it was actually Madhava who was chanting, and when He chanted Krsna Krsna, it was Srimati Radhika who chanted. Dissemination of the MahaMantra was thus a joint effort. When absorbed in the mood of Sri Krsna, Sri Gauranga chanted Hare, and when absorbed in the mood of Srimati Radhika, He chanted Krsna. Thus did they each desire to expand and diffuse (vipsa) each other’s Beauty, Qualities and Pastimes. Srimati Radharani is known as Наrа- by her adroitness in matters of confidential amorous pastimes, she abducts (haran) Sri Krsna’s heart and mind.

Karika:

*kanakambhojagarbhabham radhamadhavayor vapuh*  
*ekam vah patuharyyaksa grivam sucivikarakam*

**‘He who is the united form of SriSri RadhaMadhava, whose complexion is more beautiful than the hue of the whorl of a golden lotus, whose shoulders and neck are more powerful than a young lion’s, and who is the transformation of the purest prema-rasa, in person - may that Sri Gauranga protect you.’**

**Purport**

*radha—рurnа-sakti, krsna—purna-saktiman*  
*dui vastu bheda nai, sastra-paramana*

**‘Sri Radha is the full power, and Lord Krsna is the possessor of full power. The two are not different, as evidenced by the revealed scriptures.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila(**[**4.96**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.96)**))**

*radha-krsna aiche sada eka-i svarupa*  
*lila-rasa asvadite dhare dui-rupa*

**‘Thus Radha and Lord Krsna are one, yet they have taken two forms to enjoy the mellows of pastimes.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.98**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.98)**)**

*tabe hasi ’ tanre prabhu dekhaila svarupa*  
*‘rasa-raja’, ‘mahabhava’—dui eka rupa*

**‘Lord Sri Krsna is the reservoir of all pleasure, and Srimati Radharani is the personification of ecstatic love of Krsna. These two forms combined as one in the person of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. This being the case, Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu revealed His form to Ramananda Ray.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLlla (**[**8.282**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.282)**)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“Ramananda Ray saw the combined form of Sri Krsna (RasaRaj- the king and master of all loving emotions, rasas) and Srimati Radhika as the embodiment of the highest expression of ecstatic love - radha-bhava dyuti-suvalitam naumi krsna svarupam. He saw both these forms combine to appear in a most wonderful and ecstatic form - the golden avatar. The most sublime, esoteric aspect of this revelation is that two Divine principles have combined to become one; simultaneously. Those who are fortunate to understand the mysterious truths regarding Sri KrsnaCaitanya and the truth of the principle of RadhaKrsna, are rewarded with the grace of Srila Svarup Damodar Gosvami, making one eligible to serve this eternal principle.

**“О Ramananda! Actually My body does not have a fair complexion. It only appears so because it has touched the body of Srimati Radharani. However, She does not touch anyone but the son of Nanda Maharaja. I have now converted My body and mind into the ecstasy of Srimati Radharani; thus do I taste My own personal sweetness in that form.”**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**8.287-288**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.287)**)**

*caitanya-sirhhera navadvipe avatara*  
*simha-griva, simha-virya, simhera hunkara*

**‘The lionlike Lord Caitanya appeared in Navadvip, with the shoulders of a lion, the powers of a lion and the loud voice of a lion.’**  
**Sri Caitanya Caritamrta AdiLila(**[**3.30**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.30)**)**

*sei simha vasuk jivera hrdaya-kandare*  
*kalmasa-dvirada nase yanhara hunkare*

**‘May that lion be seated in the core of the heart of every living being, that with His resounding roar, He may drive away one’s elephantine vices.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**3.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.31)**)**

**“When the lover and the beloved meet, they are called yukta (connected). Previous to their meeting, they are called ayukta (not connected). Whether connected or not connected, the ecstatic emotion arising due to not being able to embrace and kiss each other as desired is called vipralambha. This vipralambha helps nourish emotions at the time of meeting.’**  
**UjjvalNilamani(VipralambhaPrakarana 3-4)**  
**quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**23.62-63**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/23.62)**)Purport**

PurvaRaga is described in UjjvalNilamani.

**‘Before their meeting, when attachment produced in both the lover and the beloved by seeing, hearing and so on, becomes very palatable by the mixture of four ingredients, such as vibhava and anubhava, this is called purva-raga. The word mana is also described: mana is a word used to indicate the mood of the lover and the beloved, experienced whether they are in one place or in different places. This mood obstructs their looking at one another and embracing one another, despite the fact that they are attached to each other. Pravasa is also described as follows: pravasa indicates the separation of lovers who were previously intimately associated. This separation is due to their being in different places. Similarly, prema-vaicittya indicates an abundance of love that brings about grief from fear of separation, although the lover is present.”**  
**UjjvalNilamani(VipralambhaPrakarana 5.68,134,139)**

Srila Bhaktisiddanta Sarasvati Prabhupad has explained durvijneya-ujjvala-rasa in his translation to this verse, saying that those who worship Sri Krsna as the Supreme Enjoyer and Divine Paramour cannot understand the transformations that occur in the body of Sri GauraHari when He is imbued with feelings of intense separation (vipralambha). At such times the limbs of His transcendental body are withdrawn within His torso (kurmakar), just as a turtle pulls his limbs within his shell.

### Verse 14

*drstva madyati nutanambudacayam samviksya barham bhaved*  
*atyantam vikalo vilokya valitam gunjavalim vepate*  
*drste syamakisorake’pi cakitam dhatte camatkarita-*  
*mittham gauratanuh pracarita nijaprema harih patu vah*

**Upon seeing a multitude of fresh, monsoon-laden clouds, He becomes mad with love for Krsna; the sight of a peacock feather causes Him to become completely overwhelmed; if He should happen to see a garland of gunja berries, His body begins to tremble in ecstasy while His heart has palpitations; each time He sees a dark-complexioned young boy, He becomes startled, and then feels timid - in this way is He possessed by various and wondrous ecstacies, as He freely distributes his own commodity - Love of Krsna. May that Fair-complexioned One (GauraHari) protect and maintain your lives.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Upon seeing fresh rain-laden clouds and other forms of uddipana (stimulation for remembering Krsna), Sri Gauranga exhibits ecstatic symptoms steeped in sattvik bhava (ecstatic emotional symptoms: stambha- feeling stunned; sved- perspiration; romanca- horripilation, hairs standing on end; svarbhanga- faltering of the voice; kampa- trembling; vaivarnya- change in bodily hue; asru- tears; pralay- fainting) and vyabhicari bhavas. He falls in a faint on the ground, immersed in remembrance of GhanaSyama, that dark-hued cowherd boy.

Harih- may that Supreme Personality Sri GauraHari protect you. By showering soothing prema, the nectar of devotional service to His lotus feet, may he resuscitate you who are burning in the fire of material existence. He is known as Hari since He takes away all material contaminations and impurities of the heart, attracting everyone to His lotus feet.

‘What is He like?’

He is gaura-tanuh- his bodily complexion is like molten gold; pracarita-nijaprema- engaged in the propagation of prema (His love for Krsna; love for Himself).

‘What method does He use?’

He has set the example for us- apani acari dharma sikhay (He personally demonstrates the eternal constitutional position of the spirit soul); drstva- seeing any object can remind Him of Sri Krsna. By the sight of a deep, dark rain cloud, He becomes madyati- inebriated, excited, frenzied. (Mada indicates vyabhicari-bhava.)

*viveka hara ullaso madah sa dvividho matah*  
*madhupana bhavo’ nanga vikriya bharajo’pi ca*

**‘Mada is a state of spiritual jubilation when one is robbed of one’s conscience and rationale, where the sense of duty and discrimination are lost. It is of two kinds: due to ingesting intoxicants, and due to being smitten by Cupid’s arrows and thus overcome by lust.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**2.4.35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/2.4.35)**)**

In the instance of Sriman Mahaprabhu’s madness, mada is brought on by ananga-vikara - Cupid’s arrows. Ananga is a name of KamaDev (Cupid) meaning that he has no body. He once infuriated Lord Siva so much that Siva burnt him to ashes with his glance of wrath. However, in this instance, the abovementioned various kinds of uddipana act on Mahaprabhu as the arrows of KamaDev act upon the common man, inciting a kind of spiritual lust, which is in actuality, prema. Sri GauraSundar has thus embraced the loving sentiments of the VrajaGopis (gopibhava).

*premaiva goparamanarh kama ityagamat prathama*

**‘The gopi’s transcendental love for Sri Krsna has become famous as каmа, Divine lust.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.285**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.285)**)**

The preceptors of the science of rasa have defined prema as kama when transcendental love reaches the pinnacle of sublime sweetness, instigating the gopis to amorous pastimes. They have further described kama- when the gopi’s single-minded conjugal love for Sri Govinda shines with extraordinary brilliance.

Varham- peacock feather. When Sri Gauranga sees a peacock feather, He is reminded of Sri Krsna’s crown and is swept away with the sentiments of Srimati Radharani. He becomes vikala- extremely impatient, restless and agitated. Again, upon seeing valitam gunjavalim- a necklace of gunja berries (worn by both Radha and Krsna), Sri GauraSundara’s body begins to tremble in ecstasy (vepate- a symptom of sattvik-bhava). Upon seeing a syama-kisora (dark-complexioned young boy), Sri GauraSundar is instantly reminded of Sri Krsna’s beautiful form; thus Divine and diverse manifestations of prema erupt in His body. Remembrance is a symptom of vyabhicari-bhava.

Karika:

*bhavoddipana meghadi drstavanubhavan harih*  
*gauram pracarita-prema patu vah kampa dehakah*

**‘Sri GauraHari, upon seeing various forms of uddipan (stimulation for bhava), such as fresh, rain-laden clouds, exhibits diverse ecstatic symptoms (trembling, etc.). By this method, He propagates the glories of Divine prema. May He protect you.’**

**Purport**

When pure devotion for the Supreme Lord Krsna reaches the elevated stage where the devotee is never separated from Krsna at any moment, it is known as anuraga. In this stage of spontaneous love, the pure devotee has one goal in mind - to satisfy the object ( visaya) of his love, Sri Krsna. In this loving exchange ( vibhava), the MahaBhagavat becomes the shelter (asraya) for spontaneous love (rati). The MahaBhagavat is known as the shelter, since pure devotion (rati) takes shelter in the MahaBhagavat’s heart. For the MahaBhagavat whose eyes are anointed with the salve of rati, anything that has even the slightest resemblance to his object (visaya) of love (Krsna), acts as a catalyst; igniting (uddipana) a fire of love (vibhava) in his heart.

*maha-bhagavata dekhe sthavara-jangama*  
*tahan tahan haya tanra sri-krsna-sphurana*

**‘An advanced devotee, acting on the spiritual platform, sees everything movable and inert as the Supreme Lord. Wherever his glance may fall, Sri Krsna springs forth.’**  
**Sri Cnitanyа Cairitamrta MadhyaLila (**[**8.273**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.273)**)**

*sarva-bhutesu yah pasyed bhagavad-bhavam atmanah*  
*bhutani bhagavaty atmany esa bhdgavatottamah*

**Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu continued, “A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the Soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.”**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.2.45**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.45)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**8.275**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.275)**)**

*premanjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena*  
*santah sadaiva hrdayesu vilokayanti*  
*yam syamasundaram acintya-guna-svarupam*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**‘I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is SyamSundara, Krsna Himself, with inconceivable, innumerable attributes, whom the pure devotees see in their heart of hearts with the eye of devotion tinged with the salve of love.’**  
**BrahmaSamhita (**[**38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/38)**)**

“The SyamSundara form of Krsna is His inconceivable, simultaneous personal and impersonal self-contradictory form. True devotees see that form in their purified hearts under the influence of devotional trance. The form Syama is not the blue color visible in the mundane world but is the transcendental variegated color affording eternal bliss, invisible to the mortal eye. Considering the trance of VyasaDeva described in the sloka- bhakti-yogena manasi, it will be clear that the form of Sri Krsna is the full Personality of Godhead and can only be visible in the heart of a true devotee in the state of trance under the influence of devotion, the only true seat for the Lord to sit on. When Krsna manifest Himself in Vraja, both the devotees and nondevotees laid their eyes upon Him, but only the devotees cherished Him, eternally present in Vraja, as the priceless jewel of their hearts.”

In the age of DvaparYuga, the YugaAvatar Lord Sri Krsna exhorted everyone to give up all other religious practices and fearlessly surrender unto Him - becoming His devotee. For the conditioned soul it is impossible to follow these instructions without the perfect master and guide to show him. Realising this, the Supreme Personality Sri Krsna, the well-wishing friend of all living entities, appeared in KaliYuga in the garb of a devotee, to instruct and guide the conditioned souls by His own example of surrender to the Supreme Lord. Thus Srila Rupa Gosvami describ

### Verse 15

*krpasindhuh sandhyaruna rucivicitrambara dharo-*  
*jjvalah purnah premamrtamaya mahajyotiramalah*  
*saci garbha ksirambudhi bhava udaradbhutakalah*  
*kalanathah srimanudayatu tava svantanabhasi*

**He is a limitless Ocean of Mercy. The colour of His renunciant’s robe is like the fiery hue of the rising sun. May that supremely beautiful Moon, Sri CaitanyaCandra, saturated to full measure with the elixir of conjugal affection (prema), diffusing an intense, clear brilliance in all directions; who has arisen from the milk ocean (ksira-sindhu) of the womb of mother SaciDevi, and who is the most charming Master of the sixty-four arts (kala.), resplendently appear on the horizon of your heart.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The Supreme Lord, Sri GauraCandra is herein compared to the moon - radiating soothing, ambrosial rays of prema that dissipate the darkness of ignorance within the hearts of conditioned souls. Demonstrating these Divine distinctions, the revered author invokes His blessings- ‘May the moonlike Sri GauraCandra rise upon the horizon of your heart to disperse the gloom of nescience and bathe you with soothing moonbeams of prema.’

Kala- sixteen digits of the moon; also, the partial expansions of the Supreme Lord (incarnations like Matsya, Kurma, etc.); natha- Lord; thus, kalanatha- the fountainhead of all incarnations, svayam bhagavan.

‘From where did this GauraMoon appear?’

saci-garbha-ksirambudhi-bhavah- the milk ocean womb of Mother Saci (During the churning of the milk ocean by the demigods and demons, the moon also appeared from the ocean of milk.) This GauraMoon is udaradbhuta-kalah- the most charitable, charming master of sixty-four transcendental arts, by which He engenders extraordinary mellows (rasa) in the devotees’ hearts.

sriman- sri is the absolute repository of beauty, Srimati Radhika. Through becoming one with her, He has acquired a most attractive bodily lustre; krpasindhuh- an ocean of mercy; use of the superlative degree quantifies the quality of His mercy, that extends to the most fallen, heinous offenders, the most wretched sinners.

He is sandhya-aruna-rucira-vicitrambara-dharo- adorned with fine garments, brilliantly tinged with the hue of the rising sun. He is purnah- completely whole and perfect, the Supreme Personality. Purnah also indicates the full moon. Premamrta-the veritable form of liquid love, the personification of the nectar of prema, spotless and unblemished (like the full moon), lustrous with the light of the sublime rays of bhava (sattvik, vyabhicari, etc.) He is immaculate and impeccable, since filth and impurities are eradicated simply by remembering Him. The mundane moon of this material world is tainted, only capable of partially dissipating the darkness of night, but incompetent in removing impurities and darkness within the heart. Therefore the moonlike GauraCandra is a most wondrous moon.

Karika:

*sri gaura vidhur aruna vicitrambara sobhitah*  
*premamrtam svantarnabha udiyadvah svayam harih*

**‘May Sri GauraCandra, the self-same Sri Hari, gracefully adorned with garments tinged the saffron hue of the rising sun, dawn on the horizon of your heart and make it blush, filled with the nectar of prema.’**

**Purport**

*ananda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhavitabhis*  
*tabhir ya eva nija-rupataya kalabhih*  
*goloka eva nivasaty akhilatma-bhuto*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**‘I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, residing in His own realm, Goloka, with Radha, resembling His own spiritual figure, the embodiment of the ecstatic potency possessed of the sixty-four artistic activities, in the company of Her confidantes (sakhis), embodiments of the extensions of Her bodily form, permeated and vitalized by His ever-blissful spiritual rasa.’**  
**BrahmaSamhita (**[**37**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/37)**)**

“Although the Lord Absolute and His potency are one and the self-same existence, still they exist eternally as separate entities, as Radha and Krsna. In both the ecstatic energy and the transcendental Lord Krsna, there exists srngara-rasa (amorous love) whose quality is inconceivable. The vibhava (extension) of that rasa (mellow quality) is twofold, viz., alambana (support) and uddipana (stimulation). Of these, alambana is twofold, viz., asraya (supported) and visaya (supporter). Asraya signifies Radhika Herself and the extensions of Her own form, and visaya means Krsna. Krsna is Govinda, Lord of Goloka. The gopis are facsimile asraya of that rasa. With them Krsna indulges in eternal pastimes in Goloka. Nija-rupataya means ‘with the attributes manifest from the ecstatic energy’.

The sixty-four activities in fine arts and crafts are as follows:

(1) gita-art of singing. (2) vadya-art of playing on musical instruments. (3) nrtya-art of dancing. (4) natya-art of theatricals. (5) alekhya-art of painting. (6) visesakacchedya-art of painting face and body with colored unguents and cosmetics. (7) tandula-kusuma-bali-vikara-art of preparing offerings from rice and flowers. (8) puspastarana-art of making a covering of flowers for a bed. (9) dasana-vasananga-raga-art of applying preparations for cleansing the teeth, cloth and painting the body. (10) mani-bhumika-karma-art of making the groundwork of jewels. (11) sayya-racana-art of covering the bed. (12) udaka-vadya-art of playing on music in water. (13) udaka-ghata-art of splashing with water. (14) citra-yoga-art of practically applying an admixture of colors. (15) malya grathana-vikalpa-art of designing a preparation of wreaths. (16) sekharapida-yojana-art of practically setting the coronet on the head. (17) nepathya-yoga-art of practically dressing in the tiring room. (18) karnapatra-bhahga-art of decorating the tragus of the ear. (19) sugandha-yukti-art of practical application of aromatics. (20) bhusana-yojana-art of applying or setting ornaments. (21) aindra-jala-art of jugglery. (22) kaucumara- a kind of art. (23) hasta-laghava-art of sleight of hand. (24) citra-saкарupa-bhaksya-vikara-kriya-art of preparing varieties of salad, bread, cake and delicious food. (25) panaka-rasa-ragasava-yojana-art of practically preparing palatable drinks and tinging draughts with red color (26) suci-vaya karma-art of needle works and weaving. (27) sutra-krida-art of playing with thread. (28) vina-damuraka-vadya-art of playing on lute and small x-shaped drum. (29) prahelika-art of making and solving riddles. (29a) pratimala-art of capping or reciting verse for verse as a trial for memory or skill. (30) durvacaka-yoga-art of practicing language difficult to be answered by others. (31) pustaka-vacana-art of reciting books. (32) natikakhyayika-darsana-art of enacting short plays and anecdotes. (33) kavya-samasya-purana-art of solving enigmatic verses. (34) pattika-vetra-bana-vikalpa-art of designing preparation of shield, cane and arrows. (35) tarku-karma-art of spinning by spindle. (36) taksana-art of carpentry. (37) vastu-vidya-art of engineering. (38) raupya-ratna-pariksa-art of testing silver and jewels. (39) dhatu-vada-art of metallurgy. (40) mani-raga jnana-art of tinging jewels. (41) akara jnana-art of mineralogy. (42) vrksayur-veda-yoga-art of practicing medicine or medical treatment, by herbs. (43) mesa-kukkuta-lavaka-yuddha-vidhi-art of knowing the mode of fighting of lambs, cocks and birds.
