(44) suka-sarika-pralapana-art of maintaining or knowing conversation between male and female cockatoos. (45) utsadana-art of healing or cleaning a person with perfumes. (46) kesa-marjana-kausala-art of shampooing the hair. (47) aksara-mustika-kathana-art of talking with letters and fingers. (48) mlecchita-kutarka-vikalpa-art of fabricating barbarous or foreign sophistry. (49) desa-bhasa-jnana-art of knowing provincial dialects. (50) puspa-sakatika-nirmiti-jnana-art of knowing prediction by heavenly voice or knowing preparation of toy carts by flowers. (51) yantra-matrka-art of mechanics. (52) dharana-matrka-art of the use of amulets. (53) samvacya-art of conversation. (54) manasi kavya-kriya-art of composing verse mentally. (55) kriya-vikalpa-art of designing a literary work or a medical remedy. (56) chalitaka-yoga-art of practicing as a builder of shrines called after him. (57) abhidhana-kosa-cchando-jnana-art of the use of lexicography and meters. (58) vastra-gopana-art of concealment of cloths. (59) dyuta-visesa-art of knowing specific gambling. (60) akarsa-krida-art of playing with dice or magnet. (61) balaka-kridanaka-art of using children’s toys. (62) vainayiki vidya-art of enforcing discipline. (63) vaijayikl vidya-art of gaining victory. (64) vaitaliki vidya-art of awakening the master with music at dawn.

“All of these arts manifest their own eternal forms, ever visible in the region of Goloka as the ingredients of rasa, and, in the mundane sphere, they have been unstintedly exhibited in the pastimes of Vraja by the spiritual (cit) potency, YogaMaya. Sri Rupa says, sadanantaih... santitah, i.e., Krsna is ever manifest in His beauty with His infinite pastimes in Goloka. Sometimes the variant manifestation of those pastimes becomes visible on the mundane plane.”

### Verse 16

*badhnan premabhara prakampitakaro granthin katidorakaih*  
*sankhyatum nijaloka-mangala-harekrsneti namnam japan*  
*asrusnatamukhah svameva hi jagannatham didrksurgata-*  
*yatair gaura tanurvilocanamudam tanvan harih patu vah*

**Having tied knots in the waistband of His loincloth to keep count of the rounds of HariNam chanted, with trembling hands and heart overflowing with prema, He is engaged in the silent and repeated recitation (japa) of His most auspicious HolyNames (the MahaMantra) HareKrsna HareKrsna KrsnaKrsna HareHare HareRama HareRama RamaRama HareHare. He bathes the world in the rays of the benediction moon as His face is bathed in the tears that flow from His lotus eyes. Overwhelmed by spiritual yearning to see Lord Jagannath (His self-same form), He restlessly moves hither and thither. May the fair-complexioned One (GauraTanu), a veritable feast for the eyes, bring joy to your hearts; May Sri GauraHari always protect you.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sriman Mahaprabhu taught by His example that the MahaMantra must be chanted, keeping count of a prescribed number of rounds, thus did he tie knots in the waistband of his loincloth. Various manifestations of sattvik-bhava were manifest in His transcendental body while chanting. In this condition, Sriman Mahaprabhu used to go to see Lord Jagannath. Thus are His blessings invoked, painting a picture of His ecstatic lila.

‘Generally speaking, the mantra that one chants silently to oneself is not meant to be chanted in kirtan. So is it permissable to chant the MahaMantra in kirtan?’

*harernama parnm japyam, dhyeyam, geyam, nirantaram*  
*klrttaniyanca bahudha nivrttirbahudhecchata*

**‘Of all names, HareKrsna Nama is the best for chanting japa , the best for meditation, for singing and for kirtan , for those who are desirous of prosperity and well-being.’**  
**Sri HariBhaktiVilasa (**[**11.255**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbv/11.255)**)**

*japyo dhyeyah kirttaniyasca, mahamantratvat,*  
*uccaih satagunam bhavet*

**‘This HareKrsna Nama is most suitable for japa . for meditation and for kirtan , thus has it received the appellation - MahaMantra. Specifically, if one chants this mantra loudly, he receives one-hundred times the benefit.’**  
**Sri Jiva Gosvami / Sandarbha**

*japakartta haite ucca sankirtankari,*  
*satagunadhik phala puranete dhari*

**‘Those who chant loudly in kirtan receive one-hundred times the benefit as those who chant silently to themselves.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaBhagavat AdiLila (**[**15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/15-zhenitba-na-vishnuprie)**)**

*sadhya sadhantattva ye kichu sakal,*  
*harinam sankirtan milibe sakal*

**‘HariNam SanKIrtan can award the fruits of all spiritual means and their attainable goals.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaBhagavat AdiLila (**[**14.143**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/14.143)**)**

May Gauratanu- the golden complexioned harih (Lord Hari), patu vah- protect you with the nectar of prema (service to His lotus feet).

‘How will He do this?’

vilocana-mudam tanvan- by expanding the delight of the eyes of his intimate devotees (giving them His darsan).

‘What else is He doing?’

premabhara... chanting the HolyNames, His heart filled with love {prema). Trembling in ecstasy, He keeps count of the mantras chanted by knotting the cord around His waist; nija-loka-mangala- chanting the MahaMantra initiates auspiciousness for the entire universe, as well as for the chanter himself.

asrusnata-mukhah- whose countenance is bathed in tears of prema.

He heightens the exultation of His devotees as He goes back and forth from His own quarters to the temple to see His own image (svameva) - that of Lord Jagannath - jagannatham didrksuh.

Karika:

*utkirttita mahdmantro gauro’sru snapitananah*  
*svaprakasa-jagannatham didrksuh patu vah sada*

**‘Overcome with yearning to see His self-same form of Lord Jagannath, Sri GauraHari’s face is bathed in tears while chanting the HareKrsna MahaMantra. May he always protect you.’**

**Purport**

*madhur madhuram etan-mangalam mangalanam*  
*sakala nigamavalli sat-phalarh cit svarupam*  
*sakrd api parigitam sraddhaya helaya va*  
*bhrguvara naramatram tarayet krsna nama*

**‘The HolyName of the Supreme Lord is all-auspicious in every respect; the highest benediction. It is sweeter than nectar and it is the transcendental eternal fruit of the tree of knowledge and awareness. О best of the Brgus! Whether one chants Krsna’s Name with faith, or derisively, uttered even only once, this Name will deliver the chanter from material bondage.’**  
**MahaBharat Prabhasa Кhanda**

The Supreme Lord GauraHari came to teach the science of yukta vairagya, detachment through specific attachment; through the practice of devotional surrender (bhakti-yoga). This process of bhakti-yoga begins with the tongue:

*sevonmukhe hi jihvadau*

**‘This refers to chanting. By chanting HareKrsna, one begins the service of the Lord. Another function of the tongue is to taste and accept the Lord’s prasada. We have to begin our service to the Unlimited with the tongue and become perfect in chanting, and accepting the Lord’s prasada.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.234**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.234)**)**

The Lord thus chanted His own Name for the benefit of the entire creation. He came to benedict not just the human beings but all living entities by propagating the Sankirtan movement. The goal of the Sankirtan movement is to chant constantly. However, to come to this stage one must chant regularly a fixed number of HolyNames of the Supreme Lord and avoid committing offenses.

Srila Srinivas Acarya Thakur describes the glories of the six Gosvamis of Vrindaban, the eternal associates of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, in his famous composition SadGosvamyAstakam.

*sankhya-purvaka-nama-gana-natibhih kalavasani-krtau*

They were engaged in chanting a fixed number of rounds of the HolyNames, bowing down and offering obeisances. In this way they utilised their time in KrsnaConsciousness.

The process of nama-bhajan, chanting and meditating on the HolyNames, is the first step towards realisation, relished by perfected and liberated devotees in their highest states of ecstasy, as by neophytes in the beginning stages of sadhana-bhakti.

*sampratika ‘dui brahma’ ihah ‘calacala’*  
*jagannatha-acala brahma, tumi ta’ sacala*

‘At the present moment I see two Brahmans. One Brahman is Lord Jagannath, who does not move, and the other Brahman, who is moving, is You. Lord Jagannath is arca-vigraha, the worshipful Deity, and it is He who is the nonmoving Brahman. You are Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, and You are moving here and there. Both of You are the same Brahman, Supreme Master of material nature, but You are playing two parts - one moving and one not moving. In this way, two Brahmans are now residing at Jagannath Puri, PurusottamKsetra.’

*tumi-gaura-varna, tenha-syamala-varna*  
*dui brahme kaila saba jagat-tarana*

‘Of the two Brahmans, You are fair complexioned, and the other, Lord Jagannath, is blackish. However, both of you deliver the whole world.’  
Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila([10.163-164](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/10.163))

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Jagannath, has taken the immovable transcendental form of a ‘wooden’ Deity - daru brahman - while the Supreme Personality Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu is moving about in His own transcendental form. Both Supreme Personalities, controllers of maya, are one and the same personality, residing at the same time in PurusottamKsetra. ”

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu was always eager to see Lord Jagannath, as much as Lord Jagannath was always eager to see Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Thus, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu wrote in His composition - Sri Jagannathastakam.

*jagannathah svami, nayana-patha-gami bhavatu me*

**‘May Lord Sri JagannathDeva be the object of my vision!’**

### Verse 17

*antardhvantacayam samasta jagatamunmulayanti hathat*  
*premanandarasambudhim niravadhi prodvelayanti balat*  
*visvam sitalayantyativa vikalam tapatrayenanisam*  
*yusmakam hrdaye cakastu satatam caitanyacandracchata*

**Suddenly, the deep darkness of ignorance in the hearts of all living entities throughout the universe has been uprooted; the constant ebb and flow of the Ocean of Ecstatic Love has produced powerful waves that cause the ocean to swell; a cooling, soothing light now pervades this world, having thoroughly overcome the glowing hot trident in the hand of DurgaDevi (the three-fold miseries of material existence). May the lustrous splendour of Sri CaitanyaCandra forever illuminate your hearts!**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The revered author once again uses the analogy of the moon to describe the radiance and beauty of Sri GauraCandra’s bodily effulgence, thus invoking His benign grace. Sri CaitanyaCandra is the moon whose rays are the effulgence of His lustrous body. May this brilliant radiance always enlighten our/your hearts. \[There are two readings of this verse: 1) yusmakam- your; 2) sa’smakam- our\]

‘Just what kind of moonbeams are these?’

samasta jagatam.....by force they root out nescience and ignorance, the result of unlimited sins that causes the pall of illusion in the hearts of the inhabitants of the universe; premananda- allowing them to relish the nectarean bliss of prema, which is like an ambudhi (ocean); thus do these rays vigorously swell the ocean of prema at every moment. They visvam-sitalayanty- cool down the universe engulfed in the unabating flames of tapatrayena- the three-fold miseries of material existence (adhyatmika- miseries arising from one’s own body and mind; adhibhautika- miseries caused by other living entities; adhidaivika- miseries caused by the Devas; those arising from natural calamities) - the trident in the hand of DurgaDevi. This inundation of nectarean prema is supremely soothing and cooling. The mundane moon of this world removes darkness, causes the ocean to swell, and has a cooling effect -thus the analogy is very appropriate.

Karika:

*antah kalusa hanta ca svapremambudhi vardhanah*  
*visvam sitalayantam sri-gauracandras cakastu vah*

**‘Sri GauraCandra destroys the contamination in the jivas’ hearts, increases the ocean of prema and cools the universe. May He beautify our hearts.’**

**Purport**

*vande sri-krsna-caitanya*  
*nityanandau sahoditau*  
*gaudodaye puspavantau*  
*citrau sandau tamo-nudau*

**‘I offer my obeisance to SrlSrl Nityananda and KrsnaCaitanya, who are like the sun and moon. They have arisen simultaneously on the horizon of Gauda to dissipate the darkness of ignorance and thus wonderfully bestow benediction upon all.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**1.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.2)**)**

SrimadBhagavatam (1.2.11) describes the AbsoluteTruth (non-dual substance) as Brahman, the Supreme Lord’s bodily effulgence. Similarly, BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (1.2.233) quotes a verse from PadmaPurana - ‘Krsna’s Name is always liberated and spiritual, never conditioned by the laws of material nature because the name of Krsna and Krsna Himself are identical, hence the Supreme Lord’s Name, Form, Bodily effulgence, and so on, are all identical with Him.’

The easiest way for a jiva to associate with the Supreme Lord, especially in KaliYuga, is to glorify His HolyNames, Beauty, Qualities Pastimes, and the like. This process purifies the jiva’s consciousness and enlightens him with the knowledge of his eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord.

‘Where the Krsna sun is present, there, the darkness of maya cannot exist.’

Maya, the Lord’s material energy, puts the conditioned jiva into illusion regarding his original spiritual identity; deludes him into thinking that he is this body. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur states that illusion is simply ignorance; the darkness of nescience. This ignorance is of five types:

1. jiva's forgetfulness of his spiritual identity,
2. jiva's false material identification with his gross and subtle bodies,
3. jiva's false assertion of himself as the enjoyer of all he surveys,
4. the influence of duality and engrossment in matter upon jiva,
5. jiva's constant fearfulness, and acceptance of this perverted reflection known as the material world - these five comprise the illusion of the jiva.

**These five types of ignorance generate the darkness of nescience, giving rise to the four aims of mankind - mundane religiosity, wealth, material desires and the pursuit of liberation. As long as ignorance and the darkness of nescience keep the jiva imprisoned in illusion about his real identity, and about his relationship with the Supreme Lord, he continues to suffer repeated birth, death, old age and disease, in the endless continuum of material existence. Only when he cries out to Krsna for help, the supremely merciful Lord of Compassion destroys the darkness born of ignorance, with the shining lamp of knowledge.**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**10.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.11)**)**

*dhatar yad asmin bhava isa jivas*  
*tapa-trayenabhihata na sarma*  
*atman labhante bhagavams tavanghri-*  
*cchayam sa-vidyam ata asrayema*

**‘O Father, О Lord, О Supreme Personality, the living entities in the material world can never have any happiness because they are overwhelmed by the three kinds of miseries (adhyatmik, adhibhautik, adhidaivik). Therefore, they take shelter of the shade of Your lotus feet, which are full of knowledge, and we also thus take shelter of them.’ (SrimadBhagavatam** [**3.5.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.40)**)**

## PART IV - Eulogy of the Devotees of Sri Gauranga

### Verse 18

*bhrantam yatra munisvarairapi pura yasmin ksamamandale*  
*kasyapi pravivesa naiva dhisana yadveda no va sukah*  
*yanna kvapi krpamayena ca nije’pyudghatitam saurina*  
*tasminnujvala bhaktivartmani sukham khelanti gaurapriyah*

**Before the advent of Sriman Mahaprabhu, great sages and philosophers in this world were confused; they had lost their way on the path of devotion. By intelligence or intellect they were unable to enter the path of bhakti, characterized by ardent, ecstatic, devotional mellows. Even the enlightened sage Sri Sukadeva Gosvami had no inkling of it. Indeed, the supremely merciful Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna Himself did not reveal this path to His confidential devotees.**  
**However, the dearest followers of Sri GauraSundar very happily wander along this path of sweet mellows (bhakti marg- the path of unalloyed devotional service), playing as they progress along the way. They are well acquainted with the successive landmarks.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The description of the glories of Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s devotees commences. The revered author contends herein that

Sri Caitanya’s devotees alone are eligible to relish transcendental rasa, the mellifluous and esoteric meaning of VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna’s confidential and resplendent pastimes with the Vraja gopls.

TasmIin...- on the path of pure bhakti, Sri Caitanya’s devotees alone are able to relish conjugal, madhur rasa: kbelayanti- they dally along the path in great delight, solely by the mercy of Sri Caitanya. Even munisvaraih- the best amongst great sages, like Srila VyasDeva, lose their way (bhranti) on the slippery path of bhakti, wet with madhur rasa (sweet mellows). BhaktiMarga was an indistinct and equivocal matter for the devotees prior (pura) to the advent of Sri Caitanya. In truth, this madhur-bhakti-marga remained undisclosed; an uncharted path, hidden within this world, here referred to as- ksama mandala- the ‘sphere of forgiveness’. In a world of sinners, what more can this world ever hope to be?

What to speak of others, even Srila SukaDeva Gosvami may or may not have fully understood something of the esoteric intricacies of bhakti (even if he did know, he didn’t fully reveal this knowledge). This most rare spiritual gem, GopiPrema, was not revealed by NandaNandan Sri Krsna to even His own beloved devotees, although He is infinitely compassionate upon them. Therefore, the finer details of raganuga-bhakti, the most exalted realm of spontaneous devotional service, are revealed only to Sri GauraSundara’s devotees, not to others; even more so with kamanuga-bhakti- the path of confidential, conjugal devotion masquerading as lust.

Karika:

*nа prakasi raso yo ’tra munibhih saurinapi ca*  
*gaura-bhaktah sukham tatra khelantyujjvala-bhaktike*

**‘The resplendent and sublime path of bhakti-rasa (conjugal affection) was not revealed to any sage or preceptor, not even by the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna. However, the devotees of Sri Caitanya joyfully play along this path, pleased to their heart's content.'**

**Purport**

Lord Sri KrsnaCaitanya and VrajendraNandan Krsna are one and the same - the source of all incarnations, the cause of all causes, the original cause; Himself - His own cause. From His countless incarnations, the YugaAvatar appears in every Yuga, to initiate the prescribed religion for each particular age. However, the vuga-dharma propagated by the YugaAvatars prior to Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s advent does not include the most exalted devotional mood of loving surrender exhibited by the young maidens of Vraja.

**“My dear gopis, you have severed all family attachments for my sake. Such an achievement is very rare, even for great philosophers and yogis. Our meetings with each other are completely pure and unblemished. If I wanted to repay the debt that I have incurred by your love, devotion, service and renunciation, even with my immortal body and for all eternity, I would be unable. I am obligated to you life after life. You may succeed in acquitting me of this debt by your gentle and divine demeanor - nay, your sublime love; but I will always remain indebted to you. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.32.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.22)**))**

**“O beloved gopis, simply for my sake you have disregarded social taboos, Vedic injunctions, even cut yourselves off from your relatives and family members. Your meditation on me has been single-minded; with no consideration for your nuptial bliss. I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to me. Even when I removed myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you. Therefore, my beloved gopis, please do not harbor any bad feelings toward your beloved, since you are as dear to me as I am to you.”**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.32.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.21)**)**

*cira-kala nahi kari prema-bhakti dana*  
*bhakti vina jagatera nahi avasthana*

**‘For a long time I have not bestowed unalloyed loving service to me upon the inhabitants of the world. Without such loving attachment, the existence of the world is useless.’**

*sakala jagate more kare vidhi-bhakti*  
*vidhi-bhaktye vraja-bhava paite nahi sakti*

**‘Everywhere in the world people worship me according to scriptural injunctions. But simply by following such regulative principles, one cannot attain the loving sentiments of the devotees in VrajaBhumi.’**

*aisvarya-jnanete saba jagat misrita*  
*aisvarya-sithila-preme nahi mora prita*

**‘Knowing my opulences, the whole world looks upon me with awe and veneration. But devotion made feeble by such reverence does not attract me.’**  
**Sri СаitanуаСаritamrta AdiLila (**[**3.14-16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.14)**)**

Srila Visvanath Cakravati Thakur comments:

“Before Lord Krsna lifted Govardhan Hill, the residents of Vraja had no inkling that He was God. But after Krsna had lifted Govardhan Hill and visited Varuna’s underwater abode, the residents realized that their beloved Lord Krsna was the Supreme Controller.

“Nevertheless, this aisvarya-jnana did not even remotely affect them. Their hearts remained saturated with madhurya-jnana. The following verse from the SrimadBhagavatam clearly demonstrates that the gopis of Vraja were well informed about Lord Krsna’s aisvarya (opulences), but were neither impressed nor attracted by them.

*mrgayur iva kapindram vivyadhe lubdha-dharma*  
*striyam akrta virupam stri-jitah kama-yanam*  
*balim api balim attvavestayad dhvanksa-vad yas*  
*tad alam asita-sakhyair dustyajas tat-katharthah*

**‘Like a hunter, He cruelly shot the king of the monkeys with arrows. Because He was conquered by a woman, He disfigured another woman who came to Him with lusty desires. And even after consuming the gifts of Bali Maharaja, He bound him up with ropes as if he were a crow. So let us give up all friendship with this dark-complexioned boy, even if we can’t give up talking about Him.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.47.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.17)**))**

“Karmis, jnanis, yogis, tapasvis and the students of Vedic literature who are not Krsna conscious simply beat around the bush, without any final profit since they have no clear knowledge of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Nor do they have faith in approaching Him by the execution of devotional service, although everywhere such service is repeatedly emphasized, as in this verse from SrimadBhagavatam ([11.14.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/14.20)):

‘My dear Uddhava, the unalloyed devotional service rendered to me by my devotees brings me under their control. I cannot be thus controlled by those engaged in mystic yoga, Sankhya philosophy, pious work, Vedic study, austerity or renunciation.’

*bhaktya mam abhijanati yavan yas casmi tattvatah*

**‘One can understand the Supreme Personality as He is only by devotional service.”**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**18.55**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)**))**

If one wants to understand the Supreme Personality factually, he must take to the path of devotional service and not waste time in profitless philosophical speculation, fruitive activity, mystic yogic practice or severe austerity and penance.

*ahara-nidra-bhaya-maithunam ca*  
*samanyam etat pasubhir naranam*  
*dharma hi tesam adhiko viseso*  
*dharmena hina pasubhih samanah*

**‘Both animals and men share the activities of eating, sleeping, mating and defending. However, the special propensity of the humans is that they are able to engage in spiritual life. Therefore, without spiritual life, humans are on the level of animals.’**  
**(Hitopadesa)**

### Verse 19

*tavad brahmakatha vimuktipadavi tavanna tiktibhavet-*  
*tavaccapi visrnkhalatvamayate no lokavedasthitih*  
*tavacchastravidam mithah kalakalo nana bahirvartmasu*  
*sri caitanya padambuja priyajano yavanna drggocarah*

**So long one does not see or meet the devotees, impersonalism, monistic philosophy and the pursuit of liberation (sayujya, salokya, and the like) will not seem onerous and despicable. Neither will one consider social and Vedic scriptural edicts as being the cause of chaos and anarchy in religious thought (therefore fit to be rejected); nor will one be able to realize the futility of endless speculation by arrogant, mundane academics posing as erudite scholars, who cling to their own opinions and inevitably engage in acrimonious arguments leading nowhere. By seeing the devotees of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, like bumblebees attracted by the nectar pollen of the Lord’s lotus feet, our inner vision becomes sanctified.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The esoteric and intimate truths regarding the Supreme Personality cannot be realized without taking association of Sri Gauranga’s devotees. As long as one does not see or meet a devotee, drunk from drinking the nectar of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, that person will remain enthusiastic about brahma-katha-topics of impersonal, non-qualitative Brahman. He will also not categorically reject vimukti-padavi- becoming one with, or merging into the form of Paramatma (sayujya mukti). Only in the association of Sri Gauranga’s devotees does a person understand that adherence to loka-veda-sthitih- social and Vedic norms, is indeed visrnkhalatvam- the cause of an unregulated, disorganized life. Though following these edicts and tenets gives one the impression that he is on a regulated path (compared herein to the links of a chain), it is actually the opposite. Without the bond of bhakti, all the links fall apart. However, as soon as one associates with Sri Caitanya’s devotees, esoteric truths, the particulars of the science of pure bhakti, assist that person to overcome all hurdles and confusion; they are swept away in the current of attachment to Sri Krsna.

As for the sastra-vidam- those who consider themselves erudite scholars by studying Vedic scriptures, they remain attached to the path of heated debates and futile arguments, since each adamantly adheres to his individual, speculative, and therefore mundane or nonessential arguments - nana-bahir-vartmasu (paths which only lead one away from the source). Conversely, the path of pure bhakti is substantive and progressive, ultimately aimed at transcendence.

Karika:

*sangah sri-gaura bhahtanam yavan na syat kalau yuge*  
*tavad brahma-vicaradi tavac chastra-vidarh kalih*

**‘In KaliYuga, as long as one does not obtain the association of Sri Gauranga’s devotees, the dangers of impersonalism (brahma-jnana - knowledge of Brahman) and the endless but futile war of words by the scriptural scribes continue to harass everyone.’**

**Purport**

*aksnoh phalam tvadrsa-darsanam hi*  
*tanoh phalam tvadrsa-gatra-sangah*  
*jihva-phalam tvadrsa-kirtanam hi*  
*sudurlabha bhagavata hi loke*

**‘My dear Vaisnava, seeing a person like you is the perfection of one’s eyesight. Touching your lotus feet is the perfection of the sense of touch. Glorifying your good qualities is the tongue’s real activity, for in the material world it is very difficult to find a pure devotee of the Lord.’**  
**(HariBhaktiSudhodaya(**[**13.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbs/13.2)**))**

The devotees who have surrendered everything and taken complete shelter at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord are rare souls. They are rare because the all-powerful Supreme Lord willingly becomes their property. The Lord chooses to reside in their hearts and eagerly provides His own heart as an abode for His pure devotees to reside in. By this act, the Supreme Lord places His pure devotees even above Himself. Thus we hear Lord Siva, the best of the Vaisnavas, telling His dear wife Parvatl in the PadmaPurana, that although the Vedas mention the worship of demigods, the worship of Visnu is the topmost. Yet, higher than the worship of Lord Visnu, is the worship of unalloyed Vaisnavas of the Lord.

Lord Siva also advises the Pracetas (SrimadBhagavatam [4.24.57](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.57)), saying that, if, even by chance, one associates with a pure devotee of the Lord, even for a fraction of a moment, it cannot be compared to the insignificant spiritual benefit of residing in the heavenly planets or the attainment of moksa. Thus, to see or meet a devotee of the Lord is indeed the result of immense pious activities.

Lord Caitanya, in describing the three different grades of devotees, says that the highest class of devotee is able to purify the consciousness of conditioned souls simply by his presence, to such an extent that they are inspired to immediately utter the all-purifying HolyNames of the Lord. Therefore, Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati mercifully exhorts us to take shelter of Lord Caitanya’s devotees, knowing full well the heart’s desire of the Supreme Lord, never to reject anyone who seeks shelter of His pure devotee.

*sri-bhagavan uvaca*  
*aham bhakta-paradhino hy asvatantra iva dvija*  
*sadhubhir grasta-hrdayo bhaktair bhakta-jana-priyah*

**The Supreme Personality said to the brahmana: “I am completely under the control of my devotees. Indeed, I am not at all independent. Because my devotees are completely devoid of material desires, I sit within the cores of their hearts. What to speak of my devotee, those who are devotees of my devotees are even more dear to Me.” (SrimadBhagavatam(**[**9.4.63**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/4.63)**))**

It is clear from this statement that those blessed by the Supreme Lord’s pure devotee are immediately enlightened with transcendental knowledge, by which they understand their eternal position as the Lord’s servitors, as well as the ultimate goal of life.

*mat-sevaya pratitam te salokyadi-catustayam*  
*necchanti sevaya purnah kuto ‘nyat kala-viplutam*

**‘My devotees are always satisfied to be engaged in My loving service; they are not interested even in the four principles of liberation (salokya, sarupya, samipya and sarsti), although these are automatically achieved by their service. What then is to be said of such perishable happiness as elevation to the higher planetary systems?’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**9.4.67**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/4.67)**))**

Philosophical speculation and dry logic are always inconclusive, even when debating mundane topics, what to speak of their inability to enlighten one of the transcendental AbsoluteTruth. Yudhisthir Maharaj remarks:

*tarko ’pratisthah srutayo vibhinna*  
*nasav rsir yasya matam na bhinnam*

**‘Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, full with variegated relative truths, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated self-realized person. Consequently, as the sastras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahajanas advocate.’**  
**(MahaBharat)**

### Verse 20

*kva tavad vairagyam kva ca visayavarttasu narake-*  
*svivodvegah kvasau vinayabharamapuryyalahari*  
*kva tavattejo’laukikamatha mahabhaktipadavi*  
*kva sa va sambhavya yadavakalitam gauragatisu*

**The single-minded followers of Lord GauraHari, whose only goal is the Lord’s lotus feet, develop a unique mood of unmotivated renunciation and undeviating attachment to Him. Is renunciation of such a high degree to be found anywhere else? No one other than the Lord’s devotees experience such great distress, as though being plummeted into hell, by having to listen to mundane talks or common gossip. Where else can one find such a sublime mood of submission that caresses with soft and gentle waves of sweetness and charm! Where else can one find such transcendental energy, suffused with lustrous spirit and imposing prowess! And where else can one find such exceptional pursuance of loving spiritual sentiments? - except in the hearts of Sri GauraHari’s esteemed servitors, laden with devotion.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In this verse, the venerable author Srila Prabodhananda, having experienced in his heart the sublime and extraordinary spiritual potency of Sri Caitanya’s devotees, allows their eulogies to flow freely from his pen.

The quality of vairagyam- renunciation or apathy towards materialism that is found in gaura-gatisu- those whose only goal or object of surrender is Sri GauraHari, is observed (avakalitam) in them alone - ‘kva? Where else can it be found?’ no where else.

Here, vairagyam suggests single-minded attachment to the Supreme Lord. Viraga (vi-specific, raga-attachment) implies attachment to a specific object, Sri Krsna; hence the feeling (bhava) that arises is vairagyam, or exclusive and deep attachment to Sri Krsna (entailing a concomitant lack of interest in anything, or anyone, or anywhere else).

visaya-varttasu narakesviva- mundane topics, without a trace of spirituality or connection to the Supreme Lord, constitute a hellish hole of suffering for Sri Gauranga’s devotees; vinaya-the exalted quality of humility, which emanates in endless waves from the GauraBhaktas is not found in other personalities; alaukika tejah- the extraordinary spiritual potency that GauraBhaktas display is rarely found elsewhere.

These devotees have Sri Gauranga as their sole shelter. The elevated path of pure devotion (suddha bhakti) they cultivate is impossible to surpass or equal, neither can it be imitated. Therefore, the only way one can easily acquire these wonderful spiritual qualities is to serve the lotus feet of Sri Cauranga’s beloved devotees.

Karika:

*vairagyadi guno yadrg gaura-bhaktesu drsyate*  
*tadrso guna-leso ‘pi kvapy anyatra na drsyate*

**‘The excellent qualities of vairagya, deep attachment to Sri Krsna, and so on, manifest in the devotees of Sri Gauranga, are not seen anywhere else, even in the slightest degree.’**

**Purport**

Surrendered devotees of the Lord automatically develop all the good qualities present in the demigods. They lose interest in material sense gratification. In truth, detachment or renunciation of the material world occur proportionate to the degree that the devotee develops attachment to Sri Krsna’s lotus feet. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu taught уukta-vairagya- to dovetail everything in the Lord’s service and in this way free ourselves from material attachments. This material world is a transformation of the Supreme Lord’s potency; hence, everything is meant for the Lord’s service. When someone becomes attached to Krsna and sees Krsna in everything (as Krsna mentions in BhagavadGita [6.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/6.30): ‘For one who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, I am never lost, nor is he ever lost to Me.’) such a soul is a first class devotee; as also confirmed in SrimadBhagavatam ([11.2.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.45)):

‘The most advanced devotee sees within everything the Soul of all souls, the Supreme Personality, Sri Krsna. Consequently he sees everything in relation to the Supreme Lord and understands that everything that exists is eternally situated within the Lord.’

Devotees who have developed loving attachment to the Lord are always careful not to waste a single moment in activities which have no connection with devotional service. Mundane topics and philosophical speculation, sense gratification, and the like, are detriments on the path to spiritual progress. Srila Jagadananda Pandit, in His PremaVivarta, advises everyone on the path of bhakti-yoga to abstain from such engagements. To lose taste for inferior mundane things is only possible by experiencing a higher taste (as stated in BhagavadGita [2.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.59)). The truth is that Lord Caitanya’s followers are prepared to go to hell for the purpose of propagating the Sankirtan movement; but they are truly afraid of associating with nondevotees and gross materialists attached to sensegratification, since such association may hinder their service.

*narayana-parah sarve na kutascana bibhyati*  
*svargapavarga-narakesv api tulyartha-darsinah*

**‘Devotees solely engaged in the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Narayana, never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation and the hellish planets are all the same, for such devotees are interested only in the service of the Lord.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.17.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/17.28)**))**

*bhaktih paresanubhavo viraktir*  
*anyatra caisa trika eka-kalah*  
*prapadyamanasya yathasnatah syus*  
*tustih pustih ksud-apayo ’nu-ghasam*

‘Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things - these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating.’ (SrimadBhagavatam ([11.2.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.42)))

### Verse 21

*sakrnnayana gocarikrta tadasrudharakula-*  
*praphulla kamaleksana pranayakatara sri mukhah*  
*na gauracaranam jihasati kadapi lokottara-*  
*sphuranmadhurimarnavam navanavanuragonmadah*

**That person who is intoxicated by newer and ever fresh forms of affectionate attachment and passionate devotion, brought on by even once having seen Lord Gauranga’s love-smitten, beatific face decorated with lotus-shaped eyes blossoming from pools of tears - such a devotee will never ever desire to distance himself from the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari, who is the embodiment of the mystically manifest ocean of madhurya-rasa. Thus does intense love-in-separation experience the ever-fresh variegated waves of ecstasy, churned from the ocean of madness in love.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The devotees of Sri Gauranga are worthy of the highest glorification since they have reposed their love and affection solely at the lotus feet of Sri GauraSundar. These devotees never desire under any circumstance to distance themselves from Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet. They want to always remain absorbed in the bliss of meditating on Sri Gauranga.

‘Who are these devotees?’

They are sakrn nayana gocarikrta tad asru-dhara- those who have witnessed the most gorgeous, beatific face (sri-mukhah) of Sri Gauranga, decorated with signs of distress, having been smitten by intense love (pranaya-katara). A beautiful face adorned with prafulla-kamaleksana- eyes resembling fully blossomed lotus flowers. Due to excruciating pangs of separation from Sri Krsna, they are dilated, raining down torrents of tears. Those devotees who have seen Sri Gauranga’s sri-mukha even once are extremely fortunate. They are navanavanu ragonmadah- intoxicated by ever fresh symptoms of affectionate madness. This loving attachment to Sri Krsna makes them oblivious to their duties and responsibilities, having suffused them with Divine exhilaration.

anuraga:

*sadanubhrtam api yah kuryyan navanavam priyam*  
*rago bhavann eva navah so’nuraga itlryyate*

**‘Though the beloved is always felt to be within one’s perception, the loving emotions that dawn in the heart are experienced in novel ways; the quality of ever-freshness is unique.’**

Another definition of raga is:

*duhkham apy adhikam citte sukhatvenaiva vyajyate*  
*yatantu pranayotkarsat sa raga iti kirttyate*

**‘When loving attachment reaches a state where even excessive sorrow is experienced as bliss in the heart, it is known as raga.’**

‘What is the quality of GauraCarana?’

They are lokottara- when beauty and splendour reach their pinnacle, they melt, and an ocean is formed. His lotus feet are that ocean. Sri Gauranga’s beloved devotees always sport in that nectarean ocean. They never renounce His lotus feet.

Karika:

*srimad gaura-mukham yena sakrd drg gocankrtam*  
*sa hi tac caranam hatum na saknoti kadacana*

**‘Whoever is fortunate enough to gaze upon the sublime countenance of Sri Gauranga, will never be able to distance himself from His lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Personality’s form and beauty are transcendental. He is the embodiment of sat-cit-ananda- eternality, transcendental knowledge and unlimited spiritual bliss. Every limb, every part of His transcendental body is saturated with Divine ecstasy. Anyone who sees the form of the Lord either in person or in His Deity manifestation is immediately rewarded with spiritual blessings. This is confirmed in the VarahaPurana, quoted in BhaktiRasamrtuSindhu.

*vrndavane tu govindam ye pasyanti vasundhare*  
*na te yamapuram yanti yanti punya krtam gatim*

**‘Those who see the form of Lord Govinda in Vrindaban. never enter into the abode of Yamaraja (Lord of death), but are rewarded with the results of immense piety.’**

Srila Visvanath Thakur comments:

“The pious results mentioned in this verse are meant for the materialistic nondevotees, not for those persons who are on the platform of niskama karma (detached from the results of fruitive activity). When they see the Lord, they automatically develop love and attachment for Him (rati).”

**‘The supreme occupation (dharma) for all humanity is that by which man can attain to loving devotional service unto the transcendental Lord.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.2.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6)**))**

The ultimate result of pious activity is bhakti - the highest spiritual goal for humanity. The SrimadBhagavatam ([10.29.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.36)) confirms that those who see Him develop attraction for unalloyed service to Him.

**‘O lotus-eyed one, the Goddess of Fortune considers it a festive occasion whenever she touches the soles of Your lotus feet. You are very dear to the residents of the forest, and therefore we will also touch those lotus feet. From that time on we will be unable even to stand in the presence of any other man, for we will have been fully satisfied by You.’**

*viksyalakavrta-mukham tava kundala-sri*  
*ganda-sthaladhara-sudham hasitavalokam*  
*dattabhayam ca bhuja-danda-yugam vilokya*  
*vaksah sriyaika-ramanam ca bhavama dasyah*

**‘Dear Krsna, we have simply surrendered ourselves as your maidservants, for we have seen Your beautiful face decorated with tresses of hair, your earrings falling upon Your cheeks and the nectar of your lips. We have also seen the beauty of your smile and have been embraced by your arms, which give us courage. Because we have seen your chest, which is beautiful and broad, we surrender ourselves to you.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.29.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.39)**))**

Devotion to Krsna, or bhakti-yoga, is inherent in every living entity. It is not something external to be gained from another source. When the heart is purified by hearing and chanting, bhakti gradually and naturally awakens. The jiva's subservience to Krsna as His servitor is eternally present in his original spiritual identity, but in latent form. In his conditioned state this nature is shrouded in the gloom of nescience. By practicing the regulative principles of vaidhi- bhakti under the guidance of a liberated spiritual master, it is awakened. And once the jiva experiences this higher taste for hearing and chanting, he loses attraction for inferior mundane attachments.

### Verse 22

*acaryya dharmmam paricaryya visnum*  
*vicaryya tirthani vicaryya vedan*  
*vina na gaurapriyapadasevam*  
*vedadi dusprapya padam vidanti*

**A person may follow the principles of VarnasramDharma, worship the Deity of Lord Visnu, visit hundreds of places of pilgrimage, or even scrutinize the entire Vedic literature, but still he will not have the slightest clue about that most rare gem amongst spiritual abodes, the transcendental venue of SriSri Radha Govinda’s eternal pastimes - Vrindaban - if he has not served the lotus feet of Sri GauraSundara’s dearmost associates.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In this verse our honoured author asserts, that without taking shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga’s devotees, no one can attain realized knowledge or the truth about param-purusartha, the highest and ultimate goal of human life recommended in the Vedas. Service to the devotees of Sri Gauranga is the path to perfection. The activities of dharma- following varnasrama-dharma; visnum- faithfully worshiping the Supreme Lord Sri Visnu; tirthani- circumambulating the holy places of pilgrimage; vicaryya vedan- scrutinizing the Vedas, and the like, bear limited results. Without serving the lotus feet of GauraBhaktas, the possibility of attaining vraja-vrndavana-prema, is practically nil.

Karika:

*dharma-krd visnu-sevi ca tirthati vedaparagah*  
*na vetti vraja-tatvam hi gaura-bhaktasrayam vina*

**‘Even if a person follows the religious principles of Varnasrama, visits all the holy places, or is well-versed in the Vedas, he cannot know the eternal truth about Vraja without taking shelter of Sri Gauranga’s devotees.’**

**Purport**

The conditioned living entities are forced to take new bodies due to karmic reactions of their past deeds in the continuous cycle of births and deaths. In their embodied state, they forget their original spiritual identity. They do not even understand why they have to suffer the three-fold miseries. Hence, they do not know how to inquire about the goal and purpose of life and the means by which they can attain it, which will put a permanent end to their sufferings and repeated births. The revealed scriptures inform us, that unless the jiva acts according to his original nature, he cannot be satisfied. Satisfaction and happiness are available only on the platform of Brahman, where one is free from all lamentations and anxieties (BhagavadGita [18.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.54)). After attaining the brahma-bhuta platform, one attains devotion to the Supreme Lord (bhakti). Bhakti is not available by any means other than association with pure devotees. This is confirmed in BrihanNaradiyaPurana, quoted in HariBhaktiVilasa ([10.2.79](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbv/10.2.79)):

*bhaktistu bhagavat-bhakta-sangena parijayate*

**‘Bhakti is awakened only in the association of the Lord’s devotees.’**

The pure devotees of the Lord are described in the scriptures as asraya-tattva - the shelter of bhakti-rasa; eternal associates of the Supreme Lord. Hence, only such liberated souls can plant the seed of pure devotion in the hearts of the conditioned souls. Their association can destroy material attachments and bring Sri Krsna under their control, as confirmed by the Supreme Lord Krsna Himself:

*sri-bhagavan uvaca*  
*na rodhayati mam yogo na sahkhyam dharma eva ca*  
*na svadhyayas tapas tyago nesta-purtam na daksina*  
*vratani yajnas chandamsi tirthani niyama yamah*  
*yathavarundhe sat-sangah sarva-sangapaho hi mam*

**The Supreme Lord said: “O Uddhava! The association of pure devotees dissolves all material attachments and is able to completely captivate me like no other pious deed can. Other pious deeds include yoga, sahkhya-philosophy (philosophical analysis of the elements of material nature), astanga-yoga, nonviolence, religiosity, chanting of Vedic hymns, penance, renunciation, sacrifices, digging of wells, planting trees and the performance of other public welfare activities, charity, vows, worshipping demigods, chanting secret mantras, pilgrimage, and so on. The performance of such activities, does not bring Me under one’s control.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.12.1-2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/12.1)**))**

The transcendental realm, where SriSri RadhaGovinda perform their eternal Lila (pastimes) is the highest spiritual abode:

*goloka nami nija dhamni tale ca tasya*

**‘Lord Hari’s abode, the abode of Mahesa and the mundane world (DeviDham) are all located below Goloka.’**  
**(BrahmaSamhita (**[**5.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/43)**))**

**‘RasaRaj Sri Krsna never leaves GolokaDham, not for even a moment. In Goloka, he sports with Srimati Radharani, who resembles His own spiritual Figure, the embodiment of His ecstatic pleasure-giving potency.’**  
**(BrahmaSamhita (**[**5.37**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/37)**))**

### Verse 23

*aparavarancedamrtamaya pathodhimadhikam*  
*vimathya praptam syat kimapi paramam saramatulam*  
*tathapi sri gaurakrti madanagopala carana-*  
*cchatasprstanam tadvahati vikatameva katutam*

**If, by most vigorously churning the shoreless ocean of nectar, incomparable and ineffable treats are obtained, such delights nevertheless taste horribly bitter to those exalted devotees who have been touched by the sublime rays emanating from the lotus feet of MadanGopal, who has now appeared in the form of Sri GauraSundar.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The Supreme Lord Sri Gauranga’s beloved devotees are eulogized here by exhibiting their neglectful attitude towards objects very difficult to obtain, priceless and extremely rare. To them these are all insignificant. If a shoreless (aparavara) ocean of amrta (nectar of immortality) were vigorously churned, then unique and fabulous things might be obtained. Such gifts from the ocean of nectar are paramam saramatulam- absolutely perfect and incomparably quintessential. However, to those devotees who are attached to the transcendental rays emanating from the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga, none other than MadanGopal Sri Krsna Himself, they are vikatam eva katutam-unbearably bitter.

sri-gaurakrti-madanagopala-

Sri- Srimati Radhika; MadanGopal- Sri Krsna, having accepted the golden complexion of Srimati Radhika, has become Sri Gaura; caranacchata- the beauty of the rays radiating from His lotus feet; sprstanam- ‘in touch with’; indicating those who are overwhelmed by such beauty. For these devotees, who relish the sublime sweetness of Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet as the essence of everything enjoyable, all else is insipid and distasteful. In this way can we recognize the most fortunate position of the Gaura Bhaktas.

Karika:

*samasta vastu saranam saramsa-bhuta vastuni*  
*tucchatam dadhati srimad-gauranga-pada-sevakah*

**‘The servitors of the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga consider the cream of the best of everything substantive (creme de’la creme) as insignificant.’**

**Purport**

The BhagavadGita describes this material world as duhkhalayam asasvata (a temporary place of miseries). The embodied soul living in this material world is by nature spiritual, part and parcel of the sat-cit-ananda-vigraha SriKrsna, therefore naturally inclined to search out ananda (bliss). Pure uninterrupted happiness is not of this mundane world. Ananda in this material world is temporary, merely a state of being devoid of suffering and distress. Pleasures available in the higher planetary systems are superior to earthly joys. Brahmananda (bliss experienced in impersonal Brahman realisation) is transcendental to the material nature and superior to mundane happiness. However, brahmananda is bereft of the ecstasy derived from a relationship in loving devotion to the Supreme Lord. Therefore, those exalted souls who have tasted the nectar of Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet are apathetic to all other joys.

*dhatar yad asmin bhava isa jivas*  
*tapa-trayenabhihata na sarma*  
*atman labhante bhagavams tavanghri-*  
*cchayam sa-vidyam ata asrayema*

**‘О Father, О Lord, О Supreme Personality, the living entities in the material world can never have any happiness because they are overwhelmed by three kinds of miseries. Therefore, they take shelter of the shade of Your lotus feet, that are full with knowledge, and we also thus take shelter of them.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**3.5.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.40)**))**

*ekantino yasya na kancanartham*  
*vanchanti ye vai bhagavat-prapannah*  
*aty-adbhutam tac-caritam sumangalam*  
*gayanta ananda-samudra-magnah*

‘Unalloyed devotees, who have no desire other than to serve the Lord, worship Him in full surrender and always hear and chant about His activities, which are most auspicious. Thus they always merge in an ocean of transcendental bliss. Such devotees never ask the Lord for any benediction.’  
(SrimadBhagavatam ([8.3.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-8/3.20)))

The Supreme Personality Sri Krsna, is both the source and cause of unlimited ecstatic bliss:

*angani yasya sakalendriya-vrtti-manti*  
*pasyanti panti kalayanti ciram jaganti*  
*ananda-cinmaya-sad-ujjvala-vigrahasya*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, whose transcendental form is full of bliss, truth, substantiality and is thus full of the most dazzling splendor. Each of the limbs of that transcendental figure possesses in Himself, the full-fledged functions of all the organs, and eternally sees, maintains and manifests the infinite universes, both spiritual and mundane.’**  
**(BrahmaSamhita (**[**32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/32)**))**

“For want of a taste of things spiritual, a grave doubt arises in the minds of those who are enchained by worldly knowledge. On hearing a narration of the pastimes of Sri Krsna, they think that the truth (tattva) regarding Krsna is the mental concoction of certain scholars created by their imaginative brains out of material drawn from mundane principles. With the object of removing this harmful doubt, in this and the three following slokas, Brahma distinguishes between the two things (viz - spirit and matter) in a rational manner, trying to make one understand the pure Lila of Krsna that he obtained by his unmixed ecstatic trance. Brahma wants to say that the form of Krsna is allexistence, all-knowledge and all-bliss, whereas all mundane experiences are full of palpable ignorance. Although there is specific difference between the two, the fundamental truth is that spiritual affairs constitute the Absolute Source; specification and variegatedness are ever present. By them are established the transcendental Abode, Form, Name, Quality and Sports of Sri Krsna. It is only by a person, possessed of pure spiritual knowledge and freedom from any relationship with maya, that these amorous pastimes of Krsna can at all be appreciated.”

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“The gross and subtle material bodies of the jiva, having been completely destroyed; the infinitesimal soul regains his (her) original pristine purity. Although the jiva is anu, or minutely small, his spiritual happiness is not minute. To remove this misapprehension, Lord Caitanya uses the word (in His Sri Siksastaka) - anandambudhi-vardhanam- ‘an ever-increasing ocean of bliss’. In other words, the HolyNames of the Lord endlessly expand the spiritual bliss inherent in the soul. He thus becomes eternally fixed in one of the spiritual mellows, namely dasya, sakhya, vatsalya or madhurya (servitorship, friendship, parenthood or conjugal love). Established in his eternal spiritual mellow, he begins to relish limitless nectar at every stage of his transcendental relationship, through exchanges of extraordinary loving emotions with the Supreme Lord. The Supreme Lord Krsna’s enchanting Beauty, His Divine Qualities and His sublime Pastimes are increasingly ecstatic and ever-fresh. Inebriated with Divine prema. The pure jiva continuously drinks this sweet nectar, but still the Lord’s captivating beauty remains ever-fresh and ambrosial, relished in endlessly unique and novel ways.”  
(Sri Siksastaka /Purport)

In the teachings of the Christian Bible, Jesus Christ has also explained that the test of one who has genuinely experienced Love of God. is that such love must necessarily be accompanied by a concomitant lack of taste for Mammon (riches, prosperity, affluence, worldly possessions and so on).

### Verse 24

*trnadapi ca nicata sahaja saumya mugdhakrtih*  
*sudhamadhura bhasita visaya gandha thuhiitkrtih*  
*haripranaya vihvala kimapi dhiranalambita*  
*bhavanti kila sadguna jagati gaurabhajamami*

**The ardent followers of Sri Gauranga are the only devotees whose immaculate character is ornamented with the following excellences: humility more than a blade of grass (freedom from false prestige); their innate nature suffused with innocent simplicity; their peaceful appearance enhanced by an inner grace; their tempered speech nectarean. They are contemptuous of anything that has even a scent of worldly or sensual connotation. Inebriated with KrsnaPrema, they are oblivious to the mundane world.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In asserting that the devotees of Sri Gauranga are repositories of all Divine qualities, the esteemed author broadcasts their exceptional glories. The numerous good qualities found in this world surely decorate the character of Sri Gauranga’s devotees.

‘What are these qualities?’

trnad api sunicata- more humble than blades of grass. Just as the grass bears the burden of people trampling on it, so also the GauraBhaktas never become intolerant or enraged even when others try to repress them. This quality is also known as ksanti- forbearance; forgiveness. The symptoms of ksanti are mentioned in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu ([1.3.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.3.27)):

*ksobha-hetav api prapte ksantir aksubhitatmata*

**‘Even when there is valid reason to get angry or upset, one nevertheless remains unperturbed and calm.’**

sahaja-saumya-mugdhakrtih- the devotee’s physical appearance is naturally tranquil, soothing and pleasing to all; sudha-madhura-bhasita- his speech is as sweet as nectar; visaya-gandha thdhutkrtih- he is apathetic towards materialistic, worldly dealings, absolutely rejecting anything that is not connected with Sri KrsnaCaitanya. His mind and intelligence are totally absorbed in prema, transcendental love of the Supreme Personality Sri Hari. He is unconcerned and dispassionate towards anything devoid of a link with the Supreme Lord, as if it was a black hole leading into the void. Thus do these qualities set him apart and accentuate his glorious personality.

Karika:

*kayikd vacika hrdya buddhiyah sobhana gunah*  
*santi ye gaura-bhaktesu te gunah kvapi na sthitah*

**‘The auspicious qualities in body, words, heart and intelligence of the peaceful devotees of Sri Gauranga are not found anywhere else.’**

**Purport**

The scriptures have described the good qualities and attributes that decorate the personality and character of a saintly person. The SrimadBhagavatam enumerates twenty-six qualities essential to a pure devotee’s character, known as sadhubhusanam. These qualities are not found in ordinary persons. Of these qualities, the four mentioned in this verse are found only in Sri GauraSundara’s dear associates.

Humility, when compared to a blade of grass, conveys a high degree of modesty, together with an attitude of not wanting any honor and recognition for oneself. When there is reason to feel insulted at being disregarded and shown disrespect, the person who is as humble as a blade of grass will not become angry or feel insulted.

Followers of Lord Chaitanya will always remember His instructions regarding the chanting of His HolyNames. He advented in KaliYuga specifically to inaugurate the YugaDharma - chanting of the HolyNames of Sri Hari. Thus the best means to chant is to follow this instruction of Caitanya Mahaprabhu in Sri Siksastaka:

*trnad api su-nicena taror iva sahisnuna*  
*amanina mana-dena kirtaniyah sada harih*

**‘One who thinks himself lower than a blade of grass, who is more tolerant than a tree, and who does not expect personal honor, yet is always prepared to give all respect to others, can very easily always chant the HolyNames of the Lord.’**

Lord Caitanya’s followers are very attached to chanting Sri Nama (the beautiful HolyNames). Having the constant association of the HolyNames that purify the consciousness of all mundane dirt and impurities, the heart and subtle body also begin to shine with splendorous beauty. Thus did Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu describe the symptoms of a MahaBhagavat:

*yanhara darsane mukhe aise krsna-nama*  
*tanhare janiha tumi ‘vaisnava-pradhana’*

**Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu said, “A first-class Vaisnava is he whose very presence makes others chant the HolyNames of Krsna.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**16.74**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/16.74)**))**

### Verse 25

*upasatam va guruvaryya kotir*  
*adhiyatam va sruti sastrakotih*  
*caitanya karunya kataksa bhajam*  
*sadyah param syaddhi rahasya labhah*

**Even if a person worships, serves and glorifies millions of the best amongst so many instructing spiritual masters (gurus), or scrutinizingly studies millions of Vedic scriptures (Agama, Nigama), there is no possibility for him to quickly attain the essence of all desirable things, namely Love of God (prema). However, those who have been graced by the merciful glance of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, easily attain within an instant, this most mysterious, Divine and exalted Love of Krsna (KrsnaPrema).**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s devotees form a singular group, eligible to attain the purest and loftiest levels of prema. This amazing dispensation further enhances their greatness. Thus without taking shelter of Sri GauraCandra’s lotus feet, upasatam va guruvarya kotir- many gurus may be considered as advanced, and even if one receives instructions regarding the process of devotion to the Supreme Lord from millions of such gurus, it won’t be possible to attain nigudha VrajaPrema- the purest and loftiest prema exhibited by the gopis in Vraja.

sruti-sastra-koti- one may scrutinize and study the entire Vedas, Puranas, Agamas, and so on, ten million times over, but only by taking shelter of those devotees who are blessed with the merciful glance of Sri Caitanya is a person able to immediately understand and relish prema, otherwise it remains shrouded in mystery. In conclusion, let us say that only those who have sought complete shelter at the lotus feet of GauraBhaktas are guaranteed to attain the most rarely obtainable - VrajaPrema. Thus can we understand something of the glories of the GauraBhaktas.

Karika:

*sevitasankhya gurvvadi-jananam yah kvacin na hi*  
*gaura-bhaktaih sa labhyate nigudha priyata rasah*

**‘That which is unattainable (nigudha VrajaPrema-rasa) even after serving countless gurus and preceptors for many long years, is readily available to the devotees of Sri Gauranga, or it may be obtainable by help from the GauraBhaktas, or through their association.’**

**Purport**

*brahmanda bhramite kona bhagyavan jiva*  
*guru-krsna-prasade paya bhakti-lata-bija*

**‘According to their karma, the living entities are wandering throughout the universes. Out of many millions of wandering living entities, one who is very fortunate gets an opportunity to associate with a bonafide spiritual master, by the grace of Sri Krsna. By the mercy of both Krsna and the spiritual master, such a person receives the seed of the creeper of devotional service. ’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.151**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.151)**))**

Srila A.C Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad explains:

“When we speak of brahmanda, we refer to the whole universe, or to the clusters of many millions of universes. In all universes there are innumerable planets and innumerable living entities upon those planets, in the air and in the water. There are millions and trillions of living entities everywhere, and they are engaged by maya in suffering and enjoying the results of their fruitive activities, life after life. This is the position of the materially conditioned living entities. Out of many of these entities, if one is actually fortunate (bhagyavan), he comes in contact with a bonafide spiritual master by Krsna’s mercy.

**“The seed of the creeper of devotional service continues to grow, watered by the process of hearing and chanting. Penetrating through the coverings of the illusory world of maya, it finally reaches the lotus feet of Sri Krsna in Goloka Vrindaban and bears the sweet, ripened fruit of prema - love of Krsna.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**19.152-154**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.152)**)**

The process of pure chanting of the Lord's HolyNames was inaugurated by Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, thus this transcendental seed, which flourishes by the watering of chanting and hearing, can only be sown by an eternal associate of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Other gurus are capable of giving transcendental knowledge and the seed of devotion to the Supreme Lord, but the seed which sprouts into a bhakti-lata, bearing the fruit of vipralambha-rasa (the transcendental lovein-separation of the Vrajabasis for Krsna in Vrindaban; especially the parakiya mood of the gopis), can be transplanted into the heart of a faithful seeker (sraddhavan) only by a follower of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, who has himself tasted the fruit of prema.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“The pure devotee (spiritual master) blesses his disciple by initiating him in the highest service to Krsna. The Supreme Personality of God, in order to shower his grace on pious and eligible candidates, so that they may receive the highest spiritual benediction, sends forth His dearmost associates, empowering them with His mercy potency (krpa-sakti) to distribute His mercy in the role of a mahanta-guru- an exalted, liberated spiritual master. Thus Sri GuruDeva shows compassion to his disciple by engaging him in Krsna’s service.”

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“Devotees must worship SriSri GuruGauranga. One should always meditate on Lord Gauranga, knowing Him to be nondifferent in every way from Sri Krsna. Sri Guru is known to be Lord Mukunda’s dearest devotee. Without first remembering and worshipping the spiritual master and Lord Gauranga, one cannot render pure loving devotional service to the Divine Couple SriSri RadhaKrsna. Deviation from this process will curb all spiritual advancement.”

Foremost amongst Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu's dearest associates, Srila Raghunath DasGosvami, recapitulates Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu's teachings in the second verse of his Sri ManahSiksa:

*nа dharmam nadharmam sruti-gana-niruktam kila kuru*  
*vraje radha-krsna-pracura-paricaryam iha tanu*  
*sacisunum nandisvnra-pati-sutatve guruvaram*  
*mukunda- presthatve smara paramajasram nanu manah*

**‘My dear mind, please do not perform religious activities prescribed in the Vedas, nor the sinful activities denounced in the scriptures. The ultimate conclusion of the Vedic literatures is that the DivineCouple SriSri RadhaKrsna are the supreme object of worship, and that loving service to them is the most relishable experience of all. Therefore, О mind, engage yourself fully in serving them with love and devotion. Always meditate on Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, the son of mother Saci, understanding Him to be absolutely nondifferent from Sri Krsna, the son of Maharaj Nanda. О mind, meditate as well on Sri Guru, who is the dearmost devotee of Lord Mukunda (Sri Krsna).’**

### Verse 26

*astam vairagya kotirbhavatu samadamaksanti maitryadikoti-*  
*stattvanudhyana kotirbhavatu va vaisnavl bhakti kotih*  
*kotyam so’pyasya na syat tadapi gunagano yah svatah siddha aste*  
*srimaccaitanyacandra priyacarananakha jyotiramoda bhajam*

**A person may practice severe austerities and renunciation and may possess innumerable qualities like peacefulness, selfcontrol, tolerance, being a kind friend to all, and so on. He may submerge himself in meditation on the jiva ’s oneness with Brahman or cultivate profound devotion to Lord Visnu, engaging in endless service to the Supreme Lord. Let it be. Millions and billions of such qualities cannot equal even a millionth part of the excellences automatically manifest in the character of those who are fortunate enough to have been illuminated by the rays emanating from the toenails of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s intimate and eternal associates.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

What more can be said about the glories of GauraBhaktas? The host of excellent qualities manifest in the devotees, who are in the shelter of Sri Caitanya’s beloved followers, are not to be seen in anyone else.

Let some persons practice vairagya-kotih- innumerable types of austerities and abnegation, even up to the most acute limits of renunciation. This does not compare to even a drop of the excellences that decorate the Divine personalities of GauraBhaktas. Let persons cultivate and obtain the results of sama-dama-ksanti-maitradi - sama- mind-restraint, to single-mindedly direct the mind to the Supreme Lord; dama- sensecontrol, withdrawing the senses from their attachment to the world of phenomena; ksanti- forbearance and mental equanimity; maitra- friendliness towards all living entities. Let them pursue tattvanudhyana-kotih- uninterrupted absorption in meditation on the AbsoluteTruth (meditating on tat tvam asi- ‘you are that Brahman’, tat = Paramatma, the SuperSoul in the heart; tvam - Jivatma, the living entities; asi- ‘their oneness’). Tattva also means the SupremeTruth, Personality of Godhead; anudhyana- continuous meditation on Him. Let them possess avaisnavi-bhakti-kotih- unlimited devotion to the Supreme Lord Sri Visnu. Let it be (astam).

The beloved devotees of Sri CaitanyaCandra are eternally connected to the Supreme Lord’s quintessential internal energy, hladini-sakti. Thus, those who worship their lotus feet and who relish the sublime illumination emanating from their toenails, have all the Divine qualities automatically manifest in their persons to such a degree that even a billionth particle of those qualities cannot be equalled by millions and billions of the aforementioned qualities. If this be the case with the followers of GauraBhaktas, then how glorious indeed are the GauraBhaktas themselves? Here the Kaimutya-Nyaya argument, a fortiori is applicable (‘for a stronger reason’; used of a conclusion logically more certain than another).

Karika:

*caitanya-bhakta-bhaktanam yo gunah svatah iritah*  
*tasya kotyamhsa-leso’pi na kvapi bhajatam kimu*

**The host of excellences that naturally appear in devotees of the devotees of Sri Gauranga cannot be found even in a billionth part in any other worshiper or spiritualist.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

‘ Vairagya-kotih means both strict renunciation and various types of renunciation. Renunciation (vairagya) is of two kinds- phalgu and yukta. To reject or renounce anything connected to the Supreme Lord Hari as mundane is known as phalgu-vairagya. To accept only those things related to Sri Krsna and favourable for devotional service is called yukta-vairagya.’

*anasaktasya visayan yatharham upayunjatah*  
*nirbandhah krsna-sambandhe yuktam vairagayam ucyate*

**‘Renunciation in which there is no attachment for the objects of the senses, but in which everything is seen in relationship to Sri Krsna and all things are engaged in His service is called yukta-vairagya, or practical renunciation.’**

*prapancikataya buddhya hari-sambandhi-vastunah*  
*mumuksabhih parityago vairagyam phalgu kathyate*

**‘Renunciation which is practiced by those desirous of impersonal liberation and which rejects things having connection with Lord Hari, thinking them to be material, is called phalgu-vairagya., superficial or false renunciation.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu** [**1.2.255-256**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.255)**)**

### Verse 27

*kecit sagarabhudharanapi parakramanti nrtyanti vai*  
*keciddeva purandaradisu mahaksepam ksipanto muhuh*  
*anandоdbhatajalavihvalataya te’dvaitacandradayah*  
*ke ke noddhatavanta idrsi punascaitanya nrtyotsave*

**It seemed that some devotees, like Murari Gupta (incarnation of Hanuman), were striding over oceans and mountains, in extreme exultation, oblivious to the world outside. While dancing, devotees like Sri Srivas Pandit, overwhelmed by outlandish ananda, repeatedly berated Indra, the King of Heaven, and the other demigods for not participating. Which devotee, including AdvaitAcarya, can remain calm and not become bumptious and excited while participating in Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s magnificent Festival of Dance?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

By describing the GauraBhaktas’ uncommon but wonderful physical expressions of transcendental bhava, the respected author, full of awe and affection, continues to broadcast their glories.

In Sri Caitanya’s festival of dance, ke kim no krtavantah \[alternate reading\]- ‘Who was there who was not behaving in some wild, eccentric fashion?’ Who could restrain himself from dancing wildly like a madman, including Sri AdvaitAcarya? Amongst Mahaprabhu’s transcendental followers, Sri Murari Gupta and company were in such ecstasy, it seemed they were ready to jump over oceans and mountains while Lord Nityananda, Sri Advaita and others were absorbed in dancing. While dancing, Srila Srinivas and company were castigating the king of heaven, Indra and the other demigods, for being tied to celestial pleasures.

‘Why these erudite and sober personalities are behaving in such fashion? it appears strange (udbhata).’

The reason - anandodbhata-jala- vihvalataya: ananda- they are experiencing the bliss of relishing the nectar of prema; udbhata-bizarre, fantastic, outlandish; jala- a large net; inducing them to become oblivious to the external world, due to vihvalataya- total absorption - thus causing them to dance wildly. The analogy of a net is meant to convey the sense of gossamer, shutting out the external world. Ecstatic dancing is a symptom of anubhava:

*anubhavastu cittastha bhavanam avabodhakah te bahir vikriya-*  
*prayah prokta udbhasvarakhyaya nrtyam viluthitam gitam*  
*krosanamtanumotanam hunkaro jrmbhnam svasabhuma lokan apeksita*

**Anubhava- external physical transformations that denote the internal action of bhava in the heart; also known as udbhasvara- illuminating. They include dancing, singing, shouting, rolling on the ground, roaring, remaining oblivious to Others presence, etc.**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu** [**2.2.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/2.2.1)**)**

Karika:

*ananda-rasa-purasthas caitanya pada parsadah*  
*nananubhavam isasya prakasante natotsave*

**‘Filled with the mellows of ecstatic revelry, the associates of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet exhibit various rapturous, spiritual transformations (anubhava) during His dance festival.’**

**Purport**

In BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu ([2.2.1-2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/2.2.1)), Srila Rupa Gosvami writes that anubhava, also known as udbhasvara, is defined as ‘spiritual sentiments lodged in the heart’, manifest through symptoms of ecstatic love. These symptoms include: dancing, singing, shouting, stretching the body, sighing, becoming oblivious to external phenomena, drooling, loud laughter and hiccupping. Thus, dancing is an ecstatic symptom, expressed by those elevated devotees who are eternally liberated and eligible to relish this most rare spiritual experience of bhava - the first stirring of prema. The Divine influence of Sri GauraSundar was so potent, that not only ordinary human beings could experience bhava by participating in His festival of dance, but even wild ferocious animals in the forest were made to dance by Him.

The Sankirtan movement, inaugurated by Sri GauraHari, is specifically meant to spiritually inspire and motivate the conditioned souls caught in the network of illusion, punished by the ill effects of KaliYuga. By this process of singing the Lord’s Names and dancing, one can easily counteract the debilitating effects of the Lord’s insurmountable external energy, maya. This is confirmed in the DvarakaMahatmya, quoted in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu:

*yo nrtyati prahrstatma bhavayir vahasu bhaktitah*  
*sa nirdahati papani manvantara-sated api*

**‘One who dances with joy and devotion burns to ashes the sins of many births, accumulated over many millenniums (manvantara).’**

### Verse 28

*bhuto va bhavitapi va bhavati va kasyapi sah ko’pi va*  
*sambandho bhagavat padambujarase nasmin jaganmandale*  
*tatsarvam nijabhakti rupa paramaisvaryena vikridato*  
*gaurasyasya krpa vijrmbhitataya jananti nirmatsarah*

**Who is there in this world who has ever, in the past, in the future, or at present, managed to develop any sort of relationship with the indescribable yet profound rasa (taste) of loving attachment to the nectarean mellows of love situated at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord? Yet, by the ever expanding mercy of Sri GauraHari, continually absorbed in His pleasure dalliance with the supreme opulence of devotion to Himself, the nonenvious, pure devotee gradually becomes aware of these sweet mellows (his or her relationship with the Lord), through the medium of devotional service to His lotus feet.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Those fortunate souls, touched by the compassionate glance of Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet, can alone become enlightened in the most confidential knowledge of VrajaPrema. Thus, the devotees of Sri GauraHari are glorious. Other than GauraBhaktas (because they are non-envious), no one in the entire creation, past, present or future, was, are or will be cognizant of the unique prema-rasa emanating from Sri Krsna’s lotus feet.

He who cannot tolerate the superiority or greatness of others is an envious person; he who can is non-envious. Nirmatsarah (non-envious) - those who are endowed with the temperament to endure another’s eminence.

‘How can one postulate that GauraBhaktas are non-envious and that they alone know nigudha-prema-rasa of the VrajaGopis?’

The answer: gaurasyasya krpa- they have been enriched by the mercy of Sri GauraHari; thus they easily become nirmatsarah, nonenvious, compassionate towards all; since they are enlightened about nigudha vraja prema-rasa. Nigudha-secret, mysterious, profound.

‘Who is Sri GauraHari?’

He amuses himself by revealing the supreme opulence of nija-prema-bhakti, superbly potent prema-bhakti to Himself. The compound word tat-sarvam means sa casau sarvas ceti vigrahah- Sri Gauranga, the combined form of SriSri RadhaMadhava, is everything; nigudha-gopi-prema is obtained only by His devotees and through His mercy alone.

Karika:

*krsna-padambuja-rasa-sambandhah kasya na kvacit*  
*jananty anubhavantyevam tam rasarh gauraparsadah*

**‘No one from this world has ever had contact with the taste of the ambrosia flowing from Sri Krsna’s lotus feet. Only the associates of Sri Caitanya are familiar with this rasa (liquid mellows) through their personal experience.’**

**Purport**

Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur has mentioned in MadhuryaKadambini (First shower):

“Devotees from previous ages like Sri Uddhava, Narada Muni, Sukadeva Gosvami, Sri Yamunacarya, Sri NathMuni, and others, have rendered loving devotional service to the Supreme Lord. Later, Lord Caitanya propagated spontaneous, unalloyed devotion, and on His order Srila Rupa Gosvami delineated the details of this devotional science. This process is therefore available only to the followers of Srila Rupa Gosvami, and so I (Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur) offer my invocatory prayers to Sri Rupa.”
