It is confirmed in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta, that Sri CaitanyaDeva, the combined form of SriSri RadhaKrsna, has appeared in KaliYuga by His causeless mercy to bestow upon the world what no incarnation ever offered before - the most sublime spiritual knowledge of devotional service in manjari bhava- serving as an assistant to the VrajaGopis, following in the wake of their devotional moods, but without any desire for sambhoga-rasa (personal satisfaction or enjoyment through union with the beloved).

The eternal associates of Lord Caitanya advented at the same time as He, to assist Him in His pastimes as YugaAvatar, to propagate the Sahkirtan movement. They firmly established the path of spontaneous devotional service in this world through their writings, speeches, personal example and by rediscovering the lost transcendental sites of Lord Sri Krsna’s eternal pastimes in Vraja. The SandilyaSutra confirms this - quoted in MadhuryaKadambini (First shower):

*bhaktih purvaih srita tantu rasam pasyed yadattadhih*  
*tam naumi satatam rupa nama priya. janam hareh*

**‘In the past, saintly persons have always taken shelter of devotional service. Five hundred years ago such a person appeared, by whose mercy such seekers are able to distinctly perceive that path of devotional service to Lord Krsna, a path steeped in spiritual rasa. I offer my repeated obeisances to that great soul, Srila Rupa Gosvami, very dear to Lord Krsna.’**

The exhaustive writings of Sri Caitanya’s associates on the subject of pure bhakti expand upon the various grades of devotional surrender from the initial stages up to the lofty regions of loving devotion in complete surrender to the Supreme Lord. This enables us to understand that the priceless gem of spiritual knowledge (raja-vidya) bestowed by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, leads to the stage of perfection, where spiritual bliss (susukham) is experienced at every step. Srila Rupa Gosvami has enumerated the different stages of elevation in the cultivation of bhakti in Sri BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu ([1.4.15-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.4.15)):

*adau sraddha tatah sadhu-sahgo ’tha bhajana-kriya*  
*tato 'nartha-nivrttih syat tato nistha rucis tatah*  
*athasaktis tato bhavas tatah premabhyudancali*  
*sadhakanam ayam premnah pradurbhave bhavet kramah*

**‘In the beginning there must be faith. Then one becomes interested in associating with pure devotees. Thereafter, one is initiated by the spiritual master and executes the regulative principles under his orders. Thus one is freed from all unwanted habits and becomes firmly fixed in devotional service. Thereafter, one develops taste and attachment. This is the way of sadhana-bhakti- the execution of devotional service according to regulative principles. Gradually emotions intensify, and finally there is an awakening of love. This is the gradual development of love of God for the devotee immersed in Krsna consciousness.’**

The exalted regions of bhakti beyond these eight levels and beyond prema are specifically described in Madhurya Kadambinl, (Eighth shower):

‘If a tree represents bhakti or true devotional service, these lofty devotional exchanges with the Lord can be described as the mature fruit that ripens on the tree of bhakti. These devotional exchanges are defined as follows:

- sneha (when the heart melts with excessive love)
- mana (extreme sneha that uncovers new, delightful regions of loving exchanges, making the beloved behave externally in a capricious way)
- pranaya (a type of mana that induces the beloved to feel on equal terms with the lover, thus inducing love-quarrels)
- raga (conflicting emotions in the beloved - sometimes unbearable lamentation, sometimes extreme happiness - while waiting expectantly to meet her lover, Sri Krsna).
- anuraga (love that makes the beloved experience she is meeting Him for the first time)
- mahabhava (the highest expression of love with all its diversity and complexity. This is not found in any of the other loving exchanges)

These elevated regions of DivineLove are inaccessible to the practitioner (sadhaka). He cannot taste this transcendental fruit. The sadhaka (acolyte or novice) is incapable of absorbing within himself and manifesting the tempestuous and contradictory emotions generated by pure spiritual love.’

### Verse 29

*mahapurusamaninam sura-munisvaranam nijam*  
*padambujamajanatam kimapi garvanirvasanam*  
*aho nayanagocaram nigamacakra cudacayam*  
*sacisutamacikarat ka iha bhuri-bhagyodayah*

**The great sages among the demigods, unacquainted with the sweetness of Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet, become burdened with the unjustifiable pride of thinking, ‘ I am a MahaPurusa (a great or eminent person)’ Aho! (I say!) Is there anyone more fortunate than he, who instead aspires for the darsan of Sri SaciNandan, the crest jewel that the personified Vedas continually search after?**  
**the banisher of the pride of the sages.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Our esteemed author, feigning little or no recollection of the greatness of GauraBhaktas, who always remain in the shade of the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari, has composed this verse in a mood of regret. Thus he exclaims, kah! Who was that infinitely kind soul that brought Sri SaciNandan GauraHari to meet such a wretched and undeserving person like me? This is most amazing! How did this happen? Only as a result of immense good fortune. Only one blessed with immense good fortune is capable of arranging such a meeting; no one else.

‘Who is SaciNandan?’

He is nigama-cakra-cudacayam- the Supreme Personality, Sri GauraSundar, sought after by the crest jewels of Vedic literature, who nevertheless remain unsuccessful in their search. In front of Him, the pride of knowledge of the demigods and best of sages must bow its head.

‘Which demigods and sages?’

Nijam padambujamajanatam - those who have never perceived the sublime nectar of Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet and who thus arrogantly think themselves very exalted (mahapurusamaninam).

Karika:

*gaurangopasanadarsi yena sa prabaro mahan*  
*bhuribhagyodayah samyak sastrartha vidhi darsakah*

**‘Those who demonstrate the ways and means to serve Sri GauraHari are the best among all devotees since they are realised in the scriptural conclusions and are the bestowers of good fortune.’**

**Purport**

The Upanisads are described here as the head of the transcendental body of the VedaPurusa (personification of the Vedas). The word upanisad is formed by the conjugation of upa (very close to, without a space in between), ni (with certainty) and sad (knowledge): brahmanah upa samipe nisidati anayah ity upanisat- ‘the scripture which helps a sadhaka to attain liberation, and enables him to be in the intimate association of the Lord, is known as upanisad.’

Another meaning of upanisad is upa (close to) and ni (with certainty); sad (to halt, destroy and attain): ‘that education or cultivation of knowledge which definitely halts the living entities’ attachments to, and dependence on, material existence.’ This knowledge destroys the ignorance that makes one falsely identify with this material body. Finally, it helps one to attain to one’s eternal relationship with ParamBrahma, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, united with Him in one’s original spiritual identity. In BhagavadGita this knowledge is known as RajaVidya; in SrimadBhagavatam as RahasyaVidya. The Supreme Personality, Sri Krsna instructs Lord Brahma:

*sri bhagavan uvaca*  
*jnanam parama-guhyam me yad vijnana-samanvitam*  
*sa-rahasyam tad-angam ca grhana gaditam maya*

**The Personality of Godhead said, “Knowledge about Me as described in the scriptures is very confidential, and has to be realized in conjunction with devotional service. The necessary paraphernalia for that process is being explained by me; you may take it up carefully.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**2.9.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.31)**)**

The entire Vedic scriptures have a singular agenda - searching for and proving that the Absolute Truth exists. The Absolute Truth has been defined in the SrimadBhagavatam as the non-dual substance, in three manifestations: Brahman (impersonal aspect), Paramatma (the SuperSoul, all-pervasive aspect of the Lord in the heart) and Bhagavan (the Supreme embodiment of eternality, absolute knowledge and unlimited bliss):

*vadanti tat tattva-vidas tattvam yaj jnanam advayam*  
*brahmeti paramatmeti bhagavan iti sabdyate*

**‘Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth call this nondual substance Brahman, Paramatma or Bhagavan.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatarn** [**1.2.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.11)**)**

Sri Krsna Himself confirms this in BhagavadGita:

*sarvasya caharh hrdi sannivisto mattah smrtir jnanam apohanam ca*  
*vedais ca sarvair aham eva vedyo vedanta-krd veda-vid eva caham*

**‘By all the Vedas I am to be known; indeed I am the compiler of Vedanta, and I am the knower of the Vedas’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**15.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.15)**)**

Those persons, very proud of their knowledge and exalted position in society are not eligible candidates for receiving the Lord’s mercy. They miss the point that real education and cultivation of knowledge are meant to dissipate ignorance and nescience and to give direct perception of the Supreme Lord through the process of self-realisation in devotional service. Otherwise, knowledge, penances, yogic perfection and renunciation - all pose major obstacles on the path of spiritual progress. Someone may say, that aside from devotees who always seek shelter at the Lord’s lotus feet, there are those who are not devotees but who have accepted the different processes for attaining salvation. ‘What happens to them?’

In answer to this question, Lord Brahma and the other demigods said,

*ye 'nye 'ravindaksa vimukta-maninas*  
*tvayy asta-bhavad avisuddha-buddhayah*  
*aruhya krcchrena param padam tatah*  
*patanty adho ’nadrta-yusmad-anghrayah*

**“O lotus-eyed Lord, although non-devotees who accept severe austerities and penances to achieve the highest position may think themselves liberated, their intelligence is impure. They fall down from their position of imagined superiority because they have no regard for your lotus feet.”**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.2.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.32)**)**

The only hope that materially successful persons and mundane scholars have in regard to removing ignorance and arrogance - two of the biggest hindrances on the path of attaining perfection in human life - is to pray for the causeless mercy of the eternal associates of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the most munificent Personality of Godhead.

### Verse 30

*sarva sadhanahino’pi paramascarya vaibhave*  
*gaurange nyastabhavo yah sarvarthapurna eva sah*

**Though deficient in the practice of spiritual discipline, if a person fully offers his heart and intelligence to Sri GaurangaSundar, who is endowed to the fullest extent with awe-inspiring, Divine grandeur - such a person can nevertheless attain KrsnaPrema in full measure.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

This section concludes the glorification of the excellence of GauraBhaktas by proclaiming that only those who have surrendered totally to the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga have singularly attained perfection, not others. If one is sarva-sadhana-hino 'pi- not having performed any fruitive activity, yoga, cultivation of knowledge, renunciation, and so on, but has surrendered body, mind and words at Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet, then he will obtain fully the results of all types of sadhana (spiritual disciplines). Such persons attain the highest perfection of nigudha-gopi-prema, beyond the four perfections of religiosity, wealth, sense gratification and liberation.

‘What is Sri Gauranga like?’

He is paramascaryya-vaibhave- the possessor of the most astonishing and unsurpassable opulence. Since the highest perfection of human aspiration is GopiPrema, his opulence is that he is the distributor of this prema. Those who have surrendered to Sri Gauranga are thus, truly great.

Karika:

*sadhanadi vihlno ’pi gauranga arpita manasah*  
*purusartha siroratnah prema-purnah sa eva hi*

**‘Even without executing any spiritual discipline, those who have offered their minds, hearts and souls to Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet are full recipients of the crest jewel of all human endeavours, GoplPrema.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Lord is the source of both the material and spiritual worlds. Everything emanates from Him, and His opulence and potencies are limitless (BhagavadGlta 10.8). The affairs of the material and spiritual worlds are smoothly conducted by His inconceivable potencies. Thus does he manifest his eternal Goloka pastimes in Gokula (earthly abode of Goloka), simultaneously pervading the multitude of universes with his presence. Without understanding the absolute nature and multifarious potencies of the Supreme Lord and how they work, it is easy to be victimized by deviant philosophies like the Mayavadi concept.

*nа tasya karyam karanam ca vidyate*  
*na tat-samas cabhyadhikas ca drsyate*  
*parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate*  
*svabhaviki jnana-bala-kriya ca*

**‘Narayana, the Supreme Personality of God, is almighty, omnipotent; the possessor of multifarious energies. Therefore he is able to remain in his own abode, supervising and manipulating the entire cosmic manifestation without endeavor through the interaction of the three modes of material nature- sattva-guna, rajo-guna and tamo-guna.'**  
**(SvetasvataraUpanisad (**[**6.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/6.8)**))**

This Supreme Personality, acting as YugaAvatar, descends to earth in every yuga to initiate the prescribed religion for that yuga by eradicating evil-doers and evil concepts that propagate atheism, thus re-establishing the principles of eternal religion (sanatana dharma).

The different religious principles for each yuga are prescribed as follows:

*krte yad dhyayato visnum tretayam yajato makhaih*  
*dvapare paricaryayam kalau tad dhari-kirtanat*

‘Whatever result was obtained in SatyaYuga by meditating on Visnu, in TretaYuga by performing sacrifices, and in DvaparYuga by serving the Lord’s lotus feet, can be obtained in KaliYuga simply by chanting the HareKrsna MahaMantra.’  
(SrimadBhagavatam [12.3.52](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.52))

As YugaAvatar for KaliYuga, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu inaugurated his Sankirtan movement (congregational chanting of the HolyNames of God) as the prescribed religion for this age. He knew that KaliYuga is the age of hypocrisy and quarrel, when human beings have but short lives, warped mentalities, disturbed minds and little or no good fortune; thus He simplified the process of executing religious principles, making it accessible to everyone without consideration of caste, creed, education or other mundane qualities.

*prabhu bale- kahildm ei maha-mantra*  
*iha japa giya sabe kariya nirbandha*  
*iha haite sarva-siddhi haibe sabara*  
*sarvaksan bala ithe vidhi nahi ara*

The Supreme Lord GauraSundar said, “I have told you this MahaMantra. By chanting this mantra with intentness and strong attachment you will attain all perfection. So simply chant this MahaMantra continuously; there is no other method or precept.”  
(Sri CaitanyaBhagavata, MadhyaLila [23.77-78](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-madhya/23.77))

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“To chant Vedic mantras one requires eligibility. One must observe specific rules and regulations. However, no such rules and regulations apply to chanting the MahaMantra, especially when one endeavors to chant all the time. The chanter is sure to acquire all-round perfection, meaning he automatically attains the results of the four aims of mankind (sense enjoyment, wealth, religiosity and liberation). These he naturally shuns due to his development and cultivation of Love of Krsna. Thus by obtaining Love of Krsna, he becomes eligible for attaining complete perfection.”

## PART V - In Censure of those who do not follow Sri Caitanya

### Verse 31

*apyaganya mahapunyamananya saranam hareh*  
*anupasita caitanyamadhanyam manyate matih*

**A person may have executed innumerable pious activities and be single-mindedly surrendered to the Supreme Lord Visnu - but if he does not worship Sri Caitanya, then I consider him most unfortunate.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author exhorts us to denounce the company of those who are antagonistic to Sri KrsnaCaitanya. Beginning with this verse, he castigates these nondevotees in the next fifteen verses. However, one must not wrongly think that he is doing this out of envy or malice. On the contrary, his vilification is for the purpose of making them inclined towards attaining VrajaPrema. Wellwishers of all living entities, such as our venerable author, can never fall victim to envy or any other moral decrepitude. Those who do not worship and serve Sri KrsnaCaitanya are considered to be bereft of virtues and good fortune. The ability to arrive at the right conclusion about reality and truth, after deliberation, is called matih. Thus, {matih) proper intelligence refuses to accept that those who do not worship Sri Caitanya are (dhanya) fortunate.

‘Who are these unfortunate persons?’

They are apyaganya mahapunyam - those who have heaps of piety; and who are ananya saranam hareh- fully surrendered at the lotus feet of Sri Hari as their only refuge. Thus, even the single-minded, surrendered devotees of Sri Hari are not dhanya. What shall we say then of persons who have amassed immense piety? Dhana means wealth (spiritual wealth). So those who are bereft of wealth are adhanya. The greatest wealth is VrajaPrema; those who have attained VrajaPrema are dhanya.

To attain VrajaPrema without worshiping Sri Krsna Caitanya, especially in KaliYuga, is impossible, since He is the only worshipful tattva (First Principle, fundamental truth, reality) for this yuga. This fact was established with scriptural evidences in the first verse of this book.

nana-tantra-vidhanena kalavapi tatha srnu- kindly hear the truth about the worshipful incarnation of KaliYuga.

In the Agamas and in KramaDipika there are detailed instructions how to meditate on Sri GauraGopal with a four-syllable mantra. If anyone sincerely chants this mantra after receiving initiation from a bonafide guru, and accepts full shelter at the lotus feet of Sri KrsnaCaitanya, he can become rich, with the wealth of VrajaPrema.

Karika:

*caitanyopasanam yasya kalau nasti kadacana*  
*ananya hari-bhakto’pi sa dhanyo manyate na hi*

**‘One who has never worshiped Sri Caitanya in KaliYuga, be he an unalloyed devotee of Sri Hari, is not to be considered fortunate, because he is bereft of real spiritual wealth - VrajaPrema.’**

**Purport**

The highest spiritual goal {param purusartha), beyond the four aims of mankind, is love of God - KrsnaPrema. Those who do not worship Sri CaitanyaDeva are considered unfit for attaining the highest goal of devotion- KrsnaPrema.

The jiva, in his original spiritual identity, is an eternal servitor of Sri Krsna. In the BhagavadGita ([15.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.7)), Sri Krsna confirms that the jiva is His eternal fragmental part, but due to conditional life in the form of material attachments (mamata), he is struggling very hard to overcome the urges of the mind and senses. The Supreme Lord’s illusory energy (maya) keeps the jiva in illusion and oblivious to his eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord and the Lord’s multifarious energies. This is all accomplished through the agency of the three modes of material nature and her avarana-atmika-sakti (potency that covers the Absolute Truth) and viksep-atmika-sakti (potency that hurls the jiva into lower life forms).

Only transcendental knowledge, beyond the influences of material nature, is able to destroy nescience and enlighten the jiva regarding his spiritual identity.

Transcendental knowledge (divya-jnana) begins with sambandha-jnana- understanding the jiva ’s eternal relationship to the Supreme Creator Sri Krsna and His multifarious energies. Sambandha-jnana initially reveals Krsna’s Divine opulence (aisvarya), but ultimately His sublime sweetness and enchanting lila (madhurya) - demonstrated in His NaraLila (Divine play enacted in the form of a human being).

To relish spiritual exchanges with the Supreme Lord in the mood of spontaneous devotion (raganuga-bhakti) is only possible when one takes shelter of one of the eternal associates of the Lord in Vraja. If a sadhaka aspires to worship RasaRaj / VrajaRaj Sri Krsna, he must be a rupanuga-bhakta (follower of Srila Rupa Gosvami and the other eternal associates of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu).

Devotees who worship VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna’s partial expansion, Lord Sri Hari (Narayana), and surrender unto His lotus feet, worship Him in aisvarya-jnana (awe and reverence). Thus is He able to reciprocate only in aisvarya-bhava, devoid of madhurya (sublime sweetness and enchantment).

VrajendraNandan Krsna alone is able to fully reciprocate with His devotees in all the different spiritual humours (rasa). This is not possible even for Dvarakadhisa Krsna. Krsna of Vrindaban is the fountainhead of all incarnations, while all His expansions and incarnations are endowed with partial potencies.

*diparcir eva hi dasantaram abhyupetya*  
*dipayate vivrta-hetu-samana-dharma*  
*yas tadrg eva hi ca visnutaya vibhati*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**‘The light of one candle, communicated to other candles, although it burns separately in them, is the same in quality. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda who exhibits Himself equally in the same mobile manner in His various manifestations.’**  
**(BrahmaSamhita** [**46**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/46)**)**

*ramadi-murtisu kala-niyamena tisthan*  
*nanavataram akarod bhuvanesu kintu*  
*krsnah svayam samabhavat paramah, puman yo*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami*

**‘I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who manifested Himself personally as Krsna and the different avataras in the world in the forms of Rama, Nrsimha, Vamana, etc., as His subjective portions.’**  
**(BrahmaSamhita** [**39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/39)**)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“His subjective portions as the avataras, viz., Rama, etc., appear from Vaikuntha and His own form Krsna manifests Himself with Vraja in this world, from Goloka. The underlying sense is that KrsnaCaitanya, identical with Krsna Himself, also brings about by His appearance the direct manifestation of Godhead Himself.”

### Verse 32

*dhigastu brahmaham vadanapariphullan jadamatin*  
*kriyasaktan dhigdhig vikatatapaso dhik ca yaminah*  
*kimetan socamo visayarasa mattannarapasun*  
*na kesancil leso’pyahaha milito gauramadhunah*

**Shame on the gross materialists, so attached to fruitive, ritualistic performances according to the Smrtis; shame on the mystic yogis who perform severe penances, following the eight-fold path of mystic perfection; shame on the impersonalists who utter aham brahmasmi (I am Brahman) - brimming with arrogance, they claim they are liberated, and thus, with blissful countenance, sink deep into meditation upon themselves. All these persons are mad for mundane pleasures devoid of any connection to the Supreme Personality. What sorrow can I express for these beasts in human form? Hai! Alas! (Oh me oh my!) Not one of them has received even a minute particle of the honey-drenched pollen from the lotus feet of Sri GauraSundar.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The impersonalists, fruitive workers, the stringently austere, etc., who couldn’t obtain even a drop of the honey nectar from Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s lotus feet, are severely chastised in this verse. Simply by repeating brahmaham- ‘I am Brahman’, without understanding the real import of the maha-vakya (great saying) - tat-tvam-asi (correct meaning: you belong to Him \[Krsna\]; as His eternal servitor), may make one’s face glow with bliss (vadana pariphullana), nevertheless, these empiric philosophers are condemned for their offensive attitude. Also censured are the kriyasaktan- those who are very attached to ritualistic performances (nitya-naimittika-karma) or fruitive, pious activities recommended in the Vedas. Thus are they known as jada-matin, persons with mundane consciousness, gross materialists. Jada means that which is bereft of consciousness, inert, inanimate, inactive, dull matter. Such persons are incapable of enquiry into Reality, Spiritual Truth; mati - one possessing such a level of consciousness. As they are all engrossed in searching after a flickering hope for mundane, illusory and transitory happiness, they are equally criticised.

Similarly vikata-tapasah- those who perform terrible austerities and severe penances are also berated. Vikat- horrible, grotesque, formidable - to stand, day after day, at midday in the middle of summer, circled by a ring of flames; to stand through the monsoon without shelter; to remain submerged in water up to the neck during the winter; allowing the nails, hair and beard to grow; abstaining from food and water (even bathing); going without sleep; standing with lowered head and upraised arms; and so on. Accompanying these practices are meditation and the chanting of mantras. Yaminah - those who try to control their senses through sensual restraint (yama), vows, rules and regulations (niyama), pranayam (regulation of the breathing) and other aspects of astanga-yoga. Dhik! - Fie on them all! They are all objects of pity and ridicule since they have rejected the nectar of devotion to Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet. Ahaha!- (exclamation of affliction and regret) for the nara-pasun- beasts in human form. Although they have received the rare gift of human life, they remain ignorant of their weal and woe, thus they are not even worthy of grief.

‘Why not?’

Because they are visayarasa-mattan- engrossed in and inebriated from the wine of carnal pleasures. Just as animals are engrossed in eating, sleeping and mating, these men who have no connection to the Supreme Lord and His service, are also engaged in these animalistic activities; so where is the difference between them and the animals? Without the shelter of Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet, everything is useless, including knowledge, devotion and anything else one might come up with.

Karika:

*jnana-karma-tapo-yoga-yamino bhoginasca ye*  
*tan dhig gaura-padambhoja madhu-lesa vivarjjitan*

**‘Fie on them! that they are only engrossed in the cultivation of knowledge, fruitive, ritualistic activities, austerities, yoga, sense restraint, sense gratification and so on, having deprived themselves of even a drop of the honey nectar of Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

Kriyasaktan- ‘attached and eager to perform ritualistic activities like sandhya-vandana (evening prayers)’; therefore, jadamatin- inconscientious in the matter of enquiries into the AbsoluteTruth; engrossed only in the search for ephemeral mundane pleasure. Vikatatapasah- those who practice severe penances like tolerating the hot sun outdoors in summer, the incessant monsoon rains, remaining submerged in water during autumn and winter, not shaving the hair or beard, or cutting the nails; standing continuously with head down and arms raised, going without eating or sleeping, and so on. Yaminah- those who try to subdue the mind and senses through the process of astanga-yoga (eightfold mystic path) and pranayam (regulated breathing).

All the practices mentioned above are indeed endorsed by Vedic injunctions. The Vedas are, described as kalpa-vrksa (wishfulfilling desire trees). Any individual, at any level of spiritual advancement, who approaches these sacred texts with a desire for fulfillment or shelter from inevitable mundane existential dilemmas, will find appropriate guidance to uplift him from lower modes to higher modes and ultimately to the exalted level of pure goodness (visuddha-sattva). This gradual process offers a permanent solution to all problems of life. The Supreme Lord therefore encourages all living entities, whatever their level of consciousness, to take the first step towards perfection by abandoning all such forms of religion and accepting shelter at the lotus feet of Bhagavan Sri Krsna.

*sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekarh saranam vraja*  
*aham tvam sarva-papebhyo moksayisyami mа sucah*

**‘Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear. ’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**18.66**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.66)**)**

The various forms of religion, other than bhakti-yoga, are inadequately equipped to permanently cut the jiva’s shackles, freeing him from the continuous cycle of birth and death.

Liberation from the cycle of birth and death, from the influences of the three modes of material nature, and permanent eradication of mundane identification, is possible only when Sri Mukunda (who awards mukti) gives His sanction. Even when a practitioner attains the level of transcendence - the lofty region beyond the influences of the material modes, and of repeated births - if he does not develop attachment to the Supreme Lord’s lotus feet, he falls back into the quagmire of material existence.

*patanty adho ’nadrta-yusmad-anghrayah*

**‘They fall down from their supreme position \[of imagined superiority\], because they have no regard for the Lord’s lotus feet.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.2.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.32)**) )**

After many births throughout the evolutionary cycle, the living entity finally attains a human birth, most rare indeed. Human birth is meant for self-realisation and self-realisation means to become permanently fixed in our eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord, the creator and maintainer of all animate and inanimate, organic and inorganic existence. Those who do not aspire for dharma, or devotional service to the Supreme Lord, are beasts in human bodies.

### Verse 33

*pasanah parisecito’mrta rasairnaivankurah sambhavet*  
*langulam saramapatervivrnatah syadasya naivarjjavam*  
*hastavunnayata budhah kathamaho dharyam vidhormandalam*  
*sarwam sadhanamastu gaurakarunabhave na bhavotsavah*

**Oh most wise and intelligent among men! A piece of stone watered with nectar can never sprout into a sapling; repeated pulling will not straighten a dog’s tail; nor can one touch the moon, no matter how high he raise his hands. Aho! (I say!)**  
**In the same way, though a practitioner (sadhaka) may perfect different spiritual disciplines (sadhana), without the mercy of Sri GauraCandra he will not be able to participate in his Festival of Love (BhavaMahotsava).**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

All spiritual practices are futile unless one receives the merciful glance of Sri GauraHari.

First addressed, are the scholars - He budhah! - Oh erudite scholars of the scriptures! Even if you are able to follow your specific sadhana (spiritual discipline) to its furthest reaches, in the absence of Sri GauraHari’s grace, there is no chance for you to ever experience the sublime ecstasy that comes from cultivating loving devotion to Sri Krsna in the transcendental mood of the gopis.

For example - pasanah parisecito'mrta rasairnaivainkurah sambhavet - a stone, even if constantly watered with nectar will remain a stone and not sprout at any time. Similarly, langulam saramapatervivrnatah - if a dog’s tail is smeared with fat and repeatedly stretched, it will neve become straight. And simply by hastavunnayata - raising up the hands towards heaven, the moon cannot be captured. So neither can anyone experience the unlimited bliss of VrajaPrema without receiving Sri Gaura Hari’s mercy.

Just as the above attempts - sprouting a stone with nectar, straightening a dog’s tail with fat and catching the moon with raised arms - are futile, so too is the performance of spiritual discipline (sadhana) if not executed in the shelter of Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s lotus feet. Those in contempt of Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet are thus severely reprimanded.

In this verse the actual address is to be understood as He abudhah! - О foolish persons! not ‘learned scholars’, since an intelligent person will not attempt to do the impossible, like sprouting stones, catching the moon from the earth, or straightening dog’s tails.

Karika:

*yatha sri-krsna caitanya karunam antarena vai*  
*sarva sadhana sattve’pi bhava sambhavana na ca*

**‘Without Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s compassion, to experience bhava (the stirrings of DivineLove for Sri Krsna) is not possible, even if one were to practice all the spiritual disciplines.’**

**Purport**

In any material endeavor, even if the following prerequisites are in place - correct working tools, auspicious time, appropriate place, conducive circumstances and a capable performer - success still depends entirely on the Lord’s sanction.

‘O mighty-armed Arjuna, according to Vedanta there are five causes for the accomplishment of all action. Now learn of these from Me.’

*adhisthanam tatha karta karanam ca prthag-vidham*  
*vividhas ca prthak cesta daivam caivatra pancamam*

**‘The place of action \[the body\], the performer, the various senses, the many different kinds of endeavor, and ultimately the Supersoul—these are the five factors of action.’**  
**BhagavadGita (**[**18.13-14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.13)**)**

Success in bhakti-yoga, and in all spiritual activities, depends solely on the Lord’s mercy.

*yesam sa esa bhagavan dayayed anantah*  
*sarvatmanasrita-pado yadi nirvyalikam*  
*te dustaram atitaranti ca deva-mayam*  
*naisam mamaham iti dhih sva-srgala-bhaksye*

**‘Anyone specifically favored by the Supreme Lord as a result of unalloyed surrender to the service of the Lord, can overcome the insurmountable ocean of illusion and can understand Him. However, those who are attached to this body, which is meant to be eaten at the end by dogs and jackals, cannot do so.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam** [**2.7.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.42)**)**

Sri Caitanya appeared in KaliYuga by His causeless mercy to freely distribute KrsnaPrema to everyone, without considering the person’s eligibility or background. Only the Supreme Personality is able to exhibit such unlimited mercy, so dynamically potent that it qualifies the most unqualified person.

### Verse 34

*avatirne gauracandre vistirne premasagare*  
*suprakasita ratnaughe yo dino dina eva sah*

**When the Moon of Gaura appeared, the Ocean of Love {prema) expanded beyond its shores, revealing the most resplendent gems in the form of hearing and chanting Sri Krsna’s Names, along with the other nine kinds of devotional service. In the face of such a wonderful opportunity, those who remained poor (didn’t pick up any of these gems) are the most wretched, unfortunate souls in existence.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya has revealed the most rare spiritual gems- KrsnaNam and KrsnaPrema, their facets shining with splendour and magnificence. Those who are denied these gifts, as a result of their refusal to seek refuge at His lotus feet, are truly poor and destitute.

Just as the rising of the moon does not drive away the paucity of the impoverished, similarly, even with the rising of the Moon of GauraCandra, the spiritually impoverished remain so. Here the word dina (poor) means spiritually impoverished and ignorant.

‘What is this moon, Sri GauraCandra like?’

He is the moon that has vistirne prema-sagara- swelled and expanded the ocean of prema. When the full moon rises, it causes tides and waves in the ocean, exposing its many treasures; similarly, when the Sri GauraMoon arose, the tides in the ocean of prema exposed so many priceless gems lying in its bed.

One may ask, ‘How can the rising moon, that causes tides in the ocean, eradicate indigence (dinata)?

The answer is: suprakasita-ratnaughe... ‘when the GauraMoon appeared, the ocean of prema revealed priceless gems like the nava-vidha-bhakti, nine processes of devotional service: hearing, chanting, remembering, etc., the nine devotional limbs: anubhava, sattvika, vyabhicarl, etc.; priceless spiritual gems comprising the entire range of bhava (transcendental loving sentiments); and especially the priceless gems of the MahaMantra, the HolyNames - HareKrsna HareKrsna KrsnaKrsna HareHare HareRama HareRama RamaRama HareHare.

Another name for the ocean is ratnakara- the repository of priceless gems. Someone staying near the ocean at the time of moonrise, when the ocean reveals its scintillating jewels, due to not being able to identify or recognise these gems, searches instead for silt and scum. Such a foolish person will never rid himself of poverty. Sri GauraCandra has revealed to the world the priceless gem of KrsnaPrema, DivineLove unto Himself, with it’s full field of bhavas, yet those who refuse to take shelter at His lotus feet will never be able to overcome their ignorance. They will remain in the gloom of nescience.

Karika:

*tatah svaprema-jaladhi-ratnam nama vitanvatah*  
*gaurendoh padaratnam yo nasrito mudha eva sah*

**‘Those who refuse to seek the shelter of the jewels of the lotus feet of Sri GauraCandra, who came to distribute the priceless gems of the HolyNames culled from the ocean of His very own prema, are truly foolish and ignorant.’**

**Purport**

*sri prahlada uvdca*  
*sravanam kirtanam visnoh smaranam pada-sevana*  
*arcanam vandanam dasya sakhyam atma-nivedanam*

**Prahlada Maharaj said, “Hearing and chanting about the transcendental HolyNames, Form, Paraphernalia and Pastimes of Lord Visnu, remembering Him, serving the lotus feet of the Lord, offering Him respectful worship with sixteen types of paraphernalia, offering prayers to the Lord, becoming His servant, considering the Lord one’s best friend, and surrendering everything unto Him (in other words, serving Him with body, mind and words) - these nine processes are accepted as pure devotional service.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**7.5.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/5.23)**))**

The goal of Vedic literature is not to become materially rich, powerful and famous, but to attain immortality, knowledge and bliss in the service of the Supreme Lord. The reality of material existence is that everyone is suffering. To solve this problem one must take up devotional service.

**‘Krsna is the central point of attraction (sambandha) in Vedic literature and our service to Him is our main occupation (abhideya). To attain the platform of love of Krsna is life’s ultimate necessity and goal {prayojana).’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**20.134**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/20.134)**)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“The purport of this verse is that the Vedic literatures are indeed authentic scriptures. Whatever is in the Vedas reveals Krsna - either directly or indirectly; in some places as the principal topic, in other places as the subordinate topic. Therefore, when discussing the principle of sambandha, the Vedas point to Krsna alone. Similarly, devotion to Krsna is the real abhidheya principle, and Love of God, KrsnaPrema, is the singular necessity of human life- prayojana- the ultimate objective of the entire Vedic literature.”    (DasaMulaSiksa)

The first business of the conditioned soul seeking spiritual elevation and knowledge is to re-establish his lost and forgotten relationship with God. This stage of development of consciousness is called sraddha (faith), defined by Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj Gosvami as follows:

**‘By rendering transcendental loving service to Krsna one automatically performs all subsidiary activities. This confident, firm faith, favorable to the discharge of devotional service, is called sraddha'**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**22.62**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.62)**)**

After sambandha (initial relationship) follows abhidheya-the direct means to achieve the desired goal within the framework of our eternal relationship to God. Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj Gosvami describes this as follows:

*bhajanera madhye srestha nava-vidha bhakti*  
*‘krsna-prema’,‘krsna’ dite dhare maha-sakti*

**‘Among the ways of executing devotional service, the nine prescribed methods are the best, for these processes have great potency to deliver Krsna and ecstatic love for Him.’**

*tarn madhye sarva-srestha nama-sankirtana*  
*niraparadhe nama laile paya prema-dhana*

**‘Of the nine processes of devotional service, the most important is to always chant the HolyNames of the Lord. If one does so, avoiding the ten kinds of offenses, one very easily obtains the most valuable wealth of love of God.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila** [**4.70-71**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/4.70)**)**

In his purport to this verse, Srila A.C.Bhaktivedanta SvamI Prabhupad reminds us of Srila Jiva Gosvami’s instructions from BhaktiSandharbha (270):

“Chanting the HolyNames is the chief means of attaining Love of God. This chanting, or devotional service, does not depend on any preconditions; on one’s birth in a good family or any other prerequisite. With humility and meekness one attracts the attention of Krsna. That is the verdict of all the Vedas. Therefore, if one becomes very humble and meek, he can easily attain the lotus feet of Krsna in this age of Kali. That is the fulfillment of all great sacrifices, penances and austerities, because when one achieves ecstatic Love of God, he attains the complete perfection of life. Therefore, whatever one does in the execution of devotional service, it must be accompanied with the chanting of the HolyNames of the Lord.”

### Verse 35

*avatirne gauracandre vistarne premasagare*  
*ye na majjanti majjanti te mahanarthasagare*

**The brilliant Full Moon, Sri GauraCandra has arisen out of the shoreless ocean of prema, revealing its reality; yet those who miss the opportunity to bathe therein, only drown themselves instead in an ocean of meaningless absurdity.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The virtuous author stresses the utter spiritual impoverishment of those who do not accept refuge at Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet and who are thus deprived of the transcendental treasure, prema. They are reprimanded for not immersing themselves in this nectarean ocean of prema, only to drown in an ocean of abject folly.

Karika:

*gaura-pada nasritasya premambhodhavamajjanam*  
*kintu nindyatara kharaksaran mutre nimajjati*

**‘Those not sheltered in the sanctuary of the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga have not only missed the opportunity to bathe in the ocean of prema, they are moreover forcibly drowned in a most contemptible bath of the urine of asses.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Lord describes this material world in the BhagavadGita as asasvatam dukhalayam, a non-permanent place of constant suffering. This temporary world is the Supreme Lord’s inferior energy {jada-prakrti) comprised of five gross elements and three subtle elements. The part and parcel of Krsna, jiva-atma is constitutionally pure, but by intimate contact with jada-prakrti it has become polluted. This pollution of consciousness has been described as anartha- unwanted material desires in the heart that pollute the consciousness with pride, hate, envy, lust, greed, anger, desires for profit, distinction, adoration, wealth, etc.

Srila Visvanath Cakravati Thakur has mentioned the four kinds of anarthas in MadhuryaKadambini:

- duskrtottha (anartha as a resultt of sinful1 activities);
- sukrtottha (anartha as a resultt of piouss deeds);
- aparadhottha (anartha as a result of offenses);
- bhaktyuttha (anartha caused by devotional service).

Malefic effects of material attachments, such as envy and anger, are causes of distress, born of sinful activities (duskrti). The craving for temporary sensual pleasures is also a detrimental desire in the heart; an anartha stemming from sukrti (pious activities). Suffering comes from impious deeds, whereas pious deeds facilitate enjoyment of the senses. Some scholars say that sukrtottha anarthas are part of the five causes of distress: envy, pride, anger, ignorance and attachment. Obstacles on the path of pure devotion are caused by aparadhottha anartha (unwanted desires coming from offenses). These offenses refer particularly to nama-aparadha, offences against the HolyName. Bhaktyuttho-anartha is due to offenses committed in execution of devotional service and is known as seva-aparadha. Srila Rupa Gosvami mentions thirty-two seva-aparadhas in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (entering the temple riding in a vehicle or with shoes, not offering obeisances to the Deity in the temple, etc.).

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur enumerates four anarthas in Sri Harinama Cintamani:

1. ignorance or nescience;
2. hankering for temporary and illusory things;
3. weaknesses of the heart and mind;
4. offenses.

These anarthas keep the jiva in the gloom of constant suffering.

1\) ajhana - lack of knowledge of the transcendental nature and identity of the HolyName creates a mist of ignorance that plunges the jiva into darkness. One who is ignorant of Lord Krsna’s supremacy becomes confused and begins to worship demigods. Thus he becomes entangled in the cycle of fruitive action (karma). Persons who haven’t realised the jiva ’s transcendental nature are in material consciousness; thus they are deluded and always in ignorance.

When Lord Caitanya enquired about the glories of the HolyName from Namacarya (preceptor of the HolyName) Srila Haridas Thakur, he enthusiastically replied, “О, I am so fortunate today! My beloved Lord wants to hear about the HolyName from me! One who is in ignorance doesn’t know the spiritual nature of the Name, or Lord Krsna’s supremacy over all. The demigods are Lord Krsna’s servitors; the jiva ’s nature is transcendental; and maya (illusion) is the nature of matter. Anyone who understands these truths is freed from the darkness of ignorance and attains enlightenment.”

2\) asattrsna - thirsting for the illusory. This anartha makes one desire things not related to Lord Krsna; the craving for so-called material gains, which are by nature ephemeral.

3\) hrdaya-daurbalyam - propensities of the heart and mind that arise from a condition of spiritual weakness (old bad habits, etc.).

4\) aparadha - offenses, as mentioned above.

These four anarthas are to be avoided, for they create a cloud that hides the sun of the HolyName. The HolyName is always perfect, but namaparadha obfuscates the jiva ’s vision of it.

As long as the jiva is not firmly established in the knowledge of sambandha-tattva, the correct understanding of the relationship between God, His energies and the jiva , he has no chance of eradicating anarthas. Only when he accepts the shelter of a bonafide spiritual master and becomes expert in executing devotional service under his guru’s guidance, do the clouds and mist of anarthas gradually disperse.

In the anvaya (word-for-word) Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Prabhupad explains that an ocean of the urine of asses, or very hot and pungent urine is a simile for the anarthas pratisthasa (desires for name, fame, profit, reputation, honour, adoration and distinction) and kutinati (duplicity, diplomacy, trickery).

### Verse 36

*prasarita-mahaprema-piyusa-rasa-sagare*  
*caitanyacandre prakate yo dino dina eva sah*

**With the rising of the Moon, Sri CaitanyaCandra, the ocean of ambrosial prema rasa expanded in all directions. Those wretched, unfortunate souls who demur to drink this nectar are truly condemned to remain destitute.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Deprived of the ocean of prema, the jivas are thirsty; this in turn makes them restless and wretched. These are symptoms of ignorance; thus such ill-fated souls are here vehemently vilified.

An impecunious person is constantly besieged by thoughts and plans for making money. For him - taking a dip in a cool, serene pool, or enjoying sweet delicacies and refreshing drinks - are dreams beyond his wildest imagination. Even if he travels to a far off land in search of wealth, there also he must give up all luxuries. While travelling, he has to contend with drinking fetid, disgusting water from the roadside.

Similarly, those who are not devotees of Sri GauraHari, due to being bereft of the transcendental wealth of prema, cannot bathe in the ocean of prema nor can they taste the nectar of prema. Their ill fate forces them to search for abominations that bring only unabated misery.

Karika:

*prasarito yeha mahan prakrsta*  
*premnaiva piyusa rasasya sindhuh*  
*janaya tasmin prakate tadanghrim*  
*yo nasrito mudhatarat sa mudhah*

**‘Sri Gauranga expanded the vast nectarean ocean of exalted prema to benedict the entire universe. Those who do not take refuge at His lotus feet are certainly more foolish than the greatest fool.’**

**Purport**

The jiva ’s original spiritual nature prompts him to continually search for happiness in the material world, in spite of his conditioned state. Being constantly thwarted in this attempt, he becomes disillusioned and accepts his wretched position as a permanent sufferer. The jiva ’s position in this materially conditioned state is one of forgetfulness of his true spiritual identity.

Sri Caitanya appeared five hundred years ago in the holy land of Navadvip, to dispense prema to every living being without discrimination, through the method of sankirtan. The jivas who embrace distress and deprivation as their lifelong companions, continue to wallow in the mire of material existence and thus miss this golden opportunity.

The jiva has by choice brought upon himself his incarceration in the prison house of material existence. In his desperate search for happiness, he turns his back to the Supreme Lord, the perennial spring of eternal bliss, and instead searches for satisfaction with his mundane senses, mind, intelligence and false ego, in the transient world of illusory existence. This close and intimate contact with the Supreme Lord’s illusory potency is the root of the jivas’ sufferings.

*bhayam dvitiyabhinivesatah syad*  
*isad apetasya viparyayo ’smrtih*  
*tan-mayayato budha abhajet tam*  
*bhaktyaikayesam gurn-devatatma*

‘Fear arises when a living entity misidentifies himself as the material body, because of absorption in the external, illusory energy of the Lord. When the living entity thus turns away from the Supreme Lord, he also forgets his constitutional position as a servant of the Lord. This bewildering, fearful condition is effected by the potency of illusion, called maya. Therefore, an intelligent person should engage unflinchingly in the unalloyed devotional service of the Lord, under the guidance of a bonafide spiritual master, whom he should accept as his worshipful Deity and his very life and soul.’  
(SrimadBhagavatam [11.2.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.37))

As soon as the embodied jiva takes up chanting the HolyNames his consciousness begins to clear and free itself from material contamination. Good fortune comes his way and distress is reduced. He regains transcendental knowledge and the ocean of bliss expands increasingly as confirmed by Sri Caitanya Himself in the first verse of Sri Siksastaka:

*anandambudhi-vardhanam prati-padam purnamrtasvadanam*

**‘The chanting of the HolyNames of Krsna expands the blissful ocean of transcendental life.’**

### Verse 37

*acaitanyam-idam visvam yadi caitanyamisvaram*  
*na viduh sarva-sastra-jna hyapi bhramyanti te janah*

**The greatest amongst scholars, though they be adept in numerous scriptures, if unaware of Sri Caitanya’s position as the SupremeController of all universes (material and spiritual), must continue to wander throughout this lifeless, inert world, devoid of consciousness (caitanya).**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Those who fail to perceive Sri Caitanya as the Supreme Personality, though they may be great scholars knowledgeable in all the scriptures, are nevertheless condemned to perpetually continue their wanderings throughout the continuous cycle of birth and death in this material world, characterized by a lack of consciousness.

**Purport**

Jivas who are forced by their own karma to remain in this material world must suffer the pangs of threefold distress (adhyatmik, adhibhautik and adhidaivik), the miseries of birth, disease, old age and death and constant attacks by the three material modes. Pious deeds elevate one to heavenly planets and impious work degrades one to hellish suffering. However, from the highest planet to the lowest, this material creation is a place of untold suffering. Thus the jiva ’s real freedom from suffering comes in the form of liberation from this material world; in entry into the eternal, spiritual abode of the Supreme Lord.

Any pursuit, whether of knowledge or of any other discipline, must have as its goal the desire to transcend the mundane plane of miseries and enter sublime spiritual space, totally devoid of any fear, death or anxiety. SrimadBhagavatam ([4.29.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.49)) has aptly defined the goal of education and knowledge as: sa vidya tan-matir yaya- ‘real knowledge’ is that realisation which increases our attachment for the Supreme Lord. Erudition, scholasticism, and the like, are indeed laudable qualities, but if any branch of knowledge does not bring the seeker closer to the Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, then it is simply a matter of so much useless labor.

*dharmah svanusthitah pumsam visvaksena-kathasu yah*  
*notpadayed yadi ratim srama eva hi kevalam*

**‘The occupational activities a man performs according to his own position are so much useless labour if they do not provoke attraction for the message of the Personality of Godhead.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam** [**1.2.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.8)**)**

Vedic literature is the crest jewel in the diadem of the scriptures of the world, since it comprises direct revelations regarding the AbsoluteTruth, compiled by the fountainhead of the AbsoluteTruth, Sri Krsna Himself. Sri Krsna states in BhagavadGita that the whole purpose of the Vedas is to know Him. The central purpose of studying scriptures is to realize God, the compiler of the scriptures (BhagavadGita [7.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.24)). Simply scrutinizing the sacred texts without realising the quintessential conclusions, is like the washerman’s donkey who carries a huge load of laundry (compared to information gleaned from the scriptures) throughout his life and in return gets only to munch on some dry grass. Lord Brahma therefore warns us about the dangers of becoming enamored by knowledge and erudition while neglecting devotional service - vedesu durlabham...

**I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is inaccessible to the Vedas, but obtainable by pure unalloyed devotion of the soul, who is without a second, who is not subject to decay, is without a beginning, whose form is endless, who is the beginning, and the eternal Purusa; yet He is a person possessing the beauty of blooming youth.**  
**(BrahmaSamhita (**[**5.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/33)**))**

In his Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta, Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj Gosvami recounts a spiritual dialogue that took place between Sri Caitanya and Srila Ramananda Ray on the banks of the sacred Godavari River. The dialogue is in the form of a question and answer session. Sri Caitanya poses the most important questions a conditioned human being must ask if he desires liberation from the cycle of birth and death and the attainment of prema. Lord GauraSundar enquires about the ultimate goal of human life {sadhya-sadhan tattva) and Ray Ramananda replies by citing verses from the different scriptures that establish bhakti to the Supreme Lord Visnu as the summum bonum of all human aspirations. Initially, Lord GauraSundar rejected Sri Ray Mahasoy’s answers because they did not espouse unalloyed devotion. Finally He acquiesced when bhakti, devoid of jnana (the pursuit of knowledge) and karma (fruitive activities) was postulated as the ultimate goal. In Vaisnava etymology, as explained by Srila Jiva Gosvami, the word jnana denotes sambandha jnana, knowledge of the eternal relationship between the Supreme Lord, his multifarious energies and the jiva - not the pursuit of knowledge for the sake of knowledge. Srila Ramananda Ray quoted the following verse to illustrate this point:

*jnane prayasam udapdsya namanta eva*  
*jivanti san-mukharitam bhavadiya-vartam*  
*sthane sthitah sruti-gatam tanu-van-manobhir*  
*ye prayaso jila jito ’py asi tais tri-lokyam*

**‘Those who, even while remaining situated in their established social positions, throw away the process of speculative knowledge and with their body, words and mind offer all respects to descriptions of Your personality and activities, dedicating their lives to these narrations, which are vibrated by You personally and by Your pure devotees, certainly conquer Your Lordship, although You are otherwise unconquerable by anyone within the three worlds.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam** [**10.14.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.3)**)**

Thus, pure bhakti begins with the execution of devotional service enlightened with sambandha jnana, without which all activities, including chanting the HolyName, worshiping the Deity in the temple, etc., are merely mundane, pious deeds.

### Verse 38

*svadam svadam madhurimabharam sviya namavalinam*  
*madam madam kimapi vivasibhutavisrastagatrah*  
*barambaram vrajapati gunan gaya-gayeti jalpan*  
*gauro drstah sakrdapi na yairdughata tesu bhaktih*

**Always absorbed in chanting HareKrsna, relishing the Divine, nectarean taste of His own HolyNames, Lord GauraSundar becomes intoxicated with ever-increasing, rapturous passion. Sometimes He swoons, falling to the ground in a display of ineffable exultation. The Lord invites everyone, repeatedly encouraging them to sing the wonderful qualities of Sri Krsna, the Prince of Vraja; but for those who have never seen, or perceived in meditation, if for only a brief flash, the most resplendent GauraHari, for them, the attainment of prema bhakti is next to impossible.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Those who have never experienced the nectar of the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari, continuously immersed in the spiritual sentiments of Srimati Radhika, are doomed to perdition. For them the path of pure devotion to the Supreme Lord is unattainable. For those who have never had darsan of Sri GauraHari, bhakti is impossible to realize.

‘What is Sri GauraHari like?’

He constantly relishes the nectar of His own HolyNames by incessantly chanting the Hare Krsna MahaMantra. Intoxicated by this beverage, He sometimes falls to the ground in a swoon, sometimes He is paralysed, and at other times He repeatedly insists that others glorify the qualities of the Prince of Vraja, Sri Krsna.

Why make bhakti difficult to attain for oneself? - those who do so can only be condemned.

Karika:

*svanama-madhumattasya gaurasya padapadmayoh*  
*mahimananubhutesu haribhaktih kadapi nah*

**‘Those who have failed to perceive the Divine glories of the lotus feet of Sri Gaurariga, who is mad after relishing the honey-sweet nectar of His own HolyNames, can never develop pure bhakti.'**

**Purport**

From the time of His birth, Nimai (Sri GauraSundar) inspired everyone to chant the Supreme Lord's HolyNames. The babe appeared just as the moon came out of total eclipse. At this auspicious moment, amongst tumultuous chanting of Vedic Mantras and the Lord’s HolyNames, the child Nimai was born. As soon as the ladies taking care of Him chanted Krsna’s HolyNames, the baby would stop crying. This became a secret game the ladies loved to play with Nimai.

Later, after Nimai (Visvambhar) returned from Gaya, having performed the last rites for his departed father, Sri Jagannath Misra, and having received formal spiritual initiation from his guru, Sri Isvara Puri, he embarked on his mission of propagating the Sankirtan movement, the prescribed religion for KaliYuga. During the eighteen years He traveled throughout India as a sannyasi, Sri KrsnaCaitanya once passed though the JhariKhanda forest. There, He instigated even the most ferocious beasts to chant the HolyNames and dance in ecstasy. All these activities were possible because they were performed by the Supreme Lord. Even the most powerful yogis, what to speak of ordinary mortals, cannot imitate such wonderful pastimes. Sri GauraSundar is non-different in every aspect from Lord Sri Krsna. Sri Gauranga is the YugaAvatar, the bonafide incarnation of Godhead for KaliYuga as predicted in the revealed scriptures. As a part of his transcendental pastimes, he does not reveal his Divinity as an incarnation, but acts from the role of a pure devotee. Hence he is constantly chanting his own HolyNames. He is the best example of a perfect devotee.

*channah kalau yad abhavas tri-yugo 'tha sa tvam*

**‘In the age of Kali, however, you do not assert yourself as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore you are known as TriYuga, or the Lord who appears in three yugas.'**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam** [**7.9.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/9.38)**)**

A pure devotee of the Supreme Lord is always engaged in hearing and chanting the Lord's HolyNames, describing His Beauty, Qualities, Pastimes and so on. Such a devotee inspires everyone around him to also do the same. The pure devotee never thinks about his own salvation because he is jivanmukta, a liberated saint, present in the material world to guide embodied souls out of the quagmire of suffering and illusion. Lord Krsna tells Arjuna in the BhagavadGita that the devotee who propagates the science of bhakti is very dear to Him. So Sri GauraSundar, enacting the role of a pure devotee, not only propagated this infallible process but also displayed the different ecstatic symptoms a pure devotee experiences in the rarefied realms of bhava and prema.

### Verse 39

*vina bijam kim nanikurajananamandho’pi na katham*  
*prapasyenno pangurgirisikharamarohati katham*  
*yadi sri caitanye harirasamayascarya vibhave-*  
*‘pyabhaktanam bhavi kathamapi parapremarabhasah*

**Why shouldn’t there be a sprout without a seed? or a blind man who can see? or a lame man climbing to the crest of a mountain range? if it is possible that someone can obtain Sri KrsnaPrema on his own, without worshiping Sri Caitanya, endowed with the most dazzling wealth - the mellows of his love for Sri Hari?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may argue, ‘How can the respected author be so sure, that if someone does not worship Sri Caitanya, then he cannot attain prema-bhakti? - since it is not difficult to develop prema-bhakti if one takes initiation from a guru and executes the process of hearing, chanting, etc. under his guidance.'

As a rebuttal, the author demonstrates in no uncertain terms that prema-bhakti is extremely rare; equally strong is the castigation of those who turn their backs on Sri Caitanya. Somehow, if there was a possibility, however bleak, for those who are not devotees of Sri KrsnaCaitanya to develop prema for the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna, then another likely question would be - vina bijam kim nankura- Sprouts without seeds? Why not?

Answering a question with another question, one may insist on knowing how it will be possible for someone to obtain prema by receiving Sri Caitanya’s mercy?

In reply: Sri Govinda, imbued with the sentiments of Srimati Radhika, personally relishes, without cessation, his own most extraordinary prema-rasa, and simultaneously exhibits his most wonderful influence as Sri Gauranga. He disburses the same to everyone, without considering whether the recipient is fallen or not. Thus prema-rasa is obtained solely on the merit of receiving Sri Caitanya’s Divine grace.

One may postulate that the Cat’sEye gem is found beneath the earth’s surface and may very well sprout at some given time, hence, why are there no exceptions regarding the attainment of prema? To refute this, a second example is presented: Exceptions do not apply to every rule, just as a person blind from birth will never be able to see in the normal course of affairs. One may further argue that by proper hearing and remembering even a blind person may develop enough perception to gain the result of partial vision. To counter this speculation, it is said, that in the same way a maimed or lame person cannot climb the highest mountain peak on his own strength, the blind remain blind. In conclusion, just as a sapling cannot sprout without a seed, the blind cannot see and the lame cannot climb mountain peaks, similarly, a person without the shelter of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet cannot develop prema or relish prema-rasa.

Karika:

*abijad ankuro’ndhasy eksa pangor giri langhanam*  
*na yatha na tatha gaura-abhaktasya prema lambhanam*

**‘Just as a sapling cannot sprout without a seed, the blind cannot see and the lame cannot climb mountains, similarly a person who is not a devotee of Sri Gauranga cannot obtain prema.'**

**Purport**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya is the YugaAvatar who has advented in KaliYuga to establish the yuga-dharma, or prescribed religion for this age. The religion for the age of Kali is chanting of the HolyNames of the Supreme Lord. This fact is supported by the revealed scriptures. As the Supreme Controller of the universe, the Supreme Lord chooses the identity of his incarnation and the dharma for each yuga (era), specifically according to the nature of the human beings of each age.

At the onset of KaliYuga, thousands of sages assembled in the sacred forest of Naimisaranya, the epicentre of this world, to perform a yajna (sacrifice) to usher in peace and spiritual prosperity for the residents of MotherEarth. These self-realized souls were aware that KaliYuga, last in the cycle of the four yugas, is the most degraded. Religious culture will be on the wane and sinful activities will become rampant. The assembled sages enquired of Sri Suta Gosvami, the most learned amongst them, regarding the most efficacious religious practice recommended for this age. KaliYuga is symptomised by the short duration of men’s lives; their quarrelsome and lazy nature; the fact that they are always misguided; their unfortunate fate; and problems with mental disturbance (SrimadBhagavatam [1.1.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.10)). In the next verse ([1.1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.11)), the sages reiterate the problems to be faced in formulating a befitting methodology for this age:

“There are many varieties of scriptures and in each of them many religious duties and practices have been recommended. To study all of them is time consuming; thus, impossible for the citizens of KaliYuga. Therefore, О learned sage (Suta Gosvami), kindly present the essence of all these scriptures for the benefit of human society.”

**One among the numerous purposes achieved by Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s incarnation, was to establish the yuga-dharma - the prescribed religious practice for KaliYuga - chanting Krsna’s Names without committing offense. This means that other religious practices, also glorified in the scriptures, are not really meant for this age, as confirmed in the (BrhadNaradiyaPurana 3.8.126):**

*harer nama barer nama barer namaiva kevalam*  
*kalau nasty eva nasty eva nasty eva gatir anyatha*

**‘In this age of quarrel and hypocrisy, the only means of deliverance is the chanting of the HolyNames of the Lord. There is no other way; no other way; no other way.’**

The import of thrice repeating nasty eva (‘indeed, no other way’), forcefully stresses that no other spiritual process is efficacious in KaliYuga. The processes prescribed in previous yugas (Satya, Treta, Dvapar) are also not applicable in this yuga for attaining the ultimate spiritual goal. The paramount importance and necessity of following the instructions of Sri KrsnaCaitanya is thus highlighted in this verse. Narrations of the Divine character and extraordinary activities of Sri Caitanya, as well as the immensely purifying potency of the HolyNames of God - Krsna (Sri KrsnaCaitanya) - when taken shelter of, provide the perfect means for the conditioned souls lost in illusion and drowning in the ocean of faults, to obtain the highest spiritual realisation. Sri KrsnaCaitanya introduced the process of chanting so that the jivas can utilize the rare human birth to end the vicious cycle of repeated births and attain the most precious spiritual endowment from the Supreme Lord -the matchless gift of prema-bhakti. However, this gift can be achieved only by following Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s instruction of chanting the HolyName regularly, without committing offenses and in a humble state of mind. In the absence of this, no one in KaliYuga can attain liberation.

*kaler dosa-nidhe rajann asti hy eko mahan gunah*  
*kirtanad eva krsnasya mukta-sangah param vrajet*

**‘My dear king, although KaliYuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age - simply by chanting the Hare Krsna MahaMantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam** [**12.3.51**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.51)**)**

### Verse 40

*alaukikya premonmadarasa-vilasaprathanaya*  
*na yah sri govindanucara-sacivesvesu kritisu*  
*mahascarya premotsavamapi hathatdatari na yan*  
*matirgaure saksat para iha sa mudho narapasuh*

**Even if a person is not the most fortunate soul to be an associate (parsad) of SriSri RadhaMadhava, assisting the DivineCouple in their eternal pastimes, all the same, Sri GauraSundar can suddenly reward one with the wonderful experience of sublime exultation, wherein one relishes ecstatic emotions churned in the most extraordinary fashion from the ocean of prema, Sri Gauranga’s unending Festival of Love (Premotsava). Hence, those who are not favorably disposed toward Sri GauraSundar are truly foolish rascals - beasts in human form.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Although very wretched and fallen, caught in the heaving and swelling waves of the ocean of material distress, without a shelter in any port, those who, in spite of everything, refuse to take refuge of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya, bestower of the highest bliss of prema, thinking Him to be an ordinary mortal, are berated as beasts in human form. Persons in this world who have not developed devotion and affection for Sri Gauranga, the fountainhead of all incarnations, are indeed two-legged animals; this is the scriptural conclusion (dvi-pada pasu). They are all in the grip of illusion, and are therefore designated as mudhahs (dolts, asses).

Someone might ask. 'Why must one surrender to Sri Gauranga?'

He is esu- only a moment’s association with him, or even a mere glimpse of him, makes one relish the nectar of his Divine lila and infuse one’s heart with the supremely wonderful bliss of prema. He is the Supreme Personality, Sri Caitanya.

‘Who are these fortunate souls that have received such Divine grace?’

They are- na yah sri-govindanucara- though not the eternal associates of SriSri RadhaGovinda, they are nevertheless -krtesu- most pious and fortunate, since Sri Gauranga bestows prema upon them.

‘How is this accomplished by Sri Gauranga?’

Premonmadarasa- the rasa generated by prema evokes intense exultation bordering on madness; this rasa He sprinkles upon the fallen souls. This effulgent spiritual gem -GopiPrema- was revealed by Sri GauraHari and distributed to his beloved followers. However, the disbursement of GopiPrema is alaukika- not performed in this loka (planet); not in this realm, but in the transcendental plane. Thus, those who have not reached the stage of surrender to the Supreme Personality, whose faith is not fully anchored in the Truth that Sri GauraSundar is the only worshipful Supreme Lord in KaliYuga, are indeed two-legged animals. Mudha means ‘who lacks specific knowledge’ (stupid, foolish, ignorant, infatuated); so they are called beasts in human form, since such so-called humans do not search for any higher meaning or purpose in life beyond eating, sleeping, mating and defending.

Karika:

*bhaktesu nasti tasmai yo’dadat prema-vilasatah*  
*premotsavam tatra gaure yan matir na pasuh sa hi*

**‘The devotees are always pining for that person who is constantly absorbed in His pleasure pastime of giving the ecstatic madness of prema to whomever will accept it. Who but a gross animal could fail to be attracted by Sri GauraHari, ecstatic in the midst of this Festival of Love?'**

**Purport**

An associate of SriSri RadhaKrsna must necessarily be an eternally liberated, pure devotee. The DivineCouple are always assisted in their lila only by these fortunate souls who have attained the ultimate perfection of KrsnaPrema. These highly exalted personalities are forever imbued with devotional emotions arising from loving exchanges with their Divine Objects of love, SriSri RadhaKrsna. However, Sri GauraSundar is the most munificent avatar, since it is that He rewards the fallen souls with the goal of their loftiest spiritual aspirations -Divine exultation experienced in the mature stage of prema.

In a pastime {lila) described by Srila Vrndavan das Thakur in Sri CaitanyaBhagavat, MadhyaLila (Chap. [22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-madhya/1.22)), Sri Visvambhar sits down on Lord Narayana’s throne and begins to speak about the purpose of his advent, declaring that He has incarnated to freely distribute prema-bhakti to one and all.

**‘One day Sri GauraSundar sat on the throne of Lord Visnu, placing the salagrama-silas in his lap. He exclaimed, “I am Krsna; I am Narayana, the Supreme Godhead; I am Lord RamCandra, the very same person who bridged the ocean. I was lying on the ocean of milk when Nara’s (Sri Advaita’s) thunderous calls woke Me. I have appeared in KaliYuga to distribute prema-bhakti to one and all - so you, Advaita, and you, Srinivas, ask and you shall receive.”**

**‘As Sri Gauranga was freely disbursing love of Krsna, everyone begged for it on behalf of their beloved ones. One devotee pleaded, “kindly reform my wayward, unrighteous father, by rewarding him with bhakti-yoga, so that I may perform my devotional service without hindrance.” In this way, the devotees solicited the Lord to reward prema-bhakti to their guru, or disciple, son or wife, and so on. Sri Visvambhar, who always upholds the words of his devotees, smilingly blessed everyone with the boon of prema-bhakti.'**  
**(Sri CaitanyaBhagavat. MadhyaLila (Chap.** [**22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-madhya/1.22)**))**

In this pastime, the Lord rewarded everyone, eligible and ineligible, with the gift of KrsnaPrema. Only Sri GauraSundar can accomplish this, since He is the Supreme Autocrat, the topmost Independent Personality. No rules can bind him. However, as Sri Krsna says in the BhagavadGita, if He would neglect his duties and not adhere to rules, the entire creation would fall apart.

**‘Sri Caitanya has freely given love of Krsna to everyone, everywhere; even to sinful and fallen persons like Jagai and Madhai - to say nothing of the righteous. Although KrsnaPrema is the most precious and profound spiritual treasure, Sri Caitanya, the Supremely Independent Personality, rewarded anyone and everyone He fancied with this rare gift, simply due to his sweet will. ’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta, AdiLila (**[**8.20-2l**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/8.20)**))**

### Verse 41

*asankhyah srutyadau bhagavadavatara nigaditah*  
*prabhavam kah sambhavayatu paramesaditaratah*  
*kimanyat svapresthe kati kati satam napyanubhavas*  
*tathapi sri gaure hari hari na mudha haridhiyah*

**In countless scriptures the innumerable incarnations of Godhead have all been mentioned. Other than the SupremeController of all controllers, Sri Paramesvar, where is it possible to find such majesty, such splendor and dignity, as is found in Sri KrsnaCaitanya? What more is there to say? Have not his most dedicated devotees perceived in their dearmost his unparalleled influence? Hari! Hari! In spite of this, the foolish rascals cannot recognize him as Sri Hari, He (Sri GauraHari) who is Himself absorbed in chanting ‘Hari! Hari!’**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Although details of countless incarnations of Godhead and their activities are described in the Sruti and other scriptures, not a single incarnation was ever observed to be so generous in making everyone, down to the lowest, relish the sublime ambrosia of His own prema. Thus those who cannot develop enough faith and understanding to worship that munificent person as the Supreme Personality are severely criticized for being so stolid (mudha). The potency and power exhibited by Sri GauraSundar are found only in the SupremeController, not elsewhere. What more is there to say? Those saintly devotees who have realized that the dearmost Lord of their heart, Sri Krsna has appeared as Sri Gauranga, have witnessed in him an abundance of wonderful and extraordinary spiritual influence. However, the unfortunate souls cannot perceive Sri GauraSundar as the Supreme Lord.

‘One may question, why is it so?’

Why do they fail to realize the obvious truth? Because they are mudhas- their consciousness and intelligence are enveloped by illusion. Hence, out of deep sorrow for them, we exclaim-‘Hari! Hari!’

*avatara hy asankhyeyd hareh sattva-nidher dvijah*  
*yathavidasinah kulyah sarasah syuh sahasrasah*

**‘O brahmanas, the incarnations of the Lord are innumerable, like rivulets flowing from inexhaustible sources of water.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.3.26**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.26)**))**

Now, one may ask for proof of Sri GauraSundara’s power and influence. His Divine potency was unequivocally revealed when He delivered Jagai and Madhai, the brahmana leper, Srivasa’s Mohammedan tailor, and many others. Again, when He manifested his sadabhuja-murti (six-armed form), He revealed His Divine potency. The crest jewel among scholars, Sri Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya thus experienced the immense impact of such Divine potency and composed (now famous) verses in His glorification:

*vairagya-vidya-nija-bhakti-yoga-*  
*siksartham ekah purusah puranah*  
*sri-krsna-caitanya-sarira-dhari*  
*krpambudhir yas tam aham prapadye*

*kalan nastam bhakti-yogam nijam*  
*yah praduskarttum krsna-caitanya nama*  
*avirbhutas tasya padaravinde*  
*gadham gadham liyatam citta bhrngah*

**“Let me take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, who has descended in the form of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu to teach us real knowledge, devotional service to Himself, detachment from matter and attachment to everything connected to Sri Krsna. He incarnated because He is an ocean of causeless mercy. Let me surrender unto His lotus feet.”**  
**“By the influence of time, the process of bhakti-yoga was almost lost, so to resurrect this eternal process, He advented as Sri KrsnaCaitanya. Let the bumblebee of my mind be always absorbed in the nectar of His lotus feet.”**

So many noble-hearted, high-spirited souls have perceived Sri GauraHari’s Supreme Divinity, his ability to attract the hearts and minds of everyone, and his absorption in tasting the nectar of his own prema. Yet those who are mudha cannot recognise Sri GauraHari as the Supreme Personality. Only that they might one day obtain a particle of his mercy, have these statements been uttered.

Karika:

*ару aganyavataranam satdm apy anubhutata*  
*prabhavo yasya tasmims ca mudhanam haridhirna hi*
