**‘The Supreme Lord has countless incarnations, but from among these the saintly devotees perceive Sr! GauraHari as one endowed with unique and unprecedented spiritual influence, due to his freely distributing prema. Only the stolid fools do not recognise Him as the Supreme Lord, Sri Hari.’**

**Purport**

There are many instances wherein Sri GauraHari exhibited His Supreme Divinity to a select few. Srila Krsnadas Kaviraja describes the transcendental form the Lord displayed to Sri Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya, the foremost scholar and royal priest of Maharaja PratapRudra:

**‘To show him mercy, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu allowed him to see His Visnu form. Thus He immediately assumed four hands. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu first showed him His four-handed form and then appeared before him in His original form as Krsna, with a blackish complexion and a flute to His lips.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**6.202-203**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/6.202)**)**

The next chapter of Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta describes Sri Caitanya’s tour of South India. There a brahmana named Vasudev was suffering from severe leprosy for a very long time. He heard about Lord Caitanya’s visit to his village. Desiring to see him, he came to the home of another brahmana, named Kurma, where the Lord was staying. The Lord had, however, already left when Vasudeva arrived at Kurma’s home. He lamented bitterly, how unfortunate and sinful he was to have missed meeting the Lord; crying very loudly, he fell down unconscious. Lord Caitanya immediately appeared before him and embraced him. Vasudeva was immediately cured of his leprosy and his body appeared very beautiful. After instructing Vasudeva to chant the HolyNames, the Lord disappeared.

In Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila, towards the end of the eighth chapter, after an extended question and answer session between Lord Caitanya and Srila Ramananda Ray regarding sadhya-sadhana tattva (tattva- principle; the ultimate goal and the means to achieve it), Lord Caitanya revealed His true identity to Sri Ramananda - the combined form of Sri Krsna (the reservoir of pleasure - RasaRaj) and Sri Radha (the embodiment of the highest ecstatic love - MahaBhava). Seeing this unprecedented form of the Lord, Ramananda fell down in an ecstatic swoon.

*tabe nityananda-svampera agamana*  
*prabhuke miliya paila sad-bhuja-darsana*

**‘Thereafter Nityananda Prabhu arrived in Navadvip. When He met Sri Caitanya, He was shown the six-handed form of the Lord. ’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**17.12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/17.12)**)**

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“The form of sad-bhuja, the six-armed form of Sri GauraSundar, is a representation of three incarnations: Sri RamCandra- holding in his two hands a bow and arrow; Sri Krsna- holding a staff and flute; and Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, who holds a sannyasa staff (danda) and kamandalu{water pot).”

Thus we see that on numerous occasions Lord Gauranga displayed extraordinary pastimes and characteristics to His intimate associates.

### Verse 42

*saksanmoksadikarthan vividhavikrtibhistucchatam darsayantam*  
*premanandam prasute sakalatanubhrtam yasya lila-kataksah*  
*nasau vedesu gudho jagati yadi bhavedisvaro gauracandrastat*  
*prapto’nisavadah siva siva gahane visnumaye namaste*

**Pregnant with the capacity to instill a variety of transcendental transformations and laden with his own ecstatic emotions, the passion of His Divine dalliance, Sri GauraSundara's compassionate glance on the embodied jivas diminishes to insignificance, the stature of the four aims of mankind, up to and including ultimate freedom, moksa (liberation). For those who have tasted this delicacy known as ecstatic prema, where is the necessity for religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation? If Sri GauraCandra is not the SupremeController secretly alluded to in the Vedic scriptures, then the ‘doctrine of night’ is all that remains. Siva! Siva! Propitious auspiciousness! О inscrutable VisnuMaya, our reverential salutations unto you.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri GauraHari’s merciful glance is laden with such ecstatic love, that the four objects of human pursuit (purusartha, moksadikarthan) culminating in final emancipation (liberation-moksa) are rendered ineffectual and insignificant. Yet, for those who cannot perceive Him as the Supreme Personality, there remains only victimization by the illusion of atheism. In this verse, the illusory potency (maya), credited for giving birth to atheism, is ostensibly being offered obeisance, but in reality is being condemned.

If Sri GauraCandra is not the SupremeController, then the entire universe will be plunged into the vortex of voidism. In deep anguish the author cries out, “Siva! Siva! О Propitiousness! Avail yourself. Hail auspiciousness! О VisnuMaya! О illusory potency of the Supreme Lord Visnu, my obeisance unto you. You are truly inscrutable and unfathomable; the AbsoluteTruth is kept hidden within your impenetrable darkness. Your deluding potency is such, that by it’s influence none can recognize Sri GauraHari as the Supreme Being.”

One may question, ‘what is the secret with Sri GauraHari?’

Truly, He is a secret unto Himself - vedesu gudho- who is hidden in the Vedas. His DivinePlay (lila), enacted during his rare visits to this world, is the medium through which He expresses his compassionate glance of love-laden grace. This bliss of prema is unlimitedly variegated, exposing the triviality of ultimate freedom (moksa - liberation), highest of the four (ordinary) goals of human life. Those who are not recipients of Sri Gauranga’s merciful glance, who never worship him and are thus atheists, are doomed to the depths of darkness.

Karika:

*уat karunya kataksa premanandas tucchatam nayet*  
*brahmanandam tamisam yena janantyajaya hatah*

**‘His compassionate glance instantaneously bestows the exultation of prema, shrivelling to insignificance the bliss of Brahman realisation, left in the dark. Those who do not know that Supreme Personality Sri GauraHari, are indeed incapacitated victims of maya, the illusory potency.’**

**Purport**

The voluminous Vedic literature with its corollaries is manifest by Lord Brahma so that human beings might make good use of this exhaustive knowledge to enrich their lives on earth. Yet, the essence of the entire Vedic scriptures is to know the Supreme Personality directly. Described by Srila VedaVyas as a wish-fulfilling desire tree, the Vedas offer advice to all who seek succour from the inevitable onslaughts of material nature, as well as to those who foolishly desire to exploit material nature. The four goals of dharma, artha, каmа and moksa are, in truth, not the highest goals or perfection of human life. The ultimate perfection propounded in the Vedas is KrsnaPrema, since the Supreme Personality Bhagavan Sri Krsna is the summum bonum of everything, the vital principle of life. Lord Sri Krsna replies to Uddhava’s query regarding the purpose and philosophy of the Vedas.

**“In the entire world no one but Me factually understands the confidential purpose of Vedic knowledge. Thus people do not know what the Vedas actually prescribe in the ritualistic injunctions of karma-kanda, the objective of the different formulas of worship found in the upasana-kanda, or that which is elaborately discussed through various hypotheses in the jnana-kanda section of the Vedas. I am the ritualistic sacrifice enjoined by the Vedas, and I am the worshipful Deity. It is I who am presented through various philosophical hypotheses, and it is I alone who am then refuted by philosophical analysis. The transcendental sound vibration thus establishes Me as the essential meaning of all Vedic knowledge. The Vedas, having elaborately analysed all material duality as nothing but My illusory potency, ultimately completely negate this duality and achieve their own satisfaction.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.21.42-43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/21.42)**))**

**‘By all the Vedas I am to be known. I am the compiler of Vedanta, and I am the knower of the Vedas'**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**15.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.15)**)**

These and many other statements from the revealed scriptures prove that prema is the mature fruit of devotion. The other aims and objects of human aspiration are in comparison insignificant, temporary distractions to those who aspire for the highest perfection.

Once, in an assembly of learned scholars, Srila Haridas Thakur, the acarya for chanting the HolyNames, established the fact that mukti (liberation), the most sought-after aspiration, is only a subordinate or subsequent result of chanting the HolyNames in the clearing stage (namabhasa). The primary result obtained from chanting offenselessly is prema. Mukti can be easily obtained from chanting the HolyNames in the stage of namabhasa (a reflection of the PureName). Thus liberation is considered insignificant by those who have taken full shelter of chanting the HolyNames. Although Krsna is ready to offer liberation easily, the unalloyed devotees refuse it, because they experience a much higher pleasure in serving the Supreme Lord in loving devotion.

\*Namabhasa- a glimpse of the light of the HolyName, before its full light is perfectly visible. The namabhasa stage is between that of nama-aparadha, or chanting of the HolyName with offenses, and pure chanting. There are three stages in chanting the HolyName of the Lord. In the first stage, one commits ten kinds of offenses while chanting. In the next stage, namabhasa, the offenses have almost stopped, and one is coming to the platform of pure chanting. In the third stage, when one chants the HareKrsna mantra without offenses, his dormant love for Krsna immediately awakens.

*mriyamano barer nama grnan putropacaritam*  
*ajamilo ’py agad dhama kim uta sraddhaya grnana*

**‘While suffering at the time of death, Ajamila chanted the HolyName of the Lord Narayan. Although the chanting was directed toward his son, he nevertheless returned home, back to Godhead. Therefore, if one faithfully and inoffensively chants the HolyName of the Lord, where is the doubt that he will return to the Spiritual World?’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.2.49**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/2.49)**))**

The Supreme Lord Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu is described in the SrimadBhagavatam as channah avatar- a secret, clandestine incarnation. Hence, He is referred to by Prahlad Maharaja, (who was speaking to Lord NrsimhaDeva) as triyuga - one who appears in three yugas. In KaliYuga he does not assert himself as the Supreme Lord, but remains incognito. In many places in the Vedic scriptures Lord Caitanya’s appearance is referred to only indirectly.

In SvetasvataraUpanisad ([3.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/3.12)) He is described as- mahan prabhur vai purusah - ‘The Supreme Personality becomes the Purusa to initiate the expansion of this cosmos.’ In MundakaUpanisad ([3.1.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/mundaka/3.1.3)) He is described as- rukma-varnam krattaram isam purusam brahma-yonim - ‘One who sees that golden-colored Personality of Godhead, the Supreme Lord, the supreme actor, who is the source of the Supreme Brahman, is liberated.’

In KaliYuga especially, without receiving the merciful glance of Sri GauraSundar, no one can experience the ecstasy of KrsnaPrema, nor can anyone develop a taste for chanting the MahaMantra. The via medium of this glance of compassion is his eternal lila (DivinePlay).

### Verse 43

*dhigastu kulamujjvalam dhigapi vagmitam dhigyaso*  
*dhigadhyayanamakrtim navavayah sriyancastu dhik*  
*dvijatvamapi dhik param vimalamasramadyanca dhik*  
*na cet paricitah kalau prakatagauragopipatih*

**Shame on being born in a high-class, righteous family; shame on oratory skills: shame on fame, study of the Vedas, physical beauty, youthfulness and fortune; shame on brahminical initiation and the development of brahminical qualities; shame on cultivating the pure path of celibacy within the Varnasrama system, and shame on the performance of austerities, sacrifices and yoga. All this is futile without attaining recognition of the incarnation for KaliYuga -Sri GauraKrsna Bhagavan, beloved of the VrajaGopis (GopijanaVallabha). Without immersing oneself in meditation on Him, adoration of Him and worship of Him, then everything, even pious activities, are contemptible.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Though born in an exalted, aristocratic family, if one does not worship Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, then his high birth is actually contemptible. Sri Krsna, lover of the gopis, has accepted Srimati Radhika’s golden complexion and has manifest Himself as Sri Gauranga in KaliYuga. If He is not recognized as the Supreme Lord and worshiped as such, then high birth and mundane qualifications are a disgrace. The address, GopiPati-lord or husband of the cowherd damsels, implies Sri Krsna, beloved of the gopis; yet He is not their lawfully wedded husband (pati). For example, brahmanipati means the brahmani’s paramour (upapati), not her legal husband. Similarly, Sri GauraSundar is the same as Sri Krsna, the upapati of the gopis.

A person may acquire high social status, due to kulam ujjvalam- birth in an exalted family, characterized by proper behaviour and correct etiquette. He may also be vagmitam- an eloquent orator; possess a good reputation, fame; be practised in study of the Vedas: have a charming and attractive appearance, possessed of robust youthfulness and immense wealth. He may have received dvijatva- initiation into gayatri mantra, following vows of celibacy, and engagement in worship and the performance of fire sacrifices, yoga, and renunciation. Nevertheless, if one does not worship Sri GauraCandra, all these activities are accursed; confined to damnation.

Karika:

*kula-vakpatuta veda-patha akrti-bayah sukhan*  
*dhik tesam iha yesam vai na gaura-carane ratih*

**‘High birth, eloquence, charming appearance, robust youthfulness and immense fortune are nothing more than disgraceful for those who have no love or attachment for Sri Gaura’s lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

The cultivation of good qualities and noble human values is indeed a sign of progress on the path of advancement of civilization. In the final consideration, however, these mundane excellences have no real, lasting worth, since inevitable death will ultimately expose their temporary, fleeting nature. The scriptures inform us that a devotee of the Supreme Lord will surely and steadily develop all the finer qualities that ornament such elevated beings as the demigods. Though non-devotees cultivate such respectable qualities, their singular failing is apathy towards the SupremeLord, which will eventually degrade them to lower levels of animal consciousness.

In the SrimadBhagavatam ([11.11. 29-32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/11.29)), Sri Krsna enumerates to Uddhavji the twenty-eight essential symptoms of a sadhu (saintly devotee) such as: mercy, tolerance, truthfulness, pure-heartedness, freedom from lust, sharp intellect, mastery over the senses, gentleness, cleanliness, and the like. However, the most important and indispensable of these qualities is acceptance of the lotus feet of Sri Krsna as one’s only shelter. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

**“In general, qualities can be divided into two categories: svarupa, the direct and indigenous qualities of any substance, and, tatastha-laksana, qualities that are ornamental, visible when a substance comes in contact with something foreign. The sadhu's acceptance of Lord Sri Krsna as his only shelter is his svarup-laksana, all other qualities are tatastha. If by some good fortune, one associates with a Vaisnava, he develops a taste for chanting the HolyNames and takes complete shelter of Krsna’s lotus feet. This way he develops his innate svarup-laksana, then, through continued chanting he gradually develops all other laksanas (symptoms). Though these laksanas are all tatastha, they are essentially present in a Vaisnava.”**  
**(Sri HariNamaCintamani)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“By the Supreme Lord’s sweet will, the Vedic scriptures contain prescriptions and proscriptions invaluable for human society’s spiritual elevation and general weal. When a fortunate soul really understands that all these are, however, ‘tailor-made’ for, and solely applicable in this transient world, and are therefore to be completely discarded, then only can he comprehend that human necessity is encapsulated in the act of rendering loving devotional service to the Supreme Personality. Such a fortunate soul is the best amongst so many sadhus.

“The process of devotional service to the Supreme Lord demands rejection of both desires for sense pleasure (bhoga) and renunciation (tyaga). The Supreme Lord, even when He allows Himself to be captivated, can never be transformed into an object of exploitation. His external energy maya imprisons the jivas in this phenomenal world - by propagating evanescent, non eternal religious principles. When the jiva’s mundane nature (which covers his original identity) gains prominence, it manifests itself as false-ego. Permanent engagement in eternal service is impossible for mundane objects, because the object of service, the servitor and the service itself are subjected to the influences of time, and other circumstances of this material world. When the conditioned jiva considers himself a puppet, completely controlled by time, his identification as the ‘enjoyer’ or ‘renouncer’ forces him into further confusion about his true identity; pushing him deeper into the ‘false-ego syndrome’. Thereafter, he begins to judge everything by mundane standards of good and evil, which in turn distances him further from devotional service to the SupremeLord. Yet, the conditioned jiva believes this to be most beneficial for himself.”

Material progress without spiritual upliftment is a road leading to hellish suffering in the darkness of ignorance. This is poignantly expressed by Queen Kunti in her prayers to the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna:

*janmaisvarya-sruta-sribhir edhamana-madah puman*  
*naivarhaty abhidhatum vai tvam akincana-gocaram*

**‘My Lord, those who are on the path of (material) progress, trying to improve themselves with high birth, opulence, learning and beauty, remain intoxicated by false ego and thus cannot approach you, due to lack of sincere faith. You manifest Yourself only to those who are materially bereft.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.8.26**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.26)**))**

### Verse 44

*aho vaikunthasthairapi ca bhagavatparsdavaraih*  
*saromancam drsta yadanucara vakresvaramukhah*  
*mahascarya premojjvalarasa sadavesa vivasi*  
*krtarigastam gauram kathamakrtapunyah pranayatu*

**Aho! (I say!) Highly elevated rasika devotees of Sri GauraHari, like Vakresvar Pandit, enchanted by the mellows of radiant prema, remain in a state of near paralysis, the intensity of their absorption is so overwhelming. Receiving the darsan of these rasika devotees, even the eternal associates of Lord Narayana in Vaikuntha are overwhelmed and their bodies thrill with rapture, their bodily hairs standing on end. How then can impious persons make Sri GauraSundar, Lord and master of these rasika devotees, the singular object of their affection?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri Gauranga’s devotees are so glorious, that even the eternal residents of Vaikuntha are eager to catch a glimpse of them. In presenting the greatness of GauraBhaktas, the noble author makes a comparison with the nature of those who refuse to take shelter of Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet, revealing their lack of piety.

The question is asked: kathamakrtapunyah pranayatu-‘how can a person, who has not earned any piety, surrender to Sri GauraHari and engage in His loving devotional service?’

This question is then answered with another, ‘who is Sri GauraHari?’

Someone whose eternal associates (parsad - such as Sri Vakresvar Pandit) are ardently sought after by the eternal residents of Vaikuntha, who, upon seeing them, experience ecstatic symptoms like horripilation. Thus do we find the exclamation - Aho! (indicating wonderment).

‘Of what spiritual calibre are these GauraParsada?’

They are mahascarya premojjvalarasa sadavesa- the most exalted. By remaining submerged in that most splendorous of all rasas, their bodies have become anaesthetized.

Those who do not seek shelter of Sri Gauranga, whose devotees alone are the epitome of par-excellence, must surely be bereft of pious deeds and hence, condemnable.

Karika:

*prasamsati paravyoma parsada yat priyan aho*  
*apunyavan katham tasya pada-padmam svamasrayet*

**‘Aho! Sri Gauranga’s beloved devotees are praised even by the eternal residents of Vaikuntha. How can an impious person take shelter of His lotus feet?’**

**Purport**

**“According to the particular devotee, attachment (rati) falls within the five categories of santa-rati, dasya-rati, sakhya-rati, vatsalya-rati and madhurya-rati. These five categories arise from the devotees’ different attachments (rati) to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The transcendental mellows {rasa) derived from devotional service are also of five varieties.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**19.183-184**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.183)**)**

The five types of devotees described here (and in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu) are categorized according to their intimacy with and intensity of love for Krsna - the supreme object of love. Thus the fountainhead of all incarnations and expansions, VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna reveals Himself to His devotees in different transcendental forms and expansions, to fully reciprocate His devotee’s love and affection for Him.

The devotees’ transcendental attachment (rati) for Krsna is of two varieties as mentioned in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila ([19.192-194](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.192)):

**‘Attachment (rati) for Krsna is divided into two categories: One is attachment with awe and reverence (aisvarya-jnana) and the other is pure attachment (kevala), without reverence. Pure attachment without reverence is found in Goloka Vrndavana. Attachment in which awe and reverence are prominent is found in the two capitals, Mathura and Dvaraka, and in Vaikuntha. When awe, reverence and opulence (aisvarya-jnana) are prominent, Love of God (prema) is somewhat crippled. According to kevala devotion, however, even though the devotee sees the unlimited potency (aisvarya) of Krsna, he considers himself equal with Him.’**

Thus the eternal associates of Sri Narayan in Vaikuntha, whose love for their Lord is slightly slackened by awe and veneration (aisvarya-jnana), are naturally impressed and inspired by the free flow of loving sentiments exhibited by the rasika associates of Sri GauraSundar, unencumbered by this aisvarya-jnana. Lord Sri GauraHari advented with His eternal associates (parsad) to assist Him in His sankirtana pastimes. These rasika parsadas - relishers of the radiant ambrosia of prema -were many: SvarupDamodar, VakresvarPandit, GadadharPandit and RayRamananda are but a few of these most elevated transcendental personalities. By their unparalleled devotion and intense love for the Supreme Lord they evoke deep spiritual sentiments that erupt in the hearts of the Vaikuntha residents and thrill their transcendental bodies with ‘goose bumps’ (horripilation; bodily hairs standing on end).

According to GauraGanoddesaDipika, Sri Prabhodhananda Sarasvati was the incarnation of TungaVidya sakhi. Some scholars also accept Srila VakresvarPandit as the incarnation of TungaVidya sakhi, so it is interesting that our esteemed author chose the name of Vakresvar to head the list of principal associates, out of so many companions of Sriman Mahaprabhu.

### Verse 45

*dattva yah kamapi prasadamatha sambhasya smitasrimukham*  
*durat snigdhadrsa niriksya ca mahapremotsavam yacchati*  
*yesam hanta kutarkakarkasadhiya tatrapi natyadarah*  
*saksat purnarasavatarini harau dusta ami kevalam*

**He whose lovely, lustrous face radiates a gentle smile, while his conversation stirs the nectar of his mercy. Even from a distance, his serene, affectionate glance inaugurates a grand Festival of Love (prema). Alas! Argumentative speculators, due to their crude and perverted intellect, do not develop affection for the same, Sri GauraHari, despite the fact that He is directly the incarnation of the full-to-overflowing reservoir of pleasure, billowed by waves of the mellows of prema. All of these hard-hearted polemicists are nothing more than wicked, polluted, mischievous miscreants; gross offenders; truly demoniac atheists.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The Supreme Lord, Sri KrsnaCaitanya is always engaged in freely distributing the sweet nectar of His own prema, out of His infinite compassion. Those who are not affectionate to such a person must certainly be possessed of a coarse and cruel heart. Exposing their demoniac mentality, our esteemed author severely chastises them. Those who possess kutarka karkasa dhiya- a mentality made brutal and cruel by constant polemics and wrangling, are simply mischief-mongers with a demoniac attitude. They can never develop love and attraction for the Supreme Personality Sri GauraHari.

That same Sri GauraHari is purna-rasa-avatarini- the source of all incarnations; the fountainhead of abounding rasa; one who possesses the nature to reveal these mellows of love in all their completeness. Furthermore, Sri GauraHari is yah kamapi prasadam- who bestows unprecedented and ineffable joy to the jivas, smiling benignly upon them. He speaks very endearingly to the jivas, showering compassion with His cooling, protecting glance (durat snigdha-drsa) that awards those upon whom it falls with maha-premotsavam yacchati- a grand festival of love (prema). Those who have not an iota of love for Sri GauraHari are truly wicked.

Karika:

*premotsavam yo dadati sambhasya snigdhaya drsa*  
*tasminnanadaro yesam te dusta bhuvi kevalam*

**‘Sri GauraHari inaugurates a festival of prema with his soothing, compassionate gaze and sweet words. Those who do not have love and respect for him are mischievous miscreants; evil elements in this world.’**

**Purport**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya is the most magnanimous (maha-vadanyaya avatar) of all incarnations of Godhead.

Sri Krsna’s transcendental glance is simultaneously full of compassion, when blessing the conditioned souls, and full of creative potency when impregnating material nature (jada prakrti), which manifests this material cosmos. However, foolish persons cannot comprehend the transcendental nature of the Supreme Lord when He descends in human form. Lord Sri Krsna confirms in the BhagavadGita (4.9), that His appearances and activities are transcendental and have not the slightest trace of mundane influences. To understand this truth, the conditioned jiva must cleanse his consciousness of material contamination that obfuscates his perception of reality and truth. The jiva ’s consciousness remains turbid with the gloom of ignorance, due to continued and intimate contact with material nature. Once the dirt is removed from his consciousness, by constant chanting of the HolyNames of God, he is able to see the reality of his own existence as the Lord’s part and parcel. He thus begins to fathom the truth of his eternal relationship with Krsna as His loving servitor.

Sri Krsna unequivocally describes the nature of those who evade the truth:

*nа mam duskrtino mudhah prapadyante naradhamah*  
*mayayapahrta-jnana asuram bhavam asritah*

**‘Those miscreants who are grossly foolish, the lowest among mankind, whose knowledge is stolen by illusion, and who partake of the atheistic nature of demons, do not surrender unto Me.’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**7.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.15)**)**

*moghasa mogha-karmano mogha-jnana vicetasah*  
*raksasim asurim caiva prakrtim mohinim sritah*

**‘Those who are thus bewildered are attracted by demonic and atheistic views. In that deluded condition, their hopes for liberation, their fruitive activities, and their culture of knowledge are all defeated.’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**9.12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.12)**)**

## PART VI - Self-condemnation in humility

### Verse 46

*vancito’smi vancito’smi vancito’smi na samsayah*  
*visvam gaurarase magnam sparso’pi mama nabhavat*

**Alas! I am deprived, deprived, truly deprived! The entire universe has drowned in the ocean of Sri GauraSundara’s ambrosial love, but, Alas! Not a drop of it has touched me.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Having denounced the non-devotees who cannot surrender to Sri Caitanya, the honoured author, out of humility, feels deep remorse and embarks on a scourge of self-criticism in the following eleven verses. He begins by exposing his own misfortunes- visvam gaura-rase... ‘the entire universe has drowned in the ocean of Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s prema-rasa, but alas, it did not even touch me; I am so thoroughly dismayed with myself.’ This is an example of self-condemnation out of humility.

Karika:

*gauranga prema madhurya rasadharaphitam jagat*  
*mama tat sparsanam nasti vancitasya dhig astu mam*

**“The sweet currents of Sri Gauranga’s nectarean prema-rasa have inundated the entire universe, yet not even a drop has ever touched me. Since I have been deprived of that nectar, I concede my accursed condition.”**

**Purport**

The respected author, Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati Gosvami is one of the foremost among the eternal associates of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. As an elevated Vaisnava, he is garlanded with all the noble qualities that are characteristic of a saintly person. Sri Caitanya has declared that humility is the crown jewel of all Vaisnava characteristics.

In this verse, Srila Prabodhananda exhibits this wonderful Vaisnava trait. However, out of ignorance one must not think that this Vaisnava is truly as wretched as he describes himself to be. If we were to fall prey to such a misconception, then we would end up committing the most serious of the ten offenses against the HolyNames - the ‘mad elephant offense’-

*yadi vaisnava-aparadha uthe hati mata*  
*upade va chinde, tara sukhi ’ уaya pata*

**‘If the devotee commits an offense at the feet of a Vaisnava while cultivating the creeper of devotional service in the material world, his offense is compared to a mad elephant that uproots the creeper and breaks it. In this way the leaves of the creeper dry up.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**19.156**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.156)**)**

Such an offense can uproot and break the creeper of devotion (bhakti-lata) at any stage of one’s spiritual progress.

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu defines unambiguously the symptoms to be developed for chanting the HolyNames constantly:

*trnad api sunicena taror iva sahisnuna*  
*amanina mana-dena kirtaniyah sada harih*

**‘One should chant the HolyName of the Lord in a humble state of mind, thinking oneself lower than the straw in the street; one should be more tolerant than a tree, devoid of all sense of false prestige and ready to offer all respect to others. In such a state of mind one can chant the HolyName of the Lord constantly.’**  
**(Sri Siksastaka)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“The unalloyed Vaisnava who chants offenselessly considers himself lower than the straw in the street that is trampled by the walking masses. A true saint never thinks himself an elevated Vaisnava or claims to be a guru. He always humbly regards himself as a disciple of his guru and the most meek and fallen soul in the world. Knowing every infinitesimal spirit soul as the residence of Lord Sri Krsna, he never mistreats anyone as his inferior. He is not wanting in anything, nor does he require anything from anyone. Even if others are envious and spiteful of him, he does not retaliate; on the contrary, he prays for the well being of his tormentors.”

The exalted Vaisnava and preceptor of the HolyNames, Srila Haridas Thakur begged the Lord to forgive the royal guards enlisted to lash him in twenty-two different market-places. A similar mood of humility was expressed by the great devotee Prahlada Maharaja, when he described himself to Lord NrsimhaDeva as a member of an atheistic family (asura-kula) attached to sensual pleasures. When Lord Narasimha insisted that he accept a boon, Bhakta Prahlada refused to accept anything for himself and instead begged the Lord to forgive his father, the demon Hiranyakasipu, who all along had been always trying to kill him.

### Verse 47

*kairva sarvapumarthamaulirakrtayasairihasadito*  
*nasid gaura padaravindarajasa sprste mahimandale*  
*ha ha dhig mama jivanam dhigapi me vidyam dhigapyasramam*  
*yad daurbhagyabharadaho mama na tatsambandha gandho’pyabhut*

**Is there anyone left in this entire world, touched by the pollen from Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, who has not effortlessly attained the crest-jewel of all the goals among men, namely - KrsnaPrema? Alas! Due to extreme misfortune, I have not received even a faint scent of that prema. Shame on my life, shame on my erudition and shame on my renounced order of sannyasa!**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

With the advent of Sri Caitanya, everyone, including the most fallen and wretched, received the crest jewel amongst all intents in human life - nigudha VrajaPrema. Seeing this, and at the same time considering himself ineligible to receive it, our esteemed author laments his misfortune.

Who in this world, touched by the pollen from the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya as He walked upon this earth, did not receive without any endeavour the best and highest objective - prema? In fact, everyone received it.

Akrtayasaih- to receive something without making an effort (by sadhana, etc.). What they received was sarva pumartha-maulim- according to the Vedas, the four human aspirations or necessities are dharma, artha, kama and moksa (religiosity, wealth, sensual gratification and liberation). Beyond these is the fifth and highest necessity - KrsnaPrema - and everyone received it. But Alas! (Ha! Ha! / Hai! Hai!) living itself has become only a burden. Vidyam (knowledge and study of scriptures) is useless to me now; fie on my sannyasa asrama, the highest order of life. Because of all these concerted misfortunes, I am deprived of even a drop of that prema.

Karika:

*krtavatare gaurange praptah prema-raso janaih*  
*tad gandha-leso mama na dhig vidya-jivanadikam*

**“By the appearance of the most munificent incarnation, Sri Gauranga, everyone obtained a taste of the mellow (rasa) of KrsnaPrema. I, however, did not receive even a whiff, hence my learning, life, and the like, are all futile. Fie on them!”**

**Purport**

The word rajasa- (pollen, dust) has several connotations. In the ultimate sense, it means the unalloyed devotees who have taken complete shelter at the Lord’s lotus feet. They are the via medium through which his mercy is disseminated. Through the Lord’s devotees one is afforded the opportunity of service to the Supreme. This is the principal connotation of feet, or lotus feet - implying a position of servitude - not an enviable position in this material world but the highest position possible in the worlds of transcendence.

Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur comments:

“The single cause that attracts the mercy of the Lord is bhakti,; which permanently resides in the pure devotee’s heart. In other words, Krsna’s mercy will not be invoked without that bhakti within the heart of His devotee, which attracts His mercy to appear in the first place...”  
(Sri MadhuryaKadambini(Firs shower))

Here one may present a counter argument, saying, ‘that since devotees are always under the Lord’s control, how can the devotee’s mercy appear first (independently), and not as a successor to the Lord’s causeless compassion?’

Krsna Himself provides the solution to this problem by openly declaring that He is voluntarily subservient to His pure devotees. The Lord empowers His pure devotees to distribute His mercy as they like. In this way, He broadcasts their super-excellent position.

Simply by their presence, the Lord’s devotees thus sanctify this world, due to the Lord’s constant presence in their hearts; thus can they convert an ordinary place into a place of pilgrimage {SrimadBhagavatam 1.13.10). The followers of Sri GauraSundar, who carry the Lord in their hearts, freely distribute these brilliant gems of prema - the most rare gifts, veiled before the advent of Sri Caitanya.

It is significant that Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati Gosvami condemns his own life. In his humility he feels his life was untouched by prema, due to various misfortunes. He is thus attempting to make the world aware of its existence in the gloom of nescience, steeped in illusion. The initiative to reach out for the Lord’s all-pervasive mercy is everyone’s individual decision. The Lord will never act against the jiva’s inherent free will, His very own gift. The author is ashamed of his erudition, esteemed position in society as a sannyasa, and so on, in the light of the fact that none of these mundane considerations brought him closer to receiving the Lord’s mercy.

### Verse 48

*utsasarpa jagadeva purayan gauracandrakaruna maharnavah*  
*bindumatramapi naptanmahadurbhage mayi kimetadadbhutam*

**The vast, shoreless ocean of Sri GauraCandra’s compassion has flooded the entire universe by its tidal waves. How amazing! that not a single drop falls on this wretched soul.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

‘The ocean of compassion, Sri Gauranga inundated the world with the flood waters of prema, but not a drop of his mercy has touched me since I am unfit to receive it, due to my grevious misfortune.

‘Just as the rising moon creates tides in the ocean and floods the shores, similarly gaura-candra karuna maharnavah- when the moonlike Sri Gauranga appeared, a massive tidal wave was created in the Ocean of Compassion that inundated the entire universe; only I did not receive a drop of that mercy! What a strange incident! How is it possible that the whole earth was flooded, leaving me aside? After all, I am also a part of this world. This is so amazing! What sort of person am I? maha durbhage- extremely unfortunate. I am ill-fated since not even a sprinkle of Sri Gauranga's mercy has touched me.'

Karika:

*jagat plabi daya-sindhoh karuna-lesa hinatah*  
*atmanas ca sudur bhdgyam anumiye’ham adbhutam*

**‘The Ocean of Compassion, Sri Gauranga drowned the world in His mercy. Being deprived of even a drop of that kindness, I can well surmise the extent of my unimaginable, yet extreme misfortune.’**

**Purport**

A Vaisnava’s feeling of humility is never an act of pretension or show. A fully surrendered devotee always thinks he is unqualified to serve the Supreme Lord and in this way depends solely on the mercy of the Lord. Non-devotees cultivate demoniac qualities, and thus have destructive natures, full of pride, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance {BhagavadGita 16.4). They say that this world is unreal, with no foundation, no God in control. They say it is produced of sex desire and has no cause other than lust (16.8).

*isvaro ’ham aham bhogi siddho ’ham balavan sukhi*

**‘I am the Lord of everything, the enjoyer; I am perfect, powerful and happy.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**16.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/16.13)**))**

The Supreme Lord therefore naturally takes care of and protects those who are obedient to His will. To be humble and meek before the Supreme Lord is not a sign of weakness or ignorance. On the contrary, it is a sign of a lofty intellect purified of material contamination (in the form of anarthas).

### Verse 49

*kalah kalirbalina indriya vairivargah*  
*sri bhaktimarga iha kantakakotiruddhah*  
*ha ha yami kva vikalah kimaham karomi*  
*caitanyacandra yadi nadya krpam karosi*

**This is the age of Kali. The senses are very powerful enemies, while the supremely effulgent path of bhakti is shrouded in a network of millions of thorns (in the shape of karma, jnana and the like). Alas! О Sri CaitanyaCandra! If You will not show me Your mercy, then in this completely confused condition, what am I to do? Where shall I go?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Due to the influence of KaliYuga, the enemies of the self - the senses - have become very powerful, while the path of bhakti is practically obstructed, strewn with many thorns. Hence the author seeks shelter of Sri Caitanya; soliciting his mercy with all humility. The instigator of irreligiosity, KaliYuga, is ruling the present time; thus, man’s enemies - the senses - are extremely formidable; each one an adept at drawing the consciousness and intelligence towards the sense objects.

On the other hand, in this KaliYuga, sri bhakti-marga- the radiant and sublime path of devotional service is kantaka-koti ruddha- obstructed by thorny bushes in the shape of fruitive, ritualistic performances, dry, empiric knowledge, polemics, rhetoric, false renunciation, and so on. Under these circumstances, “O CaitanyaCandra! If You do not show me Your mercy, then, confused and confounded by these thorny bushes, I will not know how to find my way, what to do, where to go. Therefore, please guide me.”

Karika:

*kali dosa vidustasya hrsika akula cetasah*  
*mamadya saranam kvapi na syade gaura-krpam vina*

**‘Afflicted by rapacious senses and contaminated by the evil influence of KaliYuga, now that my mind and intelligence have become so agitated and uncontrollable, where can I obtain shelter, without the mercy of Sri GaurangaDeva?’**

**Purport**

The six enemies of the mind are: lust, anger, greed, madness, illusion and envy. Of these, lust and anger are most destructive. The mind is the sixth sense and the master of the other five senses. Thus an uncontrolled mind must necessarily unleash a reign of terror on the consciousness and intellect. This is more pronounced in KaliYuga, since the minds of people in general are always disturbed by the threefold miseries (adhyamika, adbibautika, adhidaivika), the three gunas (sattva, rajas, tamas), a degraded mentality, a short lifespan and continuous misfortunes described vividly in the SrimadBhagavatam, [Twelfth Canto](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12).

However, as Sri Krsna says in BhagavadGita- ‘a controlled mind is man’s best friend’.

‘O twice-born sages, by serving those devotees who are completely freed from all vice, great service is done. By such service, one gains affinity for hearing the messages of Vasudeva.

‘Sri Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramatma \[SuperSoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.

‘By regular attendance in classes on the Bhagavatam and by rendering service to the pure devotee, all that is troublesome to the heart is almost completely destroyed, and loving service unto the Personality of Godhead, who is praised with transcendental songs, is established as an irrevocable fact.

‘As soon as irrevocable loving service is established in the heart, the effects of nature’s modes of passion and ignorance, such as lust, desire and hankering, disappear from the heart. Then the devotee is established in goodness, and he becomes completely happy.

**‘Thus established in the mode of unalloyed goodness, the man whose mind has been enlivened by contact with devotional service to the Lord gains positive scientific knowledge of the Personality of Godhead in the stage of liberation from all material association.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam** [**1.2.16-20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16)**)**

This is the gradual process for extricating the mind and consciousness from the clutches of lust, anger and illusion. By regularly hearing the transcendental activities and glories of the Supreme Lord from saintly persons, all material contamination in the heart and consciousness is removed; thus the consciousness becomes situated in the transcendental state of unalloyed goodness, by contact with devotional service.

Jnana, karma, yoga, vairagya, etc., are referred to in this verse as thorns on the path of bhakti. This is true if these processes are executed separately from devotional service; performed independently of bhakti. Prema, the highest human goal, is the ultimate destination of all living entities. It is achieved only through devotional service. Srila Rupa Gosvami summarises the definition of bhakti - bestower of prema -in the following verse:

*anyabhilasita-sunyam jnana-karmady-anavrtam*  
*anukulyena krsnanu-silanam bhaktir uttama*

‘One should render transcendental loving service to the Supreme Lord Krsna favorably and without desire for material profit or gain through fruitive activities or philosophical speculation. That is called pure devotional service.’  
(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu [1.1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.1.11))

Pure devotional service (suddha-bhakti) is defined as loving, continuous service to the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna with body, mind and words, under the guidance of a pure devotee of the Lord. This service attitude must be free from all material motives: desire for knowledge, fruitive results, laziness, and so on. The pure devotee is anyabhilasita-sunya, he has no motive behind his worship. He is not conducted by the influence of maya in the form of karma or jnana. The pure devotee is always prepared to execute the order of the Lord without personal consideration.The desire that must burn in the heart with increasing intensity is the single objective to satisfy Sri Krsna. Anything extraneous to this must be discarded.

There is no way a conditioned soul can remove the veil of illusion on his own. Every embodied being is born into ignorance and duality. Duality creates confusion - the inability to discriminate between matter and spirit. The self-realized guru has seen the truth, so he alone can guide a deluded soul out of nescience’s gloom into the light of the AbsoluteTruth. Only those who sincerely search for the truth will come in contact with a bonafide guru, by the mercy of the Lord in the Heart (Paramatma). By the mercy of Sri Krsna one gets a guru, and by the mercy of SriGuru, one gets Krsna.

### Verse 50

*so’pyascaryamayah prabhurnayanayoryannabhavad gocaro*  
*yannasvadi hareh padambujarasastad yadgatam tadgatam*  
*etavanmama tavadastu jagatim ye’nye’pyalamkurvate*  
*sricaitanyapade nikhatamanasastairyat prasangotsavah*

**Immense misfortune caused spiritual blindness in me so I was unable to see He who is the only object of perception, who fills the eyes of the pure in heart, that most wonderful and magnanimous personality, SrimanMahaprabhu. Neither was it written in my fate to taste the sweet nectar of service to the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari. Let it be! Whatever has happened, had to happen. I have only one plea left now- may I dance in the festival of the association of those exalted devotees who have enthroned Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet in their hearts, treasuring them with deep devotion, thereby transforming themselves into brilliant ornaments embellishing the earth, wherever they may be.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author considers himself unfit to have darsan of Sri Caitanya and to taste the nectar of service to His lotus feet. He therefore begs for the association of Mahaprabhu’s devotees.

‘Due to my abject misfortune, I could not bring that most illustrious Personality, Sri GauraHari within the range of my perception. Even though I received His darsan, my ignorance of the AbsoluteTruth covered the Supreme Lord’s real identity. Neither could I taste the nectarean rasa of service to His lotus feet. Whatever has already happened is past; over and done with; the past will not return. As regards the future, however, I desire only this much: sri caitanya-pade nikhata-manasas tair yat- that I may have the association of those devotees who embellish Mother Earth, having planted the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya in their minds and hearts. I pray to be in the company of those busy bumblebees, whose minds and hearts constantly relish the nectar from Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet.’

Karika:

*caitanyadarsane yogya ’stat padasevane tatha*  
*atastat padacittais taih sango’stu visva-bhusanaih*

**‘I am completely unfit to see Sri Caitanya or serve His lotus feet, so let me simply associate with those devotees who are like ornaments of this world since they have surrendered their minds and hearts at His lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati Thakur is a very exalted devotee and an eternal associate of the Supreme Lord. According to Sri Kavi Karnapur (author of Gaura GanoddesaDipika) Prabodhananda is the incarnation of Tungavidya, one of the eight principal gopis (asta-sakhis), cowherd girlfriends of Srimati Radhika. Transcendental personalities such as our revered author are not in the least attracted to mundane fame and the like. In describing the glorious characteristics of the Supreme Lord and His devotees he uses the choicest phrases. Yet he portrays himself as extremely fallen and inadequate. This is the nature of pure-hearted devotees of the Supreme Lord. He is an acarya- one who teaches by example. In this capacity, Srila Prabodhananda encourages all who are on the path of bhakti to exclusively cultivate the Vaisnava qualities of humility and compassion. The Supreme Lord unequivocally declares that only those who are materially exhausted can see Him.

### Verse 51

*duskarma kotiniratasya duranta ghora-*  
*durwasana nigada srnkhalitasya gadham*  
*klisyanmateh kumatikoti kadarthitasya*  
*gauram vinadya mama ко bhaviteha bandhuh*

**I am engrossed in tens of millions of abominable activities, bound firmly by the chain of unruly, vicious desires, debilitated in heart due to acute distress caused by constantly pursuing the paths of speculative knowledge, fruitive works, and so on; misdirected by millions of evil designs, the result of misinterpretations and perverted meanings. Thus have I lost my way by following the paths that lead to nowhere. In this predicament, who is there in this material existence, other than Sri GauraHari, to extend a hand of friendship to this drowning soul?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Considering himself as extremely wretched and fallen, the author declares that other than Sri GauraHari there is none who can deliver fallen degenerates like himself.

‘Who in KaliYuga is prepared to become the well-wishing friend of a heinous transgressor like myself? What sort of person am I?’

duskarma-koti-nirata- ‘worst of sinners, totally attached to engagement in billions of unrighteous activities; duranta-without end. Ghora-durvasana- those turbulent, evil desires I am unable to renounce have become insurmountable shackles binding me hand and foot.’

One may argue that iniquities committed due to evil design may well be tackled and neutralised by penance. To this, the reply is: klisyanmateh- ‘even after performing severe austerities and penances, I have not obtained the desired results. Therefore, I have become totally exhausted.’

Then the question remains, ‘why did you perform penances to begin with?’

The reply: kumati-koti-kadarthitasya- due to evil designs, misinterpretation and distorted, perverted understanding. One’s mentality is ruled by intelligence, knowledge. A vile mentality is thus produced from impersonal, deductive knowledge and an eagerness for performing fruitive activities. Enthusiasm for fruitive activities and dry, empirical speculation devoid of devotion have thus recommended the path of penance. Assailing himself in this manner, the author declares Sri GauraHari as his only saviour.

Karika:

*abhakta-sanga mugdhasya krta duskrta karmanah*  
*vina gaura-padambhojam nastyuddharta kalau yuge*

**‘Enamoured by non-devotee association and steeped in iniquities, there is no redemption for me in KaliYuga, other than the shelter of Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

This verse aptly describes the condition of jivas held captive in this world by the Supreme Lord’s illusory potency, maya. The root cause of material suffering is ignorance of our real identity as spirit soul. The jiva tries desperately to reverse this no-win situation, wherein he is blinded by ignorance, lost in a maze of illusion and unable to come out of it alone. Another person who might offer succour to this helpless jiva, must first himself possess clarity of vision. Only by seeing through the eye of the scriptures (sastra-caksu) can one find the path that leads to progressive elevation of consciousness. One must seek guidance from liberated souls.

If the jiva sincerely desires lasting peace in a life ravaged by nescience and miseries, his only hope is to follow Sri Krsna’s instructions:

*bhoktaram yajna-tapasam sarva-loka-mahesvaram*  
*suhrdam sarva-bhutanam jnatva mam santim rcchati*

**‘A person in full consciousness of Me, knowing Me to be the ultimate beneficiary of all sacrifices and austerities, the Supreme Lord of all planets and demigods, and the benefactor and well-wisher of all living entities, attains peace from the pangs of material miseries.’**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**5.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/5.29)**))**

### Verse 52

*ha hanta hanta paramosara cittabhumau*  
*vyarthi bhavanti mama sadhanakotyo’pi*  
*sarwatmana tadahamadbhutabhaktibijam*  
*sri gauracandra caranam saranam karomi*

**Alas! Oh me oh my! Alas! All attempts to plant millions upon millions of seeds of sadhana (spiritual discipline) in the hard and barren land of my heart, have proved completely futile. So now, from the innermost depth of my heart, I will sow that most wonderful seed of transcendental devotional service, by taking shelter of Sri GauraCandra’s lotus feet in complete surrender.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Continuing in his mood of self-criticism, the author submits that without the shelter of Sri GauraHari, all spiritual disciplines are futile.

‘I have performed a superfluity of spiritual disciplines, but my arid and barren consciousness is not in the least moistened by even a drop of prema-rasa. Ha!- Alas! What have I done for all these years? - nothing significant!’

To emphasize profound remorse, repetitive words, such as hanta-hanta (Hopeless! Hopeless!) have been used. ‘Now, however, with all my senses and their functions (sarvatmana), I take shelter of Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet. Sarvantah-karane-whole-heartedly, with all my heart; heart-and-soul, willingly, completely.’

One may ask, ‘how can you enrich your arid and barren consciousness with prema-rasa by taking refuge at Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet?’

The reply: adbhuta bhakti-bijam- ‘His lotus feet are like wondrous seeds of prema-bhakti.'

‘Seeds sowed in a desert do not sprout, just as innumerable spiritual disciplines have not improved the condition of my barren consciousness. My heart and consciousness were stultified and made callous by overt attachment to fruitive activities and the like. However, the wondrous seeds of Sri Gauranga's lotus feet are so potent that even though sowed in the barren land of my heart, they have already begun to sprout the creeper of devotion (bhakti-lata). Therefore, in KaliYuga, to seek shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga is the only responsibility of everyone.’

Karika:

*prema-bhakti-lata-bijam aho gaura-padasrayam*  
*vinanya sadhanam sarvvamusara-sthala bijavat*

**“For the jivas afflicted by KaliYuga, all spiritual disciplines are as futile as sowing seeds in the desert. I say! Sole refuge in Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet alone is the seed of the creeper of prema-bhakti.”**

**Purport**

It is said in the scriptures that severe austerities, penances, atheism, Mayavadi philosophy, and so on, harden the hearts of the living entities. In truth, any engagement which has no connection with the Supreme Lord dries up the heart and makes it barren, like a desert. Matter is dead, inert, without consciousness. Close contact with matter gradually influences the jiva ’s consciousness; thus he believes he is the body and not the soul. When our consciousness becomes covered, dynamic spiritual energy then gives way to material consciousness.

Mayavadi philosophy, the nastiest form of atheism, is the worst culprit to destroy all the finer spiritual sentiments in human beings. Impersonalism is spiritual suicide, as are all philosophies which do not admit brahma-vidya, the science of the soul.

*asurya nama te loka andhena tamasavrtah*  
*tams te pretyabhigacchanti ye ke catma-hano janah*

**‘The killer of the soul, whoever he may be, must enter into the planets known as the worlds of the faithless, full of darkness and ignorance.’**  
**(Sri Isopanisad(**[**3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/iso/3)**))**

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“Human life is distinguished from animal life due to its heavy responsibilities. Those who are cognizant of these responsibilities, and who work in that spirit are called suras (godly persons), and those who are neglectful of these responsibilities or who have no information of them are called asuras (demons). Throughout the universe there are only these two types of human beings. In the RgVeda, it is stated that the suras always aim at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord Visnu and act accordingly. Their ways are as illuminated as the path of the sun.”

“Intelligent human beings must always remember that the soul obtains a human form after an evolution of many millions of years in the cycle of transmigration. The material world is sometimes compared to an ocean, and the human body is compared to a solid boat designed especially to cross this ocean. The Vedic scriptures and the acaryas, or saintly teachers, are compared to expert boatmen, and the scriptural instructions are compared to favourable breezes that help the boat ply smoothly to its desired destination. If, with all these facilities, a human being does not fully utilize his life for self-realisation, he must be considered atma-hanta, a killer of the soul.”

The overwhelming majority of human beings from the four lakhs different human species are born into ignorance (gross, mundane consciousness). Thus their hearts are already polluted by false identification, lust, greed, and so on. So when the jiva tries out different methods and processes for self-elevation, his illusion is compounded. As recommended in the scriptures, the only process which effectively removes all deleterious elements in the consciousness and makes it ready and fertile to receive the seed of pure devotion (bhakti-lata-bija), is to associate with Vaisnavas and chant the HolyNames. The seed of bhakti sprouts and grows by the process of hearing and chanting (watering and nurturing) finally producing the most wonderful, nectarean fruit of prema.

### Verse 53

*ha hanta cittabhuvi me paramosarayam*  
*sadbhaktikalpalatikankurita katham syat*  
*hrdyekameva paramasvasaniyamasti*  
*caitanyanama kalayanna kadapi socyah*

**Oh! Alas! How will it ever be possible for the paradisiacal creeper of true devotion to sprout and blossom in the extremely barren field of my heart? The only solace and hope of my heart is that chanting Sri Caitanya’s HolyName can never be subject to grief or regret.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Simply chanting Sri Caitanya's Name once will cause even the most stone like heart to experience the embryonic stirrings of pure devotion. With the utmost humility, our esteemed author, under the pretext of condemning himself, continues his tirade: ‘ha hanta cittabhuvi... ’

‘My heart is like a desert. How can sad bhakti kalpalatika-single-minded, pure devotion (like a wish fulfilling creeper) sprout?’ Ha hanta- expresses despair and anguish.

The first symptom of prema-bhakti is rati (loving attachment), compared here to sprouts, or buds. Spiritual preceptors have named the initial stage of prema as bhava, synonymous with rati.

‘Of course it is true that nothing can sprout in a desert, but still there is great hope in my heart - caitanya-nama kalayan-that by the chanting of Sri Caitanya's HolyNames, no one at anytime has been victimized by grief or lamentation.’

Karika:

*уас cittosarabhumau hi na bhakti-latikankurah*  
*caitanya nama matrena bhakti-kalpa-latajani*

**‘By no means can the creeper of pure bhakti sprout in a barren and arid heart. Yet, as soon as one chants Sri Caitanya's Divine Name, the wish-fulfilling creeper of devotion is brought forth.’**

**Purport**

*krti-sadhya bhavet sadhya-bhava sa sadhanabhidha*  
*nitya-siddhasya bhavasya prakatyam hrdi sadhyata*

**‘When transcendental devotional service by which love for Krsna is attained, is executed by the senses, it is called sadhana-bhakti, or regulative discharge of devotional service. Such devotion eternally exists within the heart of every living entity. The awakening of this eternal devotion is the potentiality of devotional service in practice.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.2)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**22.105**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.105)**))**

KrsnaPrema is self-perfected, eternally present in a dormant state in the heart of every embodied living entity. It is not an alien or foreign element superimposed on or injected into the soul. Rather, the covering of illusion and ignorance that conceals it from our conscious awareness must be dispelled.

The process of excavating our buried, dormant KrsnaPrema begins with sadhana-bhakti, which in practice begins with hearing and chanting the glories of the HolyName, Fame, Form, Entourage and Pastimes of the SupremeLord. Srila Rupa Gosvami, after a thorough scrutiny of the sasvata scriptures, stipulates, however, that without sraddha (initial faith), sadhana-bhakti cannot be initiated. Furthermore, hearing and chanting without sambandha-jnana will remain on the stage of pious, or fruitive activity. Only when the sadhaka receives formal initiation into chanting from a bona fide, self-realized, liberated acarya, and begins sadhana-bhakti in right earnestness, guided in devotional service by the acarya, is he able to achieve success.

*brahmanda bhramite kona bhdgyavdn jiva*  
*guru-krsna-prasade paya bhakti-lata-bija*  
*mali hana kare sei bija aropana*  
*sravana-kirtana-jale karaye secana*  
*upajiya bade lata ‘brahmanda' bhedi’ yaya*  
*‘viraja ‘brahma-loka ’ bhedi’ para-vyoma’ paya*  
*tabe yaya tad-upari ‘goloka-vrndavana’*  
*‘krsna-carana’-kalpa-vrkse kare arohana*  
*tahan vistarita hana phale prema-phala*  
*ihan mali sece nitya sravanadi jala*

**‘In pursuance of the laws of karma, all living entities are wandering throughout the universe. Some of them are elevated to the upper planetary systems, and some go down into the lower planetary systems. Out of many millions of wandering living entities, one who is very fortunate gets an opportunity to associate with a bona fide spiritual master, by the grace of Krsna. By the mercy of both Krsna and the spiritual master, such a person receives the seed of the creeper of devotional service.**  
**‘When a person receives the seed of devotional service, he should take care of it by becoming a gardener and thus sow the seed in his heart. If he waters the seed gradually by the process of sravana and kirtana (hearing and chanting), the seed will begin to sprout.**  
**‘As one waters the bhakti-lata-bija , the seed sprouts and the creeper gradually grows to the point where it penetrates the walls of this universe and goes beyond the Viraja River, between the spiritual world and the material world. It attains BrahmaLoka, the Brahman effulgence, and, penetrating through that stratum, it reaches the spiritual sky and the spiritual planet, Goloka Vrndavana.**  
**‘Being situated in one’s heart and being watered by sravana-kirtana, the bhakti creeper grows more and more. In this way it attains the shelter of the desire tree of the lotus feet of Sri Krsna, who is eternally situated in the planet known as Goloka Vrndavana, in the topmost region of the spiritual sky.**  
**‘The creeper greatly expands in the Goloka Vrndavana planet, and there it produces the fruit of Love for Krsna. Although remaining in the material world, the gardener regularly sprinkles the creeper with the water of hearing and chanting.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta Madhya Lila (**[**19.151-155**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.151)**))**

The seed of devotion must therefore be received from an acarya whose own devotional creeper (bhakti-lata) has borne the ripened fruit of KrsnaPrema. A person acting in the capacity of an initiating guru will not be able to offer anyone the seed of bhakti-lata (pure devotion to Sri Krsna) unless he has himself first tasted the fruits. If a spiritual aspirant receives initiation from a guru who is unable to offer the seed of pure bhakti, the aspirant’s search for an acarya is not ended. Scriptures inform that the process of liberation extends over many lifetimes.

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

**“One should not become a spiritual master unless he has attained the platform of uttama-adhikari (liberated, first-class devotee). A neophyte Vaisnava (kanistha-adhikari) or a Vaisnava situated on the intermediate platform (madhyama-adhikari), can also accept disciples, but such disciples must be on the same platform, and it should be understood that they cannot advance very well toward the ultimate goal of life under his insufficient guidance. Therefore, a disciple should be careful to accept an uttama-adhikari as a spiritual master.”**  
**(Sri Upadesamrta (**[**5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/noi/5)**))**

### Verse 54

*samsara duhkhajaladhau patitasya kama-*  
*krodhadi nakra-makaraih kavalikrtasya*  
*durwasana nigaditasya nirasrayasya*  
*caitanyacandra mama dehi padavalambanam*

**I have fallen into the ocean of misery, of repeated birth and death, where the Crocodiles and Capricorns of anger, lust, greed, and the like, have come to eat me up. My hands and feet are bound by the chains of loathsome desires, and in this situation I am without any safe haven. О Sri CaitanyaCandra, kindly offer me shelter at Your lotus feet, the boat that can carry me to safety.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Out of humility, the author considers himself to be engrossed in material existence, and in his mood of self-deprecation, he prays for the shelter of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet.

‘The grief and misery of material existence is compared to an ocean, and I have fallen into this ocean. О Sri CaitanyaCandra! Kindly offer me refuge at Your lotus feet. I am without any shelter or support (nirasrayasya) and no safe harbour is in sight. Just as it is impossible to survive in the ocean without a support (a boat, a log, a piece of wood, something!), so also it is impossible to cross this ocean of material existence bereft of the support and shelter of Your lotus feet.’

One may propose, ‘that since you have hands and feet, why not swim to the safety of the shore?’

The reply: durvasana-nigaditasya- my hands and legs are bound up by the ropes of unwanted, abominable desires. Here the verbal root, gada- (fortification), implies imprisonment, being bound.

‘Having fallen into the ocean of material existence I am constantly under siege from sharks and crocodiles in the shape of lust, greed, anger, illusion, envy and madness.’

Karika:

*duhkhabdhi-patitasyadya dehi padasrayam mama*  
*kamadi-nakra makarai-rudvignasya krpanidhe*

**‘O Ocean of Compassion (Sri Caitanya)! Having fallen into this terrible ocean of misery and suffering, I am extremely fearful due to constant attacks from the crocodiles of lust, greed, etc. Therefore, kindly give me refuge at Your lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

The scriptures offer vivid descriptions of material existence in this world of inert matter, to jolt us out of illusion: samsara-‘merry-go-round’ (that isn’t so merry) of repeated birth and death; bhisam-bhavambudhau- a vast, fearsome, dangerous ocean; gabhir-vana- a deep, dark forest; duhkhalay- an abode of suffering; davanala- a raging forest fire; andha-kupat- a blind, deep dark well; and so on. Conditioned souls living in these dismal conditions, exacerbated by ominous perils at every step, have but one recourse:

*samasrita ye pada-pallava-plavam*  
*mahat-padam punya-yaso murareh*  
*bhavambudhir vatsa-padam param padam*  
*padam padam yad vipadam na tesam*

**‘For those who have accepted the boat of the lotus feet of the Lord, who is the shelter of the cosmic manifestation and is famous as Murari, the enemy of the Mura demon, the ocean of the material world is like the water contained in a calf’s hoof-print. Their goal is param padam, Vaikuntha, the place where there are no material miseries, not the place where there is danger at every Step.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.14.58**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.58)**))**

*kamadindm kati na katidha palita durnidesas*  
*tesam jata mayi na karund na trapa nopasantih*  
*utsrjyaitan atha yadu-pate sdmpratam labdha-buddhis*  
*tvam aya'ah saranam abhayam mam niyunksvatma-dasye*

**‘O my Lord, there is no limit to the unwanted orders of lusty desires. Although I have rendered them so much service, they have not shown any mercy to me. I have not been ashamed to serve them, nor have I even desired to give them up. О my Lord, О Imperial Majesty of the YaduDynasty! Recently my intelligence has been awakened, and now I am giving them up. Due to transcendental intelligence, I now refuse to obey the unwanted orders of these desires, and I now come to You to surrender myself at Your fearless lotus feet. Kindly engage me in Your personal service and save me.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**3.2.35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/3.2.35)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**22.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.16)**)**

### Verse 55

*mrgyapi sa sivasukoddhava naradadyair*  
*ascaryabhaktipadavi na dariyasi nah*  
*durbodha-vaibhavapate mayi pamare’pi*  
*caitanyacandra yadi te karunakataksah*

**О Lord of inconceivable opulence, Sri CaitanyaCandra! If Your glance of compassion might fall on such fallen souls as myself, then that most wondrous path of pure devotion, untiringly sought after by Siva, Sukadeva, Uddhava, Narada and other exalted and liberated personalities, cannot possibly remain beyond my reach.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

To attain the profoundly esoteric path of Vraja prema-bhakti is only possible by the grace of Sri Gauranga. Reproaching himself for his ineligibility to receive the Lords grace, the author begs for His mercy.

‘O CaitanyaCandra! If Your merciful gaze might fall on fallen rascals like me, then that wondrous, transcendental path of pure bhakti cannot remain distant; beyond reach.’

‘What is the quality of this path of pure bhakti?’

It is sought after by the most exalted personalities, like Siva, Sukadeva, Uddhava, Narada and others; (but even they cannot attain it).

One might ask, ‘where is the proof? that the wondrous path of pure bhakti sought out by Lord Siva and other saints is instantaneously obtained by Sri Caitanya‘s merciful glance?’ The reply: durbodha-vaibhavapate- He is the Controller of opulence that lies beyond the grasp of intellect and reason.

By calling himself pamara- most fallen, the author continues to reveal the depths of his humility.

Karika:

*devairalabhya ya bhakti-padavi ceddayatava*  
*pamarenapi labhya sa gauro durjneya vaibhavah*

**‘О Lord GauraCandra, You are the master of inconceivable potency. By receiving Your merciful glance, the path of pure bhakti, unattainable by the demigods, becomes obtainable by even a fallen wretch like me.’**

**Purport**

The best way to ensure spiritual progress is to follow in the footsteps of the mahajanas, the previous spiritual preceptors. The great epic MahaBharat exhorts us to humbly approach the mahajanas that they may kindly reveal the purport of the scriptures, sheltered within their hearts.

*svayambhur naradah sambhuh kumarah kapilo manuh*  
*prahlado janako bhismo balir vaiyasakir vayam*

**‘Lord Brahma, Bhagavan Narada, Lord Siva, the four Kumaras, Lord Kapila (the son of Devahuti), Svayambhuva, Prahlada Maharaja, Janaka Maharaja, Grandfather Bhisma, Bali Maharaja, Sukadeva Gosvami and I myself (Yamaraja) know the real religious principles.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.3.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/3.20)**))**

Regarding the Supreme Lord’s unlimited opulence, Sri Krsna Himself comments::

*nanto ’sti mama divyanam vibhutinam parantapa*  
*esa tuddesatah prokto vibhuter vistaro maya*  
*yad yad vibhutimat sattvam srimad urjitam eva va*  
*tat tad evavagaccha tvarm mama tejo-’msa-sambhavam*

**‘O mighty conqueror of enemies, there is no end to My Divine manifestations. What I have spoken to you is but a mere indication of My infinite opulence. Know that all opulent, beautiful and glorious creations spring from but a spark of my splendour. ’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**10.40-41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.40)**)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

**“Krsna is the highest of all entities. In Him is an entity termed cit (spiritual), distinct from the principle of limitation. By this inconceivable power, He can at will create numberless universes. All the mundane universes owe their origin to the transformation of His external potency.”**  
**(Sri BrahmaSamhita (**[**35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/35)**) Purport)**

By the grace of the Supreme Lord, a dumb person speaks eloquently and a lame man crosses mountains. Srila Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya describes Lord Caitanya’s mercy thusly:

*tri bhuvana pavana krpayah lesam*

**‘A mere drop of His mercy can easily deliver all the three worlds’**

The level of pure bhakti sought by exalted and liberated devotees like Uddhava and mahajanas like Siva, Suka and Narada is indeed not vaidhi-bhakti (regulative devotional service):

*sakala jagate more kare vidhi-bhakti*  
*vidhi-bhaktye vraja-bhava paite nahi sakti*

**‘Everywhere in the world people worship Me according to scriptural injunctions. But simply by following such regulative devotional service (vaidhi-bhakti) one cannot attain the unalloyed loving-sentiments of the eternal residents of VrajaBhumi.’**

*aisvarya-jnanete saba jagat misrita*  
*aisvarya-sithila-preme nahi morn prita*

**‘Knowing my opulence, the whole world worships Me with awe and reverential bhakti, but bhakti made feeble by aisvarya-jnana does not attract Me.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila** [**3.15-16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.15)**)**

The most munificent Personality, Sri Caitanya Himself states:

**‘Since time immemorial I have not bestowed prema-bhakti, without which this material creation has no meaning.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila** [**3.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.14)**)**

Srila Rupa Gosvami defines the path of raganuga-bhakti that delivers prema-bhakti.

*iste svarasiki ragah paramavistata bhavet*  
*tan-mayi ya bhaved bhaktih satra ragatmikodita*

**‘The intense and spontaneous absorption in the object of one’s deep yearning and attachment (istha) is called raga. When one becomes attached to the Supreme Personality, his natural inclination to love is fully absorbed in thoughts of the Lord. Devotional service according to this fervour, or transcendental attachment (raga), is called ragatmika, or spontaneous devotional service.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.272**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.272)**) quoted in SriCaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**22.150**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.150)**))**

### Verse 56

*kva sa nirankusakrpa kva tadvaibhavamadbhutam*  
*kva sa vatsalata saure gaure yadrk tavatmani*

**О Krsna! In Your golden incarnation (as Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu) the extent of inevitable mercy You exhibit will always remain unparalleled. Can Your mystic opulence, which enchants the entire creation, be matched by anyone? And who can surpass the protective affection (bhakta-vatsalata)**  
**You possess exclusively towards Your devotees?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may remonstrate, ‘that instead of soliciting for mercy from the unlimited numbers of omnipotent incarnations of the Supreme Lord enumerated in the Vedas and Puranas, or even from the primeval and original Supreme Lord Sri Krsna, why should one approach Sri Caitanya, desirous of His merciful glance?’

The author’s reply: kva sa nirankusa krpa- О Krsna (saura)! The unlimited mercy flowing from Your Golden Incarnation, Sri GauraHari, is not seen anywhere else. By freely offering prema to transgressors, reprobates and heinous persons, the degree of mercy manifest by Sri GauraHari is unprecedented. The inconceivable potency exhibited by Sri GauraHari when He revealed His SadBhujaMurti (his six-handed form) was never exhibited anywhere by anyone at anytime. Moreover, his vatsalata- loving, protective guardianship over his devotees is not seen anywhere else either. The (vatsalya) affection Sri GauraHari exhibited when bestowing GopiPrema to five-year-old Sri KaviKarnapur is without any equal in history. Thus, the author implores Sri GauraHari to exercise his vatsalata, that through this inconceivable potency his mercy may become available, although the author feels himself unfit to receive it.

Karika:

*krpa vaibhava vatsalyam adbhutanca krpanidhe*  
*yat tat kvapi ca nastiti kuru gaurahare krpam*

**‘O Ocean of Compassion ! О GauraHari ! Your most astonishing mercy potency and loving, protective guardianship are unprecedented, never before seen in any other personality. Kindly bestow Your mercy on me.’**

**Purport**

The author addresses Lord Sri Krsna as saure. The meaning of saure is given in the anvaya by Sri Bhakitisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur as: the light of the Sura dynasty- Soma (Moon) dynasty.

*nа me viduh sura-ganah prabhavarh na maharsayah*  
*aham adir hi devanam maharsinam ca sarvasah*

**‘Neither the hosts of demigods nor the great sages know my origin or opulence, for in every respect, I am the source of the demigods and sages.’**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**10.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.2)**))**

Srila RupaGosvami, after consulting various scriptures, has enumerated sixty-four transcendental qualities that VrajendraNandan, Sri Krsna possesses. Lord Balaram has two less, while Sri Narayan and other Visnu expansions possess sixty of these transcendental qualities (four less). Only Lord Krsna has four more qualities than Narayan and all other expansions of Godhead, what to speak of demigods or ordinary jivas.

These four qualities are: LilaMadhurya- performer of wonderful pastimes (especially His childhood pastimes and the Rasa dance); BhaktaVatsala- always surrounded by loving devotees whom the Lord protects under all circumstances; VenuMadhurya- an expert flute player, the enchanter of so many young hearts; RupaMadhurya- unmatched beauty, unrivalled anywhere, neither in the spiritual abodes and certainly not in DeviDham (the material world).

Sri AdvaitAcarya was fully aware of the Lord’s compassionate nature and his identity as BhaktaVatsala, when he decided to pray to him to descend to earth to alleviate the burden of sin in KaliYuga. Although AdvaitAcarya was himself supremely powerful, being a combined incarnation of MahaVisnu and SadaSiva, still he felt that the Supreme Lord Sri KrsnaCaitanya alone was capable of executing the task at hand.
