The Acarya thus began to worship his salagrama-sila, offering Tulasi leaves and Ganges water, while reciting the following verse from GautamiyaTantra.

*tulasi-dala-matrena jalasya culukena va*  
*vikrinite svam atmanam bhaktebhyo bhakta-vatsalah*

**‘Lord Sri Krsna is always affectionate to His devotees, protecting them like a faithful guardian. Thus does He sell Himself to those devotees who offer Him only a TulasI leaf and a palm full of water.’**  
**(Sri Caitanya Caritamrta AdiLila(**[**3.104**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.104)**))**

**When the Lord sells Himself to a devotee, He is able to do so with each and every individual devotee, because He is purnam- completely whole. Because of His purnam quality, He is inexhaustible. No matter how much He gives of Himself, He remains purnam.**  
**(Isopanisad (**[**1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/iso/1)**))**

*adbhuta-purvam mama bhavi kimva*  
*sarvam sahe me sanajam hi duhkham*  
*kintu tvad agre saranagatanam*  
*parabhavo natha nate nurupah*

**‘O Lord. What unexpected reversals in life can possibly come now? Indeed, sorrow is my natural companion, but I am able to tolerate almost anything by now. However, it is not in keeping with Your reputation (as BhaktaVatsalah) that you neglect a soul surrendered unto You, who also happens to be standing before You at this very moment.’**  
**(Sri Yamunacarya)**

## PART VII - Undeviating Surrender (Firm Faith) in One's Worshipful Deity

### Verse 57

*svatejasa krsnapadaravinda-maharasavesitavivamisvaram*  
*kamapyasesa srutigudhavesam gaurangamangikuru mudhacetah*

**Aren’t you aware of the fact that Sri Gauranga, by his inconceivable influence, caused everyone in the universe to imbibe the sweet mellows of love, latent in the lotus feet of Sri Krsna? Though he is the final object of all the Vedas, He nevertheless remains hidden within its pages, the indescribable Lord of the Universe. О you foolish mind! All you have to do is accept Him as your very own.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In KaliYuga, Sri Gauranga is the singular object of worship. This has been unequivocally substantiated in the Vedas, Smrtis and Puranas. Learned scholars of the scriptures and stalwart spiritual preceptors, like the famous pandit, Vasudeva Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya, certified Sri Gauranga as the supreme object of worship, upon witnessing His incredible spiritual prowess. Our most erudite author, as well, after carefully ascertaining this truth from the authorised scriptures and applying his own direct perception, establishes beyond doubt that Sri Gauranga is his only worshipful Supreme Lord in KaliYuga.

The author exhorts his mind to become disciplined, and to then surrender at the lotus feet of Sri GaurangaCandra. Thus he addresses his mind, mudha cetah- о foolish, incorrigible mind! It is simply a matter of angikuru- to accept, to admit that Sri Gauranga is the Supreme Personality, and to then seek shelter at his lotus feet.

‘Why must one surrender to Sri Gauranga? Who is he really?’

He is that Divine Personality who motivated the entire universe to imbibe the immortal ambrosia of prema, springing forth from the lotus feet of Sri Krsna, his own perfect counterpart. Furthermore, He is asesa-sruti-gudhavesam- that Divine Personality, kept confidentially by the Vedic literatures; not openly mentioned; covered up and kept incognito. Therefore he is каmару; inexpressible and imperceptible to most; but those who have been blessed by his merciful glance can easily perceive him, and are thus capable of revealing him to others. Such a person is my Sri GauraHari, the object of my worship.

Karika:

*krsna-premavista visvam sruti-gudham gauraharim*  
*bhaja re mudha me citta hitvanyam jagadisvaram*

**‘O you foolish mind! Leave aside the other Supreme Lords of the universe. Simply worship he who has drowned the entire universe in KrsnaPrema; whose identity is a secret of the Vedas, that Sri GauraHari. Serve Him alone.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad, desiring to draw the attention of those sadhakas who are proud of their bhajan and who consider themselves elevated Vaisnavas, addresses his own mind - taking the position of an ordinary conditioned soul, due to his inimitable humility and compassion for the falsely proud:

*dusta mana! tumi kisera vaisnava?*  
*pratisthara tare, nirjanera ghare, tava hari-nama kevala kaitava*

**“O mischievous, impetuous mind! How can you claim to be a Vaisnava! You withdraw yourself from the maddening crowd to chant in solitude, but this is just a show, a pretence! The bhajan you perform is merely for mundane name, fame and prestige.”**

Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur writes in Sri MadhuryaKadambini, that in the final stage of bhajana-kriya (third in the eight steps to prema-bhakti, described by Srila Rupa Gosvami in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu), the sadhaka may be appreciated by the public for his bhajan (worship and adoration) and knowledge, thus attracting respect and followers \[taranga-rangini (riding the multi-coloured waves of mundane success)\]. This stage is just prior to nistha- when unwanted material desires (anarthas) and nescience, that cover the pure consciousness, are gradually cleared away. In the stage of taranga-rangini, if the sadhaka believes in all the praise that people heap upon him and becomes convinced he is truly advanced, without having actually gotten rid of his anarthas (unwanted attachments-including those in the form of moods and mental conceptions) and so instead, pretends that he is advanced, then he has to make a show of executing bhajan to maintain his image. The only way to overcome this snare is to remain humbly fixed in devotional service, holding tightly SriGuru’s lotus feet (following his instructions).

Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj Gosvami has recorded Sri GauraSundara's statement, wherein the Lord expresses His desire to hide his identity as the Supreme Godhead:

*yuga-dharma pravartaimu nama-sankirtana*  
*can bhava-bhakti diya nacamu bhuvana*  
*apani karimu bhakta-bhava angikare*  
*apani acari’ bhakti sikhaimu sabare*

**‘I shall personally inaugurate the religion of the age-NamSankirtan, the congregational chanting of the HolyNames. I shall make the world dance in ecstasy, realizing the four mellows of loving devotional service. I shall accept the role of a devotee, and teach devotional service by practicing it myself.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (** [**3.19-20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.19)**))**

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“No one but the Lord Himself can teach this highest form of devotional service. Therefore, when the Lord took the place of the incarnation of KaliYuga to spread the glories of chanting HareKrsna, the system of worship recommended in this age, he also disseminated the process of devotional service performed on the platform of transcendental, spontaneous love. To teach the highest principles of spiritual life, the Lord Himself appeared as a devotee in the form of Sri Caitanya.”

### Verse 58

*sravana-manana-sankirtyadi bhaktya murarer*  
*yadi paramapumartham sadhayet ko’pi bhadram*  
*mama tu paramaparapremapiyusa-sindhoh*  
*kimapi rasarahasyam gauradhamno namasyam*

**If any sadhaka desires to worship Sri KrsnaMurari, following the nine-fold path of bhakti to attain the fifth and highest goal (prema), then good for him. I prefer, however, to drench myself in the ambrosial mellows of bhakti in that indescribable, infinite, mysterious, most secret of all secrets - Sea of Premamrta (Nectar of Love) - the abode of Sri Gaura, where I can only bow my head.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The respected author Sripad Prabodhananda Sarasvati sympathizes with even the devotees of Sri Krsna, encouraging them to also worship his worshipful Lord, Sri GauraHari. If a devotee of Sri KrsnaMurari, by executing the devotional process of sadhana-bhakti (sravana-manana-sankirtyadi-hearing, chanting, remembering...), attains the highest goal of prema, then bhadram- very good; all the best. However, mama tu (as for me), I only desire to execute that devotional process {raganuga-bhakti) by which I can attain that most mystical and rare jewel of bhakti-rasa, found in the depths of the shoreless Ocean of Prema, the abode (gaura-dhamnah) of SriGaura.

Karika:

*sri krsna-prema praptyartharh anyesamanya sadhanam*  
*mama tu sri-gauraharer bhajaniyam padambujam*

**‘Those keen to attain KrsnaPrema may gladly execute any appropriate sadhana they wish. I, however, consider the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari to be my worshipful Deity.’**

**Purport**

*radhikara bhava-kanti kari’ angikara*  
*nija-rasa asvadite kariyacha avatara*  
*nija-gudha-karya tomara—prema asvadana*  
*anusange prema-maya kaile tribhuvana*  
*араnе aile more karite uddhara*  
*ebe kapata kara,—tomara kona vyavahara*  
*tabe hasi ’ tanre prabhu dekhaila svarupa*  
*‘rasa-raja’, ‘mahabhava’—dui eka rupa*

RamanandaRay continued,

**“My dear Lord, I can understand that you have assumed the ecstasy and bodily lustre of Srimati Radharani. In this way, you relish the sweetness of your own transcendental humour {rasa), having appeared as Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu. You have descended in this incarnation of Lord Caitanya for your own personal, confidential reasons. You have come to taste your own spiritual bliss (the nectar of prema), and at the same time you are transforming the whole world by spreading the ecstasy of love of God. By your causeless mercy you have appeared before me to grant me liberation. Now you are playing in a duplicitous way. What is the reason for this behaviour?”**

**‘Sri Caitanya simply smiled as he revealed his combined form of RasaRaj Sri Krsna (the reservoir of all pleasure) and MahaBhava Sri RadhaThakurani (the personification of ecstatic love of God) to RamanandaRay. ’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**8.279-282**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.279)**))**

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“RadhaKrsna are one. Radha&Krsna are Krsna and Krsna’s pleasure-potency (hladini-sakti) combined. When Krsna exhibits his pleasure potency, he appears to be two- Radha and Krsna. Otherwise, both Radha and Krsna are one. This oneness may be perceived by advanced devotees through the grace of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu. This was the case with RamanandaRay. One may aspire to attain such a position, but one should not imitate the MahaBhagavat.”

Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj comments that the nine-fold path of bhakti is the best process of bhajan and is sufficiently potent to confer upon the worshiper the ultimate objective- Sri Krsna and KrsnaPrema, the fifth and highest goal of human life. Worship and service in the mood demonstrated by Sri Caitanya is far superior to all other processes of bhakti. This is substantiated by Sri Rupa, Sri Raghunath, Sri Sanatan, Sri Jiva and the other Gosvamis, on the basis of the revealed scriptures.

### Verse 59

*isam bhavantu purusarthacatustayasa*  
*dasa bhavantu ca vihaya harerupasyan*  
*kincid rahasyapadalobhitadhirahantu*  
*caitanyacandracaranam saranam karomi*

**Let those who desire the four aims of mankind: religiosity, wealth, sense pleasure and liberation (dharma, artha, kama, moksa), worship the Lord of the Universe, Jagadisvar. Or, if anyone wants to abandon the worship of other Deities and exclusively serve the Supreme Lord Sri Hari as His surrendered devotee, then let him. Alas! As for me, I am impatiently greedy to relish an indescribable, most rare and most confidential position of service. With this purpose in mind, I have accepted shelter at the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Without worshiping and meditating on Sri Caitanya‘s lotus feet, even the unalloyed devotees of Sri Krsna remain unacquainted with the most profound mysteries of prema (prema-rahasya). So what shall we say then as regards devotees with specific desires and motives (sakama-bhaktas)? Those who desire catur-purusartha- the four goals of human life: dharma, artha, kama and moksa (religiosity, wealth, sense enjoyment and liberation) worship the Supreme Lord Sri Narayan (isam).Let them do as they like. Others may reject the worship of all other Deities and exclusively worship Sri Krsna to become His single-minded devotee. All well and fine.

‘As far as I am concerned (aham punah), I only seek refuge at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.’

The reason for this is expressed with an attributive adjective: kincid rahasya-pada-lobhiradhira- one whose intelligence or consciousness has become restless with greed for relishing the most confidential and rare prema-rasa of KisoraKisori, the young Hero Sri Krsna and young Heroine Sri Radha. With this motive in mind has he accepted shelter at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.

Karika:

*tucchikrta catur-varga harer ekanta dasakah*  
*na prapuste yadrahasyam tallabho gaurapadatah*

**‘The profound nectar of SriSri RadhaKrsna’s prema-rasa cannot be obtained even by those exclusive, single-minded devotees of Sri Hari who have rejected the four goals of human life. Such mystical secrets may only be obtained in the shelter of Sri Gaura’s lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

The most unique spiritual gift the MahaVadanya Avatar, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu came to distribute in this world, is the taste of prema-rasa at the feet of Sri JugalSarkar, SriSri RadhaKrsna. This prema-rasa is composed of the constituents: manjari-bhava, vipralambha-rasa and parakiya-rasa. Without surrender at the feet of Sri Caitanya, even the single-minded servitors and devotees of Sri Hari are unaware of this most rare gift.

The author exhorts his readers to reach out for this prema-rasa that infuses the heart with ParamAnanda. The ecstasy experienced in service at the feet of SriSri YugalSarkar (as taught by the followers of Sri Rupa) cannot be obtained from any other source. Even the most surrendered devotees, servitors of the Supreme Lord Hari, may not relish this acme of ananda, what to speak of the insignificant joys available to those pursuing the four aspirations of human life.

Thus Srila Bilvamangal Thakur comments:

*bhaktis tvayi sthiratara bhagavan yadi syad*  
*daivena nah phalati divya-kisora-murtih*  
*muktih svayam mukulitanjali sevate ’sman*  
*dharmartha-kama-gatayah samaya-pratiksah*

**“If I am engaged in steadfast devotional service unto you, my dear Lord, then very easily can I perceive your presence everywhere. As far as liberation is concerned, I think that liberation stands at my door with folded hands, waiting to serve me; and all material conveniences of dharma \[religiosity\], artha \[economic development\] and каmа \[sense gratification\] stand with her.”**  
**(Sri KrsnaKarnamrta (**[**107**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/kk-kkg/107)**))**

RasaRaj Sri Krsna is akhila-rasamrta-murti- the embodiment and source of all rasas. Sri Radhika is the embodiment of hladinl-sakti, Sri Krsna’s pleasure-giving potency. This Jugala prema-rasa is the mature fruit, the most rare treasure of NamBhajan. Without accepting complete shelter of Sri NamaPrabhu (the HolyName) no one can experience bhakti-rasa. Only to those who seek complete surrender at Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet, is the brilliant gem of prema-rasa revealed, by the grace of Sri NamPrabhu.

‘Most rare and confidential position of service’- the mood of a maidservant to Sri Radhika.

### Verse 60

*nistham prapta vyavahrtita tirlaukiki vaidiki va*  
*ya va lajja prahasanasamudgana natyotsavesu*  
*ye vabhuvannahaha sahajapranadeharthadharmma*  
*gaurascaurah sakalamaharat ko’pi me tivraviryah*

**Aho! A certain thief of impetuous vigour, radiant with a golden lustre, has stolen my meticulously cultivated adherence to social conduct and Vedic etiquette; my shyness in expressing myself in mirthful laughter, loud kirtan, dancing in festivals, and so on, as well as all the natural activities centered around maintaining the body and life airs.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One might rightly ask, ‘having rejected both laukika (social obligations) and vaidika (Vedic scriptural injunctions) norms for human society, what has prompted you to surrender wholesale at the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari?’

The reply: ‘Sri GauraHari is himself the cause.’

ko 'pi gauras caurah- ‘a certain thief with a golden complexion (Sri Gauranga) has stolen everything I possess.'

‘How could this happen to a cautious and careful person like you?’

tivra-viryah- ‘this thief is incredibly powerful; of ardent vigour. He stole everything by force.’

‘What is meant by everything (that he stole)?’

He stole vyavahrtitatih- customs and conducts I cultivated over the years, diligently following both social and Vedic injunctions. Similarly, he also robbed me of lajja-prahasan- my bashfulness in laughing gleefully, full-throated singing, participating in dancing and festivities. He even took away my physical urges for survival, like hunger, thirst, and ythe like. Therefore, I have accepted the refuge of his lotus feet, so that he might reciprocate by appropriating me for his own use (make me His servitor), thus rewarding me with the priceless treasure of prema, and thus keep me forever in it‘s sanctuary (situated at His lotus feet).

Karika:

*balalldja vyavahrti-prana-dehartha dharmmakah*  
*ete me’pahrta yena tam gauraharim asraye*

**‘I take complete shelter of Sri GauraHari who has forcibly plundered my religious principles: my sense of modesty, codes of conduct and physical urges for survival.’**

**Purport**

Only a few out of many millions are interested in searching for a higher purpose in life, still fewer take up the path of yoga, and out of millions of those who practice yoga discipline, only a very few know the Supreme AbsoluteTruth in his personal aspect - Lila Purusottam Sri Krsna - always eager to engage in his DivinePlay (lila).

Following Vedic rules of social etiquette (the endeavour to improve one’s short-comings in religious performances) cannot liberate one from the sensual urges that goad man into acts of (karmic = karma-producing) carnal pleasures. That is possible only by following Lord Krsna’s instructions in the BhagavadGita ([2.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.59)):

*rasa-varjam raso'py asya paramdrstva*  
*‘to cease mundane activities by experiencing a higher taste’*

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“Unless one is transcendentally situated, it is not possible to cease from sense enjoyment (mundane activities.) Sense restriction by some spiritual process like astanga-yoga is recommended for less intelligent persons who have no better knowledge. However, one who has tasted the beauty of the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna, in the course of his advancement in Krsna consciousness, no longer has any taste for dead material things.”

The same Supreme Personality, who as Sri Krsna instructed Arjuna on the battlefield of Kuruksetra, has now advented in KaliYuga in his most munificent manifestation, to encourage and guide humanity how to follow the very same instructions he had originally given to Arjuna. In this incarnation, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu enters the battlefield of KaliYuga with the most effective weapons: His disarming love and exquisite beauty. Others are of the opinion that the Sankirtan movement is his most powerful weapon. Srila Vrndavana das Thakur describes how Sri GauraSundar conquered everyone by stealing their hearts:

*vede jare nirabadhi kare anvesana*  
*se prabhu sabare kare prema alingana*

**‘Whom the Vedas endlessly search for is here amongst us all, embracing everyone with transcendental love."**  
**(Sri CaitanyaBhagavat Madhya Lila (**[**8.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-madhya/8.8)**))**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“The Supreme Personality of Godhead, by his transcendental nature of pure goodness, is always the centre of attraction for all living entities, and so he is the prime object of everyone’s meditation. The sentient world, knowingly or otherwise, is incessantly searching after him, as he is the Supreme Enjoyer and goal of everyone’s service. And that same DivinePersonality is lovingly embracing one and all, knowing them to be his dearly beloved. In this way, he fulfils their innermost desires.”

### Verse 61

*sandranandojjvalarasamaya premapiyusa sindhoh*  
*kotim varsan kimapi karuna-snigdhanetrancalena*  
*ko’yam devah kanakakadali-garbhagaurangayastis*  
*ceto’kasmanmama nijapade gadhayuktam cakara*

**From the fresh, fervent ocean of nectarean prema is born a cloud that bursts forth, showering down rainstorms of condensed ecstasy that produce tens of millions of rivulets of conjugal affection flowing from the corners of those languid eyes, softened by causeless compassion, glistening with affection. This cloud, however, is of the most unique colour, resembling the lustrous hue of ripe bananas. Who is this Deva (God absorbed in His DivinePlay) who has suddenly, as if with great force, captured my awareness and fixed it very firmly as an ornament for his lotus feet?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may protest, that since the respected author is a grave and sober person, not given to outbursts of earthly emotions, why has he fully surrendered at Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet without thoroughly considering the matter first?

In reply, the author says that his heart was captured very suddenly and forcibly and then kept firmly at the Lord's lotus feet ('binding my soul at His lotus feet.’)

‘How was this accomplished?’

‘He swept away my heart by karuna-snigdha netrancalena-the force of tens of millions of streams of nectarean prema raining from the corners of his eyes, brimming with compassion. Sandrananda- deep, concentrated bliss; ujjvala-rasa- fresh fervent mellows of love imbued with conjugal affection; prema-piyusa-sindhoh- ocean of ambrosial love. Everything happened without the usual inventory of my intelligence.’

In this state of consciousness, the power of reasoning submits to its limitations and the materially hardened heart is unable to resist the action of the intense melting potency of Divine Compassion; causeless and as free and independent as the Lord Himself, who acts according to his sweet will.

After describing the Lord’s compassion par-excellence, his unsurpassable beauty and charm is illustrated with the words kanaka-kadali- a lustrous complexion the deep hue of a golden bunch of bananas.

Karika:

*каrunуа-рrеmа plyusa-sindhu-magnikrtam jagat*  
*hemarambha garbha gauraharir me hrtavan manah*

**‘Sri GauraHari, resplendent as a golden banana, has submerged the entire universe in the nectarean ocean of prema, born of his infinite compassion, now engaged in the theft of my mind.’**

**Purport**

**‘Just as the Supreme Lord appears by his independent will, as Lord Krsna in the Yadu dynasty, or as Lord Rama in the Raghu dynasty, by his sweet will he similarly reveals himself to the jivas, so that they can perceive him with their senses.’**  
**(MadhuryaKadambini)**

**“Even the greatest philosophical speculators cannot have access to the region of the Lord. It is said in the Upanisads that the SupremeTruth, the Absolute Personality, is beyond the range of the thinking power of the greatest philosopher. He is unknowable by great learning or by the greatest brain. He is knowable only by one who has His mercy. Others may go on thinking about him for years together, yet he is unknowable. This very fact is corroborated by Queen Kunti, who is playing the part of an innocent woman. Women in general are unable to speculate like philosophers, but they are blessed by the Lord because they believe at once in his superiority and almighty stature, thus do they offer obeisance without reservation. The Lord is so kind that he does not show special favor to one who is a great philosopher. He knows the sincerity of purpose. For this reason only, women generally assemble in great numbers in any sort of religious function. In every country and in every sect of religion it appears that the women are more interested than the men. This simplicity of acceptance of the Lord’s authority is more effective than showy, insincere religious fervor.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.8.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.20)**) Purport)**

*atho yathavan na vitarka-gocaram*  
*ceto-manah-karma-vacobhir anjasa*  
*yad-asrayam yena yatah pratlyate*  
*sudurvibhavyam pranatasmi tat-padam*

**‘Therefore let me surrender unto the Supreme Personality and offer my obeisances unto Him, who is beyond conception, beyond human speculation, beyond the mind, activities, words and arguments, who is the original cause of this cosmic manifestation, by whom the entire cosmos is maintained, and by whom we can conceive of its existence. Let me simply offer my obeisances, for he is beyond my contemplation, speculation and meditation. He is beyond all my material activities.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.8.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.42)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“One simply has to realize the greatness of the Supreme Personality. One should not try to understand him by any material means, subtle or gross. Mother Yasoda, being a simple woman, could not find out the real cause of her vision; therefore, out of maternal affection, she simply offered obeisance unto the Supreme Lord to protect her child. She could do nothing but offer obeisances to the Lord.

“It is said, acintyah khalu ye bhava na tams tarkena yojayet (MahaBharata BhismaParva 5.22). One should not try to understand the SupremeCause by argument or reasoning. When we are beset by some problem for which we can find no reason, there is no alternative but to surrender to the Supreme Lord and offer Him our respectful obeisances. Then our position will be secure. This was the means adopted in this instance by mother Yasoda. Whatever happens, the original cause is the Supreme Personality of Godhead (sarva-karana-karanam \[Brahma Samhita [5.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/1)\]). When the immediate cause cannot be ascertained, let us simply offer our obeisances at the lotus feet of the Lord. Mother Yasoda concluded that the wonderful things she saw within the mouth of her child were due to him, although she could not clearly ascertain the cause. Therefore, when a devotee cannot ascertain the cause of suffering, he concludes:

*tat te ‘nukampam susamiksamano*  
*bhunjana evatma-krtam vipakam*  
*hrd-vag-vapurbhir vidadhan namas te*  
*jiveta yo mukti-pade sa daya-bhak*

**He accepts that it is due to his own past misdeeds that the Supreme Personality has caused him some small amount of suffering. Thus he offers obeisances to the Lord again and again. Such a devotee is called mukti-pade sa daya-bhak, that is, he is guaranteed liberation from this material world.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.14.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.8)**))**

“We should know that material suffering due to the material body will come and go. Therefore, we must tolerate this suffering and proceed with discharging our duty as ordained by our spiritual master. Only by his grace, which he showers on his followers by the sweet will of Sri Caitanya, can living entities attain an eternal life of unlimited bliss. Following the process of rupanuga-bhakti, anyone can quickly attain the fortunate position of being showered by Divine Grace.”

### Verse 62

*svayam devo yatra drutakanakagaurah karunaya*  
*maha premanandojjvalarasavapuh pradurabhavat*  
*navadvipe tasmin pratibhavanabhaktyutsavamaye*  
*mano me vaikunthadapi ca madhure dhamni ramate*

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead has appeared, by His causeless mercy, in a body composed of the mellows of erotic sentiments saturated with the most intense ecstasy of Conjugal Love, with a lustre the colour of molten gold, in the celestial abode known as Navadvip, where every home is filled with festivities in devotion. My mind delights in that sweet abode even more than in Vaikuntha.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

While remembering the wonderful childhood lila of Sri GauraHari in Navadvip, the author desires to see those activities projected on the screen of his mind.

‘My mind delights (ramate) in that illustrious place, Sri Navadvip.’

‘What is Navadvip like?’

Sri GauraSundar, the fountainhead of all incarnations, chose Navadvip (also known as Svetadvip) as the place to make His Divine appearance. In this eternal abode, he revealed to the world unprecedented, nectarean pastimes, resplendent with purity.

It is the place (yatra) where the Supreme Personality appeared, out of his infinite compassion; (pratibhavana-bhaktyutsavamaye) where every home resounds with festivities in honour of Srimati PremaBhakti Devi.

In Sri KaviKarnapura’s play, Sri CaitanyaCandrodaya Nataka, Viraga hears a description of NavadvipDham from an oracle:

*gauda ksauni jayati katama punya-tirthavatamsa*  
*praya yasau vahati nagarim sri-navadvipa namnim*  
*yasyam camikara-caya-rucir isvarasyavataro*  
*yasmin martya puri puri parispandate bhaktidevi*

‘All glories to Gaudadesa, where the diadem of countless holy pilgrimages, Sri Navadvip is situated. With the advent of the Supreme Personality in His golden incarnation of Sri Gauranga, every home in Navadvip celebrates a great festival in honour of Sri BhaktiDevi.’

(Gaudadesa- pronounced GauraDesh)

Sri Navadvip is vaikunthadapi ca- in Goloka, madhurya (sweetness) reigns supreme; it is a more sublime realm than Vaikuntha; but more nectarean and sublime than Goloka is Sri Navadvip; this is implied by the use of the word ca (also).

The Lord’s body is druta-kanaka-gaurah- the colour of molten gold; and maha premanandojjvalarasavapuh- composed of the most intense ecstasy in love, permeated with erotic sentiments (srngara-rasa). Mahaprema means mahabhava, the pinnacle of prema, its embodiment - personified ujjvala-rasa (erotic sentiments) indicates that Sri Gauranga is the embodiment of Sri Radhika’s prema.

Karika:

*paravyomaditah sresthe prema-bhakti-vilasake*  
*gaura-krsna avataradhye navadvipe manascala*

**‘O mind! Go to Sri Navadvip, a superior realm to Paravyoma, where Sri GauraKrsna has descended. PremaBhakti is sporting there in great exultation.’**

**Purport**

The pre-eminence of Navadvip as the Supreme Lord’s lila-ksetra is due to the fact that, as GauraSundar, he descended there to propagate the spiritual process prescribed for this age (yuga-dharma). He freely distributed prema-bhakti, steeped in radha-dasya (mood of service to SriRadha). As the Divine embodiment of srngar-rasa, Sri GauraSundara’s inner complexion is syama (RasaRaj Sri Krsna), yet his external complexion is molten gold (MahaBhavamayi Srimati Radhika).

Navadvip resounds with the sound of kirtan. Every home is a stage for Sri GauraSundar, Sri NitaiCand and their eternal associates, to perform ecstatic dancing and singing in the Divine mood of audarya (munificence). BhaktiDevi was too inebriated with the excessive flow of sublime ambrosia to even try and leave these homes.

**‘All glories to the land of Gauda (Bengal), the crest jewel of all sacred pilgrimages, where Sri Navadvip is always present. Due to the Divine advent of the golden avatar, Sri GauraSundar, every home is hosting grand festivities in honour of BhaktiDevi’s appearance.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCandrodayaNataka)**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

**“The devotees attain Goloka, the transcendental region above Vaikuntha, according to the quality of rasa of their respective services. In reality, that region is none other than Svetadvip or ‘the White Island’, being exceedingly pure. Those who attain the highest rasa, in the shape of realisation of pure devotion in this world, viewing the reality of Svetadvip in Gokula, Vrndavana and Navadvip, within this mundane world, designate the same as Goloka. In that transcendental region of Goloka there are always visible, in their supreme beauty, all the distinctive entities that are incorporated in the pure cognitive principle.”**  
**BrahmaSamhita (**[**56**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/56)**) Purport**

### Verse 63

*yattadvadantu sastrani yattad vyakhyantu tarkikah*  
*jivanam mama caitanya-padambhojasudhaiva tu*

**Let the scriptures reveal their wealth of wisdom; let the erudite scholars and empirical philosophers write their elaborate commentaries. My life and soul exist but in the sublime ambrosia of the dust pollen of the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

A pilgrim on the path of raganuga-bhakti (unalloyed, spontaneous devotional service), our honoured author reveals his devotion to the methodology of developing lobha (spiritual greed).

‘The scriptures should continue to instruct through rules and regulations, and the panditas of rhetoric and dialectics should continue to postulate new logic based on newer and newer arguments. As far as I am concerned, however, my life and soul will continue to remain merged in the glistening nectar of prema, like drops of dew on the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra.’

Karika:

*vadantu vidhi-vakyani yuktim kurvvantu tarkikah*  
*ahantu gaura-padabjam vinanyat kvapi nasraye*

**‘Let the scriptures instruct, with their rules and regulations; let the logicians present their arguments. I, however, am not willing to take shelter anywhere other than at Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

A MahaBhagavat rasika devotee, such as our author, is greedy only for relishing the sublime beauty of the transcendental visaya (object) of his bhajan and loving devotion. In this stage of devotional surrender, scriptural injunctions are secondary. They are helpful to a sadhaka, while treading the razor sharp path of yoga. However, to a siddha, a self-realized traveller on the path of raga bhakti, scriptural prescriptions and proscriptions are not applicable.

*tat-tad-bhavadi-madhurye srute dhir yad apeksate*  
*natra sastram na yuktim ca tal lobhotpatti-laksanam*

**‘When an advanced rasika devotee hears about the activities and characteristics of an eternal ragatmika devotee of Vraja (in a specific transcendental humour \[rasa\]) he develops lobha (greed) to render seva in that mood, and his intelligence takes note of the prevailing bhava in devotion. Thus when lobha is awakened within him, his intelligence no longer depends on the instructions of the sastras, logic or argument.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.292**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.292)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**22.155**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.155)**))**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“The natural propensity of a raganuga devotee is to aspire to fulfil the greed (lobha) he develops for devotional sentiments in the mood of the eternal residents of Vraja. Thus, scriptural injunctions, logic and arguments about the birth of raganuga-bhakti are redundant. Raganuga devotees, who have a mature level of ruci (taste), have naturally mastered the conclusions of all the scriptures and are therefore experts in debate and explanation. Anyone trying to challenge their realisations regarding ruci, which is eternally self-manifest, will not be entertained. Noteworthy here is that the prakrta sahajiyas and other such pretenders and charlatans, whose taste (ruci) for transcendental devotional service has not in the least developed, but who arrogantly pretend to have developed the same, avoid discussing devotional scriptures and forsake the path of Srila RupaGosvami’s teachings. They engage in illicit activities with women and, out of ignorance, cultivate mundane tastes for sensual pleasures. In this way they invite their own doom. They are truly unfortunate and deprived of the real object.”

### Verse 64

*patanti yadi siddhayah karatale svayam durlabhah*  
*svayam ca yadi sevakibhavitumagatah syuh surah*  
*kimanyadidameva va yadi caturbhujam syadvapus*  
*tathapi mama no manak calati gauracandranmanah*

**If all the mystic perfections like anima, laghima, and so on, very difficult to obtain, were to come within my grasp; if all the demigods were to stand in attendance before me, ready at my beck and call; indeed, even if my body was transformed into a four-handed form - still, my heart and mind would not budge a fraction from their total absorption in my Sri CaitanyaCandra.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author is reaffirming his devotion to Sri GauraHari by insisting that the minds of those who are devoted to Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet are never attracted anywhere else; patanti yadi siddhayah- even if the rarely attainable eight mystic perfections - becoming infinitesimally small (anima-siddhi); becoming lighter than a soft feather (laghima-siddhi); the ability to get anything and everything from anywhere and everywhere (prapti-siddhi), to become heavier than the heaviest (mahima-siddhi), to act freely to create something wonderful or to annihilate anything at will (isitva-siddhi), to control all material elements (vasitva-siddhi), to possess such power as will never be frustrated in any desire (prakamya-siddhi), or to assume any shape or form one may even whimsically desire (kamavasayita-siddhi); (all these expediencies are as common as natural gifts for the inhabitants of the higher planets) - were effortlessly obtained by me; and if the demigods on their own accord volunteered to become my servants; what more can I say? even if I was awarded a four-handed form! my mind would still not deviate a fraction from Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet.

Karika:

*siddhayah syuh karasthas cet bhaveyuh sevakah surah*  
*catur-bahu-vapuscenme tathapi na calen manah*  
*sri gaurahari padambujad iti sesah*

**“Let mystic perfections sit in the palm of my hand, let the demigods become my servants, let my body acquire four hands - still my mind will not move an iota from Sri Gauranga's lotus feet!”**

**Purport**

The Supreme Personality, having accepted the role and devotional mood of a pure devotee, has incarnated in KaliYuga to propagate the yuga-dharma - NamaSankirtan. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the fountainhead of all incarnations, came personally to teach vairagya-vidya and bhakti-yoga to the conditioned souls of KaliYuga.

*nа dhanam na janarm na sundanrim kavitam va jagadisa kamaye*  
*mama janmani janmanisvare bhavatad bhaktir ahaituki tvayi*

**“O almighty Lord, I have no desire to accumulate wealth, nor do I desire beautiful women, nor do I want any number of followers. I only want Your causeless devotional service birth after birth.”**  
**(Sri Siksastaka (4))**

The trademark of a rasika bhakta who considers himself a maidservant of Sri Gandharvika (SrimatiRadhika), is that he has developed total apathy towards anything mundane, be it securing mystic perfections or lordship over the demigods. He is repulsed even at the idea of sarupya mukti band the other forms of liberation as well. His only desire is, as Srila Narottama das Thakur describes:

*lila-rasa sada gana yugala-kisora prana prarthana kariba abhilase*  
*jibane marane bhai ar kichu nahi cai kahe dina narottama dase*

**‘The only desire I nurture in my heart, is that I can pray, with intense yearning, to have the DivineCouple, SriSri RadhaGovinda as my very life and soul; so I may always engage in singing about and glorifying their nectarean lila, saturated with transcendental rasa. In life or in death, there is nothing more for me to aspire after. So says Narottam das.’**  
**(SriSri PremaBhaktiCandrika)**

*na vai yace rdjyam na cakanaka-manikya-vibhavam*  
*na yace’ham ramyam sakala-jana kdmyam vara-vadhum*  
*sada kale kale pramatha-patina gita-carito*  
*jagannathah svami nayana-patha-gami bhavatu me*

**‘I do not pray for a kingdom, priceless jewels and material opulence, nor for a beautiful wife desired by all men. My only prayer is that my Lord and master Sri Jagannath, who is also the Lord of Siva, and who is praised always in glorious hymns, be the constant object of my vision.’**  
**(Sri JagannathAstkam(7))**

*krsna-bhakta-----niskama, ataeva ‘santa’*  
*bhukti-mukti-siddhi-kami-----sakali ‘asanta ’*

**‘Because a devotee of Lord Krsna is desireless, he is peaceful. Fruitive workers desire material enjoyment, jnanis desire liberation, and yogis desire material opulence; therefore they are all lusty and cannot be peaceful.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.150**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.150)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“The devotee of Lord Krsna has no desire other than serving Krsna. Even so-called liberated people are full of desires. Fruitive actors desire better living accommodations, and jnanis want to be one with the Supreme. Yogis desire material opulence, yogic perfections and magic. All of these non-devotees are lusty (kami). Because they desire something, they cannot have peace.”

The peace formula is given by Krsna in the BhagavadGita ([5.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/5.29)):

*bhoktaram yajna-tapasam sarva-loka-mahesvaram*  
*suhrdam sarva-bhutanam jnatva mam santim rcchati*

**“One who simply understands that throughout the entire universe, Krsna is the supreme enjoyer and beneficiary of all kinds of sacrifices, penances and austerities, which should be performed only to attain His devotional service, that Krsna is the Supreme Being and thus the proprietor of all the material worlds, and that Krsna is the only friend who can actually do good to all living entities (suhrdam sarva-bhutanam)—one who understands these three principles about Krsna immediately becomes desireless (niskama) and therefore peaceful. A KrsnaBhakta knows that his friend and protector in all respects is Krsna, who is able to do anything for His devotee. Krsna says \[BhagavadGita (9.31)\]: kaunteya pratijanihi na me bhaktah pranasyati “O son of Kunti, declare it boldly that My devotee never perishes.”**

Since Krsna gives this assurance, the devotee lives in Krsna and has no desire for personal benefit. The background for the devotee is the All-Good Himself (meaning that whatever Krsna does is ultimately meant for the good of his devotee, even when at the time the situation may not appear to be favourable). Why should the devotee aspire for something good for himself? His only business is to please the Supreme by rendering as much service as possible. A KrsnaBhakta has no desire for his own personal benefit. He is completely protected by the Supreme. Avasya raksibe krsna visvasa palana. Bhaktivinoda Thakur says that he is desireless because Krsna will give him protection in all circumstances. It is not that he expects any assistance from Krsna; he simply depends on Krsna just as a child depends on his parents. The child does not know how to expect service from his parents, but he is always protected nevertheless. This is called niskama (desirelessness).

“Although karmis, jnanis and yogis fulfil their desires by performing various activities, they are never satisfied. A karmi may work very hard to acquire a million dollars, but as soon as he gets a million dollars he desires another million. For the karmis, there is no end of desire. The more the karmi gets, the more he desires. The jnanis cannot be desireless because their intelligence is unsound. They want to merge into the Brahman effulgence, but even though they may be raised to that platform, they cannot be satisfied there. There are many jnanis or sannyasis who, after taking sannyasa and giving up the world as false, return to the world to engage in politics or philanthropy or to open schools and hospitals. This means that they could not attain the real Brahman (brahma satyam). They have to come down to the material platform to engage in philanthropic activity. Thus they again cultivate desires, and when these desires are exhausted, they desire something different. Therefore the jnani cannot be niskama, desireless. Nor can the yogis be desireless, for they desire yogic perfections in order to exhibit some magical feats and gain popularity. People gather around these yogis, and the yogis desire more and more adulation. Because they misuse their mystic power, they fall down again to the material platform. It is not possible for them to become niskama, desireless.

“The conclusion is that only the devotees, who are simply satisfied in serving the Lord, can actually become desireless. Therefore Caitanya Mahaprabhu says, krsna-bhakta niskama. Since the KrsnaBhakta, the devotee of Krsna, is satisfied with Krsna, there is no possibility of falldown.”

### Verse 65

*vaso me varamastu ghoradahanajvalavalipanjare*  
*sri caitanyapadaravinda vimukhairma kutracit sangamah*  
*vaikunthadipadam svayanca militam no me manо lipsate*  
*padambhojarajaschata yadi manak gaurasya no rasyate*

**I consider living inside a furnace preferable to even a moment’s association with persons who are inimical to the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya. Neither am I desirous of accepting elevation to Vaikuntha, even if offered to me without my having to endeavor for it through vigorous sadhana, if my heart and mind are unable to relish but a fraction of the lustrous beauty emanating from the pollen particles on the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One must scrupulously shun the company of those who are antagonistic toward Sri Caitanya, for their company is more excruciating than the worst suffering. The happiness one experiences in serving and worshipping Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet is not available even in Vaikuntha. It is better to be in a cage engulfed by raging fire than to associate with those who reject Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet.

One may propose, that it is better to ignore going into an analysis of whether or not to associate with those inimical to Sri Caitanya; rather, concentrate on executing the process by which one may attain Vaikuntha.

The reply: gaurasya... if I am unable to catch even a glimpse of the radiant, mellifluous rays shining from the particles of pollen on His lotus feet, then, though the abode of Vaikuntha may appear before me without any endeavour on my part, still my mind will not be attracted to reside there.

Karika:

*varam hutavahajvala panjarantar vyavasthitih*  
*mastu gaura-padambhoja vimukhaih saha sangamah*

**‘I prefer being inside a cage engulfed by fire, than association with persons who are opposed to Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

**‘One who does not accept Sri Krsna as the Supreme Personality of Godhead is certainly a demon. Similarly, anyone who does not accept Sri KrsnaCaitanya as Krsna is also a demon. One who does not show respect unto this merciful Lord, Caitanya Mahaprabhu, or does not worship Him should be considered a demon, even if he is very much exalted in human society. If one is infested with the ten offenses in the chanting of the Hare Krsna MahaMantra, despite his endeavour to chant the HolyName for many births, he will not get the Love of God that is the ultimate goal of this chanting.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrtam AdiLila(**[**8.9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/8.9)**,**[**12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/8.12)**,**[**16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/8.16)**))**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“If a person is engaged in executing any of the nine limbs of pure devotion, beginning with hearing and chanting, he will never attain the treasure of KrsnaPrema without taking shelter of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, even after many lifetimes of Brahma. According to Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s teachings, he who is humbler than a blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree, and ready to offer all respect to others without demanding respect for himself, will surely develop a taste for chanting the MahaMantra incessantly (if devoid of the ten offenses to the HolyNames). Ultimately he alone can obtain KrsnaPrema.”

*rajan patir gurur alam bhavatam yadunam*  
*daivam priyah kula-patih kva ca kinkaro vah*  
*astv evam anga bhagavan bhajatam mukundo*  
*muktim dadati karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam*

**Sukadeva Gosvami continued: “My dear King, the Supreme Person, Mukunda, is actually the maintainer of all the members of the Pandava and Yadu dynasties. He is your spiritual master, worshipful Deity, friend, and the director of your activities. To say nothing of this, He sometimes serves your family as a messenger or servant. (This means He worked just as ordinary servants do.) Those engaged in getting the Lord’s favour attain liberation from the Lord very easily, but He does not very easily give the opportunity to render direct service unto Him.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**5.6.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.18)**))**

*vararh huta-vaha-jvala panjarantar-vyavasthitih*  
*na sauri-cinta-vimukha-jana-samvasa-vaisasam*

**‘Better to be situated in a cage engulfed by a raging fire than to reside with those averse to Krsna consciousness. Such association is a very great hardship.’**  
**(KatyayanaSamhita / quoted in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.51**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.50)**))**

*alinganam varam manye vyala-vyaghra-jalaukasam*  
*na sahgah salya-yuktanam nana-devaikasevinam*

**‘It is better to live with or embrace a snake, a tiger or an alligator than to associate with those whose hearts are filled with varieties of material desires and who worship various demigods.’**  
**(VisnuRahasya (BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu** [**1.2.112**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.112)**))**

### Verse 66

*astam nama mahan mahaniti varam sarvaksamamandale*  
*loke va prakatastu namamahati siddhiscamatkarini*  
*кamam caru caturbhujatvamayatamaradhya visvesvaram*  
*ceto me bahumanyate nahi nahi sri gaurabhaktim vina*

**Even if my fame as a great personality be acclaimed over the entire globe; or even though I may manifest miraculous, mystic perfections in this world; or even though my worship of the Lord of the universe, Visvesvar, bestows upon me an enchanting four-handed form, long wished for, thus admitting me into the ranks of the Lord’s eternal associates - my heart and mind do not acknowledge any of these excellences as having any value in the absence of loving devotion to Sri GauraSundar. They are, rather, quite insignificant; thus they are not worth striving for.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Those who, for the sake of acquiring distinction and mundane position, refrain from worshiping Sri Caitanya and instead engage in worship of the Administrators of the Universe, are admonished herein.

‘I may acquire worldwide fame as a great personality (mahan). Similarly, mahati- marvelous, mystic perfections may appear before me in person on this earth, to stay permanently with me. Furthermore, by worship of the Supreme Controller, I may even attain a much sought-after four-handed form. But none of the above mentioned is worthy of my respect. I have regard only for devotion to the Supreme Lord Sri GauraHari.’ The repetitive use of nahi nahi is a sure and certain negation, implying that worship of SriGauranga is superior to all else.

This world is herein referred to as- ksama mandala- the ‘sphere of forbearance’. This world and its inhabitants must tolerate so much just to maintain their existence.

Karika:

*loke mahattva vikhyatih parama paramadbhuta*  
*siddhis caturbhujatvan ca vrtha gaurasraynm vina*

**‘Worldwide fame, the best of miraculous, mystic perfections, even attainment of a four-handed, spiritual form -all are worthless without the shelter of Sri Gauranga.’**

**Purport**

The transcendental realm of suddha bhakti is beyond bhukti (sense gratification), mukti (liberation) and siddhi (mystic perfection). Bhukti is mundane, hence temporary. It can never be properly relished since its enjoyment is spoilt by the interference of tri-guna (three modes of material nature-goodness, passion & ignorance) and tri-tapaklesa (the threefold miseries- adhyamika, adhibautika, adhidaivika). It is only aspired after by the less intelligent karmis (fruitive workers). Siddhis are also impermanent, therefore mundane as well. Mukti is not desired by suddha-bhaktas who worship the Supreme Lord in the mood of Vrajabasis.

*sakala jagate more kare vidhi-bhakti*  
*vidhi-bhaktye vraja-bhava paite nahi sakti*  
*aisvarya-jnanete saba jagat misrita*  
*aisvarya-sithila-preme nahi mora prita*  
*aisvarya-jnane vidhi-bhajana kariya*  
*vaikunthake yaya catur-vidha mukti pana*  
*sarsti, sarupya, ara samipya, salokya*  
*sayujya na laya bhakta yate brahma-aikya*

**‘Everywhere in the world people worship Me according to scriptural injunctions. But simply by following such regulative principles, one cannot attain the loving sentiments of the devotees in VrajaBhumi. Knowing My opulences, the whole world looks upon Me with awe and veneration. But devotion made feeble by such reverence does not attract Me. By performing such regulated devotional service in awe and veneration, one may go to Vaikuntha and attain the four kinds of liberation. These liberations are sarsti (achieving opulence equal to that of the Lord), sarupya (having a form the same as the Lord’s), samipya (living as a personal associate of the Lord) and salokya (living on a Vaikuntha planet). Devotees never accept sayujya, however, since that is oneness with Brahman.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta Adi Lila (**[**3.15-18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.15)**))**

### Verse 67

*caitanyeti krpamayeti paramodareti nanavidha-*  
*premavesita-sarvabhtita hrdayetyascaryadhamanniti*  
*gaurahgeti gunarnaveti rasarupeti svanamapriye-*  
*tyasrantam mama jalpato janiriyam yayaditi prarthaye*

**My prayer is this- that my life may pass, tirelessly singing the praises of the Supreme Lord Sri Caitanya, chanting His innumerable names and attributes: О Caitanya - Divine attractor of the hearts and minds of all living entities! О Moonlike Sri Caitanya, the embodiment of eternality, absolute knowledge and unlimited bliss! Ohe Krpamaya - О Ocean of Kindness! Ohe Paramodara - О Most Munificent Lord! О You who incite various levels of love in the hearts all living beings! О Most Beautiful Lord, whose bodily effulgence is as lustrous as molten gold! Ohe Gauranga! How amazing it is that You come to this world, accepting a transcendental body to be among us! О Ocean of all Benevolent Qualities! Your form is composed of the mellows (rasa) of DivineLove! О Personification of the most rare spiritual rasa of relishing Love of God in Separation (vipralambha-rasa)! О You who relish the nectar of Your own Name!**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri Caitanya is Himself a practitioner of prema-bhakti, both the highest spiritual process and the highest spiritual goal. Therefore, in KaliYuga it is recommended to glorify His HolyName. By asserting this truth the author demonstrates that Sri Caitanya is his Supreme Object of Worship; thus he exhorts all to chant and meditate on His name. By calling out His names, one thus prays: ‘He Caitanya! О Compassionate One (krpamaya), О Most Munificent Lord, He who infuses in the jiva’s hearts- dasya, sakhya, vatsalya and madhurya prema, О Abode of Wonders, О Golden-Complexioned One. О Ocean of Auspicious Qualities, О Embodiment of Rasa, О You who are infatuated with Your own Name. Other names are figurative: О son of Mother Saci, О Sustainer of the Universe (Visvambhar), О Moon of Navadvip, О Golden Moon, О Saviour Incarnate of KaliYuga, О Bestower of Prema, О Protective Guardian of devotees. My wish is to chant these names at all times, especially when leaving my body.’

Caitanya- the embodiment of eternality, absolute knowledge and unlimited bliss; or, one who sees, receives and attracts everyone’s heart; or, one who is present in everyone’s realisations. Krpamaya- the abode of compassion, or personified compassion. Paramodara- one who rewards prema to even the most fallen wretches; yet He is the crest-jewel of all incarnations, exhibiting infinite munificence. Ascarya-dhaman- the abode of supreme wonder; Gauranga- whose bodily complexion is golden. Rasarupa- the embodiment of srngara-rasa (conjugal love). Svanama-priya- one who is fond of His own Names; thus Sri Krsna in His golden incarnation as Sri Gauranga constantly chants His own Names with Divine Love.

Karika:

*krsna-caitanya gauranga visvambhara sacisuta*  
*avadhauta-priya prema-sindho kuru krpam mayi*

**‘O Sri KrsnaCaitanya. Sri Gauranga, Sri Visvambhar, Sri Sacisuta, AvadhutaPriya (beloved of Avadhuta Nityananda), PremaSindho, О Ocean of Prema, kindly be merciful unto me.’**

**Purport**

According to Srila Rupa Gosvami, the easiest and the surest way in KaliYuga to obtain KrsnaPrema, the highest and fifth goal of human life, is to chant the HolyNames of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Sri Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of God, fountainhead of all incarnations, incarnated in KaliYuga as the official incarnation predicted in the Vedas to propagate and establish the prescribed religious principle for this age. But to do so He covered His real identity as the SupremeLord and instead manifest His pastimes as a pure devotee.

*yuga-dharma pravartaimu nama-sankirtana*  
*can bhava-bhakti diya nacamu bhuvana*  
*apani karimu bhakta-bhava angikare*  
*apani acari’ bhakti sikhaimu sabare*  
*араnе na kaile dharma sikhana na yaya*  
*ei ta’ siddhanta gita-bhagavate gaya*

**‘I shall personally inaugurate the religion of the age-NamSankirtan, the congregational chanting of the HolyNames. I shall make the world dance in ecstasy, realizing the four mellows of loving devotional service (dasya, sakhya, vatsalya and madhurya). I shall accept the role of a devotee, and I shall teach devotional service by practicing it Myself. Unless one practices devotional service himself, he cannot teach it to others. This conclusion is indeed confirmed throughout the Gita and Bhagavatam.'**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**3.19-21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.19)**))**

*jalpita nija-guna-nama vinodam*  
*tam pranamami ca sri saci-tanayam*

**‘I offer my repeated obeisances to Sri GauraSundar, son of mother Saci, who continuously and softly utters His own HolyNames, that describe His wonderful attributes.’**  
**Sri Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya Sri Saci TanayaAstakam(3)**

### Verse 68

*kada sauregaure vapusi parama premarasade*  
*sadekaprane niskapatakrtabhavo’smi bhavita*  
*kada va tasyalaukikasadanumanena mama hrdya-*  
*kasmat sriradhapadanakhamani jyotirudagat*

**When oh when will pure, undivided, sincere love for Sri GauraKrsna (Sri Krsna in the form of Gaura, the most munificent bestower of the mellows of devotional love) spontaneously awaken in my heart? And when, as a result of this transcendental hope, will my heart suddenly be illuminated by the effulgence emanating from the gemlike toenails of the lotus feet of Sri Radha Thakurani.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One who has developed unalloyed (devoid of duplicity) prem a for Sri GauraHari, will have his heart illuminated by the brilliant rays emanating from the gemlike toenails of Srimati Radhika’s lotus feet.

‘O Saure, Sri Krsna! When will I develop unmotivated, undivided prema for your golden form, giving up all other desires? When will this prema awaken in my heart?’

One may enquire, ‘instead of developing loving attachment for the form of Sri SyamSundar, why do you wish to develop love for the golden GauraSvarup?’

The answer: vapusi... ‘this golden form awards the most rare spiritual gem, radiant prema-rasa. This golden form is sadekaprana- the life and soul of devotees fully conversant in the knowledge of prema-rasa.’

The Lord is addressed here as saure- valorous and intrepid, in the matter of showering mercy on His unmotivated, unalloyed devotees.

Unmotivated, unalloyed KrsnaPrema is transcendental to sensual perception, hence it is described here as sadanumanena- perceivable only through true perception and inference. Then, sriradhapadanakhamani- the sparkling rays from the gemlike toenails of Srimati Radhika’s lotus feet will suffuse my heart with their brilliance.

Concomitantly, that heart bereft of love and devotion for Sri Gauranga, is never illuminated by the radiance from the gemlike toenails of Srimati Radhika’s lotus feet. Thus, the degree that the intensity of illumination from Srimati Radhika’s toenails suffuses the heart of a GauraBhakta is relative to the measure of unalloyed and unmotivated prema for Sri Gauranga in his heart. This point is clarified with a mundane analogy: In logic it is said, ‘where there is smoke, there is fire’, similarly, ‘where there is no smoke, there cannot be any fire (like on the surface of water).’

Karika:

*srimad gauranga visaya bhavo yatra na vidyate*  
*tatra sri radhikapadapadme jatu ratir na hi*

**‘Where there is no pure love for Sri Gauranga, love and attachment for Srimati Radharani’s lotus feet can never manifest.’**

**Purport**

The MahaBhagavat’s (our rasika author’s) ardent prayer to Lord Krsna to reward him with GauraPrema is not a philosophical faux-pas. In KaliYuga, Sri GauraSundara’s HolyName is most powerful. Sri GauraSundar advented for the sole purpose of distributing freely that paramount and most brilliant prema-rasa, which had never been given before. It is but natural for the rasika devotees {paramo nirmatsaranam satam / the most elevated devotees; one hundred-percent pure in heart; persons completely free from malice and envy) to yearn for unnata ujjvala-rasam- the resplendent pinnacle of all rasas - conjugal, erotic love. It is available only with Sri GauraHari. The liberated souls are disinterested in anything mundane. Once they taste the nectar of the mature fruit of the Vedas, SrimadBhagavatam, their only goal automatically becomes the most delectable KrsnaPrema.

KrsnaPrema in madhura-rasa cannot be obtained without the mercy of Srimati Radhika. All rasika devotees in madhura-rasa must first be accepted by Srimati Radharani as her maid-in-waiting, thereafter he, or she, gains eligibility to render service to the DivineCouple. So, one who has developed pure, unmotivated love for Sri GauraHari alone will have his heart illuminated by the divine sparkle from Srimati Radhika’s gemlike toenails. To make this point crystal clear, the author has composed this verse.

Concomitant to the degree of GauraPrema awakened within a devotee, his spiritual sentiments in madhura-prema will blossom from prema, to sneha, to mana, etc. In this rarefied realm of prema-bhakti, Lord Krsna’s golden incarnation is our only shelter.

The eligibility to approach Sri Caitanya depends on one’s sincerity in following Srila Rupa’s instructions. Srila Rupa Gosvami knows Lord Caitanya’s desires in depth. Thus a rupanuga rasika bhakta has an unhindered approach to Sri Caitanya. Srila Rupa Gosvami defines the quality of uttam bhakti (elevated devotion) required by one who seeks Sri Caitanya’s shelter:

*anyabhilasita-sunyam jnana-karmady-anavrtam*  
*anukulyena krsnanu-silanam bhaktir uttama*

**‘When one who is not inspired by material desires and is not contaminated by the processes of fruitive activity and empiric speculation, fully engages in the favourable service of the Lord, his service is called bhagavad-dharma, or pure devotional service’**  
**(Sri BhaktiRasamrtaSindhи (**[**1.1.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.1.11)**))**

Thus without following Srila Rupa Gosvami’s instructions it is not possible to gain the mercy of Sri GauraSundar. This truth has been firmly expounded by Sri GauraSundar himself. Lord Caitanya is displeased with anyone who does not follow Sri Rupa’s mission.

### Verse 69

*uddamadamanakadamaganabhirama-*  
*maramaramamaviramagrhitanama*  
*karunya dhama kanakojjvala gauradhama*  
*caitanyanama paramam kalayami dhama*

**That self-willed, impetuous soul is decorated with a garland of fragrant Damanaka blossoms; He is the source of absolute bliss and causeless mercy for the common people; incessantly chanting the HolyNames in a solitary garden, He is immersed in the happiness of the self. I meditate on the radiant, golden abode of Gaura, the Treasure Chest of Compassion, Sri Caitanya, the foremost shelter for all.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

A particular form of Sri GauraSundar, the subject of our meditation, is being described.

I meditate on CaitanyaNama- ‘who is known by the name Caitanya; the abode of the most resplendent, golden lustre (kanakojjvala gauradhama). His garland of exquisite Damanaka flowers (damanaka-dama) in full bloom around his neck gives joy to the inhabitants of this world. He is completely unrestrained in immersing everyone in his sweet charms (uddama ganabhiramam). Able to give himself pleasure by incessantly chanting the HolyNames (avirama-grhita-nama), he sits in solitude in a quiet pleasure garden {arama-ramam). Thus do I meditate upon Sri KrsnaCaitanya, karunya-dhama- the abode of compassion.

Karika:

*gauram damanakoddama-malyamarama-ramakam*  
*pragrhita-hare-krsna-nama dhama manah smara*

**‘O mind! Please remember the ever-fresh Cupid, Sri Gauranga decorated with a garland of indomitable Damanaka flowers, enjoying himself in a pleasure grove, sheltered in the abode of HareKrsna Nama.’**

**Purport**

The author encourages his readers to meditate on Sri GauraSundara’s brilliant, golden complexion, an exceptional feature of his exquisite beauty. According to Srila Rupa Gosvami, meditation, or dhyana, is primarily of four kinds, depending on the subject of meditation: ruра (form), guna (qualities), krida (activities) and seva (service). Each of them is explained in the Sri BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu.

Rupa-dhyana: It is stated in the NarasimhaPurana, that by fixing the mind on the Supreme Lord’s lotus feet, one is freed from fear and anxiety stemming from duality. Even the most sinful person, by meditating on the Supreme Lord, is rewarded with unimaginable auspiciousness - he can attain the Lord's Supreme abode.

Guna-dhyana: The VisnuDharmottara says that those who regularly meditate with devotion on the Supreme Lord Hari’s transcendental characteristics and qualities, eradicate unlimited sinful reactions. At the end of their life they enter the spiritual world of Vaikuntha.

Krida-dhyana: The PadmaPurana describes how meditation on the Supreme Lord Hari’s activities which are all absolutely nectarean in essence, most wonderful, and extremely enchanting to the heart and mind, cuts asunder the insurmountable network of material bondage, even for one still embodied in this material world (jivana mukta).

Seva-dhyana: The PadmaPurana states that by rendering mental service to Lord Hari, with imagined paraphernalia, anyone can meet the Supreme Lord face to face, although he is beyond the grasp of human thoughts and words, what to speak of the results of direct service.

Srila Rupa Gosvami narrates an incident from the Brahma Vaivarta Purana:

“A poor brahmana from Pratisthanapura in South India was living a frugal but contented life. One day, at a brahmanas' assembly, he heard that devotional service can be performed even by meditation. In other words, if a person is unable to actually perform Vaisnava activities physically, he can meditate upon the Vaisnava activities and thereby acquire all the same results. From that day forth, taking this Vaisnava practice to heart, he would go daily to bathe in the holy Godavari and then sit down to complete his brahminical rituals in a solitary place on the river bank. Going into deep meditation after practising pranayama, he would install in his mind Lord Hari’s Deity in an imagined temple. He would then wash and mop the temple room, offer obeisances to the Deity, bathe Him with the sacred waters from Ganga, Jamuna and Godavari, kept in pots made of gold and silver. This brahmana, instead of chanting some mantra, imagined that he was physically securing water from all these rivers in golden and silver waterpots. Then he collected all kinds of paraphernalia for worship - flowers, fruits, incense and sandalwood pulp. He collected everything to place before the Deity. All these waters, flowers and scented articles were then very nicely offered to the Deities for their satisfaction. Then he offered arati, and with the regulative principles he finished all these activities in the correct worshiping method. In this way, everyday he felt great spiritual satisfaction, being able to serve and worship the Lord of his heart in an opulent, imperial style.

“Many years later, he desired in his mind one day, to offer the Lord sweet-rice cooked in ghee. However, he was not very satisfied with the offering because the sweet rice had been prepared recently and it was still very hot. (This preparation, sweet rice, should not be taken hot. The cooler the sweet rice, the better its taste.) So because the sweet rice had been prepared by the brahmana very recently, he wanted to touch it so that he could know whether it was fit for eating by the Lord. As soon as he touched the sweet rice pot with his finger, he immediately was burnt by the heat of the pot. In this way, his meditation broke. He immediately came out of samadhi and feeling pain in his two fingers he saw boils appear on them.

“In Vaikuntha, Lord Narayan suddenly smiled. At this, his eternal consort Srimati LaksmiDevi looked questioningly at her husband. Then the Lord personally went on the back of Garuda to meet this brahmana devotee and take him to Vaikuntha.”

Dhyana is one of the sixty-four limbs of bhakti which begin with sri-guru-padasraya (taking shelter of a bonafide spiritual master).

### Verse 70

*sada range nilacalasikhar srnge vilasato*  
*harereva bhrajanmukhakamalabhrnge ksanayugam*  
*samuttunga premonmadarasa-tarangam mrgadrsa-*  
*manangam gaurangam smaratu gatasangam mama manah*

**May my mind always remember Sri Gauranga, completely free from attachment and yet always engaged in transcendental enjoyment, sporting in Divine Play on the summit of the peak of NilacalaDham. His eyes are like a pair of bumble bees suckling nectar pollen from the radiant and blossoming lotus face of Lord Jagannath, for moments that become eons, while lofty waves of the mellows of ecstatic madness in Divine Love crash on the shore of His emotions. All along, the exquisite doe-eyed damsels see Him as Cupid incarnate, due to His breathtaking beauty.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author meditates on Sri GauraSundara’s splendorous beauty as He (rapt in the mood and sentiments of Srimati Radhika) feasts His eyes on the unique loveliness of His own immovable form, the Moon of Nilacala, Sri Jagannath.

‘O mind! Meditate on Sri Gauranga, who is gatasangam-fully liberated from all mundane attachments; the SupremeRenunciant. Though he is completely indifferent to worldly concerns, his existence is not dry; he is not living a morose life. Quite the contrary, he is having fun (ranga), enjoying himself in transcendental merriment that we can hardly conceive of. Although he is so detached, having no connection with the supreme object of enjoyment for a man in this world (a woman), the doelike eyes of the damsels of Sri PurusottamKsetra, fawn upon his handsome form, seeing him as the ever-fresh Cupid.

harereva bhrajanmukhakamalabhrnge- whose eyes, like a pair of bumblebees, drink nectar from the radiant lotus face of Sri JagannathDev.

‘What are the characteristics and qualities of Sri JagannathDev?’

sada range nilacalasikhar srnge vilasato- Lord Jagannath resides on the summit of Nilacala, a place of continuous festivities; bhrajanmukhakamala- His lotus face shines with a brilliance that dazzles one’s mind and heart.

‘What are the characteristics of Sri GaurangaDev?’

samuttunga premonmadarasa-tarangam- lofty waves of Divine madness in ecstatic love, make his heart heave and swell with their onslaughts; mrgadrsa-manangam gaurangam- while on the shores of this ocean of the mellows of devotional insanity, the doelike eyes of the young maidens of Nilacala fawn all over this new Cupid who dances amidst them.

Karika:

*sri nilacala srnge svamukha-padmarpiteksanam*  
*mahabhava tarangadhyam gaurangam smara me manah*

**‘O my dear mind! Please remember this ever-fresh Cupid. Sri Gauranga, richly adorned with waves of the ecstasy of MahaBhava, His eyes having been entrusted to the blooming lotus face of His very own form of Sri JagannathDev, who sports on the summit of Nilacala.’**

**Purport**

VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna, as Sri KrsnaCaitanya, is the mobile Jagannath, while the Deity of Jagannath performs the pastime of sitting motionless. The proof that Sri Krsna is attracted by his own beauty is the appearance of his golden incarnation, Sri KrsnaCaitanya, imbued with the spiritual sentiments of Srimati Radharani, eternally enamoured by Krsna’s beauty. Sri KrsnaCaitanya has appeared to relish Krsna’s beauty; Krsna has come to taste the nectar of his own enchanting elegance, in the mood of Srimati Radhika.

**‘Srimati Radha is the embodiment of complete, absolute energy, and Sri Krsna is the fountainhead of energy, the energetic principle par excellence. Between them there is no difference - this is the verdict of the scriptures. Thus Radha and Krsna are one, yet they have taken two forms to enjoy the mellows of pastimes.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.96**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.96)**,**[**98**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.98)**))**

**“RasaRaj Sri Krsna, the King of Rasa, and MahaBhavamayi Srimati Radhika, the embodiment of ecstatic love, have combined to become one (Sri GauraSundar).’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (8.282))**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“RasaRaj Sri Krsna and MahaBhavarupa Srimati Radha merge together and become one transcendental, Divine identity - radha-bhava dyuti-suvalitam naumi-krsna-svarupam. The transcendental reality of a simultaneous singular / plural identity is amazing; two absolute principles or spiritual identities combined in one, then that one absolute identity separates to become two, simultaneously. Those who are able to comprehend the spiritual truth about Sri KrsnaCaitanya, and the truth about SriSri RadhaKrsna, are eligible, by the infinite grace of Srila Rupa Gosvami, to render devotional service to these eternal spiritual identities.”

Srila Bhaktivinoda explains further in JaivaDharma, quoting from Srila Rupa Gosvami’s Sri UjjvalNilamani.

*syad-drdhe’yam ratih prema pradyuh snehati kramadayam*  
*syan manah pranayo mago’nurago bhava ityapi*

**‘Conjugal love (madhura-rati) becomes firm and unambiguous by the influence of bhava. This stage is described as prema. As prema begins to reveal its transcendental, conjugal intensity of sweetness, it converts to sneha, mana, pranaya, raga, anuraga and bhava (mahabhava).’**

MahaBhava is the particular province of Srimati Radhika. She is the epitome and embodiment of asraya-tattva. She wears the crown of MahaBhava as the crest jewel of all ornaments, for the pleasure of RasaRaj Sri Krsna, the pinnacle of the visaya-tattva.

### Verse 71

*alnikarah pankeruhanayana-nihsyandipayasam*  
*prsad bhih sanmuktaphalasulalitairyasya vapusi*  
*udancadromancairapi ca parama yasya susama*  
*tamalambe gauram harimarunarocisnuvasanam*

**I take shelter of Sri GauraHari, whose ornaments are the tear drops on his face, like drops of fresh milk, or a necklace of milky white pearls. Such beauty is further accented by the ‘goose bumps’ all over his body, produced by intense ecstasy, causing his bodily hairs to stand on end, while his garments reflect the beauty of the rising sun.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author has painted a pleasant picture of Sri GauraHari’s resplendent form, decorated with the symptoms of sattvik-bhava, a picture for our constant meditation. The person in the portrait is my only shelter and support in life (alambe / alamban).

His eyes, like lotus petals {pankeruha), are garlanded with tears, resembling a pearl necklace (sanmuktaphala), or drops of fresh milk (nihsyandipayasam). Such exquisite beauty is enhanced by the appearance of his bodily hairs, standing erect (udancadromancairapi) like the petals of a Kadamba flower. His garments are the colour of the rising sun (arunarocisnuvasanam). All glories to Sri GauraHari!

Karika:

*muktaphala sadrn netra-baribindu vibhusitam*  
*romanca susamam sona vastram gauraharim bhaje*

**‘I worship Sri GauraHari, decorated with pearly drops of tears and ‘goose bumps’ that enhance the sweet grace of his bodily beauty. His golden garments reflect the colour of the rising sun.’**

**Purport**

The ecstatic transformations (asta-sattvika-vikara) are transcendental manifestations in the body of a MahaBhagavat rasika devotee. Others may, out of deep sentiment, manifest some symptoms akin to sattvika- vikara, but they are caused only by mundane sentimentalism.

*vigalita nayana-kamala-jaladharam*  
*bhusana nava-rasa-bhava-vikaram*

**‘Tears cascade incessantly from Sri SaciNandana’s lotus eyes, like dense clouds that pour down the rain of pain in separation from Sri Krsna. His ornaments are the ecstatic transformations of MahaBhava, in ever fresh rasas’**  
**(Sri SaciTanayastakam)**

*rodana-bindu-maranda-syandi-drg-indivaradya govinda*  
*tava madhura-svara-kanthi gayati namavalim bala*

**‘О Govinda, this youthful girl named Radhika is today constantly pouring forth tears like nectar falling from flowers as She sings Your HolyNames in a sweet voice.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.3.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.3.38)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**23.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/23.33)**))**

These symptoms are not to be imitated like the prakrta sahajiyas do. Prakrta sahajiyas, aulas, bauls, and so on, are unbonafide cults, claiming to be followers of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. They never follow Sri Caitanya’s instructions on righteous living, nor his personal example as a strict householder, what to speak of the real meaning of what it means to become a sannyasi. Thus without performing sadhana and bhajana they want to jump to the highest level of bhakti to relish rasa. When a sadhaka ’s faith (sraddha) reaches the stage of bhava, after anartha-nivrtti, nistha, ruci, and so on, then these symptoms will manifest automatically. Of the twenty-six qualities of a sadhu (known as sadhu-bhusanam) described in the Srimad Bhagavatam, the most important one is to become a devotee of the Supreme Lord. Without this, all the other qualities are simply mundane, especially when they decorate the character of a non-devotee.

*bhagavad-bhakti-hinasya jatih sastram japas tapah*  
*apranasyaiva dehasya mandanam loka-ranjanam*

‘For a person devoid of devotional service, birth in a famous or aristocratic family, knowledge of scriptures, performance of penances and austerities, chanting of Vedic mantras, etc., are all like ornaments on a dead body. Such ornaments are meant simply to entertain and give cheap pleasure to the public.’  
(HariBhaktiSudhodaya ([3.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbs/3.11)))

### Verse 72

*kandarpadapi sundarah surasaritpuradaho pavanah*  
*sitamsorapi sitalah sumadhuro madhvikasaradapi*  
*data kalpamahiruhadapi mahasnigdhau jananya api*  
*premna gauraharih kada nu hrdi me dhyatah padam dhasyati*

**Aho! He is more charming than KamaDev (Cupid), more purifying than the sacred currents of MaGanga, more cooling and soothing than the moon’s rays, sweeter than immortal nectar, more generous than the wish-fulfilling kalpa-vrksa desire tree, and so full with parental affection, that He is more loving than a mother. When indeed will Sri GauraHari become the constant object of meditation in my heart, having affectionately entered therein?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**
