The respected author, desirous of having Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet manifest in his heart, remembers the Lord’s incomparable and immaculate qualities: his beauty, his magnanimity upon the fallen souls, the cooling effect of his compassion, felt in the burning hearts of the distressed; his sweet personality, gentleness, etc.

‘When will Sri GauraHari become the subject of my meditation (dhyatah); and out of love {premna), place his lotus feet in my heart?’

He is kandarpadapi-ka (Brahma): and one who crushes Brahma’s pride (darpa) - kandarpa (KamaDev / Cupid) - whose beauty and opulence overshadow even that of Lord Brahma. He who is substantially more beautiful than Cupid and who enchants Cupid himself, is Sri GauraHari.

He is surasarit- the holy river Ganga is the most efficacious purifier of sins, but Sri GauraHari is even more purifying than her. All sinful reactions are nullified in the sacred current of MaGanga, but she is unable to transform the heart of a sinner. Sri GauraSundar purifies the sinner's heart and instils prema there. This is the marvel of his ability to purify.

Sri GauraHari is sitamsoh- more cooling than the moon. Moonlight dissipates the darkness of night and the heat of the sun. However, Sri GauraHari destroys the darkness of ignorance and the burning heat of material suffering, replacing them with ecstatic bliss.

He is madhvika rasadapi- sweeter than the nectarean Madhvika fruit. The demigods become arrogant and jealous, after getting inebriated by drinking worldly ambrosia. However, the nectar of Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet is very rarely obtained by demigods. It eradicates arrogance and jealousy, replacing them with ecstatic joy.

Sri GauraCandra is more charitable and magnanimous than the wish-fulfilling desire tree. The kalpa-vrksa (desire tree) rewards only as much as one prays for, but Sri GauraHari, out of his causeless compassion, awards prema to fallen and unfit persons, even unsolicited.

He is more loving and caring than a mother. Mothers smother only their own children with love and affection, but Sri GauraHari’s love extends to all living entities.

Karika:

*smara gangendu madhvika surapadapamatrtah*  
*adbhuta-sripavitradi yasya tam gauramasraye*

**‘I take shelter of Sri Gaura, who’s incomparable, transcendental beauty, sacredness and other characteristics are in every respect far superior to those of Cupid, Ganga, the moon, the nectar of immortality, wish-fulfilling desire trees and the mothers of this world.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“Worldly Cupid is the cause of trouble, anxiety, suspense and illusion in the lives of ordinary mortals of this earth. However, Sri GauraHari’s beauty dissipates anxiety and illusion and makes one experience deep exhilaration and joy. This is the wonder of his beauty.  
“GangaDevi’s potency to purify sins is unmatched in this world. However, Sri GauraHari not only purifies and transforms the hearts of the most heinous reprobates, but releases a free- flowing spring of prema to flow in their hearts. Hence he is more benevolent and purifying than even GangaDevi.  
“The moon’s rays dissipate darkness and cool the earth. Lord GauraSundar completely destroys the impenetrable gloom of ignorance and nescience accumulated over millions of lifetimes in the jiva ’s heart. He extinguishes the incinerating heat caused by distress and suffering in the jiva ’s conditioned state. With his soothing touch he inundates the heart with the protective rays of the Divine ecstasy of prema.  
“The sweetness of the nectar of immortality (amrta) was relished only by the demigods. This produced mundane pride, arrogance and envy in them. However, the ambrosia of Sri GauraSundara’s charm and beauty is practically unattainable by the demigods. By a mere drop of this ambrosia, pride, arrogance, envy, and the like, are nullified, and transcendental joy of prema permeates the heart.  
“The wish-fulfilling desire tree (kalpa-vrksa) grants the wishes of all those who approach it, but Lord GauraSundar is so munificent that he rewards everyone with the greatest treasure of prema, even those who do not approach him and are undeserving.  
“A mother’s affection for her child becomes an affliction for both in the future, because it is related to the mutable, destructible body. Whereas Sri GauraSundara’s love and affection are lodged in the jiva ’s heart where they gradually expand, making him eligible to experience the highest transcendental ecstasy derived from prema. A mother’s love is generally restricted only to her own progeny, but Sri GauraSundar showers all living entities with Divine Love.”

### Verse 73

*punjam punjam madhura madhura prema madhvi rasanam*  
*dattva dattva svayamurudayo modayan visvametat*  
*eko devah katitata milanmanjumanjisthavasa*  
*bhasa nirbhatsita-navataditkotireva priyo me*

**He has come, overflowing with magnanimity, to distribute Prema, sweeter than heaps and heaps of the sweetest nectar of immortality drunk by the demigods, thus making the universe dance in jubilation. Around his waist is bound a most charming cloth, dyed the colour of the Indian madder plant. His bodily lustre rebukes the brilliance of tens of millions of lightning flashes. May that most magnanimous Deva (whose Divine pastimes are unparalleled) be the sole object of my affection.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author proclaims his love for Sri GauraHari, while describing his enchanting loveliness and by revealing his extraordinary virtue as the bestower of ecstatic bliss upon the inhabitants of the universe, through distributing an inexhaustible surplus of nigudha-vraja-bhakti.

‘Sri GauraHari alone, has thus become very dear to me.’

One may ask, ‘why?’

The answer: madhura madhura prema madhvi rasanam-prema-rasa is sweeter than any ambrosia of immortality. GauraHari has freely dispensed, in immeasurable quantities, this prema-rasa, thereby drowning the world in transcendental happiness.

‘What is the reason for this abundant distribution of prema-rasa?

Uru-dayah- His compassion is prodigious; He is supremely magnanimous.

He wears around his hips (katitata) a cloth coloured with the ruddy Cordifolia flower. His bhasa (bodily effulgence) censures the brilliance of the flashing of ten million lightning bolts. May this supramundane personality (devah) become most dear to me (eko priyo me).

Karika:

*premamrta rasa-vrata dana-hrsta jagaddharih*  
*anga nindita vidyut-sri-mаnjisthamsuh priyo’stu me*

**‘Sri GauraHari, through his charitable act of distributing premamrta-rasa (the mellow flavour of nectarean, DivineLove) in great profusion, has thus engladdened the inhabitants of this world. The beauty of his bodily limbs surpasses that of lightning flashes. He looks so pleasant, dressed in garments a lovely saffron colour. May he be my most precious love.’**

**Purport**

The HolyNames of Sri Krsna are the priceless treasure of sublime prema from Goloka Vrndavana. Hence, prema is available in unlimited supply. Displaying audarya-rasa (unprecedented magnanimity and compassion), Sri Krsna Caitanya freely distributed this most rare gift to everyone.

The Supreme Lord says in His own words: “I am the father of this universe, the mother, the support and the grandsire.” (BhagavadGita [9.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.17)). As a loving parent, he does not deprive his wards of the best things of life. The fortunate ones take advantage of the Supreme Father’s generosity while the wayward and unfortunate souls cannot look beyond the temporary benefits of this material world. Like a loving father, the Lord never forcibly imposes His mighty will on the jiva ’s minute, but free, will.

Madhvi / Varuni -

intoxicating beverage - Dolichos Sinensis intoxicating liquor - Gaertnera Racemosa

Indian madder - Rubia Manjistha

### Verse 74

*kantya nindita koti-koti madanah srimanmukhenducchata*  
*vicchayikrta koti-koti saradunmilattusaracchavih*  
*audaryena ca koti-koti gunitam kalpadrumam hy alpayan*  
*gauro me hrdi koti-koti janusam bhagyaih padam dhasyati*

**Sri GauraSundara’s charming good looks defame the beauty of tens of millions of Cupids. The sublime effulgence of His countenance makes the splendour of ten million autumnal full moons wane away. His infinite magnanimity dwarfs the benevolence of many millions of wish-fulfilling kalpa-vrksa desire trees. Will He ever appear in my heart, which through many millions of pious deeds in as many births, has been purified in preparation for receiving Him?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Feeling very deeply within himself something of the Lord’s most exquisite splendour and infinite magnanimity, the author prays that he may anchor himself in profound meditation on his lotus feet.

Thus will Sri GauraHari place his lotus feet on the throne of my heart, as a result of many millions and billions of pious deeds; koti-koti janusam- good fortune accumulated over billions of lifetimes; the pious results of sadhana.

Kantya- whose immaculate and sublime beauty defeat the beauty of billions of Cupids. In reality there is only one Cupid (Madana), however, as per the profundity of the subject, poets use tautology, hyperbole and other figures of speech to lend imagery to their comparisons (metaphors and similes). If the beauty of billions of Cupids fades away in the presence of Sri GauraHari, then what shall we say of only one Cupid? The same analogy is applicable to the full moon.

The moonlike CaitanyaCandra is further described as sriman mukhenducchata- whose supremely charming and sublime face emanates Divine effulgence that vicchayikrtah- makes the splendour of billions of autumnal moons wane; rising full moons that are tusarecchavih- as white and pristine as virgin snow.

As a charitable person, Sri GauraSundar is infinitely generous (audaryyena). Even unsolicited, he bestows prema upon those who are most fallen, thus his generosity is far greater than that of billions of kalpa- vrksas (wish-fulfilling desire trees).

Karika:

*aganya vidhu jidvaktro dyuti nindi smarayutah*  
*koti kalpa-taror data gaurah kim dhasyate padam me hrditi sesah*

**‘The captivating attractiveness of the lotus face of Sri GauraHari puts to shame the splendour of millions of moons. His bodily effulgence outshines countless Cupids. His boundless generosity dwarfs the benevolence of billions of kalpa- vrksas. When will the day finally come, when He will place His lotus feet on the throne of my heart?’**

**Purport**

The prime purpose of spiritual sadhana is to gain (adhikar) eligibility to enthrone the Supreme Lord's lotus feet in the core of one's heart. Sri GauraSundar never tires of trying to retrieve the conditioned souls from their fall into the Ocean of Maya by placing His lotus feet on the throne of the sadhaka's heart. However, if the jiva has not acquired adhikar, then his false-ego forces him to forget the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord and Sri Guru. Sri Narottam das Thakur sings:

*ahankare matta haiya nitai-pada pasariya, asatyere satya kari mani*

**‘Intoxicated with false prestige, the jiva forgets the lotus feet of PrabhuNityananda, thus is his delusion further compounded and he is unable to distinguish between reality (that which will remain) and illusion (that which is perishable).’**

NityanandaPrabhu is both the Supreme Lord, the presiding Deity of sandhini-tattva, and, adi-guru, the original spiritual master. Dhruva Maharaj, Prahlad Maharaj and other pure devotees acquired adhikar by sadhana. However, without guru-krpa, their sadhana would not have born any fruit. First, they received the mercy of Narada Muni, and then only were they able to proceed further. It must be understood that if anyone intensely desires to meditate on the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord, he or she must have developed ruci and mamata (taste and deep attachment). This will only be possible when the heart is purified of all material contaminations. The sadhaka in this stage thinks of nothing else but the lotus feet of the Lord of his heart.

*аnаnуа-mamata visnau mamata prema-sangata*  
*bhaktir ity ucyate bhisma-prahladoddhava-naradaih*

**‘When one develops an unflinching sense of ownership or possessiveness in relation to Lord Visnu, or, in other words, when one thinks Visnu and no one else to be the only object of love, such an awakening is called bhakti \[devotion\] by exalted persons like Bhisma, Prahlada, Uddhava and Narada.’**  
**(NaradaPahcaratra quoted in BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.4.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.4.2)**) and Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**23.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/23.8)**))**

*vrndavane ‘aprakrta navina madana’*  
*kama-gayatri kama-bije yanra upasana*

**‘In the spiritual realm of Vrndavana, Krsna is the spiritual, ever-fresh Cupid. He is worshiped by the chanting of the KamaGayatri mantra, with the spiritual seed klim.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**8.138**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.138)**))**

*purusa, yosit, kiba sthavara-jangama*  
*sarva-cittakarsaka, saksat manmatha-madana*

**‘The very name Krsna means that He attracts even Cupid. He is therefore attractive to everyone—male and female, moving and inert living entities. Indeed, Krsna is known as the all-attractive One.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila(**[**8.139**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.139)**))**

*ye madana tanu-hina, para-drohe paravina,*

*duhkha deya, na laya jivana*

**“In My loving affairs there is a person named Madana. His qualities are thus: Personally He possesses no gross body, yet He is very expert in giving pains to others. He has five arrows, and fixing them on His bow, He shoots them into the bodies of innocent women. Thus these women become invalids. It would be better if He took My life without hesitation, but He does not do so. He simply gives Me pain.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**2.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/2.22)**))**

“Srimati Radharani is the center of all Vrndavana’s activities. In Vrndavana, Krsna is the instrument of Srimati Radharani; therefore all the inhabitants of Vrndavana still chant “Jaya Radhe!” From Krsna’s own statement, it appears that Radharani is the Queen of Vrndavana and that Krsna is simply Her decoration. Krsna is known as MadanaMohana, the enchanter of Cupid, but Srimati Radharani is the enchanter of Krsna. Consequently Srimati Radharani is called MadanMohanMohini, the enchanter of the enchanter of Cupid.”  
(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila ([13.150](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/13.150)) Purport)

*radha-sange уada bhati tada ‘madana-mohanah’*

**The female parrot said, “When Lord Sri Krsna is with Radharani, He is the enchanter of Cupid; otherwise, when He is alone, He Himself is enchanted by erotic feelings even though He enchants the whole universe.”**  
**(GovindaLilamrta (**[**13.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/gl/13.32)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**17.216**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/17.216)**))**

*cadi ’ gopi-manorathe, manmathera mana mathe,*  
*ama dhare ‘madana-mohana’*  
*jini ’ pancasara-darpa,    svayam nava-kandarpa,*  
*rasa kare land gopi-gana*

‘Favoring the gopis, Krsna rides on the chariots of their mind. Just to receive loving service from them, He attracts their minds like Cupid. Therefore He is also called MadanMohana, the attractor of Cupid. Cupid has five arrows, representing form, taste, smell, sound and touch. Krsna is the owner of these five arrows, and with His Cupid-like beauty He conquers the minds of the gopis, though they are very proud of their superexcellent beauty. Becoming a new Cupid, Krsna attracts their minds and engages in the Rasa dance.’  
(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila ([21.107](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/21.107)))

*krsna-kara-pada-tala, koti-candra-susitala, tara sparsa yena sparsa-mani*  
*tara sparsa nahi yara,    se yauk charakhara,*  
*sei vapu lauha-sama jani*

**The palms of Krsna’s hands and the soles of His feet are so cool and pleasant that they can be compared only to the light of millions of moons. One who has touched such hands and feet has indeed tasted the effects of touchstone. If one has not touched them, his life is spoiled, and his body is like iron.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**2.34**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/2.34)**))**

*krsna-kara-pada-tala,    koti-candra-susitala,*  
*jini’ karpura-vena-mula-candana*  
*eka-bara yara sparse,    smara-jvala-visa nase,*  
*yara sparse lubdha nari-mana*

**‘The combined cooling effect of camphor, roots of khasakhasa and sandalwood is surpassed by the coolness of Krsna’s palms and the soles of His feet, which are cooler and more pleasing than millions upon millions of moons. If women are touched by them even once, their minds are enticed, and the burning poison of lusty desire for Krsna is immediately vanquished.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**15.76**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/15.76)**))**

*ei vrajera ramani,    kamarka-tapta-kumudini,*  
*nija-karamrta diya dana*  
*praphullita kare yei, kahan mora candra sei,*  
*dekhaha, sakhi, rakha mora prana*

**“The women of Vrndavana are just like lilies growing hot in the sun of lusty desires. But moonlike Krsna makes them all jubilant by bestowing upon them the nectar of His hands. О My dear friend, where is My moon now? Save My life by showing Him tO Me!”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**19.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/19.38)**))**

*jiniya tamala-dyuti,    indranila-sama kanti,*  
*se kantite jagat mataya*  
*srngara-rasa-sara chani”, tate candra-jyotsna sani',*  
*jani vidhi niramila taya*

**‘Krsna’s bodily luster shines like the IndraNila gem and surpasses the luster of the Tamala tree. The luster of His body drives the entire world mad because Providence has made it transparent by refining the essence of the mellow of conjugal love and mixing it with moonshine.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLiia (**[**19.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/19.41)**))**

*namo maha-vadanyaya krsna-prema-pradaya te*  
*krsnaya krsna-caitanya-namne gaura-tvise namah*

Srila Locana dasa Thakur has also sung,

*anarpita-carim cirat karunayavatirnah kalau*

Consequently Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu is accepted as the most magnanimous incarnation. It is He only who distributed love of Krsna while exhibiting the superexcellence of loving Krsna in Conjugal rasa.**

*aisvarya-madhurya-karunye svarupa-purnata*

*yan-mitram paramananda*

### Verse 75

*antardhvantacayam samastajagatamunmulayanti hathat*  
*premanandarasambudhim niravadhi prodvelayanti balat*  
*visvam sitalayantyativa vikalam tapatrayenanisam*  
*sasmakam hrdaye cakastu cakitam caitanyacandracchata*

**Suddenly, the deep gloom of nescience in the jivas ’ hearts has been uprooted throughout the universe; the Ocean of Nectar of the Mellows of Love (prema) is in a constant state of agitation due to the force of the choppy waves of ecstatic emotions, ebbing and flowing as they are wont to. The universe is now suddenly filled with the cooling breezes of a moonlit night, whereas only a moment before it was engulfed in the raging fire of the threefold miseries. May the enlightening, cooling, soothing moonbeams from that DivineMoon, Sri CaitanyaCandra, that cause tides in the Ocean of Devotion, shine in our hearts, startling us into awareness, even if for only a moment.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Once again using the analogy of the moon, the author implores Sri GauraHari to enlighten his heart (consciousness). ‘May CaitanyaCandracchata (the rays of the moonlike Sri Caitanya) cakitam- if for only a moment, illuminate my heart. With sudden force (hathat), a single such ray fully dissipates the dense darkness of ignorance in the heart.’

The moon in the sky of this mundane world can only limitedly eradicate the darkness of night. It is not equipped to destroy the gloom of nescience in the hearts of the conditioned jivas. The rays emanating from Sri CaitanyaCandra create incessant high tides in the immense ocean of prema-rasa, inundating the entire universe with Premananda. These rays visvam sitalayanti- cool and sooth the residents of this material world, singed by the three-fold miseries (adhyamika, adhibautika, adhidaivika).

Karika:

*jagad antas tamo hantri premambudhi vivardhini*  
*cakastu hrdaye’smakam sri gauranga vidhucchata*

**‘The rays emanating from the moonlike Sri CaitanyaCandra destroy the darkness of ignorance in this world and expand the Ocean of Prema. May the brilliance of Sri GaurangaCandra illuminate our hearts.’**

**Purport**

The unlimited ocean of prema is like the all-pervasive Supreme Godhead, eternally present but unmanifest to gross, mundane vision. Only (santas) saintly souls whose eyes are anointed with the salve of prema can see it.

With the rising of the Moon Sri GaurangaCandra, this Ocean of Prema became turbulent. Sri Nityananda used His transcendental plough to excavate a canal and inundate the universe with prema. Thus does Sri Locan das Thakur sing:

*nitai guna mani amar, nitai guna mani*  
*aniya premer banya bhasayila avani*  
*premera banya laiya nitai aila gauda-dese*  
*dubila bhakata-gana dina hina bhase*  
*abaddha karuna-sindhu (nitai) katiya muhan*  
*ghare ghare bule prema, amiyar ban*

**‘My beloved Lord Nityananda is a jewel mine of wonderful qualities. Having brought a Flood of Love, he has caused this earth to float in that inundation. Bringing this Deluge of Prema with him, Nitai came to GaudaDesh (Bengal). The devotees drowned in this Ocean of Ambrosia, while the wretched and fallen were simply floating. Nitai cut a canal from this unbounded Ocean of Mercy, thus bringing a flood of nectarean prema to each and every home.’**

The SupremePreceptor Sri Gauranga has made it plain for all to see, that without Sri Guru's grace, visuddha-sattva (perception of pure transcendence) will always remain an elusive dream. Made turbid by contact with matter, man's consciousness can only be purged by offenseless chanting of the HolyNames. Sri Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur has commented in his purport to the first verse of Sri Siksastaka:

*sreyah-kairava-candrika-vitaranam. vidya-vadhu-jivanam*

“Whole-hearted chanting of Sri Krsna's HolyName is the highest goodness and munificence. Sreyah. benediction; kairava: white lilies; candrika: moon rays. Just as the illuminating, soothing rays of the rising moon highlight the white beauty of the lily in the night, similarly, the chanting of Sri Krsna's Name brings out the best in man and enlightens the darkened universe, showering it with Divine benediction. Human society cannot benefit from material desires for sense gratification, speculative knowledge or fruitive activities, but chanting Krsna's Names blesses all with the greatest prosperity.”

*yasya narayano devo bhagavan hrd-gatah sada*  
*bhaktya kevalayajnanam dhunoti dhvantam arkavat*

**‘Narayana, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is full in all opulences, is predominant within the core of your heart because of your being a pure devotee. He always drives away the darkness of ignorance, as the sun drives away the darkness of the universe.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**7.13.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/13.22)**))**

*manye tvam deva-devanam trayanam purusarsabham*  
*yad badhase guha-dhvantam pradipah prabhaya yatha*

**‘I think You are the Supreme Personality among the three chief gods, since You drive away the darkness of this cave as a lamp dispels darkness with its light.’ (SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.51.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/51.29)**))**

Srila Prabhupad:

“Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti points out that with His effulgence Lord Krsna dispelled not only the darkness of the mountain cave but also the darkness in MucuKunda’s heart. In Sanskrit the heart is sometimes metaphorically referred to as guha, “cavern,” a deep and secret place.”

*tarn nirvyajam bhaja guna-nidhe pavanam pavananam*  
*sraddha-rajyan-matir atitaram uttamah-sloka-maulim*  
*prodyann antah-karana-kuhare hanta yan-nama-bhanor*  
*abhaso ’pi ksapayati maha-pataka-dhvanta-rasim*

**‘O reservoir of all good qualities, just worship Sri Krsna, the purifier of all purifiers, the most exalted of the personalities worshiped by choice poetry. Worship Him with a faithful, unflinching mind, without duplicity and in a highly elevated manner. Thus worship the Lord, whose Name is like the sun, for just as a slight appearance of the sun dissipates the darkness of night, so a slight appearance of the HolyName of Krsna can drive away all the darkness of ignorance that arises in the heart, due to greatly sinful activities performed in previous lives.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**3.62**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/3.62)**))**

*dharmah projjhita-kaitavo ’tra paramo nirmatsaranam satam*  
*vedyam vastavam atra vastu sivadam tapa-trayonmulanam*  
*srimad-bhagavate maha-muni-krte kim va parair isvarah*  
*sadyo hrdy avarudhyate ’tra krtibhih susrusubhis tat-ksanat*

**‘Completely rejecting all religious activities which are materially motivated, this BhagavataPurana propounds the highest truth, which is understandable by those devotees who are fully pure in heart. The highest truth is reality distinguished from illusion for the welfare of all. Such truth uproots the threefold miseries. This beautiful Bhagavatam , compiled by the great sage VyasaDeva \[in his maturity\], is sufficient in itself for God realisation. What is the need of any other scripture? As soon as one attentively and submissively hears the message of Bhagavatam , by this culture of knowledge the Supreme Lord is established within his heart.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.1.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.2)**)**

*etat samsucitam brahmams*  
*tapa-traya-cikitsitam*  
*yad isvare bhagavati*  
*karma brahmani bhavitam*

**‘O Brahmana VyasDev, it is decided by the learned that the best remedial measure for removing all troubles and miseries is to dedicate one’s activities to the service of the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead \[Sri Krsna\].’**  
**(SrimadBhagavaiam (**[**1.5.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/5.32)**))**

### Verse 76

*ksanam ksinah pinah ksanamahaha sasruh ksanamatha*  
*ksanam smerah sitah ksanamanalataptah ksanamapi*  
*ksanam dhavan stabdhah ksanamadhikajalpan ksanamaho*  
*ksanam muko gaurah sphuratu mama deho bhagavatah*

**Aho! (I say!) Due to excessive devotional fervour, His transcendental body is sometimes waning and thin, sometimes waxing and obese; at times His eyes brim over with tears of ecstatic prema; at other times He smiles gleefully; again His body becomes cold and then burning hot; all of a sudden he takes off running at a swift clip, then the next thing you know, He is as though paralysed, completely inert; again He becomes garrulous, then suddenly He falls totally silent and grave, as though dumb. May the Supreme Personality Sri Gaura shine forth in my body.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In this verse the author again prays that Sri Gauranga, the embodiment of the most amazing ecstatic emotions and transformations, will manifest His presence within him.

‘May bhagavatah- the golden form of the Supreme Personality Sri Krsna spring forth within my body.’

Some of the ecstatic features (anubhava) of Sri Gauranga are being described: Consumed by the ecstatic emotions of Srimati Radhika, while experiencing love-in-separation, Sri Gauranga’s body momentarily (ksanam) becomes feeble and emaciated. Then again, while directly perceiving Sri Krsna’s presence, his body appears nourished and robust. Then joyful tears (sasruh) cascade from his eyes. Ahaha! (This is truly amazing!)

‘Why must it be concluded that he sheds tears of joy?’

Earlier his body was scorched by pangs of separation, but now, feeling Krsna’s direct presence, he feels cool (sitah). This gives way to smerah- a shy smile plays on his lips and his face brightens as he shares a humorous exchange with Sri Krsna. Then, the next moment, he is burning in the fire of prema-vaicittya- experiencing intense feelings of separation even in the close presence of the beloved.

*priyasya sannikarse’pi premotkarsa svabhavatah*  
*ya vislesa dhiyarttis tat prema-vaicittyam ucyate*

**‘Due to the capricious and intense nature of the exalted realm of prema, even if the lover is intimately close to the beloved, she nevertheless becomes very anxious, thinking he may leave. This feeling of deep consternation is known as prem a-vaiClttya. ’**  
**(UjjvalNilamani(15.147))**

Steeped in the loving sentiments of Srimati Radhika, Sri Gaura is scorched in the fire of separation, thinking, ‘Where did Krsna go?’ although he is right next to him. Then, he imagines that Sri Krsna is running away from him, and so he calls out, ‘You are captured!’ Saying this, Gaura runs to another place (dhavan), and instantly, as if embraced by Sri Krsna, he experiences simultaneous exhilaration and anger. Then he remains very still (stabdah), as if rooted to the spot.

Thereafter, Sri Gaura begins to excessively censure (adhikajalpan) Sri Krsna, saying, ‘O crest-jewel among debauchees! О paragon of illogical and harsh words. You restless vagabond! Your heart is bereft of love. You ravisher of chaste wives. Don’t you dare touch me! Stay away from me.’

Then he becomes silent (mukah), as he imagines Krsna saying, ‘O my lady-love, controller of my heart! Kindly forgive me. I will never again act in this manner. I am your obedient servitor.’ However, Sri Gaura, in the mood of Srimati Radhika,remains silent, due to the appearance of mana (amour-propresulking due to wounded feelings).

Karika:

*anubhavadi bhavanam savalyodaya santibhak*  
*bhavamudreksito gauro harih sphuratu me hrdi*

**‘Due to the mingling of different bhavas, the Lord feels excessively distraught, only to completely embody total peace and passivity a few moments later. May Sri GauraHari, overcome by an abundance of ecstatic emotions, spring forth in my heart.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“In this verse the author describes the different ecstatic symptoms of prema. The condition of Srimati Radha in vipralambha-bhava, feeling a long and intense separation from her beloved Lord SyamSundar, is here delineated. Sri GauraHari, immersed in RadhaBhava, feels intense separation from his beloved Sri Krsna. In viraha-bhava, his body shrivels up. Again, by remembering his beloved Krsna in vipralambha-bhava, Sri GauraHari’s body expands and becomes obese. Simply by remembering the Lord, he feels infinitely elated and tears of joy stream from his eyes. When Sri GauraHari pines for Krsna in the fire of separation, he is extremely besotted, and then as the darling of his heart, Sri Krsna appears, his body cools down in contentment. As Krsna reveals himself, Sri GauraHari is jubilant on receiving this fleeting association; He begins to laugh and make merry.  
“Then, due to prema-vaicittya (feeling of separation although the beloved is present), Sri GauraHari is incinerated for that moment. Fraught with the thought that his beloved may abandon his company, Sri GauraHari chases after Sri Krsna. Again feeling the touch of Sri Krsna’s body for a moment, Sri GauraHari is paralysed (stambhita- one of the eight ecstatic physical transformations). Then, like Srimati Radhika, Sri GauraHari shies away from his beloved’s touch, raving madly, ‘O You licentious rogue! You ravager of chaste women. Don’t you dare touch me!’  
“After this outburst (prajalpa), Sri GauraHari becomes silent and grave, overcome by mana, a lover’s pique.”

In Lord Krsna’s Lila, pastimes are of two categories - prakata (manifest) and aprakata (unmanifest). Manifest pastimes {prakata) are time-bound, while his aprakata-lila is eternal. Viraha (love in separation) is a part of prakata-lila. In aprakata-lila there is no going away, or returning. Whereas in prakata-lila, Krsna left Vrndavana for Mathura, leaving the residents of Vraja in deep despair (viraha).

**‘The Lord’s eternal pastimes{nitya-lila) remain eternally uninterrupted in their unmanifest form. Because nitya-lila flows incessantly, sometimes in prakata-lila the Vrajabasis externally experience separation from Krsna, when He goes away; but internally, Krsna, in His nitya-aprakata-lila, is always manifest to the residents of Vraja.’**  
**(Sri BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**3.3.128**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/3.3.128)**))**

vipralamba- to be present with Krsna, in separation from Him  
viraha- feeling only separation

### Verse 77

*patrapatravicaranam na kurute na svarh param viksyate*  
*deyadeyavimarsako na hi na va kalapratiksah prabhuh*  
*sadyo yah sravaneksana-pranamana-dhyanadina durlabham*  
*datte bhakti rasam sa eva bhagavan gaurah param me gatih*

**The fully independent Supreme Personality, when bequeathing loving devotion (bhakti rasam), does not judge the eligibility of the receiver or the extent of his inclination, neither does He wait for an auspicious moment, or differentiate about the quality of incentive from person to person. This most rare gift, rarely obtained through the practices of hearing topics about Sri Krsna, seeing the Lord’s Deity form, offering obeisance to Him, meditating on Him, and the like, He alone can offer, without hesitation. Thus, SriGauraSundar is my only momentum and destination.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

This verse expresses the author’s single-minded attachment to devotional service at the lotus feet of this Divine Personality Sri GauraHari. Who else can exhibit such infinite compassion in distributing the most confidential and most rare of spiritual gems - KrsnaPrema - to one and all, without consideration of the recipient’s eligibility or ineligibility, qualifications or lack thereof?

Sa eva bhagavan- Sri GauraHari alone is his worshipful Lord, no other, including even other forms of the same SupremeLord, since in the matter of bestowing bhakti-rasa he doesn’t discriminate against anyone. He gives instantly (sadya).

One may ask, ‘what is so special about this bhakti-rasa?’ sravaneksana-pranamana-dhyanadina durlabham- this unique form of bhakti-rasa is unattainable even by the practice of sravana, darsan, pranam, dhyan, and so on. Sravan- hearing topics about Sri Krsna; darsan- seeing the Deity form of the Lord, or his devotees; pranam- offering worship and obeisance to Lord Jagannath; dhyan- meditating on or remembering the Divine qualities and pastimes of Sri Krsna.

A justified question may be asked, as to why such a rare and precious object is given away indiscriminately?

The answer: prabhuh- the bestower is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, absolutely independent, free to act as he pleases, thus the question is redundant and irrelevant. The SupremeLord's actions do not come under any form of scrutiny or purview of any rules.

In all activities other than devotional service to the SupremeLord, time, place and circumstances must be taken into consideration. If there is any delay in executing devotional service, due to waiting for a propitious moment, and in the meantime the mortal body perishes, then the result will be disastrous. On the other hand, while executing ordinary activities, if due to mistakes of inauspicious time, uncleanliness, etc., the performance is imperfect, then simply by chanting the HolyNames of the Lord, all errors are rectified. So how can devotional service to the SupremeLord be contaminated by errors of time, place and circumstance?

*mantratas tantratas chidram desa kalarha vastutah*  
*sarvam karoti nischidram anusankirtanam tava*

**‘There may be discrepancies in pronouncing mantras and observing regulative principles, and, moreover, there may be discrepancies in regard to time, place, person and paraphernalia. But when your Lordship’s HolyName is chanted, everything becomes faultless.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**8.23.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-8/23.16)**))**

Karika:

*patrasvapara kaladi nirapeksi sudurllabham*  
*datte prema-rasam yo vai sa me gauraharir gatih*

**‘Sri GauraHari, without any prejudice or consideration of eligibility or ineligibility, time, place, and so on, nonetheless awards the most rare spiritual gift of prema-bhakti tо whomever He pleases. He is the only goal of my life, my only destination.’**

sudurlabham- which is not at all possible to be obtained by contaminated souls (but everything can be possible by the mercy of the Supreme Lord).

**Purport**

The Supreme Lord is fully independent (svarat). He is omnipotent, the source of all energies, both material and spiritual. He is the SupremeAutocrat, not accountable for his actions to anyone but himself. On the battlefield of Kuruksetra. the Supreme Personality Sri Krsna disbursed his mercy in measured degree.

**‘All of them - as they surrender unto Me - I reward accordingly.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**4.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)**))**

However, in his golden incarnation as Sri GauraSundar, the Lord opens the floodgates of the reservoir of prema-rasa, for all to relish; unconditionally.

As the Supreme Lord’s eternal parts and parcel, the living entities are, by their original constitutional position, inheritors of the Lord’s mercy. Their stint in a corporeal body in the material world brings them in intimate contact with matter, and a strong bond develops over millions of lifetimes. In this process, they often forget their real spiritual identity as the Lord’s eternal servitors. The Supreme Lord descends in every millennium to remind his deluded, materially conditioned, spiritual offspring of their original spiritual identity and their original eternal home in Vaikuntha. In all other incarnations the Supreme Lord sets his agenda, but in KaliYuga, his only agenda is to inspire everyone to realize that they have lost their connection with the Supreme Lord. Thus Sri KrsnaCaitanya, the most munificent of all incarnations, never judges the eligibility of the recipient before he gives his mercy.

His mercy descends unsolicited and unsought. This is the meaning of ahaituki-krpa, causeless mercy. Like the Supreme Lord Himself, His Mercy is also transcendental and omnipotent, non-different from the Lord Himself and invested with all His Divine potencies. The HolyNames, especially in KaliYuga, represent the Lord’s Mercy Potency. But for the conditioned jiva , it is not possible to be a commensurate receptacle of His mercy. The jiva would simply be overpowered were he to receive this mercy directly. To bear the tremendous gushing force of GangaDevi as she descends from the heavenly planets, only Lord Siva is capable of receiving her in his matted locks. Similarly, only Lord Nityananda Prabhu is able to hold the omnipotent force of the Lord’s causeless mercy, and then disburse it to all and sundry. Without first approaching Lord Nityananda, no one can withstand the impact of the Lord’s direct mercy. Thus Srila Vrndavan das Thakur in the fourth stanza of his SriSri NityanandAstakam, says: “O my dear Brother! What will be the fate of the conditioned souls born in the sinful age of Kali? You (Sri KrsnaCaitanya) My Lord, by Your causeless mercy must think of an easy way to deliver them from maya and offer them the shade of Your lotus feet. While walking together with his Prabhu, Lord Nityananda would discuss such matters in this way with Lord Caitanya. So simply worship Lord Nityananda, the root of the creeper of devotion.”

Lord Nityananda (Balaram) is adi-guru, the original source and embodiment of guru-tattva. The bonafide MahaBhagavat guru from an authorized parampara, is a representative of Lord Nityananda in whom guru-tattva is manifest. Such a guru knows the heart and the degree of dedication of the aspirant devotee, and accordingly he allows the Supreme Lord’s ahaituki-krpa to flow through him to the conditioned souls. The Lord’s mercy is ever-present; to be received by the sincere and faithful seeker. But first one must take shelter of Sri Guru.

### Verse 78

*papiyanapi hinajatirapi duhsilo’pi duskarmanam*  
*simapi svapacadhamo’pi satatam durwasanadhyo’pi ca*  
*durddesaprabhavo’pi tatra vihitavaso’pi duhsangato*  
*nasto’pyuddhrta eva yena krpaya tam gauramevasraye*

**He has bestowed His mercy on those most wicked of all sinners; on those born in the lower castes; those of bad character, those whose nefarious activities know no limit; despicable wretches, lower than dog-eating candalas, venal and characterless persons, continually besieged by vain desires; those who, due to the weight of their past sinful activities, take birth in God-forsaken countries where holy Mother Ganga refuses to flow and great devotees like the Pandavas refused to visit, where only bad association is present; His mercy is there for even the most abhorring, licentious persons. I take shelter of Sri GauraSundar, who alone can ferry such souls across the dangerous ocean of material existence.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The respected author asserts his dedication to remain in the shelter of Sri Caitanya, who’s unlimited generosity showers down upon the most fallen degenerates and derelicts, delivering them from the ocean of misery. Once in the safe sanctuary of his lotus feet, they begin to taste the nectar of prema-rasa. In this way He makes them His own.

‘What sort of persons does he deliver?’

Papiyan- even a most sinful brahmana, infected with leprosy (GopalCapal); hina-jati- Srivasa Thakur’s yavana (Muslim) tailor; duhsila- persons with bad habits (like the tax collectors of Remuna); duskarmanam simapi- the most despicable brahmana brothers, Jagai and Madhai, who stole others’ wives, robbed brahmanas, were always drunk and engaged in the most abominable activities - He has accepted all of them into his own family of devotees. Due to their nefarious ways, the two brothers, Jagai and Madhai never performed penances and their dreadful habits made them repeatedly engage in sinful activities. Even dog-eating candalas have a chance to obtain release from the result of their sinful activities, but these two most evil amongst the brahmanas, have hardly a chance. Sri GauraHari delivers even durddesa-prabhavo ’pi- those born in countries or kingdoms held to ransom by pirates and dacoits. Whether born in a pious place, or an impious place, Sri GauraHari’s mercy is still available.

Karika:

*nicatinica papistha dusta nastasca durjjanah*  
*yenoddhrta sa gaurango hair evasrayo mama*

**‘May Sri Gauranga, who is the saviour of the lowest of the low - vicious sinners, evildoers, dissolute and virtueless persons - be my only refuge.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur writes in his commentary (AmrtaPravahaBhasya) to Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila ([17.35-45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/17.35)):

“Every night when Sriman Mahaprabhu relished the nectar of kirtana-rasa behind closed doors in Srivasa Thakur’s house, many envious and mundane residents of Navadvip tried in devious ways to ridicule the Vaisnavas and disrupt their kirtana. A certain brahmana, GopalCapal by name, placed paraphernalia for DurgaDevi’s worship in front of Srivasa’s house one night. On a banana-leaf, he put red hibiscus, red sandalwood paste, wine, and such. For this grievous offense against a pure Vaisnava, GopalCapal was infected with the worst type of leprosy.  
“Vaisnavas worship only the Supreme Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna or His innumerable expansions. Hibiscus, sandalwood paste mixed with vermilion, wine, and such, are never used in Lord Visnu’s worship. GopalCapal did what he did to discredit Srivas Thakur and the Vaisnavas.  
“Later he regretted his act and realized that he had committed a serious mistake. Soon after he was infected with leprosy, he approached the Lord on the banks of MaGahga, begging forgiveness. But the Lord was not ready to forgive him for the following reasons: that he was not fully sincere, secondly, the grievousness of the offense, and most importantly, to teach the world about the consequences of vaisnava-aparadha, which retards all spiritual progress. Finally, when Sri KrsnaCaitanya returned to Bengal as a sannyasi, on being once again implored by the leper GopalCapal, the Lord suggested he request forgiveness from Srivas Thakur, the Vaisnava whom he had offended. GopalCapal was not only cured of his leprosy but also of his spiritual blindness, a much worse disease than leprosy.”  
'There is no limit to Jagai and Madhai’s sinful activities; there is not a sin they have not committed. Although born in a brahmana family, they are drunkards; they eat beef and always engage in arson, looting and robbing innocent victims.'  
(Sri CaitanyaBhagavata MadhyaLila ([13.32-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-madhya/13.32)))

Lord Nityananda and Srila Haridas Thakur took it upon themselves to reform Jagai and Madhai. Once, when Nityananda Prabhu asked them to chant Krsna’s names and give up their errant ways, they in turn chased after him and Sri Haridas. Later that night, in an encounter with them, Madhai became so furious, he threw a piece of broken clay pot at Lord Nityananda, opening a deep gash on his forehead and spilling blood profusely. As long as the two reprobates desisted from committing vaisnava-aparadha they were spared from the Supreme Lord’s wrath. Sinful actions beget suffering and distress but can be counteracted by Vedic injunctions and rituals. However, vaisnava-aparadha cannot be nullified by any means, save and except falling at the feet of the offended Vaisnava, sincerely begging his forgiveness and constantly chanting the HolyNames with genuine remorse for one’s offenses. This heinous vaisnava-aparadha was enough for Lord Caitanya to call upon his weapon, Sudarsana Cakra. What saved the two brothers was that they fell at Lord Nityananda’s and Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, praying for mercy.

### Verse 79

*kalindatanayatate sphuradamandavrndavanam*  
*vihaya lavanambudheh pulina puspa vatim gatah*  
*dhrtarunapatah parihrtasupitavasa haris*  
*tirohita nijacchabih prakatagaurima me gatih*

**The Supreme Personality Sri Hari left the splendorous groves of Vrndavana, very beautifully situated on the banks of YamunaDevi, to roam the lush, verdant flower-gardens on the shores of the salty ocean. His magnificent yellow dress is now without a master, since he has accepted flowing robes dyed the color of the rising sun. He has hidden His own dark, fresh monsoon-cloud complexion with the brilliant lustre of molten gold. He alone is my final destination.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

As substantiation of the truth that Sri Krsna (fountainhead of all incarnations), son of MaharajNanda, has advented in the form of Sri Gauranga, the revered author reasserts his dedication to Sri Gaura, by affectionately describing his disappearance from VrajaBhumi, and appearance in GauraMandalaBhumi.

Sri GauraHari is me gatih- my final destination.

Having forsaken beautiful Vrindaban, trembling with the vigour of ecstatic emotions, pleasantly situated on the banks of YamunaDevi, the daughter of Kalinda (the mountain Kalinda is referred to as the father of the Yamuna River \[Kalindi\] since this mountain is her source), that SupremePersonality has gone to reside in the flower bowers on the shore of the salt ocean. His brilliant yellow dress is now without a master, since he has now donned cloth the colour of the rising sun.

tirohita nijacchabih- He has hidden within himself his iridescent, bluish lustre that mocks the patina of a blue sapphire, and in its place accepted a brilliant golden complexion (the spiritual sentiments and complexion of his beloved Srimati Radhika). He is my only gatih- means, shelter, recourse, protection, motion, course, progress and final destination.

Karika:

*radhikarupamasadya tirohita-nijacchavih*  
*pahvarttita llladir gatir gauraharir mama*

**‘In order to encounter (attain) the form of Srimati Radhika, he (Sri GauraHari) has hidden his own lustre, exchanging it with her own, thus accepting at the same time her pastimes and sentiments. That same Sri GauraHari is my only destination.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna only leaves his garden bowers of earthly (prapanca) Vrindaban in his prakata-lila, not the Goloka Vrndavana of his eternal aprakata-lila.

*krsno ’nyo yadu-sambhulo yah pumah so ’sty atah parah*  
*vrndavanam parityajya sa kvacin naiva gacchati*

**‘The Krsna, known as YaduKumar, is VasudevKrsna. He is different from Krsna, the son of NandaMaharaj. As YaduKumar Krsna, He leaves Vrindaban to enact pastimes in Mathura and Dvaraka, but NandaNandan Krsna never at anytime leaves Vrindaban.’**  
**(Sri YamalaTantra quoted in LaghuBhagavatamrta (**[**1.5.461**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/lb/1.5.461)**))**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya is none other than VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna, the son of NandaMaharaj. NandaNandan Krsna did not leave Vrindaban to come to Nilacala. He brought it with him when he came as Sri GauraHari. As Sri KrsnaCaitanya, not only has he covered his blackish complexion with Srimati Radharani’s golden bodily effulgence and spiritual sentiments, but he has also shrouded his Supreme Divinity with the devotional sentiments of a rasika PremiBhakta. He is thus known as channa-avatar (as confirmed in SrimadBhagavatam [7.9.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/9.38)).

As Sri KrsnaCaitanya, he took sannyasa initiation from Sri KesavBharati, putting on the saffron robes of the renounced order. He entered this asrama primarily to instruct and benedict mankind. The other reasons for taking sannyasa were to fulfil the prophecy of Srila VyasaDev, and to uphold the curse of a brahmana who was debarred from participating in the nocturnal kirtan, behind closed doors at SrivasAngan (Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila [17.60-63](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/17.60)). In MahaBharata, Srila VyasaDev has prophesied the appearance and sannyasa initiation of Sri Caitanya:

*suvarna-varno hemango varangas candanangadi*  
*sannyasa-krc chamah santo nistha-santi-parayanah*

**‘The Supreme Lord’s bodily lustre is the colour of molten gold. His bodily features and construction are exquisite and proportionate. His body is smeared with sandalwood paste. He will enter the fourth and highest spiritual order (sannyasa). He will be self-controlled, peaceful, of fixed resolve in spiritual practice, bringing peace through the propagation of the HolyNames, and will be always steeped in the ecstasy of prema.’**  
**(VisnuSahasraNama)**

*tyaktva sudustyaja-surepsita-rajya-laksmim*  
*dharmistha arya-vacasa yad agad aranyam*  
*maya-mrgam dayitayepsitam anvadhavad*  
*vande maha-purusa te caranaravindam*

**‘We offer our respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of the Lord, upon whom one should always meditate. He left his householder life, leaving aside his eternal consort (LaksmiDevi), whom even the denizens of heaven adore. He went into the forest to deliver the fallen souls, who are put into illusion by the material energy.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.34**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.34)**))**

*рауо-rases tire sphurad-upavanali-kalanaya*  
*muhur vrndaranya-smarana-janita-prema-vivasah*  
*kvacit krsnavrtti-pracala-rasano bhakti-rasika*  
*sa caitanyah kim me punar api drsor yasyati padam*

**‘Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu is the topmost of all devotees. Sometimes, while walking on the beach, he would see a beautiful garden nearby and mistake it for the forest of Vrndavana. Thus was he completely overwhelmed by ecstatic love of Krsna while chanting the HolyNames and dancing. His tongue worked incessantly as he chanted, ‘Krsna! Krsna!’ Will he again become visible in the path of my eyes?’**  
**(Caitanyastaka (6) / StavaMala quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**15.97**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/15.97)**))**

## PART VIII - Instructions to Benefit the Masses General Education

### Verse 80

*are mudha gudham vicinuta harerbhaktipadavim*  
*daviyasya drstyapyaparicitapurwam munivaraih*  
*na visrambhascitte yadi yadi ca daurlabhyamiva tat*  
*parityajyasesam brajata saranam gauracaranam*

**О you foolish lot! Search for that most obscure and confidential path of devotional service to the Supreme Lord Hari, unknown even to great sages endowed with farsightedness and introspective vision. If you do not believe in this, or consider this path almost impossible to achieve, then reject your mental conceptions and simply seek shelter at the lotus feet of the SupremeLord Sri GauraHari.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In the next twenty verses, our esteemed author urges the population of MotherEarth to worship and serve the lotus feet of Sri KrsnaCaitanya. In KaliYuga, Sri Caitanya is the sole object of worship. Without His shelter it is not possible to be lifted out of this ocean of nescience and faults and attain nigudha-prema-bhakti (the essence of all revealed scriptures). Since it is impossible to obtain the most confidential spiritual perfection (VrajaPrema) without taking refuge of Sri Caitanya, it is being stressed that everyone develop the attitude of surrender at His lotus-feet - Are mudha! О you foolish lot! Harer bhakti- search out the illuminated path of prema-bhakti.

One may ask, ‘why must one look for this path?’

It is so highly confidential (gudham) that it was unknown even to the personified Vedas. Moreover, knowledge of VrajaPrema is beyond the grasp of even the great sages and philosophers like Srila VyasDev, though they witnessed its existence in deep samadhi. It is so very far away; how can one attain intimate knowledge only with one’s sight? be it farsightedness or subtle, inner vision. Unprecedented VrajaPrema was not known or revealed by anyone to anyone before, so it remained unattained by even great spiritual preceptors.

One may quite rightly wonder if Srila VyasDev could not obtain it, how can such a foolish lot as us be successful? This doubt is addressed by saying asesam parityajya- simply relinquish all attachments and mental conceptions and surrender to Sri GauraHari. For those who have taken shelter at His lotus feet this most abstruse knowledge of VrajaPrema soon becomes manifest.

Karika:

*srutigudha mahabhaktau durllabhayam munisvaraih*  
*pravesaya visantu sri gauranga-pada-pankajam*

**‘Those desirous of entering the path to the most exalted level of bhakti, a deep secret of the Vedas, rarely obtained even by the best of sages and devoted souls, must simply surrender at the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga.’**

**Purport**

**‘All living entities are born into delusion...... ’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**7.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.27)**))**

**‘People in the contaminated age of Kali are quarrelsome, lazy, misguided.... ’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.1.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.10)**))**

As described by Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati in this verse, the people of this age are mudhas (foolish, but proud). When even introspective sages, gifted with untold depths of perception, were unable to search out the transcendental path of pure bhakti, ‘the king of education, most secret of all secrets, the purest of knowledge, the perfection of religion, everlasting and joyfully performed’ - then what to speak of mudhas! How can they find out the truth?

*vedesu durlabham adurlabham atma-bhaktau*

**‘Govinda, the primeval Supreme Lord is inaccessible to the Vedas, but is obtainable only by pure unalloyed devotion of the soul**  
**(BrahmaSamhita (**[**33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/33)**))**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

“The transcendental Absolute is beyond the reach of the Vedas. The Vedas originate in sound and sound originates in the mundane ether. So the Vedas cannot present before us a direct view of the transcendental world (Goloka). It is only when the Vedas are imbued with cit potency that they are enabled to approach transcendence. But Goloka reveals itself to every jiva soul when he is under the influence of the spiritual cognitive potency, joined to the Essence of Ecstatic Energy. The ecstatic function of devotion is boundless and is surcharged with unalloyed transcendental knowledge. That knowledge reveals Goloka-tattva (the principle of the Highest transcendence) in unison with devotion, without asserting itself separately, but as a subsidiary of unalloyed devotion.”

In KaliYuga especially, Lord Caitanya is the only source. of pure, unalloyed devotion that leads to KrsnaPrema, devoid of sambhoga (the desire for self-gratification in srngara-rasa). Designated as the YugaAvatar, He inaugurated sankirtana, the prescribed dharma for this age. Chanting the HolyNames (MahaMantra) of the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna without offense is the surest method for attaining KrsnaPrema. By taking shelter of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, the jiva is initiated into the process of NamaSeva by a pure devotee of Sri GauraCandra. Nama first reveals rupa, the eternal, thrice-bent form of SyamSundar, in the heart and on the mirror of the chanter’s purified consciousness. Then gradually rupa is followed by guna, Krsna’s transcendental qualities, and so on, till, by the grace of guru and Sri Gauranga, one becomes eligible to serve the DivineCouple as a palya dasi, a maid-servant of Srimati Radhika.

*hare krsna hare krsna krsna krsna hare hare*  
*hare rama hare rama rama rama hare hare*  
*iti sodasakam namnam kali-kalmasa-nasanam*  
*natah parataropayah sarva-vedesu drsyate*

‘The sixteen words of the HareKrsna mantra are especially meant for nullifying the sinful contaminations of KaliYuga. There is no better alternative for this purpose than to chant the MahaMantra. This conclusion has been ascertained by thorough research throughout the entire Vedic literature.’  
(KaliSantarana Upanisad)

### Verse 81

*dadhanmurddhanyurddhvam mukulita karambhojayugalam*  
*galannetrambhobhih snapitamrdugandasthalayugam*  
*dukulenavitam navakamalakinjalkarucina*  
*param jyotirgauram kanakarucicauram pranamata*

**His lotus palms joined together above His head, His tender cheeks are bathed by a cascade of tears. His garments are the colour of the saffron filaments of fresh lotus flowers. Offer obeisances to the Supreme Brahman (ParamJyotih), Sri GauraSundar, that thief who has stolen Her brilliant, golden bodily lustre.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri Gauranga is offered obeisance with a description of His sublime loveliness, one of His transcendental weapons with which He dispenses the sacrosanct treasure of prema-bhakti.

Param jyotigauram- the SupremePersonality Sri Gaura is heralded by the Upanisads as ParamBrahma. Therefore, kindly fall supine {pranamata) at His lotus feet to offer your obeisance; take complete shelter there at His lotus feet. Kanaka-ruci-cauram- He is a thief who has stolen the golden complexion of Srimati Radhika and is now beaming with her lustre. dadhanmurddhanyurddhvam mukulita karambhojayugalam- His lotus hands are joined together in worship above his head. His delicate cheeks are lavished with an incessant shower of tears (galannetrambhobhih). He wears garments coloured the hue of the saffron filaments of a lotus flower (nava kamalakinjilka). Simply worship that golden incarnation Sri GauraHari!

Karika:

*siro ’njalir galannetram vibhracchona varambaram*  
*tapta-kancana gaurangam pranamantu mahah param*

**‘Offer repeated obeisances to Sri GauraHari, who prays with folded palms touched to His head, whose face is inundated with tears, who wears cloth the colour of the rising sun and whose Divinely effulgent complexion is more resplendent than molten gold.’**

**Purport**

Realisation of the unparalleled beauty of the SupremeLord is an all-important and inherent aspect of the Supreme Brahman that the unfortunate Mayavadis are deprived of. Here the author focuses our attention on the personal form of the Supreme Brahman.

Like His lotus feet (implying service), so does His beauty (another manifestation of His Mercy Potency) evoke bhakti-rasa in the hearts of everyone fortunate enough to behold His exquisite sat-cid-ananda-vigraha. As a father is always anxious for his children’s well being, so is the jiva’s Supreme Father constantly thinking of ways and means to end the sufferings of His eternal parts and parcels. To this end, His irresistible good looks attract the jivas to give up their taste for mundane objects and develop a taste for higher spiritual rasa.

All the attributes and qualities that adorn the Supreme Lord’s personality and bodily features are transcendental. Mundane similes and analogies help the jiva to get a mere glimpse of the Absolute Reality. Hence Srila Rupa Gosvami prays to Lord Krsna, begging Him to forgive him for this offense of trying to compare the Supreme Lord’s beauty with mundane objects. He also laments the fact that nothing in the mundane world is anywhere close to the Supreme Lord’s Divine attributes. All that the conditioned jiva requires, is to become attracted to and develop attachment for any one of the innumerable transcendental qualities of the Supreme Lord. The hunchback Kubja, of Mathura, was so attracted by the charming looks of the gallant young Krsna that she was immediately purified of all material contamination in her heart.

### Verse 82

*bhratah kirttaya nama gokulapateruddama-namavalim*  
*yadva bhavaya tasya divyamadhuram rupam jaganmangalam*  
*hanta premamaharasojjvalapade nasapi te sambhavet*  
*sri caitanyamahaprabhor yadi krpadrstih patenna tvayi*

**Dear brothers! You may loudly chant the supremely potent names of Sri Krsna, Lord of Gokul, or meditate on His Divinely sweet form that bewilders the entire universe, however, (Alas!), if Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s merciful glance does not caress you, then it will be impossible for you to even hope to attain that most exalted of all spiritual rasas (madhurya- conjugal, erotic sentiments), the ambrosia of the Gopis love for Sri Krsna.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

If one is truly desirous of attaining the purest prema-bhakti, then neither chanting Sri Krsna’s HolyNames, nor meditating on His exquisite form will make one successful. Success is assured only by receiving the merciful glance of Sri Caitanya.

Bhratah kirttaya- О brothers! You may chant in any manner, millions of times, all the most spiritually potent Names of the Lord of Gokul; or meditate on His splendorously radiant beauty, more nectarean than heavenly ambrosia. However, if Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s glance has not touched you, then you will not taste the sublime rasa of the most exalted prema-bhakti. Prema maha rasojjvala pade- the topmost loving emotion - erotic, conjugal emotions experienced with the SupremePerson (GopiPrema).

In the AmaraKosa (dictionary), srhgarah (conjugal rasa) has been defined as pure and resplendent; thus the gopis’ love for Krsna is sacred, transcendental.

Karika:

*sri саitanya-krparupa drstistvayi paten nahi*  
*dhyanadi napi krsnasya nasa prema-rasojjvale*

**‘If Sri Caitanya’s merciful glance has not touched you. then there is not the slightest hope that you may taste conjugal prema-rasa, even though you meditate on Sri Krsna’s Form, Pastimes, Name, and so on.’**

**Purport**

VrajendraNandan Krsna’s pleasure potency, hladini-sakti, is His internal. Divine energy. The Supreme Personality Sri RadhaRaman derives ultimate pleasure and satisfaction from His hladini-sakti, embodied in the most sublime form of Srimati Radhika. Devotees who worship the Supreme Lord, under the shelter of hladini-sakti derive maximum, ever increasing ecstatic bliss, not available from any other form of worship.

Prior to Lord Caitanya's advent, the world was deprived of the rarefied atmosphere of bhakti-rasa. The ecstasy of kamanuga-bhakti in mahjari-bhava was revealed to the world only after Lord Caitanya initiated His sankirtan movement:

*anarpita-carim cirat karunayavatirnah kalau*

**‘Out of His causeless mercy, the Supreme Lord advented in KaliYuga to distribute the most exalted devotional love (bhakti-rasa), never ever given before.’ So even if a devotee chants the all-potent HolyNames of Lord Sri Krsna, or meditates on His unparalleled beauty, without the grace of Sri Caitanya coming through the via medium of Sri Nityananda Prabhu and the other devotees of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, no one can attain the ecstatic devotional mood of manjari-bhava in kamanuga-bhakti, the ultimate in loving surrender unto the DivineCouple.**

### Verse 83

*aye na kuru sahasam tava hasanti sarwodyamam*  
*janah parita unmada harirasamrtasvadinah*  
*idantu nibhrtam srnu pranayavastu prastuyate*  
*yadeva nigamesu tat patirayam hi gaurah param*

**Ohe! Seek shelter confidently at Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet and embark not upon another spiritual path; those great souls inebriated with the ambrosia of KrsnaPrema, associates of Sri GauraHari, will laugh at your enthusiastic attempts in trying out other processes. Now listen to a well-kept secret - the Lord and Master of the subject matter \[pranaya (love of Krsna)\] of the Vedic literatures is none other than Sri GauraHari.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may raise an objection, that according to other gurus, by following the instructions of the Vedas and Agamas, and by practicing spiritual discipline (sadhana), human beings will ultimately reach the stage of perfection. Therefore, ‘what is the necessity of receiving Sri Caitanya’s merciful glance?’

Aye na kuru sahasam- О brothers! Do not be eager about taking up any spiritual discipline if it does not lead to surrender at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.

‘Why?’

Janah hasanti- seeing your enthusiasm, the devotees of Sri Caitanya will gather round to laugh and ridicule you since they alone are relishing the nectar of prema-rasa. Bhakti-rasa is the real nectar of immortality. Those who have tasted it become unmadah- mad with exultation. By drinking this nectar of KrsnaPrema, the GauraBhaktas are completely immersed in ecstatic love.

You may ask, ‘then what are we to do? kindly instruct us.’

Idantu nibhrtam srnu- just hear this esoteric truth - the transcendental principle of DivineLove (prema, pranaya) described in the Vedas is the SupremeLord himself, more specifically His pleasure potency, Srimati Radha Thakurani. Simultaneously, the object of that love and the bestower of that love is Sri GauraHari. Simply by taking shelter at His lotus feet, all perfection is attained.

Karika:

*tavanyacestane gaurabhakta atha hasanti hi*  
*srutyagamacarad vastu patim Gaurangamasraya*

**‘Sri Gauranga’s devotees will laugh at you if you endeavour in any other spiritual path, so simply take shelter of Sri Gauranga, who is the Lord and master of Prema, sought after by the Vedas and Agamas.’**

**Purport**

Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati warns us not to misuse our intrepidness (sahasam) trying out other spiritual paths instead of confidently taking shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya. In KaliYuga NamSankirtan is the prescribed religion for the age and Sri GauraHari is the YugaAvatar who initiated this yuga-dharma for the benefit of the entire world:

*dhyayan krte yajan yajnais tretayam dvapare ’rcayan*  
*yad apnoti tad apnoti kalau sahkirtya kesavam*

**‘The supreme spiritual goal, attained by meditation on Sri Hari in SatyaYuga, by performing fire sacrifices in TretaYuga and by worshipping the Deity form of Sri Krsna in DvaparYuga, is easily obtained by chanting His HolyNames in KaliYuga.’**  
**(**[**VisnuPurana**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp)**)**

*krte yad dhyayato visnum tretayam yajato makhaih*  
*dvapare paricaryayam kalau tad dhari-kirtanat*

**‘Whatever result was obtained in SatyaYuga by meditating on Visnu, in TretaYuga by performing sacrifices, and in DvaparYuga by serving the Lord’s lotus feet, can be obtained in KaliYuga simply by chanting the Hare Krsna MahaMantra.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**12.3.52**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.52)**))**

Sri Caitanya revealed to the world for the first time, that the four aims of mankind prescribed in the Vedas are not the highest, ultimate, spiritual truth. Sri GauraHari postulated that the fifth goal, KrsnaPrema, is the ultimate spiritual aspiration for all self-realized saintly souls.

The only means to achieve KrsnaPrema is by taking shelter of the HolyNames and chanting without offense. Sri GauraSundar is the combined form of SriSri RadhaKrsna. His golden complexion, taken from Srimati Radhika, covers the blackish aura of SyamSundar. Thus He is simultaneously the supreme object (visaya) of Divine Love (pranaya) as well as its supreme shelter (asraya). This esoteric truth is revealed only to those fortunate souls who follow in the footsteps of Srila Rupa Gosvami, Srila Sanatan Gosvami, and their followers. In other words, only the eternal associates of Sri GauraHari can properly explain the purport of the revealed scriptures in such a way as to ascertain the highest path to self-realisation, or svarupa-siddhi, attainment of KrsnaPrema (love of Sri Krsna).

Svarupa-sakti- the aspect of the CognitivePrinciple (cit sakti) that reveals the form or presence of the SupremePersonality of Godhead; svarupa-siddha- stage of perfection in which the devotee clearly perceives the SupremeLord, in His eternal form of knowledge and bliss, and, side-by-side, perceives his or her own eternal form in which he or she renders service to the Lord and his companions.

### Verse 84

*jnanadivartmavirucim vrajanathabhakti*  
*ritim na vedmi na ca sadguravo milanti*  
*ha hanta hanta mama kah saranam vimudha*  
*gauro haristava na karnapatham gato’sti*

**‘I do not know the supreme science of devotional service to the Lord of Vraja; that knowledge which helps breed distaste in a person towards the path of monism and knowledge of impersonal Brahman. I have also not yet met or associated with a self-realized, bonafide guru. What options do I have now? Who do I surrender to?’ Oh! Alas! what a fool you are! You are not even capable of resolving who to take shelter of? Have you never heard the name of Sri GauraHari?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

‘I do not know the process of serving and worshiping VrajaNath Sri Krsna, that process which generates disgust and aversion for the path of knowledge (jnanadivartma virucim), meaning impersonal, empirical knowledge of Brahman; knowledge that is contrary to the principle of bhakti. The suffix adi (etcetera) includes fruitive religiosity and rituals, yoga, dry renunciation, and the like. The method of bhajan which will evoke within me an abhorrence for such practices as mentioned above is not known to me. Neither do I know a bonafide spiritual master who I can approach for guidance. Alas! What will become of me now?’

Out of sympathy for these lamenting souls, the author cries out, “He vimudha! You abject fools! Has the name of GauraHari never entered your ears (karnapatham)? You have never heard of GauraHari? Good grief! Then quickly find out how to worship Him. Do not delay!”

Karika:

*bhakti-ritim na janami jnana karmady anavrtam*  
*iti nirveda cittena gauranga bhaktimadisa*

**‘To such a detached and remorseful person as he who admits to not knowing the process of bhakti, devoid of empirical, impersonal knowledge of Brahman, fruitive activity, and so on, the process of devotional service to Sri Gauranga should be taught.'**

**Purport**

The Supreme science of devotional service, bhakti-yoga is the king of education and most confidential knowledge, as stated by Lord Sri Krsna in the BhagavadGita (9.1-2). Without a guru it is impossible to ascertain this path of realized knowledge (vijnanam). Speculation and debate are futile means.

*tarko ’pratisthah srutayo vibhinna*  
*nasav rsir yasya matam na bhinnam*  
*dharmasya tattvam nihitam guhayam*  
*mahajano yena gatah sa panthah*

**‘Rational debates, dry speculation, rhetoric, logic, and so on, are inconclusive in the matter of spiritual science. A philosopher whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are voluminous and variegated one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The absolute truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated, self-realized person. Consequently, as the sastras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahajanas, or previous spiritual preceptors, advocate.’**  
**(MahaBharata VanaParva (313.117))**

When a person comes into contact with bhakti-yoga, he looses his taste for other, limited spiritual concepts like interpersonalism, voidism, pantheism, and the like. In fact, the nectarean taste of bhakti-rasa eludes those who are impressed by jnana and pursue its flavour.

*jnane prayasam udapasya namanta eva*  
*jivanti san-mukharitam bhavadiya-vartam*  
*sthane sthitah sruti-gatam tanu-van-manobhir*  
*ye prayaso ’jita jito 'py asi tais tri-lokyam*

**‘Those who, even while remaining situated in their established social positions, throw away the process of speculative knowledge and with their body, words and mind offer all respects to descriptions of Your Personality and Activities, dedicating their lives to these narrations, which are vibrated by You personally and by Your pure devotees, certainly conquer Your Lordship, although You are otherwise unconquerable by anyone within the three worlds.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.14.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.3)**))**

**The worship of the unmanifest, Impersonal Brahman is a very difficult path, especially in KaliYuga: ‘For those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest, impersonal feature of the Supreme (Brahman), advancement is extremely troublesome and difficult. ’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**12.5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/12.5)**))**

Thus, the final goal of yoga - union with the Supreme in loving devotion - is possible by His grace alone. The Supreme Lord reveals His grace in the form of guru to the fortunate, conditioned souls. Guru is the external representation of Paramatma or SuperSoul, within the heart of every jiva.

Travelling through the different species of life, a soul is most fortunate to earn the human form of life. Lord Caitanya is so merciful, He fulfils everyone’s desire to relish the highest spiritual ambrosia, thus a human being must surrender himself to Sri Gaura. The ecstatic, golden form of Sri Gauranga is so attractive that millions of Cupids are spellbound by His beauty.

### Verse 85

*vrthavesam karmasvapanayata varttamapi manak*  
*na karnabhyarne’pi kvacana nayatadhyatmasaraneh*  
*na moham dehadau bhajata paramascaryamadhurah*  
*pumarthanam maulirmiliti bhavatam gaurakrpaya*

**Attentiveness to fruitive, ritualistic activities (mentioned in the karma-kanda section of the Vedas) is completely futile; cast these far away. Neither should you pay the slightest heed to inductive, empirical philosophy. And last but not least, do not become bewildered by this material body and the persons and things related to it. In this way, by Sri GauraSundara’s grace, all of you can attain that absolutely astonishing, sweetest treat of all treats - KrsnaPrema - for the sake of the soul, the highest aim of mankind.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The edification herein is that whatever one’s individual absorption be - fruitive activities, spiritual advancement, mundane or physical culture - it should be abandoned and one should instead aspire for even a drop of Sri GauraHari’s mercy, which will ensure the most exalted perfection - KrsnaPrema.

Get rid of attachment to executing fruitive, pious activities and rituals which are temporary and non-essential. Reject the empirical, inductive process (nayatadhyatmasaraneh- process or path of research and analysis to distinguish spirit from matter); do not grant it any credibility, since even a slight indulgence here will pose stumbling blocks in the progress of bhakti. Similarly, dehadau moham- infatuation for the body and its related objects is detrimental to the growth of transcendental love for Bhagavan Sri Krsna.

‘Very well, О preceptor! According to your instructions, we shall relinquish everything mentioned above; however, kindly tell us the proper path to spiritual perfection.’

Paramascarya madhurah- the most extraordinary and marvellous spiritual perfection, the crest-jewel of all perfections (the transcendental, conjugal exchange of love) - KrsnaPrema - is possible to taste simply by receiving the grace of Sri GauraHari. Milati- acquired in the immediate future. This most rare and exalted spiritual perfection, KrsnaPrema is solely obtainable by engaging in worship and service to Sri GauraHari, under the guidance of His devotees, having rejected all other endeavours.

Karika:

*purusartha siroratna prema labhaya putrakah*  
*bhajata sri gauraharim yat krpa sarva sadhika*

**‘My dear sons! For the express purpose of attaining the best of all perfections, prema-bhakti, worship Sri GauraHari, whose mercy can award all of everything.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Lord is everyone’s only well-wishing friend and guardian. The Lord is deeply concerned about the wellbeing of His eternal parts and parcels (jivas), who in their conditioned existence have forgotten their eternal connection with Him. He is pained to see the self-imposed suffering the jivas experience in the material world in their futile attempt to lord it over material nature with the intention of trying to enjoy their senses. The jiva’s primary concern is to alleviate his suffering with as little endeavour as possible and without having to relinquish his imaginary position as an enjoyer. This, however, is an irreconcilable situation; all his attempts must end in frustration, since his material bondage is said to be eternal.

Vedic rituals, penances, and the like, cannot effect a permanent change in the jiva’s status as a conditioned soul. Good karma, as a result of pious deeds, elevates the jiva to higher heavenly planets, temporary abodes within this material world where exquisite sensual pleasures are available. Empirical knowledge leads to renunciation of the material world of phenomena. In impersonal Brahman-realisation, the jnani is elevated to a transcendental position beyond the influences of the three-fold miseries and three modes of material nature (gunas). But even that exalted position is temporary:

*ye 'nye ’ravindaksa vimukta-maninas*  
*tvayy asta-bhavad avisuddha-buddhayah*  
*aruhya krcchrena param padam tatah*  
*patanty adho ’nadrta-yusmad-anghrayah*

**Lord Brahma said: “O lotus-eyed Lord, the intelligence of those who think themselves liberated but who have no devotion is impure. Even though they rise to the highest point of liberation by dint of severe penances and austerities, they are sure to fall down again into material existence, for they do not take shelter at Your lotus feet.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.2.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.32)**))**

As long as the jiva falsely identifies with this body, he will remain bound to the constantly rotating wheel of birth and death. The jiva ’s identification with the body, as opposed to the soul, is a product of nescience. Born in the dark well of ignorance, the jiva’s only succour comes in the shape of a bonafide guru who opens his eyes with the salve of transcendental knowledge (divya-jnana). This process begins with sambandha-jnana, knowledge of the eternal relationship between Bhagavan, sakti and jiva. Without sambandha-jnana, the jiva remains eternally incarcerated in material existence.

*brahmanda bhramite kona bhagyavan jiva*  
*guru-krsna-prasade paya bhakti-lata-bija*

**‘According to his karma, the jiva wanders throughout this universe in different planets and life species.
