Out of many millions of wandering souls, one who is very fortunate gets the opportunity to associate with a bonafide guru, by Krsna’s grace. By the mercy of both guru and Krsna, the fortunate jiva receives the seed of pure bhakti.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila(**[**19.151**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.151)**))**

Thakur Srila Bhaktivinoda comments:

“The jiva travels through many species of life within this material world, according to his karma. One whose good fortune has blossomed (due to sufficient pious deeds having been converted into eligibility to engage in bhakti) comes in contact with a bonafide guru as a result of Krsna’s grace. From the guru he receives the seed of pure devotion, known as sraddha, or implicit faith in bhakti (devotional service) to Krsna. Once the seed is sown in the heart of the faithful, it sprouts into a plant, nurtured through watering in the form of hearing and chanting in the association of devotees of Sri GauraSundar. This creeper of devotion ultimately brings forth a relishable fruit called KrsnaPrema.”

Pumarthanam- the highest aim of man; for the sake of the soul.

### Verse 86

*alam sastrabhyasairalamahaha tirthatanikaya*  
*sada yosidvyayaghryastrasata vitatham thutkuru divam*  
*trnammanya dhanyah srayata kila sanyasikapatam*  
*natantam gaurangam nijarasamadadambudhitate*

**What is the use of studying volumes of scriptures? (Give it up!) Indeed, what is the need for going on pilgrimages? (Abstain from such activities.) Be always very cautious about purposeless association with women, who are compared to threatening tigresses. Consider elevation to heavenly planets that are temporary and insignificant, to be as inconsequential as blades of grass. Spit at the thought! Playing the role of a sannyasi, Sri Gauranga dances on the shore of the ocean of ecstatic prema, intoxicated with the mellows of Love of Krsna. О most fortunate devotees, ‘Go! Hurry!’ simply take shelter at His lotus feet.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

A word of advice to those who are addicted to women, who yearn for elevation to heavenly planets, who spend their time scrutinizing the scriptures, looking for ‘needles in the haystack’, and who are on constant pilgrimage. They should forsake their fascination with individual pursuits and take refuge at the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari.

Women are compared to tigresses. Men aspiring for spiritual elevation must always be extremely fearful of developing attachment to them. Just as people become terrified upon seeing a tigress, so also one should feel anxiety in associating with women.

Vitatham thutkurute re- heavenly pleasures are mundane, therefore illusory and evanescent. They are pitifully insignificant. Therefore thutkuru- one should spit on such pleasures with disgust.

The next objection- ‘supposing heavenly pleasures are impermanent- what of the various yoga disciplines mentioned in the scriptures, leading to gradual elevation and perfection?’

Alam sastrabhyasaih- yoga processes recommended in the scriptures are also futile due to the nature of the mind, which is to fall prone to distraction. What to speak of neophyte acolytes, even eminent yogis become deviated and fall down. Even if, by providential intervention, one attains perfection in yoga, due to the absence of ecstasy (ananda) obtained through bhakti-yoga, the yogi’s only reward is the immense endeavour and pain undertaken during his sadhana.

One may say, ‘if this is so, then I will acquire knowledge by travelling to holy tirthas (places of pilgrimage) and offer my services to the holy men who reside there, thus ensuring my liberation.’

Alam tirthatanikaya- repeated pilgrimage journeys are also ineffectual. Ahaha! expresses a combination of censure and regret; alam- conveys futility and superfluity of action. Pilgrimage journeys demand tedious effort and discomfiture. The holy places also do not reward the non-devotees with much pious credits, atanika- conjunction of verbal root ata- to roam, wander about; used of religious mendicants; with the suffix naka-negation (not); meaning: pilgrimage journeys are essentially worth only so much (useless) labour.

The question then remains: ‘What am I to do?’

In reply, the respected author presents his own realisations gleaned from the conclusions of the scriptures. He has delineated very clearly what are his priorities in life. In exultation he declares, dhanyah srayata kila- You are all worthy of receiving the priceless treasure of prema. Simply take shelter of Sri Gauranga and in the shade of his lotus feet, serve Him with complete conviction; kila- with certitude.

‘Who is this person we must serve?’

He is that SupremePersonalit y, dancing on the shore of the ocean.

One may be curious to know, ‘why is He dancing?’

Nijarasa madat- He is savouring prema-rasa of his undifferentiated Self (Sri Krsna); thus does Sri Gauranga feel jubilant and is therefore dancing.

One may object, ‘how is it that Sri Gauranga is nondifferent from Krsna? Sri Krsna was never a sannyasi in the renounced order.’

*sannyasa-krc chamah santo nistha-santi-parayanah*  
*(MahaBharat)*

‘Sri Krsna will enter the renounced order....etc.’

In truth, he is simply in the guise (kapat- disguise) of a sannyasi According to SrimadBhagavatam (7.9.38), in KaliYuga, Krsna has covered his identity (channah kalau) by accepting the garb of a sannyasi. Sannyasa means Paramahamsa (self-realized transcendentalist); kapat can also mean: ka: head, and pata: cloth. Sri Gauranga is thus likened to a turban wrapped around the heads of paramahamsa sannyasis. He is the topmost transcendentalist; their worshipful object.

Karika:

*yoga tirthatana strisvarabhyasatanadhi sprhah*  
*hitva bhajata gaurangam nitya kautukam*

**‘Abandoning all interest in and attachment to yoga practice, pilgrimage, women, heavenly pleasures, and the like, simply serve and worship Sri Gauranga, who is always engaged in His Divine play and who is the crest-jewel of all sannyasis.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“By comparing a woman with a tigress, association with women is strictly denounced. The question, however, then becomes- ‘how can householders become elevated to the heavenly planets if the man cannot participate in different Vedic rituals and sacrifices which require the wife’s presence at his side?’  
“In anticipation of this query the author exhorts us to realize the insignificance of attaining the pleasures of paradise since they are so evanescent. Let us for now admit that heavenly joys are impermanent; then, ‘what about practicing yoga-discipline mentioned in different texts?’  
“The process of yoga leads to the attainment of mystic perfections (yoga-siddhi). What to speak of acquiring mystic perfections, it is well known that many who have obtained the highest stage of yoga-siddhi have fallen down. Thus, if attaining mystic perfections is so unreliable, plus its execution so extremely hazardous and onerous, what is there to be gained from this endeavour?”  
If all these be true, then, ‘what about going on holy pilgrimage?’  
“It is mentioned that visiting holy sites is a very pious act, rewarding great joy to the pilgrim. The pilgrim also acquires immense spiritual knowledge, which when mature, makes him eligible for liberation (moksa). The author dismisses these claims, saying that from the bhakti-yoga viewpoint, pilgrimage is a very tiresome task. Besides, the karmis (fruitive workers) and jnanis (empiricists) are prone to committing dham-aparadha (offences to the holy tirthas), due to their mundane state of consciousness. Their pilgrimage thus becomes tantamount to mere sight-seeing; titillation of the senses. Thus all such endeavours are futile.  
So then, ‘how to establish what is truly required of the jiva?’  
“The author’s final conclusion, is that since the jiva is eligible to relish and inherit the timeless treasure of KrsnaPrema, he must simply take shelter of Sri Gauranga’s lotus feet. Lord Gauranga is Himself engrossed in tasting the nectar of Divine Love for Himself (Krsna) and thus intoxicated, He dances madly on the shores of Nilacala, wearing the robes of a renunciant. The author uses the word sannyasi-kapatam- playing the role of a sannyasi, although in truth, He is not a true renunciant. Only to keep Srila VedaVyasa’s words, ‘Sannyasa krc chamah....’ the Supreme Lord accepted the sannyasa order.”

### Verse 87

*kim tavadvata durgamesu viphalam yogadimargesvaho*  
*bhaktim krsnapadambuje vidadhatah sarwarthamalunthata*  
*asa premamahotsave yadi sivabrahmadyalabhye’dbhute*  
*gaure dhamani durwigahamahimodare tada rajyatam*

**Aho! What is the benefit of traversing the impassable and fruitless path of eight-fold mystic yoga? Better to plunder that which includes everything worthy, the most precious gems of bhakti found at the lotus feet of Sri Krsna. If you are aspiring to participate in the sublime festival of transcendental Divine Love, rarely obtained even by Lord Siva and Lord Brahma, then, my dear mind! develop deep attachment for the abode of that most munificent, Divine Personality Sri GauraHari, whose glories are not easily fathomed.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Those who are even mildly attracted to yoga are herein advised not to be swept away by their infatuations but to develop greed for the priceless treasure of KrsnaPrema. To accomplish this end they must cultivate attachment to Sri Gauranga.

The author asks, ‘O brothers! You are cultivating devotional service at the lotus feet of Sri Krsna. What value is there in the futile endeavour of pursuing the tedious and treacherous path of yoga? What will you gain?’

Bata is an expression of regret and Aho! an exclamation (I say!). Cultivate devotion to Sri Krsna’s lotus feet and thus plunder that which includes everything worthy, the topmost goal in life - KrsnaPrema. Sarvartham- the meaning of everything; premartham- the priceless treasure of prema; alunthana- to loot without constraints. Seeing the eagerness of those who aspire for yoga, the author remarks, asa premamahotsave...‘if you really and truly hope to attain this priceless treasure of ecstatic prema, then become attached to Sri GauraHari. For he is durvvigaha mahimodare- His glories and greatness are unfathomable; He is infinitely generous.’

One may ask, ‘why must the pursuit of yoga be considered valueless?’

Only by the process of KrsnaBhakti does one become eligible to plunder the most precious and essential spiritual treasure. If you want to participate in the prema mahotsava -the grand festival of prema, then you must develop attachment to Gauranga.

Karika:

*manastyajata yogadim krsnam bhajata lunthata*  
*premasu tvanmahasa cettada gaure ‘nurajyatam*

**‘O mind! Abandon the practice of yoga. Simply worship and serve Sri Krsna; plunder all His treasures. If your desire for prema is strong, then become attached to Sri Gauranga.’**

**Purport**

The goal of human life is to realize our eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord and His multifarious energies. The ultimate conclusion of the Vedas is to know the Supreme Lord. All yoga systems are meant to bring about this union between the knower and the object of transcendental knowledge. If the various yoga processes do not culminate in bhakti-yoga, then all endeavours in any of the yoga disciplines are futile. Cultivation of knowledge or practice of yoga is meant to develop one’s latent inherent faith so that it reveals itself as devotion to God. If this does not occur, then all efforts in any of these disciplines are a waste of time. In the BhagavadGita (9.3) the Supreme Lord, Sri Krsna remarks: ‘Those who have not developed faith in the process of religion (according to authorized scriptures) cannot attain me (the ultimate goal of SanatanDharma). Birth after birth they will be forced to suffer in this material world.’

*na sadhayati mam yogo na sankhyam dharma uddhava*  
*na svadhyayas tapas tyago yatha bhaktir mamorjita*

**‘My dear Uddhava, the unalloyed devotional service rendered to Me by My devotees brings Me under their control. I cannot be thus controlled by those engaged in mystic yoga, Sankhya philosophy, pious deeds, Vedic study, austerity or renunciation. I am won over only by unalloyed devotion.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.14.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/14.20)**))**

The Supreme Personality Sri Krsna is known as ajaya-unconquerable; but not by His unalloyed devotees. The pure devotee’s devotion, by its own potency, subjugates the omnipotent, since bhakti is independent and transcendental, like Sri Krsna Himself. Krsna willingly accepts the capricious dictates of prema. If one is truly seeking prema, rarely rewarded to even Lord Brahma, Lord Siva and other demigods, his only hope to attain it is by taking complete shelter of the most munificent of the Supreme Lord’s incarnations, Sri Gauranga.

### Verse 88

*yatha yatha gaurapadaravinde vindeta bhaktim krtapunyarasih*  
*tatha tathotsarpati hrdyakasmat radhapadambhoja sudhamburasih*

**As much as devotional service is gradually realized at the lotus feet of Sri Gaura, thus causing pious credits to accumulate, to that same degree one’s heart suddenly overflows with an ocean of ambrosia produced from the the lotus feet of Srimati Radhika.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The degree of subservience to the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga is the measure by which to judge the depth of mercy of Srimati Radhika. The measure of loving attachment to the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga ensures an equal amount of attachment to the lotus feet of Sri Radha.

Krtapunyarasih- accumulated results of spiritual practices (sadhana).

The degree of devotional attachment to the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga that becomes manifest through the process of surrender, concomitantly releases in equal proportion a sudden surge in the ocean of prema that bathes the lotus feet of Srimati Radhika. Service to the lotus feet of Sri Gaura is compared to the full moon on the horizon of the heart, and as this wondrous moon rises it creates tidal waves in the nectarean ocean of prema, whose source is Srimati Radhika.

Karika:

*уadrsi yadrsi bhaktis caitanya-caranambuje*  
*tadrsi hrdaye sphurttih sri radha-padapadmayoh*

**‘The quality and intensity of devotion a devotee develops for the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya is reflected in equal measure manifest as the vibrant presence of the lotus feet of Srimati Radhika in the devotee’s heart.’**

**Purport**

*bhaktistu bhagavad-bhakta-sangena parijayate*  
*sat-sangah prapyate pumbhi sukrtaih purva-sancitaih*

**‘By the purifying influence of a pure Vaisnava’s association, the propensity for bhakti is awakened within. One earns the potent association of pure devotees as a result of innumerable pious deeds accumulated over past lives.’**  
**(BrhanNaradiyaPurana)**

Only very pious souls develop love and attachment for Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet. In KaliYuga, persons endowed with pious intelligence will join the Sankirtana movement propagated by Sri Caitanya. People whose intelligence is distorted by material desires (BhagavadGita [7.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.20)) or who are of small intelligence worship demigods (BhagavadGita [7.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.23)) for limited and temporary material gains. Attachment to Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet is the surest way to attain the highest spiritual goal - Radha dasya. Followers of Sri GauraSundar understand that the most sublime rasa (taste) in devotional service is to serve the DivineCouple as a maid-in-attendance of Srimati Radhika.

### Verse 89

*aparasya premojjvala-rasarahasyamrtanidher*  
*nidhanam brahmesarccita iha hi caitanyacaranah*  
*atastam dhyayantah pranayabharato yantu saranam*  
*tameva pronmattastamiha kila gayantu krtinah*

**Ohe sargrahi sudhijana! (O most wise and intelligent seekers of the truth; who can extract the essence of the substance.) Sri Caitanya's lotus feet are worshipped even by Lord Siva and Lord Brahma, for His lotus feet are the source of a shoreless, mysterious ocean of nectarean mellows in conjugal love. Therefore, enraptured with Divine Love, meditate on those lotus feet; accept shelter there. Insane with prema, sing His glories.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

We are instructed to take complete refuge at Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s lotus feet since they are for everyone the only real sanctuary. His lotus feet are worshipped by Brahma and Isa (Siva) since it is that He is the same Supreme Personality as Svayam Bhagavan Sri Krsna.

Since the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya are indeed (hi) a treasure trove, the source of a limitless, mysterious, nectarean ocean of erotic sentiments (premojjvalarasarahasyamrtanidhe), those who are actually virtuous (krtinah- obedient) will find that their search for the quintessence of love has ended here, at these very lotus feet. Simply take shelter here; surrender here; meditate on these lotus feet. Then, as Divine madness gradually comes upon you (pronmatta), your heart suffused with ineffable ecstasy, you have only to sing out, “Ha Gauranga! Ha Radhe! Ha Krsna!” In this way do the devotees profess the majesty of the Incarnation of Mercy in this KaliYuga.

Gayantu- to hear: to sing; to give assent; to elucidate

Karika:

*siva brahmadyarccaniyam mahabhdvaparasrayam*  
*kalau bhajantu rasikas caitanya caranambujam*

**‘The venerable Deity of Siva, Brahma and their followers; the supreme shelter of the pinnacle of prema (MahaBhava); Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet are worshiped by the rasik devotees in KaliYuga.’**

**Purport**

The Srutis, SrimadBhagavadGita and the spotless and most authoritative source of evidence, the SrimadBhagavataPurana, unanimously declare that Sri Krsna (svayam rupa bhagavan) is the Supreme object of worship, not only for the Brahman-realised rsis, denizens of IndraLoka and BrahmaLoka, including Lord Brahma and Lord Siva, but by Lord Visnu, Sri Narayan and Lord Balaram Himself. Less intelligent commentators and Mayavadi philosophers attempt to undermine Sri Krsna’s paramount position by citing other Vedic texts. They may confuse and mislead a section of the innocent mass, but for an intelligent and pious seeker of the Absolute Truth, their words are nothing more than a futile and vainglorious attempt. An intelligent person knows that the different volumes of Vedic texts are not all on the same level of spiritualism. Spiritual debates are arbitrated on the basis of their source and evidence. If the source of a point in debate is from a sattvika Purana like Padma, Visnu. or BhagavataPurana.. then contentious statements from rajasik and tamasik texts are refuted, over-ruled. Similarly, among the sattvika Puranas, the SrimadBhagavatam is considered amala, without any mundane contamination.

*srimad-bhagavatam puranam amalam yad vaisnavanam priya*  
*yasmin paramahamsyam ekam amalam jnanam param giyate*  
*tatra jnana-viraga-bhakti-sahitam naiskarmyam aviskrtam*  
*tac chrnvan su-pathan vicarana-paro bhaktya vimucyen narah*

**‘SrimadBhagavatam is the spotless Purana. It is most dear to the Vaisnavas because it describes the pure and supreme knowledge of the paramahamsas. This Bhagavatam reveals the means for becoming free from all material work, together with the processes of transcendental knowledge, renunciation and devotion. Anyone who seriously tries to understand SrimadBhagavatam, who properly hears and chants it with devotion, becomes completely liberated.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**12.13.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/13.18)**))**

*dharmah projjhita-kaitavo ’tra paramo nirmatsaranam satam*  
*vedyam vastavam atra vastu sivadam tapa-trayonmulanam*  
*srimad-bhagavate maha-muni-krte kim va parair isvarah*  
*sadyo hrdy avarudhyate 'tra krtibhih susrusubhis tat-ksanat*

**‘Completely rejecting all religious activities which are materially motivated, this BhagavataPurana propounds the highest truth, which is understandable by those devotees who are fully pure in heart. The highest truth is reality distinguished from illusion for the welfare of all. Such truth uproots the threefold miseries. This beautiful Bhagavatam, compiled by the great sage VyasaDev \[in his maturity\], is sufficient in itself for God realisation. What is the need of any other scripture? As soon as one attentively and submissively hears the message of Bhagavatam, by this culture of knowledge, the Supreme Lord is established within his heart.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**1.1.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.2)**))**

*krsne sva-dhamopagate dharma-jnanadibhih saha*  
*kalau nasta-drsam esa puranarko 'dhunoditah*

**‘This BhagavataPurana is as brilliant as the sun, and it has arisen just after the departure of Lord Krsna to His own abode, accompanied by religion, knowledge, etc. Persons who have lost their vision due to the dense darkness of ignorance in the age of Kali shall get light from this Purana.‘**  
**SrimadBhagavtam (**[**1.3.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.43)**)**

In KaliYuga, the most intelligent and pious souls will participate in the sankirtana-yajna initiated by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Only these fortunate jivas, by following the process of nine-fold bhakti, will ultimately attain prema.

### Verse 90

*dante nidhaya trnakam padyornipatya*  
*krtva ca kakusatametadaham bravimi*  
*he sadhavah sakalameva vihaya durad*  
*gaurangacandracarane kurutanuragam*

**О virtuous and saintly souls! Holding a straw between my teeth I fall at your feet, to importunately plead with you hundreds of times, over and over again, that you simply give up everything and cultivate loving attachment to the lotus feet of Sri GaurangaCandra.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author humbly pleads with those devotees engaged in the vain pursuit of yoga, dhyana, jnana, and so on, to forsake their individual infatuations and persuasions to develop love and attachment to the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari.

Sakalameva- all types of sadhana (karma, jnana, sankhya, yoga, dry renunciation, dharma, artha, kama, moksa) not dedicated to the pursuit of pure devotional service to the SupremeLord must be rejected; so that vihaya durad- they will remain permanently very far away, never again to entice us to chase after them.

Thus, gaurangacandracarane- will we be able to cultivate intense attachment to the lotus feet of the transcendental moon - GaurangaCandra.

Karika:

*dante krtva trnam pade patitva vinayakulah*  
*yace hitvakhilam gaurapade rajyantu sadhavah*

**‘Holding a straw between my teeth I fall at your feet in utter humility, begging you “O sadhus, abandon all pursuits and simply develop loving attachment to the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“The revered author says that he holds the smallest blade of grass between his teeth. This attitude of the Tridandi Gosvami, as a preacher of the Sankirtan movement, indicates his humility {trnadapi sunicena - humbler then a blade of grass.) Grass is trampled under everyone’s feet, yet the author chooses to hold the tiniest of them between his teeth; meaning, he accords that blade of grass a position of utmost respect. He falls at the reader’s feet, indicating, that as a preacher of Sri Caitanya’s glories, he feels the quality of amanina- not desirous of any respect for himself. He refrains from considering himself the Supreme Lord (Narayan) as the impersonal sannyasis claim, due to their being intoxicated by arrogance. Nor does he dabble in mundane debates over the differences between a brahmana and a candala (dog eater), between who is elder and who the younger, between the gross body and subtle body, like the materialistic smarta brahmanas do, thereby depriving themselves of any spiritual vision to see the real identity (of the soul) of all living entities. The author is thus able to enthusiastically speak the truth, because he never desires any respect for himself.  
“Thus does the Tridandi Gosvami entreat his readers with thousands of solicitations, exhibiting tolerance like a tree (taror iva sahisnuna). The materialistic mass, apathetic to God-consciousness, is uninterested to hear the truth. But the renounced tridandi sannyasis will eagerly speak about the Supreme Lord (Harikatha), begging even gross materialists to come and hear. By addressing his readers as saintly souls, this renounced and inspired preacher gives evidence of his noble character, demonstrating how to treat everyone with respect (manad-dharma). He exhorts the saintly souls to fling far away all their possessions. He tells them that they are indeed sadhus, but those possessions which bloat them with false pride, and bolster their false identity as sadhus - possessions like fruitive works, empirical knowledge, sankhya, and yoga philosophy, false renunciation, the four varnas {brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya, sudra) religiosity, irreligiosity, and so on, are all to be discarded, for they are impediments in one's endeavour to satisfy Lord Krsna’s transcendental senses.”

### Verse 91

*aho na durlabha muktirna ca bhaktih sudurllabha*  
*gauracandra-prasadastu vaikunthe'pi sudurllabhah*

**Mukti (liberation- the goal of dry empirical knowledge) is easily attained by the process of regulative devotional service mixed with knowledge of the Lord’s opulences. To become an eternal servitor of Sri Narayana in Vaikuntha (by the process of vaidhi-bhakti) is also not so rare. However, Sri GauraSundara’s mercy is very rarely achieved, even by the residents of Vaikuntha.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may raise an objection as to why the author insists that everyone abandon their various pursuits- liberation, devotion

to various demigods, and so on, exhorting them to develop attachment to Sri GauraCandra?

The reply: aho na durllabha muktih- mukti (liberation) means salokya, sarupya, sarsti, samipya- attaining the same bodily features as the Lord, equal facility to live on the same planet with the SupremeLord, equal possession of opulence like the Lord, and equal association with the Lord. These may be easily attained by the appropriate means -jnana-misra bhakti- regulative devotional service mixed with awe and reverential worship (knowledge of the Lord’s opulences). However, the ecstasy from tasting the nectar of prema, made possible only by the mercy of Sri GauraSundar, is not available even in Vaikuntha. The eternal residents of Vaikuntha yearn to relish that nigudha-prema, thus do they always implore Sri Gauranga for His mercy.

(See verse 44).

Karika:

*muktir jnanadi sadhya syaddhan bhakti prasadanat*  
*gauracandra prasadattu prema vaikuntha durlabhah*

**‘Mukti is obtained by spiritual discipline on the path of jnana. Bhakti is attained by pleasing the SupremeLord Sri Hari. The priceless gift of prema one receives by the mercy of Sri Gauranga is, however, extremely rare, even in Vaikuntha.’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“One may put forward the question, ‘why must one ignore the processes of jnana- leading to liberation {mukti), or of vaidhi bhakti (regulative devotional service in the mood of awe and reverence)- leading to Vaikuntha, in order to cultivate loving attachment {anuraga) to Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet?’  
In reply, the author says: {Aho)! “I say!” (Please listen!) "Impersonal liberation (brahma-sayujya) and the four kinds of liberation, such as salokya, are not difficult to attain. They come within easy reach, either from dry knowledge or the execution of regulative devotional service mixed with knowledge {jnana-misra-vaidhi-bhakti). Pure vaidhi-bhakti is also not tenuous; the devotee is rewarded with eternal service to Lord Narayan in Vaikuntha.  
“However, satisfying the transcendental senses of Sri GauraCandra by executing devotional service at His lotus feet and thus receiving His mercy, which reveals the nectarean taste of the highest and most esoteric realm of Divine prema, is an opportunity not to be found even in Vaikuntha.  
“Gaura krpa is of three varieties: 1) unblemished, innocent (nirmala-bhakti) devotion, following in the wake of anarthanivrtti- freedom from unwanted sinful habits; relief from the pressure of the tongue, belly and genitals. 2) spiritual satisfaction accruing from resolute devotional service (bhaktisiddhantarasapraptirupa rasada). 3) Divine madness resulting from recognition of the delicious sweetness and beauty of bhakti.  
“Thus, Gauranga’s mercy is devoid of all impurities, able to uproot unwanted material desires (anartha) in the heart; succulent with the nectar that manifests pure bhakti. This intoxicating nectar is flavoured with the most sublime sweetness, that of conjugal exchanges of DivineLove; approached with a sober, respectful mind - all as a result of His mercy.”

### Verse 92

*bhajantu caitanyapadaravindam*  
*bhavantu sadbhaktirasena purnah*  
*anandayantu trijagadvicitram*  
*madhurya-saubhagya dayaksamadyaih*

**My fellow human beings! Adore the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra and be thus fully satisfied in the mellows of pure devotion. Having yourself attained ecstatic delight and attainment of transcendental qualities, bestow the same (madhurya, saubhagya, daya, ksama) upon the residents of the three worlds.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The author continues to persuade all to engage in worship and service to the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra, since it is that prema, attained only by His grace, is extremely rare, even in Vaikuntha.

'Seek all-embracing refuge at His lotus feet. By doing so you will be saturated with the paramount transcendental devotional exchange known as bhakti-rasa.

'Disseminate the sublime sweetness of devotional mellows in the universe to bring unique joy to all living entities. Spread this euphoria, endowed with such sublime qualities as: madhurya- felicitous charm; saubhagya- immaculate blessedness; daya- compassion, kindness; and ksama-forgiveness, absolution.'

Karika:

*caitanya-pada-bhaktesu nigudha-prema-purnata*  
*madhuryadi-gunair yesam jagadananda-datrta*

**'Sri Caitanya’s devotees, completely within His shelter, are perfectly situated in nigudha-vraja-prema. Thus are they able to spread this happiness in the universe through their sublimely sweet natures.'**

**Purport**

Divine qualities automatically enhance the character of surrendered devotees of the Supreme Lord. Even if a nondevotee is endowed with good character, he will gradually lose it due to not being attached to the Lord’s lotus feet.

*ynsyasti bhaktir bhagavaty akincana*  
*sarvair gunais tatra samasate surah*  
*harav abhaktasya kuto mahad-guna*  
*mano-rathenasati dhavato bahih*

**'All the demigods and their exalted qualities such as religiosity, knowledge and renunciation, become manifest in the body of one who has developed unalloyed devotion for the Supreme Personality. Vasudeva. On the other hand, a person devoid of devotional service and engaged in material activities has no good qualities. Even if he is adept at the practice of mystic yoga or in the honest endeavour of maintaining his family and relatives, he must be driven by his own mental speculations and must engage in the service of the Lord’s external energy, maya. How can there be any good qualities in such a man?’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**5.18.12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/18.12)**))**

mano-rathenasati- chariot of the mind; dhavato bahih- galloping away

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur Prabhupad comments:

Madhurya- sweet and gentle disposition; saubhagya- to relish the nectarean taste of the pinnacle of prema; karunya-to draw the materialistic-minded jiva’s attraction away from the phenomenal world of sensuality and direct it towards the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna; to propagate the HolyNames; ksama-to be humbler than a blade of grass, as tolerant as a tree; bhavantu sadbhaktirasena purnah- to be thus fully satisfied in the mellows of pure devotion (bathed in the nectar of erotic sentiments).

Anyone who sincerely takes shelter of Sri GauraSundar is sure to experience the nascent stirrings of spiritual love (prema) for the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna within his heart very soon. As this tender blossom of prema begins to awaken, Divine qualities (anubhavas) appear, as Sri Rupa Gosvami describes:

**‘When the seed of ecstatic emotion for Krsna fructifies, the following nine blossoms of bhava (symptoms) flower on the wishfulfilling desire tree of prema (manifest in one’s behaviour): forgiveness, concern that time should not be wasted, detachment, absence of false prestige, hope, eagerness, a taste for chanting the HolyNames of the Lord, attachment to descriptions of the transcendental qualities of the Lord, and affection for those places where the Lord resides - such as a temple or a holy place like Vrindaban. These are all called anubhava, subordinate signs of ecstatic emotion. They are visible in a person in whose heart the seed of Love of God has begun to fructify.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.3.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.3.25)**))**

The world experiences lasting happiness and peace only when saintly devotees, whose characters are decorated with Divine qualities, preach the HolyNames. Preaching and practice must go hand in glove, otherwise the entire effort is futile and mundane. Without cultivating exemplary behaviour, a preacher’s words will fail to bring transcendental joy into the suffering people’s lives. This was Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s instruction to His followers.

**‘I shall accept the role of a devotee, and I shall teach devotional service by practicing it Myself. Unless one practices devotional service himself, he cannot teach it to others. This conclusion is indeed confirmed throughout the Gita and Bhagavatam.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**3.20-21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.20)**))**

**‘In this way, assuming the sentiment of a devotee, He preached devotional service while practicing it Himself.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.41)**))**

**‘You (Haridas Thakur) simultaneously perform both duties in relation to the HolyName by your personal behaviour (acara) and by your preaching (pracar). Therefore you are the spiritual master of the entire world, for you are the most advanced devotee in the world.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**4.103**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/4.103)**))**

Preaching is sustained by two life-giving forces:

The Supreme Lord’s potency - krsna sakti vina nahe tara pravartana

Acara- practising what is preached (walking one’s talk), according to the Vaisnava standard of sadhu, guru and sastra.

### Verse 93

*samsarsindhutarane hrdayam yadi syat*  
*sankirtanamrta-rase ramate manascet*  
*premambudhau viharane yadi cittavrttis*  
*caitanyacandracarane saranam prayatu*

**If you sincerely desire to cross the ocean of material existence; if you hanker to enjoy the sublime, sweet nectar of chanting the HolyNames (sankirtan); if you yearn to sport in the ocean of prema - then accept shelter at the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra, with full attention.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Those who are zealously eager to be lifted out of the ocean of material existence, to enjoy the immortal elixir of sankirtan and to exult in the nectarean ocean of prema, are advised to take full shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.

Karika:

*kalau samsara taranam sanklrtana-rase ratih*  
*premambudhau viharas ca nasti gaurasrayam vina*

**‘In KaliYuga it is impossible to cross the ocean of material existence, to develop love for sankirtan and to swim in the nectarean ocean of prema, without accepting shelter at the lotus feet of Sri Gaura.’**

**Purport**

In SrimadBhagavatam, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu has been addressed several times as MahaPurusa. His lotus feet are described as bhavabdhi potam- the most suitable boat for crossing the ocean of birth and death. It is not possible for conditioned souls, imprisoned in bodies crafted according to their previous karma, to halt the continuous wheel of birth and death on their own strength.

Maya, being the Lord's external potency, is Divine; too powerful for the jivas, even by their collective effort, to surmount. Thus their only chance is to attract the Supreme Lord’s benign grace.

*daivi hy esd guna-mayi mama may a duratyaya*  
*mam eva ye prapadyante mayam etam taranti te*

**'This Divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me, can easily cross beyond it.”**  
**(BhagavadGlta (**[**7.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.14)**))**

The HolyNames of the Supreme Lord are like the proverbial philosopher’s touchstone that bestows all spiritual perfection. They are the embodiment of transcendental rasa, non-different from Krsna in every respect (PadmaPurana).

Srila Rupa Gosvami mentions that the HolyNames cannot be perceived by mundane senses. However, by constantly serving the HolyNames, they appear of their own accord, to be perceived through the chanter’s purified senses (BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu [1.2.234](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.234)). Following Sri Rupa’s instructions is to follow Sri Caitanya. Thus all His followers deeply relish the nectarean taste of the HolyNames by executing sadhana-bhakti.

Sri Caitanya has comprehensively elaborated on the process of NamaSeva. This is how He describes the process, in His own words (Siksastaka 3):

**“One should chant the HolyName of the Lord in a humble state of mind, thinking oneself to be lower than a blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree, ready to offer all respect to others, without desiring any respect for oneself. In such a state of mind, one can chant the HolyName of the Lord constantly.”**

### Verse 94

*jnana-vairagya-bhaktyadi sadhayantu yatha tatha*  
*caitanyacaranambhoja bhaktilabhya samam kutah*

**A person may cultivate knowledge, renunciation and devotion by any and every possible means. However, where can one find the super-excellent standard of knowledge, renunciation and devotion attained through service to the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaCandra? (They are not available anywhere else.)**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

‘If jnana, bhakti, vairagya, and the like, are available through other forms of sadhana, then why do you insist on engaging in the bhajan of Sri GauraCandra, to achieve the same end?’

jnana-vairagya-bhaktyadi sadhayantu yatha tatha- jnana, vairagya and bhakti are available yatha tatha- as much as / in the same way; as the endeavour (sadhana) - so the result. However, none can match the uncommon, superior result that accrues from engaging in bhajan at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya.

With other avenues of sadhana, the levels of jnana, vairagya and bhakti attained are most elementary: jnana that leads to TatSat realisation - that simply the AbsoluteTruth exists; vairagya that merely awards apathy towards material life, saturated, in any case, with the threefold miseries; bhakti that, through pleasing Lord Visnu, achieves His mercy, thus attaining much desired heavenly pleasures, or, at best, liberation.

When one engages in bhajan of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya, the intensity of realisation is far superior and fully transcendental. By His mercy, jnana means the realisation of all transcendental truths regarding Svayam Bhagavan Sri Krsna, who is always engaged in loving pastimes with His eternal associates. Vairagya means to develop the intense yearning to perceive those transcendental truths from the perspective of spontaneous loving devotion. Bhakti means the most exalted and brilliant, nigudha-prema (unalloyed, lawless love of the gopis).

Karika:

*yadrk tattvam prema-bhaktih sa vairagya gaurahareh*  
*bhaktesu tadrk kutrapi jnanadir nahi drsyate*

**‘The superior quality of loving devotion, accompanied by transcendental realisation and renunciation, found in Sri GauraHari’s devotees is not found elsewhere.’**

**Purport**

*vasudeve bhagavati bhakti-yogah prayojitah*  
*janayaty asu vairagyam jnanam ca yad ahaitukam*

**‘By rendering devotional service unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, one immediately acquires causeless knowledge and detachment from the world.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.2.7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.7)**))**

Srila A.C. Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“The principles of knowledge and detachment are two important factors on the path of transcendental realisation. The whole spiritual process leads to perfect knowledge of everything material and spiritual, and the results of such perfect knowledge are that one becomes detached from material affection and becomes attached to spiritual activities. Becoming detached from material things does not mean becoming inert altogether, as men with poor fund of knowledge think. Naiskarma means not undertaking activities that will produce good or bad effects. Negation does not mean negation of the positive. Negation of the nonessential does not mean negation of the essential.

“The quality of detachment (vairagya) described in the SrimadBhagavatam is yukta-vairagyam. Srila Rupa Gosvami explains the principles of yukta-vairagya:

*anasaktasya visayan yathdrham upayunjatah*  
*nirbandhah krsna-sambandhe yuktam vairagyam ucyate*  
*prapancikataya buddhya hari-sambandhi-vastunah*  
*mumuksubhih parityago vairagyam phalgu kathyate*

**‘ Yukta-vairagya is defined as- interaction with the objects of senses which are carried out without attachment; only with those things which are related to the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna and are favourable in the execution of one’s devotional service. This is known as real detachment, qualifying one for bhakti-yoga. When one is not attached to anything, but at the same time accepts everything in relation to Krsna, one is rightly situated above possessiveness. On the other hand, one who rejects everything without knowledge of its relationship to Krsna is not as complete in his renunciation.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu(**[**1.2.255-256**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.255)**))**

“The negation of spiritual objects (like MahaPrasad) made by Salvationists (mumuksus), objects directly related to the Supreme Lord Hari, considering them to be mundane, is known as phalgu-vairagya (false renunciation).”

Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur comments:

“Phalgu-vairagya is incompatible with the process of pure bhakti. Renouncing spiritual objects related to the Supreme Lord (like MahaPrasad) is of two kinds: not offering prayers to the Lord (upon receiving MahaPrasad) and dishonouring or neglecting prasad which one has received.”

**‘Empirical knowledge or knowledge of impersonalism leads to false renunciation, or to incomplete renunciation. Only when one rejects these processes of speculative and deductive knowledge does one become eligible to execute pure bhakti, jnane prayasam udapasya. Other types of devotion are Contaminated with jnana, karma, etc.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.14.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.3)**))**

**‘Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things - these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.2.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.42)**))**

Lord Caitanya came specifically to reveal to the world the incomparable and purest form of loving devotion (prema-bhakti) embodied in the VrajaGopis.

### Verse 95

*acaitanyamidam visvam yadi caitanyamisvaram*  
*na viduh sarvasastrajha hyapi bhramanti te janah*  
*(na bhajet sarwato mrtyurupasyamamarottamaih)*

**If this unconscious (acaitanya) universe (devoid of devotion to Krsna) does not come to understand that Sri KrsnaCaitanya is the SupremeController, worshiped by the best amongst the immortals, then, no matter how knowledgeable one may be in all the scriptures, still he must continue to tread the wheel of repeated birth and death, to experience insignificant material pleasures and terrible misery as a result of his mundane activities.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Here the question may arise, ‘then why doesn’t the entire population of MotherEarth worship Sri Caitanya?

The reply to this is indeed contrary to the hopes and desire of our esteemed author, for he bemoans the fact that the entire universe is bereft of Krsna consciousness. If this unconscious universe will not worship Sri KrsnaCaitanya, then its inhabitants (the jivas) must, by force, enter the jaws of eternal time only to be devoured.

Karika:

*brahmndyupasyam caitanyam nasrayed уо janah kalau*  
*tasya samsara saranau gamanagamanam bhavet*

**'In KaliYuga, persons who do not take shelter of Sri Caitanya. who is worshiped by Brahma and other exalted personalities, will be forced to roam about in this material existence, full of miseries.'**

**Purport**

**‘Deluded by the three modes of material nature, the whole world does not know Me who am above the modes, supreme and inexhaustible.'**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**7.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.13)**))**

Srila A.C. Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“There are many different kinds of living entities - human beings, demigods, animals, and so on. Each and every one of them is under the influence of material nature and all of them have forgotten the transcendent Personality of Godhead. Those who are in the modes of passion and ignorance, and even those who are in the mode of goodness, cannot go beyond the impersonal Brahman conception of the AbsoluteTruth. They are bewildered before the Supreme Lord in his personal feature, that possesses all beauty, opulence, knowledge, strength, fame and renunciation. When even those who are in goodness (sattva) cannot understand, what hope is there for those in passion {raja) and ignorance (tama)?”

Sri Karabhajan instructs King Nimi (while praying to Lord Caitanya):

**“My dear Lord, You are the MahaPurusa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and I worship Your lotus feet, which are the only eternal object of meditation. Those feet destroy the embarrassing conditions of material life and freely award the greatest desire of the soul, the attainment of pure love of Krsna. My dear Lord, Your lotus feet are the shelter of all holy places and of all saintly authorities in the line of devotional service and are honoured by powerful demigods like Lord Siva and Lord Brahma. My Lord, You are so kind that You willingly protect all those who simply bow down to You with respect, and thus You mercifully relieve all the distress of Your servants. In conclusion, my Lord, Your lotus feet are actually the suitable boat for crossing over the ocean of birth and death, and therefore even Lord Brahma and Lord Siva seek shelter at Your lotus feet.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.33)**))**

In KaliYuga, the process of self-realisation has been simplified, taking into consideration the many compromising factors that pose stiff impediments on the conditioned jiva's path of spiritual progress. Thus Lord Caitanya, fountainhead of all incarnation, appeared as His golden incarnation, in the guise of a devotee, to how everyone how to execute pure devotional service.

**‘Even a little endeavour on this progressive path will protect one from the greatest danger - falling down once again into the evolutionary cycle (birth in animal species or lower).’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**2.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.40)**))**

*ko nu rdjann indriyavan mukunda-caranambuja*  
*na bhajet sarvato-mrtyurupasyam amarottamaih*

**‘My dear King, in the material world the conditioned souls are confronted by death at every step of life. Therefore, who among the conditioned souls would not render service to the lotus feet of Lord Mukunda, who is worshipful even for the greatest of liberated souls?’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**11.2.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.2)**)**

The second half of this couplet from SrimadBhagavatam is the same as the second half of this verse from Sri Caitanya Candramrta.

na bhajet—would not worship; sarvatah-mrtyuh—being faced by death on all sides; upasyam—worshipable; amara-uttamaih—by the best of liberated personalities.

### Verse 96

*asa yasya padadvandve caitanyasya mahaprabhoh*  
*tasyendro dasavadbhati ka katha nrpakitake*

**Indra, king of the demigods, is as a servant of one who reposes full hope and faith in the safe sanctuary of the lotus feet of Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu; what to speak of earthly kings, who are in comparison like insects.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The doubt may arise, that kings may not want to take shelter at the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya; and since traditionally religious principles are propagated by the royal classes, then how will the Sankirtan movement spread?

Asa yasyapadadvandve- the king of the heavenly planets, Indra and other powerful personalities are always eager to serve those who have full faith and trust in Sri Caitanya, what to speak of puny earthly sovereigns? If this be the status of those who simply cultivate faith and trust in Sri Caitanya, then what about those who have fully surrendered at His feet, and what of those who are on the most exalted platform of devotion and surrender?

In this way, by the principles of a fortiori logic, one may establish the paramount position of Sri Caitanya and His devotees.

a fortiori- 'for a stronger reason'; used of a conclusion logically more certain than another

Karika:

*vusibhavanti devadya yasyasa gaurapadayoh*  
*ksudra nrpastu kim ganyas tad bhaktas tvadhikarika*

**‘Even the demigods become subservient to those who simply aspire to take shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya, what to speak of surrendered souls? In comparison to such demigods, the petty earthly rulers are not even worthy of consideration.’**

**Purport**

The most intelligent human beings in KaliYuga will participate in the Sankirtan movement inaugurated by Sri KrsnaCaitanya (SrimadBhagavatam 11.52). Sri KrsnaCaitanya and Sri Nityananda Prabhu are the sankirtanaika-pitarau -progenitors (in the sense of initiators) of the congregational chanting of the HolyNames of Bhagavan Sri Krsna, which reward the chanter with the highest benediction - KrsnaPrema. One who nurtures a hope (asa) to surrender at Sri KrsnaCaitanya's lotus feet becomes eligible to inherit the matchless gift of unnatojjvala-rasam- the most sublime and elevated spiritual rasa, loving exchanges with the Supreme Lord in the conjugal mood of the VrajaGopis. Such a rare soul is worshipful by yogis, philosophers, even by the demigods; what to speak of lesser beings.

Chanting the HolyNames drives away all mundane fear and purifies the heart of subtle desires for mukti, bhukti, siddhi, and so on. By chanting under the cooling shade of Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s lotus feet, these subtle desires give way to laulyam (greed) for VrajaBhavaSeva.

*krsna-bhakti-rasa-bhavita matih kriyatam yadi kuto ’pi labhyate*  
*tatra laulyam api mulyam ekalam janma-koti-sukrtair na labhyate*

**‘Absorption in pure devotional service to VrajendraNandan Krsna cannot be obtained by pious activities even in hundreds and thousands of lives. It can be attained only by paying one price - intense greed to obtain it. Hence, if it is available somewhere, one must purchase it immediately.’**  
**(**[**Padyavali**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/padyavali-rg)**)**

### Verse 97

*yasyasa krsna caitanye nrpadvari kimarthinah*  
*cintamanimayam prapya ко mudho rajatam vrajet*

**For one who aspires for the priceless treasure of Sri Caitanya’s lotus feet, what need is there to go to the gates of a king’s palace? After acquiring a touchstone, who is so foolish as to travel far and wide in search of silver?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may initially agree to the premise that demigods are subservient to surrendered souls and thus earthly sovereigns are petty in comparison; be that as it may. Speaking on behalf of the householders, however, the question arises- ‘how can they survive without receiving favours from kings?’

Yasya asa krsna-caitanya rajadvari kimarthinah- For one who keeps his faith and trust in Sri KrsnaCaitanya, what need has he to stand before the palace gates? Only a fool will continue to search for silver, after receiving a touchstone.

Karika:

*sri gaura bhajanam cintaratnam prapya mahajanah*  
*na yanti kvapi rajadau yanti cet karunavasah*

**‘The mahajanas, exalted saints who have received the touchstone of worship of Sri GauraHari, never visit kings to patronize their wealth. Indeed, if they go at all, it is only out of compassion; to try to deliver them.’ mahajana- also means capitalist**

**Purport**

The result of pious deeds performed according to the injunctions of the karma-kanda section of the Vedas is: bhukti (sense pleasures), bhoga (material comforts) and aisvarya (opulence). For someone too addicted to bhoga and aisvarya, the determination to act for the attainment of liberation does not develop in the heart or mind. Such a person has not the mature intelligence to perceive the insignificance of material opulence and bliss derived from bhoga. The lotus feet of Sri Caitanya are the storehouse of KrsnaPrema. Anyone who seeks shelter at His feet is certainly eligible to receive His mercy. This mercy transforms one’s heart from the habit of hankering after bhoga and aisvarya and dovetails it towards a search for permanent, eternal bliss. For this transformation to be translated into action, the association of pure devotees is needed.

Dhruva Maharaja, insulted by his step-mother and left unconsoled by his father, left the king’s palace at a tender age by the inspiration of his mother. Seeing his unwavering resolve to meet the Supreme Lord through the performance of severe austerities, Sri Narada Muni, best amongst the rsis and a highly elevated pure devotee of the Lord, came to Dhruva’s aid. He initiated Dhruva into the chanting of Sri Vasudeva’s HolyNames and left the brave young prince in the middle of the forest to continue the fulfilment of his vow. Finally, the Supreme Lord appeared before him, seated on the back of his carrier, Garuda. The enlightened Dhruva then prayed to the Lord:

**“Persons who worship You simply for the sense gratification of this bag of skin are certainly influenced by Your illusory energy. In spite of having You, who are like a desire-tree and are the cause of liberation from birth and death, foolish persons such as me desire benedictions from you for sense gratification, which is available even for those who live in hellish conditions.**  
**“My Lord, the transcendental bliss derived from meditating upon Your lotus feet or hearing about Your glories from pure devotees is so boundless that it is far beyond the stage of brahmananda, wherein one thinks himself merged in the impersonal Brahman, as one with the Supreme. Since brahmananda is also defeated by the transcendental bliss derived from devotional service, then what to speak of the temporary blissfulness of elevating oneself to the heavenly planets, which ultimately ends by the separating sword of time? Although one may be elevated to the heavenly planets, he falls down in due course of time.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**4.9.9-10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.9)**))**

### Verse 98

*dhyayanto girikandaresu bahavo brahmanubhuyasate*  
*yogabhyasaparasca santi bahavah siddha mahimandale*  
*vidya-saurya-dhanadibhisca bahavo jalpanti mithyoddhatah*  
*ко va gaurakrpam vinadya jagati premonmado nrtyati*

**There are many souls immersed deep in meditation in the depths of mountain caves, in constant contemplation of Brahman. There are also numerous yogis present within the orb of this earth, accomplished in mystic siddhis through their practice of astanga-yoga. The balance are engrossed in transient pursuits like mundane education, accumulation of wealth, power and influence, accustomed to boasting of their achievements, intoxicated as they are by false prestige and pride. Yet, in the absence of the mercy of Sri GauraHari , is there anyone now in this universe intoxicated with prema and thus dancing blissfully like a madman?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

‘Why do solitary yogis, immersed in meditation on Brahman, and others intoxicated with the pride of erudition, wealth, and so on, not aspire for the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya? Whatever taste (ruci) they may indulge in, you can be sure they are not relishing the nectar of prema.

‘Immersed deep in meditation on Brahman, in the depths of mountain caves, the jnana-yogis relish the bliss of brahmananda, thinking themselves to be non-different from that same Brahman. Yogis engage in their practices, striving to attain mystic perfections (siddhi), while the balance are intoxicated either by scholarship or wealth. Thus do they engage in endless prattle under the influence of their false pride. Let them do as they will.

‘But where in this universe is to be found that person dancing in ecstasy, inebriated with the elixir of prema-rasa, who hasn’t received the mercy of Sri Gauranga? The exultation experienced by the recipients of the grace of Sri GauraSundar is unparalleled; not to be found anywhere else. Therefore, abandon everything, and take full shelter at the lotus feet of Sri GauraHari.’

Karika:

*jnana-yoga-karma-nistha vahavah sand bhutale*  
*caitanya-caranambhoja krpajanya sukham kutah*

**‘In this universe there are innumerable adherents of jnana, yoga, karma, and the like; but where can anyone find blessed delight like this, born from the merciful lotus feet of Sri Caitanya?’**

**Purport**

*krsna-bhakta—niskama, ataeva ‘santa’*  
*bhukti-mukti-siddhi-kami—sakali ‘asanta ’*

**‘Those who desire bhukti (sense gratification), mukti (liberation) or siddhi (mystic perfections) are all agitated in the mind.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.149**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.149)**))**

Mental agitation is the result of strong material desires. From desire is born attachment to worldly relationships. Thus the karmi, jnani and yogi are all ultimately doomed to tread the treadmill of continuous birth and death, unless they realise that all processes and paths must culminate in bhakti-yoga. Only at the lotus feet of Sri KrsnaCaitanya is there to be found a safe sanctuary for all who would understand the higher values of life.

As Sri Krsna declares-

**‘once having reached My eternal abode, no one returns to this temporal material world of suffering.’ However, those who aspire for bhakti are fewer than the followers of other paths. ‘Out of many thousands among men, one may endeavour for perfection, and of those who have achieved perfection, hardly one knows Me in truth.’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**7.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.3)**)**

*prayo mumuksavas tesam kecanaiva dvijottama*  
*mumuksunam sahasresu kascin mucyeta sidhyati*  
*muktanam api siddhanam narayana-parayanah*  
*sudurlabhah prasantatma kotisv api maha-mune*

**‘O best of the brahmanas, Sukadeva Gosvami, out of many persons who follow religious principles, only a few desire liberation from the material world. Among many thousands who desire liberation, one may actually achieve liberation, giving up material attachment to society, friendship, love, country, home, wife and children. And among many thousands of such liberated persons, one who can understand the true meaning of liberation is very rare. О great sage, among many millions who are liberated and perfect in knowledge of liberation, one may be a devotee of Lord Narayana, or Krsna. Such devotees, who are fully peaceful, are extremely rare.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.14.4-5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/14.4)**))**

Srila A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupad comments:

“There are four classes of men, namely karmis, jnanis, yogis and bhaktas. This statement pertains especially to karmis and jnanis. A karmi tries to be happy within this material world by changing from one body to another. His objective is bodily comfort (bhoga), either in this planet or another (higher). When such a person becomes a jnani, however, he aspires for liberation from material bondage. Among many such persons who aspire for liberation one may actually be liberated during his life. Such a person gives up attachment for society, friendship, love, country, family, wife and children.”

Lord Caitanya’s mercy is available to all without exception. However, in order to become eligible to receive His mercy, the jiva must accumulate sufficient piety, which comes from associating with devotees; otherwise, due to his inherent ignorance and nescience, he will be ill-prepared to properly make use of the Lord’s mercy. The true sign that a jiva has become eligible, is that he has received the seed of pure devotion (bhakti-lata-bija) from a bonafide guru, a follower of Sri Rupa, Sanatana, or Raghunath Das. The fortunate jiva sows the seed in his heart, made fertile by sraddha (KrsnaConscious faith). By regularly chanting and hearing the HolyNames, as instructed by the guru, the seed fructifies and can mature into a fruit-bearing devotional creeper, bearing the sublime fruit of KrsnaPrema.

*evam-vratah sva-priya-nama-kirtya jatanurago druta-citta uccaih*  
*hasaty atho roditi rauti gayaty unmada-van nrtyati loka-bahyah*

**‘By chanting the HolyNames of the Supreme Lord, one comes to the stage of love of Krsna. Then the devotee is fixed in his vow as an eternal servant of the Lord, and he gradually becomes very much attached to a particular name and form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As his heart melts with ecstatic love, he laughs very loudly or cries or shouts. Sometimes he sings and dances like a madman, for he is indifferent to public Opinion.‘**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.2.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.40)**))**

### Verse 99

*kasivasinapi nа ganaye kim gayam margayamo*  
*muktih suktibhavati yadi me kah pararthaprasangah*  
*trasabhasah sphurati na maharaurave’pi kvah bhitih*  
*striputradau yadi krpayate devadevah sa gaurah*

**If Sri Caitanya, the worshipful Lord and Master of the Devas, confers His mercy upon me, then I do not value the association of the residents of Kasi; neither do I see any necessity of my gazing down the path to GayaDhama and the other holy places of pilgrimage? For me, liberation is like a small conchshell (cowrie), so what to speak of the other three goals: dharma, artha and kama? If I am not in the least afraid of the terrifying hell, MahaRaurava, then how can I be afraid of remaining as a grhastha, in the company of wife and children? Cowrie- a small shell formerly in use as a barter token of very low value**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

By the grace of Sri Caitanya, surrendered devotees are free from all hankerings and fears in this world. To highlight this truth, the author rebukes those who out of fear of ill treatment by family members (or over attachment to family members), take refuge in holy places like Kasi (Varanasi, Benares).

'If the object of worship of the demigods, Sri GauraCandra bestows his mercy upon me, then I will no longer have any regard for the residents of Kasi, and if this be the case, then what need have I of GayaDham?’

People take up residence in Kasi to attain mukti, while people go to Gaya to propitiate their forefathers. Compared to the mercy of Sri GauraHari, even mukti is insignificant to me, what to speak of the other purusarthas (goals of human life).

One may express reservation, not knowing how to deal with problems in the family (with wife and children).These problems are nothing compared to MahaRaurava, a most terrifying hellish planet. Yet, if for a devotee, even such a hellish situation as this instils no fear, then what is there to be feared from family life?

‘Relinquishing all mundane hopes, desires and fears, simply seek refuge of the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya. By his mercy alone one attains the pancam-purusartha, the highest spiritual perfection - GopiPrema.’

Karika:

*kasyader ganana na syanmoksah sambuka kaksakah*  
*kva bhir nirayapatnyadau sri caitanya krpa yadi*

**‘When a devotee is blessed with the mercy of Sri Caitanya, he does not have any regard for the dhamas (like Kasi); he considers mukti (liberation) as insignificant as cowries; and where is the fear of family life, when even horrible hellish planets instil no fear in him?’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“Persons seeking impersonal liberation reside in Kasi (Varanasi). People visit GayaDham to offer oblations (pinda) to their departed forefathers. Devotees of Lord GauraSundar are never eager or enthusiastic to perform karma-kanda rituals like sraddha and so on.”

The general mass, due to being conditioned by duality, are in ignorance about the Supreme Lord. They mistakenly think that the demigods in charge of the different departments of universal affairs are all-powerful.

*antavat tu phalam tesdm tad bhavaty alpa-medhasam*  
*devan deva-yajo yanti mad-bhakta yanti mam api*

**“Men of small intelligence worship the demigods though their fruits are limited and temporary. Those who worship the demigods go to the planets of the demigods, but My devotees ultimately reach my supreme planet.”**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**7.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.23)**))**

Srila Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad comments:

“The results achieved by the demigods’ benedictions are perishable, because within this material world, the planets, the demigods and their worshipers are all perishable. Therefore, it is clearly stated in this verse that all results achieved by worshiping demigods are perishable, and therefore such worship is performed by the less intelligent living entities. Because the pure devotee engaged in Krsna consciousness in devotional service of the Supreme Lord achieves eternal blissful existence that is full of knowledge, his achievement and those of the common worshipers of the demigods are different. The Supreme Lord is unlimited; His favour is unlimited; His mercy is unlimited. Therefore the mercy of the Supreme Lord upon His pure devotees is unlimited.”

Fortunate souls favoured by the Supreme Lord consider the goals of humanity (purusartha) as anarthas (unwanted material desires in the heart) that pose great obstacles in one’s spiritual progress towards achieving the supreme shelter of Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s lotus feet. Pure devotees refuse to accept moksa (liberation) even when offered by the Supreme Lord Himself.

*bhaktis tvayi sthiratara bhagavan yadi syad*  
*daivena nah phalati divya-kisora-murtih*  
*muktih svayam mukulitanjali senate ’sman*  
*dharmartha-kama-gatayah samaya-pratiksah*

**“O My Lord! If my devotion to You is steadfast and undeviating, then Your ever-fresh form of blossoming youth will automatically manifest before me. A separate endeavour for achieving mukti is unnecessary because she is ready with folded palms to offer her services. As for religiosity, wealth and sense gratification (dharma, artha, kama), they patiently wait for the time when their services are required. Neither mukti nor the other three goals of human life are required by the pure devotee.’**  
**(Sri KrsnaKarnamrta (**[**107**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/kk-kkg/107)**))**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s mercy is unlimited and inconceivable. It can reward the jiva with transcendental bliss far beyond his constitutional capacity. The first symptoms of this causeless mercy are an attraction for chanting the HolyNames, which in turn reduces material anxiety and suffering on the one hand, and on the other, augments one’s good fortune.

## PART IX - The Paramount Position of Sri Caitanya

### Verse 100

*mattakesarikisora vikramah premasindhu jagadaplavodyamah*  
*ko’pi divya navahemakandali komalo jayati gauracandramah*

**In subduing the malefic influences of KaliYuga, He is more powerful than a ferocious young lion; and yet softer than a tender bud of the golden Kundali flower. All glories to the GoldenMoon, Sri GauraCandra! always enthusiastic to cause the Ocean of DivineLove to ebb with the tides, thus inundating the world with KrsnaPrema.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

These ten verses describe Sri Caitanya’s beauty, qualities, sweet charm, potency and magnanimity, establishing the pre-eminence of His incarnation.

Jayati- He is present in the manifestation of His unsurpassable superiority. The verbal root is ji- intransitive; lending the connotation of predominance; ko ’pi- ineffable; matta-kesari- an infuriated young lion, proud of his strength that can conquer an elephant. Similarly, Sri GauraHari is victorious, like a young lion over elephant-like KaliYuga with its attendant ills and contaminations. Matta-kesari alludes to Sri GauraHari's strength, long neck, tapering waist, and broad chest.

The moonlike Sri GauraHari is always enthusiastic to create tidal waves in the ocean of prema, that flood the fourteen planetary systems. He is divya- transcendentally enchanting.

His brilliant form is softer, more lovely than the tender bud of the golden Kundali flower.

This verse contains various poetic ornaments: lupta upama (concealed simile), rupak alankar (metaphor, allegory), atisayokti (hyperbole) and vyatirek alahkar (excess of object and subject).

*yatha kathancit sadrsyam upama sa bhaved dvidha*  
*purana lupteli sadrsyevader yoga vilpayoh*

'There are two kinds of upama (partial similarity)- purna (expressed) and lupta (concealed). Conjugatives like sadrsa and iva are used in comparisons or similes; their elision is also used in upama.'

*abhinnayoh kancidamsa upamanopa meyayoh*  
*tat tadatmyarh dvayos tat tad rupakam kathyate budhaih*

**‘When certain aspects of the comparison are identical in character with the object of comparison it is known as rupaka'**  
**(AlankarKaustubha)**

Karika:

*nava kancana-handala kanta-tanuh*  
*priyatambudhi vardhi-saci-prajanuh*  
*jitakesari divya kisora madah*  
*kila gaura vidhurjjayati pramadah*

**‘All glories to Sri GauraVidhu, son of Mother Saci. Fully intoxicated with prema, may his eminence continue to shine with splendour. His bodily lustre is as resplendent as the tender bud of a golden Kundali blossom. His youthful, Divine ardour resembles that of a young lion in rut, the Supreme vanquisher of pride. He constantly expands the ocean of exclusive affection for Sri Krsna, Himself fully immersed in the same.’**  
**(Vidhu-moon)**

**Purport**

Sri KrsnaCaitanya has another unique and unprecedented feature, unlike any other incarnation of Godhead. His weapons and accoutrements are none of the usual- sankha (conchshell), cakra (disc), gada (mace) and padma (lotus). According to different Gaudiya Vaisnava acaryas like Sri Rupa, Sri Jiva and Sri Krsnadas Kaviraj, His weapons (astra) are: the HolyNames, His matchless, exquisite beauty and His expansions and eternal associates like Sri Nityananda, Sri AdvaitAcarya and others. With these weapons Sri KrsnaCaitanya nullified the ill effects of KaliYuga.

**‘There is nothing more powerfully effective in counteracting the contaminating influence of KaliYuga other than the MahaMantra. This is the final verdict of the entire Vedic literature.’**  
**(KaliSantaraUpanisad)**

**‘One can vividly see His glowing complexion of molten gold, which dispels the darkness of ignorance. The sinful life of the living beings results from ignorance. To destroy that ignorance, He has brought various weapons, such as His plenary (eternal) associates, His devotees and the HolyNames.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**3.59-62**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/3.59)**))**

The greatest ignorance consists of activities (whether religious or irreligious) that are opposed to devotional service. They are to be known as sins. Raising his arms, chanting the HolyNames and looking upon all with deep love, He drives away all sins and drowns everyone in love of Krsna.

### Verse 101

*saundarye kamakotih sakalajana samahaladane candrakotir*  
*vatsalye matrkotistridasavitapinam kotiraudaryasare*  
*gambhirye’mbhodhikotirmadhurimani sudhaksiramadhvika kotir*  
*gauro devah jiyat pranayarasapade darsitascarya kotih*

**All glories to Sri GaurangaDeva (always engaged in His DivinePlay). His beauty shames the beauty of ten million Cupids; showering mirthful delight on everyone, His presence is more soothing than millions of moons; His affection surpasses the affection of ten million mothers; His munificence is so wonderful that the generous branches of ten million wish-fulfilling desire trees (kalpa-vrksa) must hang in shame; His depth is more profound than ten million oceans; the sweetness of His charm challenges the combined potency of ten million oceans of nectar, milk and honey; the diverse and wondrous beauty of his absorption in erotic sentiments is millions of times greater than the sweet mellows of conjugal affecton previously demonstrated through his clever expertise (in KrsnaLila). All glories, all glories to Sri GaurangaDeva.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Using various poetic devices (alankar), the author continues to describe the beauty and generosity of spirit in Sri Gauranga; how He showers everyone with happiness, protects His devotees, is very grave and at the same time, charming.

Sa Gaura devah- always engaged in pastimes with His eternal associates for the purpose of tasting prema-rasa; and, to distribute this GopiPrema to the world. Next he is eulogized with seven adjectives: saundarye kamakotih- whose beauty outshines billions of Cupids; tridasa-vitapinam- whose magnanimity surpasses billions of wish-fulfilling desire trees; pranaya rasapade- who exhibits an endless kaleidoscope of ecstatic emotions in the matter of pranaya-rasa (loving exchanges); jiyat- always victorious.

*visasoktih parikarah syat sakutair visasanai*

**‘When self-perpetuating adjectives qualify the noun, this is known as parikara alankar’**  
**(AlankarKaustubha)**

Karika:

*smaracandrasuradrumamatrsata-priyasindhusudharucirddikatah*  
*atisundaratadika-kotiguno jaya madhava kancanakantitano*

**‘All glory to Madhava, whose bodily lustre is of molten gold. His qualities of beauty, comforting coolness, generosity and affection are tens of millions of times greater than the combined qualities of hundreds and hundreds of Cupids, Full moons, Heavenly desire-trees and Mothers, as though an ocean of the most delectable, pleasing, sweet nectar.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Personality Sri Krsna's transcendental pastimes are of two kinds, manifest and unmanifest. Both of them are in the plane of visuddha-sattva, though the manifest pastimes may be perceivable even with mundane vision. When Sri Krsna appeared, towards the end of DvaparYuga, many demons, like his uncle Kamsa, could clearly perceive his presence, without realising, however, his transcendental identity as the Supreme Personality. Seeing Sri Krsna's transcendental pastimes with mundane vision and realising their transcendental, spiritual nature are two very different paradigms.

Sri Krsna makes His pastimes visible to gross materialists out of His causeless compassion. Moved by the pain of their constant fear, generated by the wear and tear of living in this material world, He affords everyone a chance to purify their consciousness by witnessing His 1i1a with His eternal associates. His pastimes in Vraja are extremely confidential, esoteric. Such activities can only be understood if Sri Krsna Himself explains their mystery, as He did in His incarnation as bhakta-rupa (the form of a pure devotee), Sri KrsnaCaitanya. As Sri Krsna Caitanya, the Supreme Godhead declined to reveal His true identity as the SupremeLord and instead immersed Himself in his duty of inaugurating the Sankirtan movement. Without His advent, the world would have remained in darkness, unable to penetrate the mysteries of Sri Krsna's beauty or the sublime profundity of His pastimes. He incarnated, not as a lila-avatar but as pracchanna-avatar, in keeping with His name, Triyuga.

*kaliyuge lilavatara na kare bhagavan*  
*ataeva ‘triyuga 'kari‘kahitara nama*

**‘In KaliYuga, there is no lila-avatar of the Supreme Personality; therefore He is known as Triyuga. This is one of His HolyNames.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**6.99**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/6.99)**))**

Srila Prabhupada comments:

“A lila-avatar is an incarnation of the Lord who performs a variety of activities without making any special endeavour. He always has one pastime after another, all full of transcendental pleasure, and these pastimes are fully controlled by the Supreme Person. The Supreme Person is totally independent of all others in these pastimes.”

### Verse 102

*svapadambhojaikapranayalahari sadhanabhrtam*  
*siva-brahmadinamapi ca sumahavismayabhrtam*  
*mahapremavesat kimapi natatamunmada iva*  
*prabhurgauro jiyat prakata paramascarya mahima*

**May Prabhu GauraSundar be glorified - He who is absorbed in adoration of his very own lotus feet, where waves of affection smother the worshiper; He who strikes wonder into the hearts of the demigods headed by Lord Siva and Lord Brahma; and who, enraptured by ecstatic love, dances with the frenzy of a madman. He has revealed astonishing wonders the likes of which this world has never seen before.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Further revelations of the super-excellent eminence of PrabhuGaura include the astonishment of Lord Siva and the other demigods. His devotees experience Him as an amazing magician, holding them spellbound by his unprecedented

magnificence. Gauro jiyat- He is the Supreme, Independent Personality, the SupremeController (Prabhu); may His radiant eminence continue to shine supreme. He specifically demonstrates His astounding distinctions to His devotees.

‘How does he do that?’

svapadambhojaikapranayalahari sadhanabhrtam- His aspirants adore His lotus feet with vociferous affection, engaging all their senses in the nourishment of eternally perfected emotions that the same might manifest their full variegatedness.

*nitya-siddha krsna-prema ‘sadhya ’ kabhu naya*  
*sravanadi-suddha-citte karaye udaya*

**‘Pure love for Krsna is eternally established in the hearts of the living entities. It is not something to be gained from another source. When the heart is purified by hearing and chanting, this love naturally awakens.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**22.108**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.108)**))**

*krti-sadhya bhavet sadhya-bhava sa sadhanabhidha*  
*nitya-siddhasya bhavasya prakatyam hrdi sadhyata*

**‘When transcendental devotional service, by which love for Krsna is attained, is executed by the senses, it is called sadhana-bhakti, or the regulative discharge of devotional service. Such devotion eternally exists within the heart of every living entity. The awakening of this eternal devotion is the potentiality of devotional service in practice.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.2)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**22.105**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.105)**))**

Indeed, cultivation of Krsna consciousness cannot be accomplished with the gross, material senses. Its appearance is always a direct manifestation of the mercy of Sri Krsna or His devotees.

The demigods headed by Lord Siva and Lord Brahma have attained the paramount perception of the glories of Sri Gaura through their own experience of His astonishing attributes.
