mahapremavesat kimapi natatamunmada- mahaprema is indicative of MahaBhava; as a result of the mercy of Sri Gauranga, the devotees have become possessed by MahaBhava, and are thus dancing in ecstasy like madmen.

Karika:

*siva-padmaja-daivata vismayane*  
*svapadambuja sat pada bhakta gane*  
*vitatadbhuta hi mahimadibharah*  
*kaladhauta tanur jayatisa varah*

**‘Those lotus feet that accomplish astonishment in the Devas, headed by Lords Siva and Brahma, are the nectar of His own wealth, revealed to those devotees who, like bumblebees, are inebriated with the full-to-overflowing magnificence of his grandeur. All glories to the best among the Lords and Masters of the universes. He whose bodily lustre is of molten gold.’**

**Purport**

*‘Dancing (nrtya) is one the many symptoms of anubhava.*

**Anubhava- spiritual emotion which acts as a catalyst, manifesting in the body different physical transformations, also known as udbhasvara, brought about by intense loving sentiments (bhava) in the hear ’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu(**[**2.2.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/2.2.20)**))**

**‘He who feels profound devotional ecstasy while dancing before Me in jubilation, manifesting different features of bodily expression, can burn away all the accumulated sinful reactions accumulated over many thousands of manvantaras.'**  
**(DvarakaMahatmya)**

manvantara- there are fourteen Manus in one day of Brahma. A manvantara, the life-span of one Manu, is given as 71 multiplied by 4,320,000 years.

Sri Narada declares:

**‘All the birds of sinful activities fly away from the body of anyone who claps and dances before the Deity, showing manifestations of ecstasy.'**  
**(DvarakaMahatmya)**

Just as by clapping the hands one can cause many birds to fly away, similarly the birds of all sinful activities which are sitting on the body can be made to fly away simply by dancing and clapping before the Deity of Krsna.

### Verse 103

*madyatkoti mrgendrahunkrtirava-stigmamsukoticchavih*  
*kotindudbhatasitalo gatijita-pronmattakotidvipah*  
*namna durgatatakoti-niskrtikaro brahmadikotisvarah*  
*kotyadvaitasiromanir vijayate srisrisacinandanah*

**His voice is deep and resonant like the roaring of ten million mad young lions; His bodily effulgence is more dazzling than the splendour of ten million suns; yet He is at the same time more cooling than ten million moons. His gait is far more enchanting than ten million intoxicated elephants. Through the potency of Sri NamPrabhu He has released many millions of miscreants from their suffering. He is the Supreme Controller of tens of millions of partial controllers (demigods) headed by Lord Brahma; He is the CrestJewel, the worshipful Lord of tens of millions of monist philosophers, as the SupremeAbsolute (the impersonal Brahman being nothing more than His bodily effulgence), the full and complete manifestation of the non-dual AbsoluteTruth. May Sri SaciNandan always be victorious.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Once more Sri GauraHari’s consummate eminence is confirmed through descriptions of His superlative prowess, potency, effulgence; conciliatory, comforting qualities; alluring gait; opulence, and so on.

His thunderous outcries, while in the throes of beguiling prema, are like the roaring of millions of lions. His bodily effulgence is more dazzling than that of millions of suns. Mortals are hard-put to tolerate the heat and power of just one sun, yet His bodily effulgence is brighter than the radiance of millions of suns. Though the Lord’s bodily effulgence is more intense than ten million suns, it is simultaneously more cooling than ten million moons (kotindu), whose rays soothe the conditioned souls incinerated by the inferno of material existence.

His gati (gait), while under the influence of ecstatic prema, is more enchanting than that of a million maddened elephants. By the potency of namna (Nama- the HareKrsna MahaMantra), He is the saviour of millions of destitute wretches. He is the SupremeController of innumerable Devas (demigods- partial controllers), like Brahma and Siva. He is the quintessential, human form of ParamBrahma (the SupremeBrahman).

Sri GauraSundara’s supremacy is depicted with the help of udatta alankar.

*parasamrddhir vastunam udattamih*

**‘A comparison with the best feature of an object is called udatta alankar.'**

Karika:

*madamatta mrgendrasatayuta prema-*  
*hunkrtibhih sukhayams ca bahun*  
*sukha cinmaya koti-siromukutah*  
*kanakanci tanur jayati pranatah*

**‘His rumbling outbursts, while experiencing profound prema, defeat the roaring of billions of lions, bringing ecstatic exultation to countless people. He is the crest jewel of millions of crowns of soulful delight. May Sri Gauranga, the golden Dancer Divine, be always victorious!’**

**Purport**

The learned author describes in this verse Sri GauraHari’s Divine opulences, which He possesses in absolute, unlimited quantity. Steeped in sankirtana rasa, His thunderous exultations reverberate in the all-pervasive ether, driving away all inauspiciousness in the world.

Sri SaciNandan GauraHari initiated the prescribed religion for the age of Kali- chanting the HolyNames (the HareKrsna MahaMantra). This is the greatest benediction for humanity.

*yad-brahma-saksat krtinisthayapi vinasa mayati vinana bhogaih*  
*apaiti nama! sphuranena tatte prarabdha karmeti virauti vedah*

**‘One may continuously meditate on impersonal Brahman, but the propensity to subtlety enjoy this material nature is not reformed within the heart. As soon as one utters the HolyNames of the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna, all one’s prarabdha-karma (all the sinful and pious reactions accumulated over countless lifetimes) is instantly obliterated.’ (SriKrsnaNamastak(4))**

### Verse 104

*yo margo durasunvo bata iha balatkantako yo’tidurgo*  
*mithyartha bhramako yah sadapi rasamayananda-nihsyandako yah*  
*sadyah pradyotayamstam prakatitamahima snehavan hrdguhayah*  
*ko’pyantardhvantahanta sa jayati navadvipa-dipyatpradipah*

**That path which is very distant and isolated, practically made invisible (sunyavad), Hai! (Oh me oh my!) filled with thorns and thus very treacherous (kamyakarmavad), and which is posted with signs that give false directions, someties leading the pursuers of this path around in circles (mayavad, vivartavad) - is now, all of a sudden, flowing freely with the ecstatic mellows of bhakti, awakened by He who has revealed His glories to light up this path and to destroy the darkness in the cavelike hearts of those souls wandering around in gloomy pessimism. May He be victorious! The Lamp of Navadvip.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In this verse Sri Gauranga’s primacy as Divinity is asserted through further descriptions of His transcendental qualities. He is compared to a lamp that dissipates the darkness of ignorance in the heart, revealing the path that leads to nigudha-prema-rasa. Sri GauraHari is navadvipa-dipyat-pradipah- the lamp that illumines Navadvip (which was dipyat- to be kindled or stimulated; sunk in darkness).

That celebrated path, well worth striving for, but which was previously very far away and devoid of travellers, is now illuminated with joy, by the grace of GauraHari. Bata!-(interjection expressing astonishment or regret)- Ah! Oh! Alas! That path was previously choked by the dense thorns of dry empiricism, fruitive, ritualistic activities, and the like. Thus was it atigurgah- very hazardous. The fatal attraction for those that previously tried to traverse this path in the dark, was the false promise of material enjoyment, those evanescent will o’ the wisps (ignus fatuus).

By revealing his glories and prowess, He destroys the darkness of ignorance in the dungeonlike hearts of the jivas of KaliYuga. Dhvantahanta- destroying the darkness of: ignorance, offenses, lust, anger, and so on. Snehavan- sneha means oil, ghee or any unctuous substance, as well as love and affection-nigudha-prema.

Sri SaciNandan appeared in Navadvip as a ghee lamp, filled with the ghee of love and affection, to dissipate the darkness within the conditioned jivas ’ hearts. He has uprooted all the thorns from the path of life, lighting the way with the transcendental happiness of prema-rasa. May He be victorious.

Karika:

*ruci dipakarupa sacitanujah priyahrttama adikanasamayah*  
*nijabhdva cakasan-dipticayo jayatiha mahamahimadimayah*

**‘His bodily lustre is the form of a brilliant ghee lamp, the radiance of which is His delightful bhava, which completely destroys the darkness in the hearts of all, illuminating the entire universe at one and the same time. Such are His glories. Victory to Sri GauraHari, the darling son of Mother Saci!’**

**Purport**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Prabhupad comments:

mithyartha bhramako - an illusion wherein falsehood presents itself as truth; thus, even demigods and philosophers are put into illusion about the path of pure bhakti, falsely thinking that pseudo bhakti(michabhakti) and pretentious bhakti are the actual path of pure bhakti.

**‘Completely rejecting all religious activities which are materially motivated, this BhagavataPurana propounds the highest truth, which is understandable by those devotees who are fully pure in heart.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**1.1.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.2)**)**

*acintyah khalu ye bhava na tams tarkena yojayet*  
*prakrtibhyah param yac ca tad acintyasya laksanam*

**‘Anything transcendental to material nature is inconceivable and thus cannot be grasped through mundane arguments. Therefore, one should not try to understand transcendental subject matter through mundane intellect and argument.’**  
**(MahaBharat BhismaParva (5.22))**

*svalpapi rucir eva syad bhakti-tattvavabodhika*  
*yuktis tu kevald naiva yad asya apratisthata*

**‘If a person has even a little taste for understanding devotional service, the revealed scriptures will bring him nearer to the truth of bhakti. But for one who is only interested in speculation and book knowledge and who does not engage in practical service, understanding will never be conclusive.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.1.45**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.1.45)**))**

**‘All living entities are born into delusion, a product of their desire and hate.’**  
**(BhagavadGita** [**7.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.27)**)**

**‘Even demigods and sages are bewildered by this temporary material creation, by which the reactions of the three gunas appear factual, although they are unreal.’ (SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.1.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.1)**))**

The entire gamut of transcendental realisation is beyond our capacity. Thus, without the help of sadhu, guru and sastra externally, and sraddha (faith) internally, it is not possible to develop the minutest degree of perception of transcendental subject matters.

**‘Sraddha is confident, firm faith that by rendering transcendental loving service to Krsna one automatically performs all subsidiary activities. Such faith is favourable to the discharge of devotional service.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila** [**22.62**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.62)**)**

Thus, without these external and internal guides (guardian angels), one may blunder through life after life, searching for genuine transcendental experience, that can only come from treading the path of bhakti.

**‘The words of the spiritual master constitute the transmission of transcendental knowledge (divya jnana) revealed within the heart. Thus does prema-bhakti dawn, simultaneously destroying avidya (nescience).’**  
**(Srila Narottama das Thakur)**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur explains:

om ajnana-timirandhasya jnananjana-salakaya caksur unmilitam yena tasmai sri-gurave namah  
‘I offer obeisance to Sri GuruDeva, who, by applying the salve of transcendental knowledge has opened my eyes to the truth, destroying (the five types of) nescience:

**Ignorance of one’s real identity, false identification with the body, the delusion of being the enjoyer, duality (absorption in bodily enjoyment), and fear. These five types of nescience (ajnana) produce mundane desires for religiosity, wealth, sense gratification and liberation - thus constituting the darkness of ignorance.’**  
**(GautamiyaTantra)**

### Verse 105

*duradeva dahan kutarkasalabhan kotindu samsitalo*  
*jyotih kandalasadma-sanmadhurima bahyantaradhvantahrt*  
*sasnehasayavrtti-divyavisarattejah suvarnadyutih*  
*karunyadiha jajvaliti sa navadvtpa-pradipo’dbhutah*

**This most extraordinary Lamp of Navadvip bums with its light, even from afar, locusts in the form of fallacious sophists, whose only business centers around speculation, false logic and theories. It’s flame is more cooling than millions of moons, incomparably soothing, the source of such a sweet light that destroys the gloom both within and without. The wick is soaked in the ghee of sublime affection; its golden glow suffuses the earth with His Divine radiance, refulgent with compassion.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Once again, using the simile of a glittering ghee lamp, Sri Gaura's distinction is depicted.

In the transcendentally opulent land of Navadvip, the wondrous lamp, Sri GauraCandra is ever-shining. He enlightens the prisonlike hearts of the jivas with the brilliant bhava of sublime prema.

‘What are the special characteristics of this ghee lamp?’ An ordinary lamp burns the moths and insects that fly into its flames, whereas this lamp incinerates the speculators and mothlike empiricists, even from a great distance. Other lamps radiate heat, whereas this unique lamp is more cooling than millions of moons.

Jyotih-kandala-samvalan- the residence, the source of light in the universe, this exceptional, golden lamp is madhurima-possessed of such an incredibly sweet light, the likes of which we have never seen before. Generally lamps shed light only in open spaces, not penetrating into closed-up places, whereas this extraordinary lamp dissipates darkness both without and within (our hearts).

Sasnehasaya-vartti- the asaya, the vessel that holds the ghee (sneha- affection) is the heart. When the ghee (affection) reaches the melting point, then the vartti (wick; activity function of the heart) glows with the golden aura of prema - ‘He whose heart has been ignited with bhava, from the embodiment of MahaBhava (Srimati Radharani), and thus shines with her Divine, golden splendour, burning with compassion, (karunyadiha jajvaliti) - this amazing Lamp of Navadvip.’

Karika:

*vidhu-sitala-duradahojvalitah priyatasaya-vartti mahomahitah*  
*paramadbhuta-dipa-sacitanayah satatam jvalati pranayadimayah*

**‘Sri SaciNandan GauraHari, a most astonishing lamp, burns forever bright, filled with the light of рranауа (love, affection, friendship, good feelings, regard). Burning from afar, this most celebrated lamp is yet as cooling as the moon. The wick of affection burns in the heart (receptacle), with the intense light of benedictory welfare.’**

**Purport**

**‘To show them special mercy, I, dwelling in their hearts, destroy with the shining lamp of knowledge the darkness born of ignorance.’**  
**BhagavadGita (**[**10.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.11)**)**

Srila Prabhupada comments:

“Lord Krsna tells Arjuna that basically there is no possibility of understanding the Supreme Truth, the Absolute Truth, Personality of Godhead, simply by speculation, for the Supreme Truth is so great that it is not possible to understand Him or to achieve Him simply by making a mental effort. Man can go on speculating for several millions of years, but if he is not devoted, if he is not a lover of the Supreme Truth, he will never understand Krsna, the Supreme Truth. Only by devotional service is the Supreme Truth, Sri Krsna pleased, and by His inconceivable energy He can reveal Himself in the heart of the pure devotee. The pure devotee always has Krsna within his heart; and with the presence of Krsna, who is just like the sun, the darkness of ignorance is at once dissipated. This is the special mercy rendered to the pure devotee by Krsna.”

Ghee, clarified butter is soft and unctuous, and when it melts it becomes sneha. Sneha is the heightened state of prema, when love and affection for the beloved flows naturally and uninterrupted.

sandras citta-dravam kurvan prema ‘sneha’ itiryate ksanikasyapi neha syad vislesasya sahisnuta

**‘That aspect of prema in which the melting of the heart for the lover is concentrated is called sneha, affection. The symptom of such affection is that the lover cannot for a moment remain without the association of the beloved.’**  
**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**3.2.84**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/3.2.84)**) quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**19.178**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.178)**)**

sneha- affection, tenderness; attachment; love; viscidity; oily substance; gloss; smoothness.

### Verse 106

*citkarairdasdinmukham mukharayannattattahasacchata-*  
*vicibhih sphutakundakairavagana prodbhasi kurvannabhah*  
*sarvangam pavanoccalaccaladalaprayaprakampam dadhan*  
*mattah premarasonmadaplutagatir gauro harih sobhate*

**His loud shouts echo in all directions; waves of resounding, lustrous laughter, like peals of lightning, light up the sky like blooming Kunda and Lotus flowers; His body trembles like the leaves of a Asvattha tree, blown by the wind. Driven to madness while bathing in the mellows of prema, there is nothing more beautiful than the beatitude of Sri GauraHari.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri GauraHari’s Divine majesty waxes as anubhava and sattvika-bhava manifest in His person; sobhate- a picture of loveliness. Huhkar / citkar- loud roaring due to ecstatic sentiments (laughter, grief, etc.); mukharayan- resound. Sri Gaura, under the influence of ecstatic emotion, cries out, ‘Ha Krsna!’ lamenting in separation from His beloved, His voice resounds in all directions. The next moment attatta-hasacchata vicibhih- loud peals of laughter in excessive rapture reverberate from His lotus mouth in waves; His teeth, as white as Kunda and Kumud blossoms, light up the sky. Though His body is very well-built, emanating Divine power, it trembles like the leaves of an Asvattha tree, touched by a gentle breeze {pavanoccalat), all due to the ecstasy of prema. Thus totally absorbed in DivineLove (premarason), He becomes mad (mada), waves of ecstasy causing his swanlike gait and other movements to appear as though choreographed, meant to entrance everyone that crosses His wake.

Karika:

*mukhari krta citkrti digvidisah priyatarasam unmadakundayasah*  
*dhvanihasamahojjvala visnupadah parisobhita isavaro varadah*

**‘Pre-eminent among all the Isvaras (Divinity, Controlling administrators of the universe), including all the incarnations of Lord Visnu Himself, Sri GauraHari is beautified by blazing, bright and brilliant peals of loud laughter, as His resounding shouts fill the ten directions, having gone mad in the ecstasy of savouring the flavour of the moods and sentiments of His Dearmost.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Personality Sriman Mahaprabhu's advent in this world and His activities are full of transcendental mystery. Simultaneously He accomplished many extraordinary miracles and fulfilled the prophesies of numerous scriptures foretelling His appearance. He is a covered incarnation, whose identity as the highest Divinity is camouflaged by His disguise as a devotee.

*ei-mata bhakta-bhava kari’ angikara*  
*apani acari’ bhakti karila pracara*

**‘In this way, assuming the sentiment of a devotee, He preached the science of devotional service to the Supreme Lord while practicing it Himself.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila(**[**4.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.41)**)**

Srila Prabhupada comments:

“Svarup Damodar Gosvami has described Lord Caitanya as Krsna Himself with the attitude of Radharani, or a combination of Radha and Krsna. The intention of Lord Caitanya is to taste Krsna’s sweetness in transcendental love. He does not care to think of Himself as Krsna, because He wants the position of Radharani. We should remember this. A class of so-called devotees called the nadiya-nagaris or gaura-nagaris pretend that they have the sentiment of gopis toward Lord Caitanya, but they do not realize that He placed Himself not as the enjoyer, Krsna, but as the enjoyed, the devotee of Krsna.  
“Lord Caitanya has accepted the role of Radharani, and we should support that position, as Svarup Damodar did in the Gambhira (the room where Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu stayed in Puri). He always reminded Lord Caitanya of Radha’s feelings of separation as they are described in SrimadBhagavatam, and Lord Caitanya appreciated his assistance.”

Overcome with the spiritual sentiments of Srimati Radhika, the embodiment of Krsna’s pleasure-potency hladini-sakti, SriGauranga often went into trance, exhibiting ecstatic symptoms.

*evam-vratah sva-priya-nama-kirtya*  
*jatanurago druta-citta uccaih*  
*hasaty atho roditi rauti gayaty*  
*unmada-van nityati loka-bahyah*

**‘When a person is truly advanced in Divine prema and takes pleasure in chanting the HolyNames of the Supreme Lord, who is very dear to him, he becomes spiritually agitated and loudly chants the HolyNames. Simultaneously he also laughs loudly, cries, becomes listless and chants just like a madman, not caring for others.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.2.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.40)**))**

### Verse 107

*nirddosascarunrtyo vidhutamalinata-vakrabhavah kadacin*  
*mhsesapranitapatrayaharana mahapremapiyusa varsi*  
*udbhutah ko’pi bhagyodayarucirasacigarbha dugdhamburaser*  
*bhaktanam hrccakorasvadita pada rucirbhati gaurangacandrah*

**Bathed in ineffable splendour, the Dancing Moon, Sri GauraCandra has arisen from the Milk Ocean womb of the most pleasing and beautiful Mother Sack This moon is of spotless beauty and character, free of flaws, devoid of aberrations and deceit. It causes a rain of Prema nectar to fall upon all living entities, removing the heat of their distress. His devotees’ hearts are like Cakora birds, who only relish the ambrosial radiance of His lotus feet for their sustenance.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

A certain golden moon with a dazzling lustre, free from any flaws, spreads its radiance all around. Other moons are dependent on the night, but not this moon. Other moons do not and cannot dance, but this golden moon dances most captivatingly. The moon has various flaws: it is bent, crooked (vakra- also means crafty, cunning), has blemishes, wanders around alone at night, gradually fades, getting smaller and smaller (wanes and waxes), and is the friend of poison, having been born from the milk ocean (wherein poison was also produced). However, simply by seeing this moon, the jivas'flaws, contamination and deceitfulness are eradicated. Ordinary moons cannot destroy the threefold miseries of mankind, yet Sri GauraCandra removes the miseries of all living entities, bathing them in a deluge of the nectar of prema.

The Moon of Gaura arose (udbhutah) from the MilkOcean womb of the most fortunate and beautiful Mother Saci. The brilliant splendour (rucirbhati) of His lotus feet (pada) sustains the hearts of His devotees who are like Cakora birds.

Cakora- Greek partridge (Perdix rufa)- fabled to subsist on moonbeams

Karika:

*sa saci-jaladhijata nisapatir dina-ratri rucir nataraja gatih*  
*nija bhakta cakorakarasya padah paribhdti jagatrayatapanudah*

**‘Lord of the night, the GauraMoon appeared from the MilkOcean womb of Sri SaciDevi, to light up the night and the day with His splendour, and to drive away the heat of the afflictions of the three worlds, moving with the gait of the King of Dancers. His devotees are like thirsty Cakora birds, subsisting from the radiance of His lotus feet.’**

**Purport**

The unalloyed devotees of the Supreme Lord are jivan-mukta, liberated even while living in the material world. Their gross and subtle bodies are spiritualised due to constant contact with transcendence, like an iron rod that has accepted the fiery nature of fire after sitting in its close embrace. When Srila Sanatan Gosvami travelled from Vrindaban to JagannathPuri, he was infected on the way with puss-filled ulcers all over the body, as a result of drinking contaminated water in Jharikhanda forest. Embarrassed to meet Sriman Mahaprabhu in this condition, he wished to end his life under the wheel of Lord Jagannatha’s chariot. However, Sriman Mahaprabhu forcibly embraced him and cured him even though Sanatan tried to avoid Mahaprabhu, fearing his contaminated body would soil His beloved Lord’s transcendental form. Mahaprabhu used this pastime to underline the truth that a pure devotee’s body is not material.

At the time of initiation with the Divine mantra, the devotee’s body becomes the property of the Lord and by practicing bhakti-yoga his body becomes spiritualised. Sri Caitanya thus told Sanatan Gosvami:

*prabhu kahe,------ “tomara deha mora nija-dhana*  
*tumi more kariyacha atma-samarpana*

**Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu said, “Your body is My property. You have already surrendered unto Me. Therefore you no longer have any claim to your body.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila(**[**4.76**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/4.76)**))**

Pure devotees like Sri Sanatan are like Cakora birds who cannot sustain their lives without drinking the ambrosial moonbeams emanating from the Lord’s lotus feet. Pure devotees of this stature are not of this material world, rather, they are eternal residents of the spiritual realm, as confirmed by Srila Rupa Gosvami:

*iha yasya harer dasye karmana manasa gira*  
*nikhilasv apy avasthasu jivan-muktah sa ucyate*

**‘One who engages in the transcendental service of the Supreme Lord in body, mind and word is considered liberated in all conditions of material existence.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu(**[**1.2.87**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.84)**))**

### Verse 108

*sincan sincannayanapayasa pandugandasthalantam*  
*muncan muncan pratimuhuraho dirghanisvasajatam*  
*uccaih krandan karunakarunodgirna-haheti-ravo*  
*gaurah ko’pi vrajavirahini bhavamagnascakasti*

**Incessant tears, like oblations from His eyes, stream down His pallid cheeks; Alas! can there be no cessation to the shedding of such a waterfall. Deep sighs engender louder lamentation, as He piteously cries out (Ha Krsna!), pondering the whereabouts of His Beloved. Such a shimmering scene was presented by Sri GauraHari, lost as He was in the moods-of-separation of the VrajaGopis.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Having drowned in the mellows of the moods of those forlorn maidens of Vraja, stricken by feelings of separation from their Beloved, the symptoms of His ecstatic emotions are being portrayed.

Gaura ко api cakasti- He presents such a pretty picture, shimmering tears gliding down his pallid cheeks, immersed as He is in the mood and sentiments of Srimati Radhika (vrajavirahini).

The use of repetitive words, sincan sincan (sprinkling, pouring), muncan muncan (shedding), suggests continuation; (of) the mystic state of sattvik-bhava. The word gandasthala (cheek) is in singular number since it refers to only the left cheek (the left side of the body is the female side). The gopis would sit, languishing in lassitude, with their left cheek resting on their left arm, their tears thus falling to that side, as they ponder deeply the whereabouts of their Beloved.

Pandu (pale) signifies the ecstatic symptom called vaivarnya (pallor), one of the eight transcendental transformations exhibited in the body when ecstatic emotion is present. Heaving a deep sigh (dirgha-nisvasa), the tears start to fall, followed by loud crying, the breaths now coming in quick succession, loud lamentation pours out, in the form- Ha! (Alas!), an exclamation indicative of a preponderance of karuna-rasa (mournful, pitiful, pathos). When Srimati Radhika’s loud lamentations echoed throughout the forest, the bees, birds, deer, and even the trees and shrubs, would weep in sympathy.

Karika:

*nayanasru-jalapluta gandayugah kalitasvasana vrajabhavavasah*  
*virahartti sakhi-rati-magnatarah paribhdti ca ko’pi sugauravarah*

**‘His two cheeks bathed in incessant streams of tears falling from His lotus eyes; impelled by the winds of deep sighs, the Best among the most Brilliant, Sri Gaura has become totally subjugated by the mood and sentiments of the VrajaGopis, immersed as they are in feelings of separation from their Dearmost object of attachment.’**

**Purport**

Of the many reasons Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu accepted the role of a devotee, an important one was to be a dependable and trustworthy preceptor of the science of prema-bhakti (unalloyed, spontaneous loving devotion). He propagated this spiritual path by exemplary action; He was a preacher of impeccable integrity. Externally He engaged in distributing the HolyNames, thus personally tasting the ambrosia of audarya-rasa. Internally He relished the nectar of madhurya and vipralambha-rasa.

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura describes vipralambha-rasa in Jaiva Dharma:

“When madhurya-rasa reaches the heights of delectability it is defined as srngar-rasa and is of two kinds: vipralambha, love-in-separation; and sambhoga, love-in-union (enjoyment through direct contact). The preponderant bhava present in the hearts of the nayak (Krsna) and nayika (Radharani) during estrangement and the longed-for mutual exchange of kissing and embracing is called vipralambha. Vipralambha has the special quality of enhancing sambhoga and is also known as viraha (separation), or viyoga. Just as coloured cloth looks gayer and more vibrant when an extra hue is added, vipralambha causes the revitalization of sambhoga-rasa, taking it to ever-new, sublimely relishable peaks. Without vipralambha-bhava, sambhoga-rasa cannot be fully nurtured.”

### Verse 109

*vibhradvarnam kimapi dahanottirnasauvarnasaram*  
*divyakaram kimapi kalayan drptagopalabalah*  
*aviskurvan kvacidavasare tattadascaryalilam*  
*saksadradhamadhuripuvapurbhati gaurangacandrah*

**It is as if His celestial form has been lifted out of a vessel of molten gold. This wonderful personality sometimes reveals His divine pastimes as BalGopal (baby Krsna), then at other times He discovers, apparently for the first time, Sri Krsna’s extraordinary pastimes as a youthful cowherd boy, in His kaisora-lila. Sri GauraSundar is directly the combined form of SriSri RadhaMadhava, forever resplendent.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

In the concluding verse of this section, Sri GauraHari, the combined form of SriSri RadhaMadhav is glorified in His capacity of relishing His own pastimes (as Krsna). When His mind is absorbed in Krsna’s childhood pastimes as BalGopal, His body sometimes follows suit and He Himself appears to be an audacious young cowherd boy. Then, when immersed in Krsna’s adolescent lila, He manifests in His body ( vapur) the combined forms of SriSri RadhaMadhav.

Karika:

*vrsabhanu-suta vapurekatanuh kanakojjvala-bhrdjita puspa-dhanuh*  
*krta gopa-kumara vilasabharah paribhati vidhujjala gaura-varah*

**‘In one body are manifest the forms of VrsabhanuSuta (the daughter of VrsaBhanuRaja, Srimati Radhika), glowing with a golden complexion like a rainbow decorated with flowers, and GopaKumar, a dashing young cowherd boy, intent in His lila of love. Such does the radiant Moon of Gaura shine.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Lord’s pastimes are pregnant with extremely profound spiritual significance. When people try to analyse and understand them through mundane logic and reasoning they become bewildered and end up drawing wrong conclusions which are often either very offensive or pitifully foolish.

**‘Who can understand the grave and profound pastimes of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu?’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**14.70**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/14.70)**)**

‘Sri Gauranga, like BalGopal Krsna, performed His playful pastimes in various ways. Soon the time for His formal education approached. Fixing an auspicious day and moment, His father, Sri JagannathMisra formally placed the writing chalk in the hand of his son. After a few days, the cuda-karan ceremony (when young brahmana boys shave their heads, leaving only a topknot \[sikha\]) was performed amidst all of Nimai’s friends. Then after a few days, family and friends observed the karna-bheda ceremony (when the ear lobes are pierced, marking the beginning of hearing the Vedas). Everyone was amazed that Nimai could write all the letters of the alphabet, immediately upon seeing them. Thus did Sri GauraSundar perform His extraordinary pastimes. He would demand things impossible to obtain. If He could not catch a bird he saw flying in the sky, He would weep bitterly and roll in the dust. Sometimes He cried for the moon and stars in the heaven and would thrash His arms and legs violently, crying loudly upon being told He could not have them. The only remedy for stopping His crying was kirtan of the names of Sri Hari. The Supreme Personality, who is described in the Vedas and Puranas, thus played like a child in the courtyard of SaciMata.’  
(SriCaitanyaBhagavat AdiLila ([Chapter 6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/6.1)))

## PART X - DivineMajesty of this Incarnation

### Verse 110

*akasmadevavirbhavati bhagavannamalahari*  
*paritanam papairapi purubhiresam tanubhrtam*  
*aho vajraprayam hrdapi navanitayitamabhun*  
*nrnam loke yasminnavatarati sa gauro mama gatih*

**With the advent of Sri Gaura in the world of man, the Names of the SupremeLord also suddenly appeared with Him, wave after wave. Thus could the embodied, suffering, sinful souls here receive the supreme benediction. Aho! (Rejoice!) By the influence of these HolyNames, their hearts, hard as diamond, are melted by affection, becoming as soft as butter. May the Supreme Lord Sri GauraSundar be my singular and final destination.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Beginning with this verse, for the next twenty-one verses, the glories of the Golden Incarnation are affirmed.

‘I accept the shelter of He who has descended to this world (yasmin avatarati) and by whose advent the names of God (BhagavanNama lahari) have also descended, in waves, one after another. By this process the most sinful sufferers are greatly benefited. Aho! (denotes amazement). Even those whose hearts are as hard as diamond (or as thunderbolts- vajraprayam) found that their hearts became like butter (navanitayitamabhun), melted with affection after being embraced by the Name and/or the owner of the Name (nami). May Sri Gaura be my ultimate goal (mama-gatih).’

Karika:

*jasmin gaure’vatirne dragghare krsneti varnakah*  
*avih syus citta kaumalyam syat sri gaurah same gatih*

**‘With the advent of Sri GauraSundar in this world, the syllables of Bhagavan Sri Krsna’s HolyNames also suddenly appeared in each and every home, and by their appearance, softened the hearts of the inhabitants. May He be my ultimate destination.’**

**Purport**

KaliYuga has rightly been described in the scriptures as the age of strife and hypocrisy, worst of the four yugas. Of the four pillars of religiosity - satyam, saucam, daya and tapah (truthfulness, cleanliness, mercy and austerity) only satyam is still present, albeit in waning degree, during KaliYuga. The other three are almost non-existent. Keeping this in mind, the conditioned jivas of KaliYuga are at a great disadvantage; that is, they were at a disadvantage prior to the advent of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu. He has reversed the situation by bringing with Him - golokera prema-dhana - the priceless treasure of Goloka Vrindaban-harinam-sankirtan (congregational chanting of the HolyNames). Sri Sukadeva Gosvami, desiring to stress the inconceivable potency of the HolyNames, first graphically describes the horrendous qualities of KaliYuga in SrimadBhagavatam. Then he offers the panacea in the two following verses:

*kaler dosa-nidhe rajann asti hy eko mahan gunah*  
*kirtanad eva krsnasya mukta-sangah param vrajet*  
*krte yad dhyayato visnum tretayam yajato makhaih*  
*dvapare paricaryayam kalau tad dhari-kirtanat*

**‘My dear King, although KaliYuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age; simply by chanting the HareKrsna MahaMantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the highest spiritual kingdom. Whatever result was obtained in SatyaYuga by meditating on Visnu, in TretaYuga by performing sacrifices, and in DvaparYuga by serving the Lord’s lotus feet, can be obtained in KaliYuga simply by chanting the HareKrsna MahaMantra.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**12.3.51-52**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.51)**))**

Sriman Mahaprabhu personally enters the hearts of those who chant and hear the HolyNames to dissolve the hard shell that covers the true nature of the soul.

*sankirtyamano bhagavan anantah*  
*srutanubhavo vyasanam hi pumsam*  
*pravisya cittam vidhunoty asesam*  
*yatha tamo ’rko ’bhram ivati-vatah*

**‘When people properly glorify the Supreme Personality of Godhead or simply hear about His inconceivable potencies, the Lord personally enters their hearts and wipes away every trace of misfortune, just as the sun removes darkness or as the powerful wind disperses the clouds.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**12.12.48**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/12.48)**))**

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

“Lord Caitanya uses the expression sarvatma-snapanam-providing a cooling affect to everyone.”  
(Sri Siksastaka)

The bliss of KrsnaConsciousness is completely pure, wholly free from any desire for self-satisfaction. That is to say, in the natural course of devotional service, one attains the form of a maidservant of Srimati Radharani, who embodies MahaBhava (unsurpassable heights of exultation in prema). The maidservants assist Her in the Supreme Lord’s conjugal pastimes and thus experience unlimited ecstatic bliss. This sublime mood is untainted by even the slightest tinge of selfish lust or self-indulgent craving.

*tad asma-saram hrdayarh batedam*  
*yad grhyamanair hari-nama-dheyaih*  
*na vikriyetatha yada vikaro*  
*netre jalam gatra-ruhesu harsah*

**‘Certainly that heart is steel-framed which, in spite of one’s chanting the HolyNames of the Lord with concentration, does not change when ecstasy takes place, tears fill the eyes and the hairs stand on end.’**  
**SrimadBhagavatam (**[**2.3.24**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.24)**)**

Na adharmajam dhrdayam.

“Our heart is filled up with all dirty things, adharma. It is very difficult to purify the heart, but it is possible, tad api. Even the hard-hearted, stone-hearted, rajo-guna, tamo-guna, can be melted, can be reformed. How? Isanghri-sevaya. Isa. Isa means the Supreme Lord, Krsna. Anghri means His lotus feet. Sevaya-service. This is possible.”  
(Srila Prabhupad)

**‘Although one may neutralize the reactions of sinful life through austerity, charity, vows and other such methods, these pious activities cannot uproot the material desires in one’s heart. However, if one serves the lotus feet of the Personality of Godhead, he is immediately freed from all such contaminations’.**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.2.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/2.17)**))**

### Verse 111

*na yogo na dhyanam na ca japa-tapastyaganiyama*  
*na veda nacarah kva nu bata nisiddhadyuparatih*  
*akasmaccaitanye’vatarati dayasarahrdaye*  
*pumarthanam maulim paramiha muda lunthati janah*

**Those who have not the slightest inclination for practicing yoga, meditation, japa, austerities, renunciation, sense-control, study of the Vedas, or pure living; indeed, who are not even in favor of abstaining from sinful activities -by the sudden and unexpected appearance in this material world of the most munificent Sri CaitanyaDeva, whose heart contains the cream of compassion and kindness- (such personss) now plunder with great delight, the priceless gem of KrsnaPrema, the fifth and topmost aim of mankind.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The exceptional spirit of Sri GauraHari’s incarnation is expressed, showing how He makes even those who have no spiritual interest and are always attached to illicit activities, nevertheless receive that most exalted and rarely attained sacred treasure - prema.

By the advent of dayasara-hrdaye-caitanya- the infinitely kind Sri Caitanya, those who do not practice any kind of discipline (like yoga), nor are they willing to abandon their sinful activities, Bata! (an expression signifying disappointment and sorrow), even such persons pumarthanam maulim- now forcibly plunder, rolling on the ground in great jubilation, that most precious, sacred treasure - prema. The expression of Bata! in this context can also be taken as an expression of wonderment, - ‘even such persons as this attain the rarely obtainable -VrajaPrema! What can be more glorious than this?’

Karika:

*nasti yogadikam yasya nisiddhacaranam sada*  
*lunthati prema-ratnam sa gaura’vatarati prabhau*

**‘Persons who do not practice any discipline (such as yoga), nor restrain themselves from forbidden activities, nevertheless, now continuously plunder the jewels of prema. Such an incarnation as Sri Gaura is my Prabhu.’**

**Purport**

People born in KaliYuga are especially wretched and impious, as Sukadeva Gosvami describes:

*tatas canu-dinam dharmah satyam saucam ksama daya*  
*kalena balina rajan nanksyaty ayur balam smrtih*

**‘Then, О King, religion, truthfulness, cleanliness, tolerance, mercy, duration of life, physical strength and memory will diminish day by day because of the powerful influence of the age of Kali.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**12.2.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/2.1)**))**

*prayenalpayusah sabhya kalav asmin yuge janah*  
*mandah sumanda-matayo manda-bhagya hy upadrutah*

**‘O learned one, in this iron age of Kali men have but short lives, they are quarrelsome, lazy, misguided, unlucky and, above all, always disturbed.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.1.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.10)**)**

Thus for people to be discriminative and inclined towards freeing themselves from the ocean of misery in KaliYuga is to expect the near-impossible. Hence the incarnation for this age must necessarily be an inexhaustible reservoir of compassion if He is to save the fallen souls of KaliYuga. So kind was SrimanMahaprabhu that He refused to present Himself as Himself- as the Supreme Enjoyer. He renounced every comfort, even His wife, the Goddess of Fortune, to teach suffering humanity how to relish the highest bliss.

*dhrta-kati-dora-kamandalu-dandam*  
*divya kalevara-mundita-mundam*  
*durjana-kalmasa-khandana-dandam*  
*tam pranamami ca sri saci-tanayam*

**‘I offer obeisance to Sri GauraHari, son of Mother SacI, who wears a rope around His waist to hold the kaupin (loincloth of a renunciate), whose shaven pate is exquisite, who holds the kamandalu (water pot) in one hand and who has taken up the renunciates staff (danda) in the other, to terminate the iniquities of the reprobates. What He has to offer as succour to the atmaha (the killers of their own souls) must be unconditional, so He has offered the sublime process of chanting His HolyNames.’**  
**(SarvaBhauma Bhattacarya/ Sri Saci Tanayastakam)**

### Verse 112

*mahakarmasroto-nipatitamapi sthairyamayate*  
*maha pasanebhyo’pyatikathinameti dravadasam*  
*natatyurdhvam nihsadhanapi mahayogamanasam*  
*bhuvi sricaitanya’vatarati manascitravibhave*

**With the advent in this world of Sri CaitanyaDeva, endowed with astounding perceptive power and mystic potency, the materialists, deeply mired for so long in an endless network of fruitive activities, have now become steadfast and grave in executing devotional service. Hearts and minds harder than stone have melted, simply by coming in contact with bhakti-rasa. Great yogis, engaged in severe yogic practices, have forsaken their persistent determination (sadhan) and are now dancing with upraised hands, relishing the sweetness of prema in the transcendental realm of spiritual variegatedness.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri CaitanyaDeva encouraged everyone to give up attachment for their individual sadhana and enthused them to accept the devotional path leading to KrsnaPrema.

When the Possessor of awesome potencies appeared here, the minds of even those who were caught up in the currents of a forceful flow of fruitive activities (mahakarmasrotah) became profoundly peaceful and calm after attaining prema. Those who forsook eagerness for engagement in fruitive activities and instead became incarcerated within the stony dungeons of empirical knowledge, bereft of bhakti, had even their rigid and callous hearts melted upon receiving prema, by the mercy of Sri Gauranga.

Persons whose minds were attracted to nirvikalpa samadhi (state of unswerving meditation, concentrating on oneness with the object of meditation; no distinction between subject and object), experienced that their minds developed apathy towards yoga (nihsadhanapi maha-yoga-manasam); they thus became blissful upon relishing the elixir of prema, dancing with great enthusiasm.

Karika:

*tyakta karmagrahah karmasilo hrddravatam gatah*  
*natatyurddhvam yogimano gaure prakatatam gate*

**‘The hearts of both those who had relinquished fruitive endeavours and those who were addicted to fruitive action have melted by the appearance of Sri Gauranga. Even the minds of the yogis are exhilarated as they dance with gay abandon.’**

**Purport**

Embodied souls reincarnate again and again in this material world of duality as a result of their karma. Their misery is further compounded when even the scriptures and various immature preceptors encourage them to engage in pious, fruitive works. A few others, endowed with a slight increase of intelligence, are frustrated with this temporal illusion and want liberation from the worlds of birth and death. Whether they desire bhukti (material enjoyment), mukti (liberation) or siddhi (mystic perfection), the embodied souls never attain peace.

*bhukti-mukti-sprha yavat pisaci hrdi vartate*  
*tavad bhakti-sukhasyatra katham abhyudayo bhavet*

**‘The mundane desire to enjoy the phenomenal world of senses and the wish to become liberated from material bondage are considered to be two witches who haunt one like ghosts. As long as these witches remain lodged in the heart, how can one feel transcendental bliss? As long as these two witches reside in the heart, there is no possibility of enjoying the transcendental bliss of devotional service.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.2.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.22)**))**

*krsna-bhakta------niskama, ataeva ‘santa’*  
*bhukti-mukti-siddhi-kami-----sakali ‘asanta’*

**‘Because a devotee of Lord Krsna is desireless, he is peaceful. Fruitive workers desire material enjoyment, jnanis desire liberation, and yogis desire material opulence; therefore they are all lusty and cannot be peaceful.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta Madhya Lila (**[**19.149**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.149)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“The devotee of Lord Krsna has no desire other than serving Krsna. Even so-called liberated people are full of desires. Fruitive actors desire better living accommodations, and jnanis want to be one with the Supreme. Yogis desire material opulence, yogic perfections and magic. All of these non-devotees are lusty (kami). Because they desire something, they cannot have peace.”

### Verse 113

*striputradikatham jahurvisayinah sastrapravadam budha*  
*yogindra vijahurmmarunniyamajaklesam tapastapasah*  
*jnanabhyasavidhim jahusca yatayascaitanyacandre param*  
*aviskurvati bhaktiyogapadavim naivanya asidrasah*

**When Sri CaitanyaCandra revealed the most exalted plane of pure bhakti, persons engrossed in sense pleasures gave up discussing mundane topics and attachment to wife, family and friends; scholars refrained from futile debates and arguments on the scriptures; powerful yogis relinquished the tedious process of controlling their breathing (pranayam), a process produced from the desert of spiritual practices; tapasvis abandoned severe tapasya (austerities); what to speak of the impersonalist sannyasis who renounced their search for undifferentiated Brahman realisation (jnana-abhyasa). At that time the world was immersed only in bhakti-rasa; the presence of no other rasa was felt.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

With the advent of Sri Caitanya in this world, gross materialists, philosophers, great yogis, renunciants and sannyasis renounced their individual persuasions and pursued bhakti-yoga with single-minded determination. When Sri Caitanya revealed to the world the climax (param) of bhakti-yoga, \[nigudha-prema-position of pursuing the devotional sentiments of the residents of Vraja (Vrajabasis) - raganuga bhakti\], the visayinah (gross materialists) engaged in fruitive activities and attached to wife, family, friends, and so on, detached themselves from these mundane pursuits; budhah- philosophers, logicians, and scholastic academics engaged in rhetoric and scriptural analysis gave up their search; yogindrah- the yogis abandoned the troublesome and painful hardships involved in their intense endeavour to control their life airs; the tapasvis (ascetics) relinquished their severe penances, the path of mortification of the flesh; and the renunciants (yati, sannyasis) and monists (jnanis) forsook their quest for realising the impersonal, undifferentiated Brahman. Thus did all renounce their individual pursuits in favour of merging their interests in raganuga-bhakti-rasa (vaivanya asid rasah). With the appearance of Sri Caitanya, other than bhakti-rasa, no other rasa (taste) could maintain its palatability.

Nigudha- most confidential, grave, deep, hidden

Karika:

*visayi-budha-yogindra yatayas tapasa api*  
*jahuh svam sadhanam bhaktya caitanye prakatam gate*

**‘When Sri Caitanya descended to this world, the gross materialists, scholars, yogis, sannyasis, and hermits all forgot about their individual persuasions.’**

**Purport**

Though the true nature of the sentient beings is spiritual, this nature has become covered by the powerful, illusory external energy of the Supreme Lord. This covering has occurred as a result of the jiva ’s acquiescence, through the exercise of his inherent, infinitesimal free will. Born from the Lord’s marginal energy, the jiva may choose to participate in the activities of the external, or the internal energy. Without the shelter of the Lord’s internal energy, there is no other recourse but to come under the insurmountable influence of Maya.

**“All living entities are born into delusion, bewildered by dualities arisen from desire and hate.”**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**7.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.27)**))**

This insufferable situation is forced on him because the jiva has forgotten his eternal relationship with Sri Krsna:

*krsna bhuli ’ sei jiva anadi-bahirmukha*  
*ataeva maya tare deya samsara-duhkha*

**‘Forgetting Krsna, the jiva has been attracted by the external feature from time immemorial.Therefore, Maya (the illusory energy) gives him all kinds of misery in his material existence.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**20.117**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/20.117)**))**

The spirit soul’s natural position as Sri Krsna’s marginal energy is to engage in bhakti-yoga. BhaktiYoga is the jiva’s eternal constitutional position:

*jivera ‘svarupa ’ haya-----krsnera ‘nitya-dasa’*  
*krsnera ‘tatastha-sakti ’ ‘bhedabheda-prakasa ’*

**‘It is the living entity’s constitutional position to be an eternal servant of Krsna because he is the marginal energy of Krsna, a manifestation simultaneously one with and different from the Lord, like a molecular particle of sunshine or fire.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**20.108**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/20.108)**))**

The eternal religion of the jiva is to be an eternal servant of Krsna because he is the marginal energy of Krsna and thus a manifestation simultaneously one with and different from the Lord. Hence, it was natural that with the advent of Sri CaitanyaDeva, jivas forsook their so-called pursuits and responded to Sriman Mahaprabhu’s call to practice bhakti-yoga.

The transcendental exchanges in bhakti-yoga between the Supreme Lord and the devotees, as well as those between the devotees themselves, are so relishable that all other mundane relationships seem insipid and hollow. These exchanges are based on love and trust.

Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur comments:

Babaji Maharaja said, “Dear sir, even though the jiva is infinitesimal, his dharma is certainly absolute, complete and pure, as it is ever-existent and eternal. Tiny stature is the innate characteristic of the jiva , but only has reference to his size and not his function. The brhad-vastu (infinite entity) is the Supreme Brahman, Sri Krsna, of whom the countless jivas are minute parts. Just as tiny sparks burst from a big fire,the jivas emanate from the indivisible, Absolute Lord, Sri Krsna, the Supreme conscious being. In addition, just as each spark possesses the fiery attributes of the big fire, so every jiva can manifest the absolute excellences of the supreme Brahman. A single spark in contact with a flammable object can ignite a raging conflagration capable of consuming the entire world. Similarly, a jiva who attains the ultimate objective-KrsnaPrema-can inundate the entire universe with KrsnaPrema! However, as long as the infinitesimal jiva is out of touch with the true objective of his spiritual nature, Sri Krsna (and thereby his true dharma), he appears debilitated.”  
(JaivaDharma (Chapter 2))

### Verse 114

*abhud gehe gehe tumulaharisankirtanaravo*  
*vabhau dehe dehe vipulapulakasru-vyatikarah*  
*api snehe snehe paramamadhurotkarsapadavi*  
*daviyasyamnayadapi jagati gaure’vatarati*

**With Sri GauraSundara’s descent to this phenomenal world, unprecedented miracles became common occurrences- the tumultuous chanting of the HolyNames of Sri Hari reverberated from every home, rising in continuous waves, while ecstatic physical transformations like horripilation, tears, shivering, and so on, adorned the bodies of the residents, nourishing their souls. Moreover, with the deepening and intensification of bhakti-rasa, the path to the exalted plane of the most eminent and attractive MadhurPrema, far beyond the vision of the Vedic literature (Amnaya), gradually came within everyone’s purview, expressed through tender, loving affection (sneha).**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The eminent distinction of the incarnation of Sri Gauranga is proclaimed- abhud gehe gehe... portraying Mahaprabhu in His role as the promulgator of the devotional attitudes of anubhava (symptoms of ecstasy) and sattvik bhava (transcendental transformations occurring in the physical body due to ecstatic emotion). He has revealed the summit of DivineLove in the mood of conjugal attraction, only very nebulously discussed in the Vedic literature. With the appearance in this world of Sri GauraHari, the tumultuous (tumul) chanting of Sri Krsna’s Names burst out in each and every home. This in turn caused ecstatic symptoms: weeping, trembling, and horripilation to swell, manifesting their presence in the bodies of the residents of Navadvip.

Sneha- the maturation and assimilation of prema. All manifestations of sneha ascend the ladder of erotic VrajaPrema, pouring nectar down upon the heads of the jivas. Prior to the appearance of Sri Gauranga this VrajaPrema was beyond the cognisance of even the Personified Vedas.

Karika:

*krsna-sankirtanam gehe dehe ca pufakadayah*  
*snehe’pyutkarsata gaure'vatirne sruti-duskara*

**‘With the advent of Sri Gauranga, tumultuous chanting of the HolyNames of Sri Hari resounded in every home, ecstatic symptoms of crying, trembling, horripilation, etc. were brazenly displayed in the bodies of the residents, as the hidden secret of the Sruti (VrajaPrema) rose to prosperity, mounting the ladder of loving affection.’**

**Purport**

On Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s bequest, Sri Nityananda Prabhu has constructed a canal which brings the nectarean flood waters of DivinePrema from the eternal spring of Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet. Holding a straw between His teeth, Sri Nityananda Prabhu goes from door to door, humbly requesting whomever He meets to chant the HolyNames of Sri GauraHari. To anyone who serves Sri GauraHari’s lotus feet, Lord Nityananda promises to sell Himself. Thus bhakti (devotional service) to the Supreme Lord quickly releases the flood gates of prema-rasa.

From the moment Sri KrsnaCaitanya appeared in this world, the universe resounded with the tumultuous (tumula) chanting of the HolyNames. In fact, the new born babe appeared amidst loud chanting of the HolyNames; an auspicious indication of things to come.

*harinam-mangala uthila caturdike*  
*janmila isvara sankirtana kari age*

**‘The auspicious sound of Sri Hari’s HolyNames reverberated in all directions as the Supreme Personality of Godhead arranged for congregational chanting (sankirtan) to greet Him at His birth.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaBhagavata AdiLila(**[**1.96**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/1.96)**))**

Due to a full lunar eclipse on the evening of His birth, all of Navadvip was engaged in chanting the HolyNames of the Lord, along with Vedic mantras, to counteract the ill effects of the eclipse. Thus, the sounds of conchshells, bells, gongs and the chanting of mantras from each and every home, mingled, echoing in the vaults of heaven.

*bhajanera madhye srestha nava-vidha bhakti*  
*‘krsna-prema’, 'krsna' dite dhare maha-sakti*  
*tara madhye sarva-srestha nama-sankirtana*  
*niraparadhe nama laile paya prema-dhana*

**‘Among the ways of executing devotional service, the nine prescribed methods are the best, for these processes have great potency to deliver Krsna and ecstatic love for Him (KrsnaPrema). Of the nine processes of devotional service, the most important is to always chant the HolyNames of the Lord. If one does so, avoiding the ten kinds of offenses, one very easily obtains the most valuable gift - love of Krsna. ’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**4.70-71**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/4.70)**))**

The Vedas prescribe four goals for mankind: dharma, artha, kama and moksa. However, MadhurPrema (the mood of a lover for the beloved) is conspicuous in the Vedas by its absence. The fifth and highest human aspiration is not openly discussed there, hence, it has thus become an esoteric subject matter. With Lord Caitanya’s appearance, that arcane subject of devotional love was finally divulged. He dispensed freely to the world the devotional culture of Prema; what no other personality had ever dared to reveal.

### Verse 115

*akasmadevaitad-bhuvanamabhitah plavitamabhut*  
*mahapremambhodheh kimapi rasavanyabhirakhilam*  
*akasmaccadrstasrutacaravikarairalamabhuc*  
*camatkarah krsne kanakaruciramge’vatarati*

**The Attractor and Enchanter of the hearts of all living entities, Svayam Bhagavan Sri Krsna, has incarnated, after first accepting a splendorous complexion of molten gold. Thus has the entire universe suddenly become inundated, without warning, by a flood of MahaPrema Rasa; tidal waves of ambrosial love of Krsna that have completely filled the fourteen planetary systems. The inhabitants of all the worlds were filled with wonder to witness such ecstatic transformations in the Ocean of Prema, never seen or heard of before.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

This most glorious incarnation of Sri Gauranga is proclaimed, -akasmadevaitad-bhuvanamabhitah-demonstrating how He inundated the universe with the transcendent Ocean of PremaRasa, while Himself exhibiting inspirational manifestations of prema.

Krsne- Sri Krsna, the all-attractive, Supreme Personality of Godhead; the embodiment of ecstatic cognisance; kanakarucirange- that same SupremePerson, having accepted the bodily lustre of Srimati Radharani, has appeared as Sri Gauranga, whose enchanting bodily limbs are more brilliant than molten gold. By His appearance, the entire universe was suddenly inundated by a flood of liquid love (rasa) from the Ocean of Prema, filled to overflowing. The residents of this universe could thus witness such wonderful transformations of prema, the likes of which were never seen nor heard of before.

Karika:

*krsne’vatirne gaurange plavitam bhuvanam rasaih*  
*premambudher vikaraisca paramascaryyam apyabhut*

**‘When the golden incarnation, Sri GauraKrsna descended to this material plane, the universe was flooded with the sweet nectar of prema. Seeing such unprecedented transformations of prema. everyone was totally amazed.’**

**Purport**

**‘By all the Vedas I am to be known, indeed I am the compiler of Vedanta and I am the knower of the Vedas‘**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**15.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.15)**))**

The Supreme Godhead, fountainhead of all incarnations, Sri KrsnaCaitanya, knower of the Vedas, has advented to broadcast the most esoteric conclusion of the Vedas, never before revealed. From His intimate knowledge of the Vedas, He put forward the transcendental philosophy of acintya-bhedabheda tattva. The Supreme Lord and His multifarious energies are inconceivably, simultaneously different and non-different from each other. This transcendental principle of simultaneous oneness and difference can defeat any and all speculations based on logic and rhetoric, as well as any other Vedic theory in contradiction to this axiom. The followers of Sri RupaSanatan are strict adherents of Sri KrsnaCaitanya’s acintya-bhedabheda tattva since their hearts and minds are completely reformed from the dangerous propensity to speculate, reverting to the inductive / deductive process of inquiry. The Vedas are infallible evidences; knowledge available from them is perfect and unequivocal.

**‘By nature and construction, human beings are controlled by four inherent shortcomings: illusion, mistakes, cheating and falsehood. This limits them from experiencing inconceivable and extraordinary transcendental phenomena. The methods of knowledge they have access to and can offer others, such as direct sensual perception and subsequent theorization, are automatically faulty. Thus, direct perception (pratyaksa), inferences (anumana), and the like, cannot be accepted as perfectly authentic evidence. For the scientifically-minded seekers of the truth, the only substantive source of evidence is the Veda (Sruti- ‘what is heard’), since it has been transmitted since time immemorial through a succession of self-realized, perfected spiritual masters, repositories of both material and spiritual knowledge. Their words are supramundane, transcendental to mundane scrutiny, providing shelter to all seekers. Their knowledge possesses an inconceivable, extraordinary nature and influence.’**  
**TattvaSandarbha(**[**9.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/jg-tats-gpd/9.10)**)**

Doubts, speculations, false logic, and so on, are products of ajnana (ignorance) and avidya (nescience). As soon as the jiva attracts the Supreme Lord’s mercy, through associating with and serving devotees, the Lord from within illuminates the jiva’s consciousness and dissipates the darkness of ignorance, as Lord Krsna Himself tells us:

*tesam evanukampartham aham ajnana-jam tamah*  
*nasayamy atma-bhava-stho jnana-dipena bhasvata*

**‘Out of compassion for them, I, dwelling in their hearts, destroy with the shining lamp of knowledge the darkness born of ignorance.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**10.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.11)**))**

The flame of the lamp of Navadvip, Sri KrsnaCaitanya, is not an ordinary flame. It incinerates the moths of speculation, but like soothing moon rays, it also cools the heart and mind, scorched by the fires of doubt and dualism. It dissipates the gloom of impersonalism and enlightens the heart with knowledge of a loving, personal Omnipotent Power, addicted to performing amazing pastimes. As long as the jiva remains in ignorance of his true identity (svarupa- eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord), he remains eternally chained to the cycle of repeated birth and death, compounding his misery, life after life. The scientific knowledge that will help to bring his release from this endless suffering is acintya - inconceivable, beyond the grasp of the intellect.

*acintyah khalu ye bhava na tams tarkena yojayet*  
*prakrtibhyah param yac ca tad acintyasya laksanam*

**‘Anything transcendental to material nature is called inconceivable, whereas arguments are mundane. Since mundane arguments cannot touch transcendental subject matters, one should not try to understand transcendental subject matters through mundane arguments and speculations.’**  
**(MahaBharat BhismaParva (5.22))**

The only method by which to understand this transcendental science is bhakti-yoga, devotional surrender to the Supreme Lord under the guidance of a bonafide guru.

### Verse 116

*udgrhnanti samasta-sastram abhito durvara-garvayita*  
*dhanyam manya-dhiyas ca karma-tapa-ady-uccavacesu sthitah*  
*dvitrany eva japanti kecana harer namani vamasayah*  
*purvvam samprati gauracandra udite premapi sadharanah*

**Before the advent of Lord Gauranga, scholars afflicted with incorrigible arrogance tried to fully assimilate the entire scriptures, thinking, ‘I am now knowledgeable in all the scriptures; there is no one superior to me.’ Others were unabashedly complacent, thinking themselves successful or respectable, through their accomplishments in the fields of fruitive activity, austerity, or through following the basic tenets of Smrti sastra (periodic and occasional rituals). Still others were situated somewhere amongst the ranks of the followers of sankhya, yoga, and so on. Many were content to chant Lord Hari’s Name once or twice, yet even this endeavour was sullied by a perverse mentality; their hearts remained consumed by deceit and duplicity. This was the condition before. At present, however, with the appearance of Sri GauraSundar, the most coveted transcendental treasure of prema has become a common commodity, readily available even to the most ordinary man on the street.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The magnificence of Sri Gauranga’s incarnation is portrayed, depicting His free disbursement of the rarest of sacred treasures - Sri KrsnaPrema - to all and sundry.

Durvvara-garvayitah- so-called scholars who, when dissuaded from pursuing the path of uncontrollable pride, endeavour with even greater determination, collecting more and more books to fill their libraries, thus amassing an even more intense, invincible, unavailing and unassailable mountain of pride, declaring vociferously their intent to study the scriptures, “We have studied all the scriptures thoroughly, so who is equal to or better than us?” thus their churlish arrogance flourished. They were completely convinced that their position in society was the most commendable and respectable (dhanyamanyadhi).

Usage of the word karma in this context indicates daily, ritualistic activities enjoined in Smrti sastra; tapasa- discipline involving severe austerities with the intention of attaining the heavenly planets; adi- implies sankhya, yoga, etc. The people’s resolve to participate in such activities was firm.

Some few among them chanted the HolyNames a couple of times in a day, but, vamasayah- their aims and purposes were dubious, perverted, highly suspect of fraudulence. Due to the contamination of fruitive desires, though they accepted the Name, they could not taste the nectar of prema.

Thus was the die cast in the past, however, now, in the present, with the appearance of Sri Gauranga, everyone, from the most wicked, vile creatures to the cream of the crop, is absorbed in savouring the flavour of prema-rasa.

How wonderful! (Aho!) I say! The glories of Sri Gaura Candra are most astounding! The example of the moon echoes once more: just as the moon dissipates darkness, while its rays increase the healing properties in herbs, similarly, the appearance of the moonlike Sri Gaura Candra has dissipated the darkness of nescience in the shape of karma (fruitive work), jnana (empirical knowledge) and yoga (mystic manipulation). In infusing everyone’s hearts with the nectar of prema. He has thus imparted therein the restorative, therapeutic and medicinal properties of bhava.

Karika:

*sastra garvayitah karma-tapo nisthas ca kecana*  
*purvam samprati gauravirbhave prema samo'bhitah*

**‘Previously, scholars were intoxicated with the pride of scriptural knowledge, others with their fruitive accomplishments or austerities. However, nowadays, with the advent of Sri Gauranga, all have equally obtained the priceless treasure of prema-rasa.’**

**Purport**

The jiva can never really be satisfied with mundane objects due to his inherent spiritual nature. His material desires remain always unfulfilled, craving for newer and newer objects even after having procured what he did not earlier possess.

The nature of the soul is to be blissful. Thus unless the jiva experiences real, spiritual love he cannot be blissful. Rasa means mellow taste, churned through loving exchanges. The natural propensity of the soul is to relish supra-mundane rasa. This can only happen when the jiva situates himself on the platform of bhakti-yoga and begins to selflessly serve the embodiment of rasa: raso vai sah

*visaya vinivartante niraharasya dehinah*  
*rasa-varjam raso ’py asya param drstva nivartate*

**‘The embodied soul may be restricted from sense enjoyment, though the taste for sense objects remains. But, ceasing such engagements by experiencing a higher taste, he is fixed in consciousness.’**  
**(BhagavadCita (**[**2.59**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.59)**))**

Thakur Bhaktivinoda comments:

“The quintessence of life is to love. A large majority suffer under the misconception that fulfilment of selfish desires is the primary purpose of human existence. That is far from the truth. For love, man can sacrifice everything, and the highest expression of this love is to love the Supreme object of love, Sri Krsna.

*krsnam enam avehi tvam atmanam akhilatmanam*  
*jagad-dhitaya so ‘py atra dehivabhati mayaya*

**‘You should know Krsna to be the original soul of all atmas (living entities). For the benefit of the whole universe, He has, out of His causeless mercy, appeared as an ordinary human being. He has done this by the strength of His own internal potency.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**10.14.55**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.55)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“Pariksit Maharaja asked Sukadeva Gosvami why Krsna was so beloved by the residents of Vrindaban, who loved Him even more than their own offspring, or life itself. At that time, Sukadeva Gosvami replied that everyone’s atma, or soul, is very, very dear, especially to all living entities who have accepted material bodies. However, that atma, the spirit soul, is part and parcel of Krsna. For this reason, Krsna is very dear to every living entity. Everyone’s body is very dear to oneself, and one wants to protect the body by all means, because within the body the soul is living. Due to the intimate relationship between the soul and the body, the body is important and dear to everyone. Similarly, the soul, being part and parcel of Krsna, the Supreme Lord, is very, very dear to all living entities. Unfortunately, the soul forgets his constitutional position and thinks he is only the body (dehatma-buddhi). Thus the soul is subjected to the rules and regulations of material nature.”

### Verse 117

*deve caitanyanamanyavatarati suraprarthyapadabjaseve*  
*visvadricih pravistarayati sumadhura premapiyusavicih*  
*ко balah kasca vrddhah ka iha jadamatih ka badhuh ко varakah*  
*sarvesamaikarasyam kimapi haripade bhaktibhajam babhuva*

**Always absorbed in His DivinePlay, that DivinePurusa Sri CaitanyaDev, unto whose lotus feet the demigods pray for service, has caused a wave of the sweetest, most Divine Nectar of Prema to flood the entire universe, by His descent into this material world. By the time this Tidal Wave of Love spreads its influence in all directions far and wide, all will become qualified to receive bhakti - children, the elderly, women, gross materialists, reprobates; everyone will be drenched in the only real emotion - bhakti -singular devotion to the SupremeLord.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The glory of Sri Gauranga’s incarnation is reflected in His act of ushering everyone into the abode of erotic VrajaPrema, through His infinite compassion. By the appearance of the SupremePersonality Sri GauraHari, the entire universe is blessed with KrsnaPrema.

The word deve has a number of meanings: 1) One who, absorbed in the mood of Srimati Radharani, performs Divine play (krida), prompted by love for Himself. 2) Who, by His proclivity to perform pastimes (lila), encourages every jiva to conquer over enslavement to material existence. 3) Who kept the priceless treasure of prema-rasa as a wager, and won over Srimati Radhika, through His Divine sports. 4) Although He is Sri Krsna Himself, in the mood of ecstatic love He prays to and glorifies Sri Krsna. 5) Endowed with the most wondrous beauty, charm, and so on, He manifests Himself in splendorous ways. 6) Intoxicating everyone with prema-rasa, He makes them experience the climax of ananda. 7) Who goes completely crazy by the taste of His own DivineLove, prema. 8) Absorbed in the ecstatic sentiments of Srimati Radhika in the throes of love-inseparation, He continually falls in and out of consciousness. 9) Who, for the purpose of keeping the sanctity of Holy pilgrimages, and of propagating the path of bhakti unto Himself, travels from one holy place to another. 10) Desirous of relishing His own beauty and sweetness, He has accepted the mood and sentiments of Srimati Radhika, the absolute embodiment of the hladini potency.

The verbal root div (deve) means: play, desire to conquer or be victorious, will or desire, gambling (dyuta), prayer, effulgence (dyuti), pleasure, illusory dreams, momentum and lustre.

sura-prarthya-padabja-seve- the demigods in heaven are desirous to serve the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya, by whose appearance an especially sweet and stunning (sumadhurya, sundar) tidal wave of DivineLove (prema) broke from the Ocean of the Nectar of Prema and drowned the entire universe (visvadricih). When this sweet tidal wave of nectarean love had inundated the entire universe, spreading its influence to the farthest reaches, then everyone engaged in the culture of devotion, from the children to the elderly, became connoisseurs of bhakti-rasa.

Karika:

*bala-vrddha-vadhu ksudra jadandhavadhiradayah*  
*babhuvuh premarasikah gaura deve’vatarini*

**‘The young, the old, women, those blinded by their idle concerns, those hard of hearing, even gross materialists and small-minded persons, all became aesthetes in the matter of relishing the sublime nectar of prema-rasa, as a result of Sri CaitanyaDeva’s appearance.’**

**Purport**

Living entities are of two kinds: eternally liberated (nitya-mukta), and eternally conditioned (nitya-baddha). By the process of bhakti-yoga even a nitya-baddha jiva can easily attain liberation, at which time he joins the ranks of the nitya-mukta. Among the nitya-mukta, there are two categories of eternally liberated jivas, those eternal associates {parisads) who were never conditioned, and those who have attained liberation from material existence by the Lord’s mercy. The jivas descent into the material would and his engrossment in matter make him forgetful of his eternal relationship with his Creator, Sri Krsna. In this plight, the baddha-jiva, attempting to lord it over matter, thinks Krsna his main rival. Thus, bhakti-yoga remains farthest from the baddha jiva ’s thought. He needs to gain eligibility to practice bhakti-yoga by purifying his consciousness of false identifications.

Sri Caitanya, however, did not consider these points. He made every living entity eligible to participate in His Sankirtan movement. His magnanimous heart cried in anguish, seeing the jivas reject the wonderful, transcendental bliss of chanting the HolyNames, in favour of the evanescent pleasures of this world. So He waived the practice of austerity, Vedic studies and thelike, as conditions for eligibility, and instead elevated the entire universe by His inconceivable potency, to make them qualified to relish the rare fruit of prema.

### Verse 118

*sarve sankaranaradadaya ihayatah svayam srirapi*  
*prapta deva-halayudho’pi milito jatasca te vrsnayah*  
*bhuyah kim vrajavasino’pi prakata gopala-gopyadayah*  
*purne premarasesvare’vatarati srigauracandre bhuvi*

**With the advent on this earth of the Supreme Personality Sri GauraCandra, the crest-jewel of all connoisseurs of the mellows of loving devotion (prema-rasa), Sri Sankar, Sri Narada and others also arrived. Sri LaksmiDevi was present. The Lord’s undifferentiated Self, Sri Baladeva, full with all potencies, appeared as Sri NityanandaRay. The Vrsnis also advented. What more can I say? Indeed, Nanda Maharaj himself arrived, accompanied by the other Vrijbasis - Subala and the other friends (sakhas), the gopis, Krsna’s saktis, such as YogaMaya (Paurnamasi); all were present to participate in this most amazing GauraLila.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Such is the Divine magnitude of Sri Gauranga’s advent that he arranged for his eternal associates to accompany him, seeing such a desperate need for the propagation of bhakti-rasa - sarve sankaranaradadayah.... The appearance of Sri GauraCandra in this world ensured that Sankar and His other eternal associates also descend.

Sri Gaura is described here as purna- SvayamBhagavan (the SupremePersonality of Godhead), the crest-jewel among connoisseurs of the mellows of devotional love (prema-rasa).

Sankar refers to SadaSiva, whose incarnation, Sri AdvaitAcarya, appeared in Laur (in present-day BanglaDesh). The word sankara means one who causes auspiciousness to dawn in the hearts of everyone. Seeing the people devoid of devotion to Sri Hari, Advaita was distraught. Out of compassion for these suffering souls, he began to worship Sri Krsna, praying for their deliverance. Thus did he arrange for the dispensation of the greatest benediction, the furthermost reaches of auspiciousness - the appearance of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu.

*drstni bhucakra lokan kalimala malinan sri barer bhakti hinan*  
*krsnam samsevya nityam parimala tulast manjari-puspa-samghaih*  
*yah sri caitanya-krsnam bhuvana gurum avatarayat premadam*  
*srila advaitacarya varyarn krpayatu sa mamisvaro visvam-bandhur iti*

**‘May that Isvara, the bestower of prema, the friend of the universe, the foremost of preceptors, Srila AdvaitAcarya shower his mercy upon me. Seeing that the people of this world were contaminated by the ill effects of KaliYuga, rendering them devoid of devotion to Sri Hari, Advaita Prabhu began his worship of Sri Krsna, offering him fragrant Tulasi manjaris and flowers. Thus did he cause the universal preceptor, the guru of all the worlds, Sri KrsnaCaitanya to appear.’**  
**(Srimad AdvaitAstaka)**

Narada and the other eternal associates of the Lord incarnated as SrivasPandit and the other companions of Mahaprabhu. Svayam srirapi- MahaLaksmiDevi appeared as LaksmiPriya, VisnuPriya and GadadharPandit. Srimati Radhika, who in Vrindaban expands herself into innumerable gopis, manifest her plenary portion in the person of Sri Caitanya and in Gadadhar, as well as DasaGadadhar. Just as SvayamBhagavan Sri Krsna expands himself into an infinite variety of forms, so also does his pleasure-potency (hladini sakti) Srimati Radhika expand herself into an infinite variety of forms.
