Deva Halayudh- Sri Baladeva joined the august assembly. He is the same Supreme Personality of Godhead, appearing in GaurangaLlla as Sripad Nityananda (hala- plough; ayudha-weapon). Referring to Nityananda Prabhu as Halayudh signifies that he vanquished many atheists and demoniac forces in the course of propagating devotional service to Sri Gauranga. The Yadavas (vrsnayah), Krsna’s own family members, appeared in various guises. SaciDevI and JagannathMisra were incarnations of NandaYasoda, DevakiVasudev and KasyapaAditi. All the Vrajabasis, the eternal residents of Vraja, the cowherd boys, Krsna’s friends and servitors, the cowherd damsels, YogaMaya and various forest goddesses all made their appearance.

*anekatra prakatata rupasyaikasya yaikada*  
*sarvvatha tat svarupo ’yam sa prakasi itiryyate*

**‘The simultaneous presence in many different places of (the expansions of) one person, all having the same features, qualities, pastimes and so on, is known as prakasa.’**  
**(Sri LaghuBhagavatamrta (**[**18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/lb/i-sri-krsnamrta.1-svayam-rupa-tad-ekatma-and-avesa.text-18)**))**

Prakasa expansions can never be considered different from the original person, since none of the expansions is in any degree less than the (svarupa) original form (this is the meaning of ‘plenary’ portion; plenary- unlimited, or full). Therefore, all the associates of Sri Caitanya are eternally perfected personalities. The only difference is that sometimes they are manifest and sometimes not. They are all eternal since the SupremeLord’s incarnations, associates, pastimes and so on, are all eternal.

Karika:

*avatirne gauracandre’vateruh sarva parsadah*  
*halisa naradadya ye gopi-gopas ca vrsnayah*

**‘When Sri GauraCandra incarnated, all His eternal associates, Sri Baladeva, Siva, Narada, the gopas, gopis and the Vrsnis also descended along with Him.’**

**Purport**

Sri GauraHari’s mother, Sri SaciDevi was the daughter of Sri Nilambar Cakravarti and wife of Sri Jagannath Misra. According to Sri GauraGanoddesaDipika (38) Sri SaciDevi was the combined incarnation of mother Yasoda, Aditi, Kausalya, Prsni and Devaki. Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj Gosvami addresses her as JaganMata, the universal mother. She was popularly known as Ai, an abbreviation of arjya. In Sanskrit, arjya means: a noble lady of high-caste and repute, while in Bengal arjya also means ‘mother’. Simply by uttering this simple sound vibration-Ai - anyone can purify one’s consciousness and develop deep devotion to the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality Sri KrsnaCaitanya. Her vatsalya-seva-bhava (devotional service to her son in the transcendental humour of paternity) is unparalleled. Sri NimaiPandit could leave home to enter the renounced order of sannyasa only after He was able to convince SaciDevi and receive her blessings.

*nа tasya karyam karanam ca vidyate*  
*na tat-samas cabhyadhikas ca drsyate*  
*parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate s*  
*vabhaviki jnana-bala-kriya ca*

**‘The Supreme Lord has nothing to do, and no one is found to be equal to or greater than Him, for everything is done naturally and systematically by His multifarious energies. The Supreme Lord is the controller of all other controllers, and He is the greatest of all the diverse planetary leaders. Everyone is under His control. All entities are delegated with particular power only by the Supreme Lord; they are not supreme themselves. He is also worshipable by all demigods and is the supreme director of all directors. Therefore, He is transcendental to all kinds of material leaders and controllers and is worshipable by all. The Lord has no duty to perform to oblige anyone.**

**Nonetheless, He appears to act to protect His devotees or kill His enemies. He has no material work to perform, nor any material senses with which to perform it. The Supreme Personality of Godhead does not possess a material body which has material senses; no one is equal to nor greater than Him. Tasya means that He is a person. So what kind of person? Like me? Whole day working, for money? No. Na tasya karyam karanam ca vid... He has nothing to do. See here. Krsna has nothing to do. Simply He is enjoying, playing on his flute and enjoying with Radharani. That’s all. He hasn’t got to go to the office, to the factory. He is simply to enjoy. His inconceivable potencies are multifarious, unlimited and inseparable from Him, meaning that they are His natural energies. He doesn’t require to tax His brain how to do things. There is no difference between His body and His soul. He is absolute. He is able to remain in His own abode and without endeavor, supervise and manipulate the entire cosmic manifestation through the interaction of the three modes of material nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance. These interactions create different forms, bodies, activities, and changes, which all occur perfectly. Because the Lord is perfect, everything works as if He were directly supervising and taking part in it. All His senses are transcendental. Any one of His senses can perform the action of any other sense. They provide Him with transcendental knowledge, power and dynamism (pastimes), described in the Vedas as samvit, sandhini and hladini potencies respectively. He has such potencies that anything He wants done will be done perfectly well, through the control of material nature. His deeds are automatically performed as a natural sequence.’**  
**(Svetasvatara Upanisad (**[**6.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/6.8)**))**

Sri Krsna’s hladini sakti (Srimati Radhika) provides Him with transcendental pleasure. She embodies the Supreme Lord’s para-sakti. Sri Krsna is the Supreme enjoyer (Purusa). Though his ability to enjoy is unlimited, only Srimati Radhika can fully satisfy Him.

**‘Once, Lord Krsna considered within His heart: “Everyone says that I am complete bliss, full of all rasas. All the world derives pleasure from Me. Is there anyone who can give Me pleasure? One who has a hundred times more qualities than Me could give pleasure to My mind. Someone more qualified than Me is impossible to find in the world. But in Radha alone I feel the presence of one who can give Me pleasure. Although My beauty defeats the beauty of ten million Cupids, although it is unequalled and unsurpassed and although it gives pleasure to the three worlds, seeing Radharani gives pleasure to My eyes. The vibration of My transcendental flute attracts the three worlds, but my ears are enchanted by the sweet words of Srimati Radharani. Although my body lends fragrance to the entire creation, the scent of Radharani’s limbs captivates My mind and heart. Although the entire creation is full of different tastes because of Me, I am charmed by the nectarean taste of the lips of Srimati Radharani. And although My touch is cooler than ten million moons, I am refreshed by the touch of Srimati Radhika. Thus although I am the source of happiness for the entire world, the beauty and attributes of Sri Radhika are my life and soul.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.238-248**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.238)**))**

**The real reasons for the appearance of VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna in KaliYuga, as Lord Gauranga, are three: ‘Desiring to understand the glory of Srimati Radharani’s love, the wonderful qualities in Him that She alone relishes through Her Love, and the happiness She feels when she realizes the sweetness of His love, the Supreme Lord Hari, richly endowed with Her emotions, appears from the womb of Srimati SaciDevi as the moon appears from the ocean.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**1.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.6)**))**

Killing of demons and establishing the principles of religion are secondary works which are easily accomplished by Lord Visnu, a plenary expansion of Sri Krsna.

*prema-rasa-niryasa karite asvadana*  
*raga-marga bhakti loke karite pracarana*  
*rasika-sekhara krsna parama-karuna*  
*ei dui hetu haite icchara udgama*

**‘The Lord’s desire to appear (as an incarnation) was born from two reasons: He wanted to taste the sweet essence of the spiritual humours of love of God and He wanted to propagate devotional service in the world on the platform of spontaneous attraction. Thus He is known as supremely jubilant and as the most merciful of all.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.15-16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.15)**))**

**‘Madhura bhakti-rasa- (spiritual humour in conjugal love) is of two kinds: vipralambha (separation) and sambhoga (bliss of union). Vipralambha is further subdivided into purva-raga, mana, pravasa, etc.’**  
**(**[**BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1)**)**

### Verse 119

*bhrtyah snigdha atisumadhura-projjvalodarabhajas*  
*tatpadabjadvitayasavidhe sarvva evavatirnah*  
*prapuh purvadhikatara-mahapremaplyusalaksmim*  
*svapremanam vitarati jagatyadbhutam hemagaure*

**When Sri GauraSundar, His bodily lustre more resplendent than molten gold, appeared on the earth to freely dispense His very own KrsnaPrema, His eternal servitors (dasagan), friends (sakhas & sakhis) and lovers (preyasigan), possessed of the sweet sentiments of guileless (erotic) love, devoid of any trace of awe and reverence, all incarnated to be in intimate contact with Sri GauraSundara’s lotus feet. The wealth of prema-rasa these eternal parisads enjoyed in GauraLila (mahabhava rupa) was far in excess to what they had previously experienced.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The superexcellence of Sri Gauranga’s incarnation is demonstrated by the fact that all His eternal associates (parisad; bhrtyah snigdhah projjvalodarabhajas) who accompanied Him, experienced even greater elation in GauraLila than in their previous pastimes (lila).

The SupremeLord is addressed as hemagaure- His lustre is of molten gold. The unique, unprecedented feature of his distribution of prema is the total absence of any prejudice regarding the receivers’ eligibility or worthiness.

bhrtyah- servants; snigdha- friends (sakha); atisumadhura-concentrated sweetness of the sweetest; projjvalodarabhajas-possessed of open and honest love (ujjvala prema), conjugal love endowed with erotic sentiments, bereft of even a tinge of opulence, awe or reverence. Those gopis (preyasigan) who cultured such adoration, immersed in a myriad of moods and sentiments, advented in close proximity to the lotus feet of Sri Caitanya and thus acquired a wealth of the ambrosia of LovingDevotion(prema), in excess to what they possessed in KrsnaLila. The lila (DivinePlay) of Bhagavan is full of the flavours of loving affection; the lila of Sri Krsna is even more full of this nectar, but the lila of Sri Gaura is the most full of this rasa {prema-rasa). Thus there is no doubt that his lotus feet are the ultimate shelter, the sole object of shelter.

Karika:

*avatirne hemagaure premarnam datari prabhau*  
*avatirna vrajasthah svah prapuh purvvadhiham sukham*

**‘Golden Sri Gauranga descended within this world to churn the Ocean of Prema and distribute the nectar produced therefrom, to whomever would accept it. His eternal associates from Vraja, who accompanied Him, experienced heavenly happiness in excess of any they had previously tasted.’**

**Purport**

*krsnera sahaya, guru, bandhava, preyasi*  
*gopika hayena priya sisya, sakhi dasi*

**‘The gopis are the helpers, teachers, friends, wives, dear disciples, confidantes and serving maids of Lord Krsna.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.210**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.210)**))**

*sahaya guravah sisya bhujisya bandhavah striyah*  
*satyam vadami te Partha gopyah kim me bhavanti na*

**“O Partha, I speak to you the truth. The gopis are My helpers, teachers, disciples, servants, friends and consorts. I do not know what they are not to Me.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**4.211**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.211)**) quoted from GopiPremamrta)**

On the banks of the sacred Godavari River, Srila RamanandaRay was graced with the vision of GauraHari’s combined form of Sri Radhika, the embodiment of MahaBhava, and Sri Govinda, the fountainhead of all spiritual sentiments {rasas), RasaRaja Sri Krsna. Srila Krsnadas Kaviraj mentions, that to properly understand this esoteric truth about Sri GauraSundar, as the united form of SriSri RadhaKrsna, one must receive Srila SvarupDamodara’s mercy. Without a pure Vaisnava’s mercy, it is impossible to enter the transcendental realm of siddhanta (scriptural conclusions) and raga-bhakti (spontaneous devotion).

Sri Krsna’s lila-madhuri, the sweetness of His eternal pastimes, is one of the four extraordinary qualities He alone possesses, above all other VisnuTattva expansions. His RasaLila is considered the pinnacle of all His transcendental pastimes. His early childhood pastimes are also unique and unparalleled since, other than YasodaNandan Krsna, Dasarathi Rama and Nimai Caitanya, no other incarnation exhibits kaisora, pauganda and kaumara-lila.

Kaumara-lila is till age five, pauganda-lila is between age five and ten and kaisora ends at age fifteen, when yauvana, or youth, begins.

### Verse 120

*hasantyuccairuccairahaha kulavadhvo’pi parito*  
*dravibhavam gacchantyapi kuvisayagravaghatitah*  
*tiraskurvantyajna api sakala sastrajria samitim*  
*ksitau sricaitanye’dbhuta mahimasare’vatarati*

**Aho! Chaste ladies from aristocratic families are jubilant and laughing wildly in gay abandon (having abandoned their natural shyness); those whose hearts are as hard as stones, due to excessive sense enjoyment and sinful activities, are melting all over the place; and illiterate persons previously without knowledge of the AbsoluteTruth now ridicule the educated society - all as a result of the most amazing and supremely glorious descent into this world by Sri CaitanyaDeva.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The pre-eminence of Sri Caitanya’s incarnation is glorified, showing how chaste ladies confined to the inner chambers of their homes, never exposed to the sun shining outside, and gross materialists, with hearts hardened due to intimate contact with the obscene objects of worldly possessions, as well as uncultured illiterates - all have somehow or other received the quintessence of all the aims of mankind - Sri VrajaPrema.

Ksitau- Sri Caitanya has incarnated on this earth; ‘but what is he like?’

Adbhut-mahima-sare- the creme de’la creme of the most glorious and amazing attractions ever to be seen or heard. Sri Caitanya has appeared, therefore, these very chaste, coy ladies are laughing without the slightest hint of shyness. Hasya (laughter) is an ecstatic symptom (anubhava) due to rati (DivineLove), thus can we understand that these ladies had progressed to a mature stage of devotion. Kuvisaya-grava-ghatitah- whose hearts, herein compared to stones, were hardened due to long and intimate contact with gross objects of enjoyment; yet even such hearts as these melt when touched by prema-rasa, signifying that they had attained sattvik bhava (ecstatic transformation). By Sri Caitanya’s mercy, even the illiterate and ignorant have become highly knowledgeable regarding scriptural conclusions, thus are they able to refute even erudite scholars.

Karika:

*gaure prakatatam prapte kulabadhvah sila-hrdah*  
*ajnasca premasampanna hasadrava rasanvitah*

**‘With the manifest presence of Sri Caitanya in this world, chaste ladies, hard-hearted persons and ignorant fools became respectively endowed with gay laughter, melted hearts and rasa (perspicacity, au fait) - all due to having received prema.’**

**Purport**

The supremely potent MahaMantra: HareKrsna HareKrsna, KrsnaKrsna HareHare, HareRama HareRama RamaRama HareHare, was hidden in the scriptures, to be discovered and introduced to the world by the most munificent of all incarnations, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu. The followers of Sri Caitanya participate in the Sankirtan movement and become thus enlightened. In Sri MadhuryaKadambini, Sri Visvanath Cakravarti poses a rhetorical question, the answer to which is self-evident.

He asks, ‘who among the different yogis is sure to attain perfection?’

‘One who, in the neophyte stage is still attached to material things and has not his senses fully under control, but chants the HolyNames regularly; or a yogi from any of the other yoga schools who is equipoised, self-controlled and disciplined, but does not chant the HolyNames nor possess bhakti (devotion)?

The answer is given by Sri Krsna Himself:

**‘This Divine energy of mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.’**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**1.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/1.14)**))**

Having attained the state of Brahman realisation, mundane scholars are very proud of their erudition; in their insolence they do not feel the need to surrender to the Supreme Lord, thinking themselves potential gods. However, a devotee is adorned with all the good qualities of the demigods. Vaisnavas are specifically characterized by daya (compassion) and dainya (humility). Devotees engaged in serving the Supreme Lord receive the Lord’s causeless mercy in the form of strong spiritual resolve and mature wisdom.

*vasudeve bhagavati bhakti-yogah prayojitah*  
*janayaty asu vairagyam jnanam ca yad ahaitukam*

**‘By rendering devotional service unto the Personality Sri Krsna, one immediately acquires causeless knowledge and detachment from the world.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**1.2.7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.7)**))**

Knowledge in the shape of scriptural conclusions requires years of study and discipline. From knowledge comes apathy towards this ephemeral material existence. By rendering devotional service to the Lord, the devotee skips the long and tedious process of acquiring knowledge and is rewarded the mature fruit of realisation - the knowledge that this material world is temporary, and knowledge of the ultimate goal of human existence - attainment of Divine ecstasy found only in the cultivation of bhakti.

The Supreme Lord Sri Krsna’s HolyNames appear as the MahaMantra: HareKrsna HareKrsna, KrsnaKrsna HareHare, HareRama HareRama RamaRama HareHare. This MahaMantra is eternal and is thus always present in sound. By the Divine arrangement of Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, the MahaMantra advented in Sri Mayapur, Navadvip and spread all over the globe by the tireless efforts of His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Svami Prabhupad, the direct recipient of Sri Caitanya's mercy. The transcendental potency of Sri Krsna’s HolyNames is as unlimited and supremely powerful as the Supreme Lord Sri Krsna Himself, since the Name and the Possessor of the Name are nondifferent. So potent is the MahaMantra that the worst of sinners cannot commit so many sins that one Name of Krsna cannot eradicate. Sins may also be eradicated by other processes recommended in the scriptures, but offenses (aparadha) cannot be absolved by any process other than the chanting of the Supreme Lord’s HolyNames.

*vacyam vacakam ityudeti bhavato nama svarupa-dvayam*  
*purvasmat parameva hanta karunam tatrapi jani mahe*  
*yas tasmin vihita-aparadha-nivahah prani-samastad bhaved*  
*dasyenedam-upasya so ’ pihi sadananda-ambudhau majjati*

**‘The Lord appears in this mundane world in two forms: as the Deity and as sound vibration. I take shelter of the HolyNames (sound vibration), since in the process of Deity worship, if there is any offense, the means of atonement is to continuously chant the HolyNames. In this way the HolyNames will enable us to relish Divine nectar and thus will we swim in the ocean of Supreme Ecstasy.’**  
**(Sri KrsnaNamAstakam (6))**

### Verse 121

*prayascaitanyamasidapi sakalavidam neha purvam yadesam*  
*kharvva sarwarthasare’pyakrta nahi padam kunthita buddhivrttih*  
*gambhirodarabhavojjvalarasa-madhurapremabhakti-pravesah*  
*kesam nasididanim jagati karunaya gauracandre’vatirne*

**Prior to the advent in this world of Sri KrsnaCaitanya, the theoretical scholars, proficient in all branches of scriptural knowledge, had no awareness of devotional service; their spiritual inclination to serve Sri Krsna was obscured almost beyond recognition. Due to a poor fund of intelligence, stunted by suspicion and doubts, their eventual aim in life was far short of the ultimate conclusion - KrsnaPrema. However, after the compassionate arrival of Sri GauraCandra on this earth, who is there now who has not entered into that rarely achieved, difficult to comprehend, yet supremely exalted, prema-bhakti, love in devotion based on the sweet principle of conjugal attraction, endowed with an unlimited variety of ecstatic emotions (vibhava, anubhava...)?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The glory of Sri Caitanya’s incarnation is portrayed, depicting the state of affairs in this world prior to His appearance. At that time no one had access to the most confidential and exalted sacred treasure, Vraja bhakti-rasa. However, now that He has arrived, everyone, including the lowest of beings, have gained eligibility to enter the transcendentally sweet path of erotic love for Krsna.

Purvvam- prior to the appearance of Sri Caitanya, no one in this world was aware of bhakti, even the learned scholars were unaware (unconscious) of its existence; the function of their intelligence was not absorbed in worship (bhajan) of Sri Krsna, the ultimate aim of mankind. The reason for this is that their intelligence was overly influenced by suspicion, doubt (kunthita) and bigotry (kharvva- narrow-mindedness; less intelligent). They were attached to the most insignificant reward, namely elevation to higher heavenly planets.

However, now that Sri GauraCandra, out of His causeless mercy, has descended to this earth- gambhirodara bhavojjvalarasa / gambhir- that which is not easily understood; udara- the most wondrous ecstatic emotions (anubhava, etc.), indicative of entrance into the realm of erotic love in devotion, are common occurences. Who was there who had not gained entrance there? That is to say, by the mercy of Sri GauraSundar, everyone experienced the sweet taste of prema-bhakti. Aho! Such are the glories of Sri Caitanya.

Karika:

*acaitanyasya lokasya dhirasidanavasthita*  
*avirbhute harau gaure na kesam bhagavad ratih*

**‘Prior to Sri GauraHari’s appearance, people were without awareness of the soul’s real identity, hence, their minds and intelligence were unsettled. However, now that He has arrived, is there anyone who has not developed attachment (rati) for the SupremeLord (Bhagavan)?’**

**Purport**

The most magnanimous Supreme Personality Sri Krsna Caitanya advented in KaliYuga to propagate the prescribed religious principle for this age, the chanting of the Lord’s HolyNames. Chanting the Supreme Lord’s Names and glorifying His extraordinary pastimes are transcendental, purely devotional activities. Any living entity who takes shelter of Sri Krsna Caitanya is instantly inspired to utter the HolyNames of God. By doing so, such a person performs bhakti-yoga, the only means to attain KrsnaPrema. No process other than the practice of any one of the nine limbs of bhakti is potent enough to arouse the eternally present, but dormant love of Krsna within the conditioned souls.

*nitya-siddha krsna-prema ‘sadhya’ kabhu naya*  
*sravanadi-suddha-citte karaye udaya*

**‘Pure love of Krsna is eternally established in the hearts of the living entities. It is not something to be gained from another source. When the heart is purified by hearing and chanting, this love naturally awakens.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**22.107**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.107)**))**

When a fortunate person begins to chant Sri Krsna’s names regularly, it is to be understood that he is an advanced soul, due to having performed pious deeds in previous lives.

*aho bata sva-paco ’to gariyan yaj-jihvagre vartate nama tubhyam*  
*tepus tapas te juhuvuh sasnur arya brahmanucur nama grnanti ye te*

**‘Oh, how glorious are they whose tongues are chanting Your HolyNames! Even if born in a family of dog-eaters, such persons are worshipful. Persons who chant the HolyNames of Your Lordship must have executed all types of austerities and yajnas and cultivated the noble behaviour of Aryans. To chant the HolyNames of Your Lordship, they must have bathed at all holy places of pilgrimage, studied the Vedas and fulfilled everything required.’**  
**(Srimad Bhagavatam (**[**3.33.7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.7)**))**

For the conditioned soul to realize that the ultimate goal of human life has nothing to do with the four ordinary objectives of human life (dharma, artha, kama, moksa) requires him or her to surrender to a self-realised rasika guru. Such a rasika-mahatma should be a strict follower of Sri Rupa Gosvami’s teachings and thus a representative of one of the disciplic successions coming from Sri KrsnaCaitanya. Without the blessings of a rupanuga rasika guru it is hardly possible to relish the fruit of KrsnaPrema. Indeed, it is rare to find such fortunate souls who aspire for the ultimate aim of mankind, KrsnaPrema. Sri Krsna Himself declares in the BhagavadGita ([7.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.3)), that only a very few out of many millions of conditioned souls will develop lobha (greed) for serving the DivineCouple, SilSri RadhaSyamSundar, in the devotional mood of the eternal residents of Vraja. Thus, though KrsnaPrema is a lofty, transcendental goal, taking shelter of a rasika guru will ensure success in one’s spiritual endeavours.

Rasika- capable of comprehending the inner or true significance or the flavour (of); appreciative; having a discriminating taste; aesthetic, devoted to; witty, humorous.

### Verse 122

*srimadbhagavatasya yatra paramam tatparyamuttankitam*  
*srivaiyasakina duranvayataya rasaprasange’pi yat*  
*yadradharatikeli-nagararasasvadaika-sadbhajanam*  
*tadvastu prathanaya gaura-vapusa loke’vatirno harih*

**Vaiyasaki Srila SukaDeva Gosvami merely gave a hint regarding the subject of Sri Krsna’s RasaLila pastimes, the most esoteric essence of the SrimadBhagavatam, since the subject matter is so abstruse. Sri Hari has appeared in this world in the form of Sri Gauranga as the proper agent for elaborating on the purport of SrimadBhagavatam, the erotic play of Sri Radha with her most beloved Paramour. Since he was himself the vessel of MahaPrema, he was an adept in relishing this delectable treat, and as well, highly competent in disseminating the same.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The magnificence of Sri Caitanya’s incarnation is that He distributed to each and all, the sweet ambrosia of the most esoteric VrajaLila, that He had Himself performed.

Srivaiyasakina- son of Srila VyasaDev, Sri SukaDev Gosvami, merely touched upon the subject of the most confidential dealings between Radha and Krsna when discussing the topic of RasaLila. Though these pastimes comprise the basic intent, purpose and culmination of SrimadBhagavatam , he gave only a brief representation, declining to give a detailed description as we would have thought such a subject deserved.

‘The reason?’

duranvayata- abstruse; difficult to penetrate or enter into; duh- nullity, absence; anu- cultivation, application - that which is not obtainable through cultivation or application. Since there were none who were eligible to properly perceive or relish such uncommon, transcendental activities, he declined to give the full particulars. Nevertheless, he personally was in complete understanding of the fundamental truths regarding this lila, being the son of Srila VyasaDev \[obtained by Sri Vyasaji through trance of meditation (samadhi) specifically for the purpose of presenting this BhagavatRasa\]. He has himself participated in the RasaLila pastimes as an attendant, in his form as SukaPaksi (parrot), that he might properly portray this lila. That he was in fact a member of the Vraja entourage is communicated by Sri Krsna himself to Naradaji:

*ekah sa metat vraja-loka-vat priyastadrk mahapremabhara prabhavatah*  
*vaksyatyadah kincana badarayanir majjivite sistavare samanvita*

**‘Just as the residents of Vraja are very dear to me, so is Sri SukaDev also dear to me. Due to his deep love for me, his life and soul are surrendered to me and in the future he will speak of these topics (my pastimes) in an august assembly of saintly persons.’**  
**(Sri BrhatBhagavatamrta** [**PurvaKhanda**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bb/1.1.1)**)**

yadradharatikeli- Sri Krsna is the great gallant (nagar) of the DivineDalliance that goes on in the forest arbours and bowers (nikunjakeli); the crest jewel of connoisseurs among the libertines. A fitting receptacle worthy of receiving the nectar of Sri Krsna’s RasaLila pastimes must be quite extraordinary indeed. Only in the presence of intense DivineLove can one relish the sweetness of SriSri RadhaMadhava’s nikunjakeli (amorous pastimes in the forest arbours). (Only fire can accommodate fire, without getting burnt.)

nagar- indicates a lady’s paramour (parakiya-bhava- the conjugal rasa of Vraja). \[This VrajaRasa PremaMadhuri is nitya-siddha (eternally existing in complete perfection). It bears absolutely no similarity with the lustful attraction between heroes and heroines of this world. Bhagavan Sri Krsna is the condensed form of the AbsoluteTruth, eternally present, full of transcendent knowledge and felicity. His dearly beloved (preyasi- girlfriends) gopis are of the same constitution. They do not have material bodies. This is the purport.\]

The conclusion of SrimadBhagavat, namely the confidential cordial of SriSri RadhaKrsna’s nikunjalila, finds a fitting and competent receptacle only in the presence of MahaPrema. Bhagavan Sri Krsna has appeared as Sri GauraHari to disseminate this overflowing cordial of ambrosia to the inhabitants of this earth, just at the beginning of KaliYuga.

Here, a point may be raised, that propagation is best accomplished through literature. Since Sri KrsnaCaitanya did not author any books, how will the precepts of MahaPrema be publicized?

In reply: SvayamBhagavan Sri Krsna did not also compose any treatise; rather he infused the heart of Sri Brahmaji with the knowledge of the Vedas. Similarly, Sri KrsnaCaitanya instilled in the heart of Srila RupaGosvami and the other Gosvamis of Vrindaban the potency to compose transcendental literature.

*hrdi yasya preranaya pravartite’ham varaka-rupo’pi*  
*tasya hareh padakamalam vande caitanya devasya*

**‘Although I am the lowest of men and have no knowledge, the inspiration to write transcendental literature regarding devotional service has been mercifully bestowed upon me. Therefore, I offer my obeisance at the lotus feet of Sri CaitanyaDeva, who has employed me to write these books.’**  
**(BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu (**[**1.1.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.1.2)**))**

Many devotional books saturated with scriptural conclusions and transcendental principles of rasa, depicting the pastimes of Sri Krsna, have been composed and compiled by many of his eternal associates. Therefore, the precepts and instructions of Sri Caitanya are available without change or deviation. Thus are the glories of Sri GaurangaAvatar.

Karika:

*srimad bhagavatatatparyya radhasvarati vibhramam*  
*vistarayan gauracandro’vatara svayam harih*

**‘SvayamBhagavan Sri Hari incarnated as Sri GauraCandra to promulgate the conclusion of SrimadBhagavatam - the enchanting, affectionate attachment of Sri RadhaThakurani (the sweet lila of SriSri RadhaMadhava).’**

**Purport**

**The Supreme Lord Ksirodakasayi Visnu, part of a plenary expansion of VrajendraNandan Sri Krsna, appears in unlimited incarnations in every millennium for the purpose of protecting the righteous and punishing the demons. This is all a part of the work of the maintainer of the creation - Sri Visnu. When the fountainhead of all incarnations (avatari), Sri CaitanyaDeva descends to this world, the work of universal affairs is conducted automatically by Lord Visnu, who is contained within the form of Sri KrsnaCaitanya. The golden incarnation of KaliYuga, Sri Caitanya came to propagate the transcendental science of pure bhakti. However, this was only the external or secondary reason for His appearance. He appeared primarily to relish Divine rasa, since He is raso vai sah rasam hy evayam labdhvanandi bhavati-‘He Himself is rasa, the taste or mellow of a particular relationship. And certainly one who achieves this rasa becomes anandi, filled with bliss.’**  
**(Taittiriya Upanisad (**[**2.7.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/taittiriya/2.7.1)**))**

Firm in their resolve to see their beloved Lord, Sri Caitanya Deva undisturbed in His sublime pastime of tasting the sweet nectar of rasa, Sri NityanandaPrabhu, Sri Haridas, Sri Svarup, Sri Sanatan, Sri Rupa, Sri Raghunath Das, all the six Gosvamis of Vraja, took up the work of preaching the science of pure bhakti. Without Lord Nityananda’s blessings no one can advance in spiritual life. His mercy alone will reward the jiva with KrsnaPrema. It was Lord Nityananda who encouraged Sri KrsnaCaitanya to be lenient towards the conditioned souls of KaliYuga so that they may easily obtain this most rare gift of bhakti,

*aye bhratarnrnam kali-kalusinam kim nu bhavita*  
*tatha prayascittam racaya yadanayasata ime*  
*vrajanti tvamittham saha bhagavata mantrayati yo*  
*bhaje nityanandam bhajana-taru-kandam tiravadhi*

**‘I eternally worship Sri NityanandaPrabhu, the root of the tree of pure bhakti, who advised Sri Caitanya- ‘My dear brother Gauranga! What will become of the sinful souls of KaliYuga? how can they be saved! Kindly devise a method by which they can easily attain KrsnaPrema.’**  
**(Sri NityanandAstakam (4))**

Bhakti alone is potent enough to elevate the eternally conditioned souls to the highest platform of visuddha-sattva.

*yat-pada-pankaja-palasa-vilasa-bhaktya*  
*karmasayam grathitam udgrathayanti santah*  
*tadvan na rikta-matayo yatayo ’pi ruddha-*  
*sroto-ganas tam aranam bhaja vasudevam*

**‘Devotees always engaged in the service of the toes of the lotus feet of the Lord, can very easily overcome hard-knotted desires for fruitive activities. Because this is very difficult, the non-devotees -jnanis and yogis - although trying to stop the waves of sense gratification, cannot do so. Therefore you are advised to engage in the devotional service of Krsna, the son of Vasudeva.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**4.22.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.39)**))**

Lord Nityananda, the adi-guru (original guru) appears in the body of the bonafide spiritual master to guide the conditioned souls to the lotus feet of Sri KrsnaCaitanya. There, at the Lord’s feet, the jiva relishes the mature fruit of bhakti- KrsnaPrema.

### Verse 123

*kecid dasyam avapur uddhava-mukhah slaghyam pare lebhire*  
*sridamadi padam vrajambu-drsam bhavanca bhejuh pare*  
*anye dhanyatama dhayanti sudhiyo radhapadambhoruham*  
*sricaitanyamahaprabhoh karunaya lokasya kah sampadah*

**Some devotees, headed by Sri Uddhava, attained servitorship; some obtained that most laudable mood of fraternal affection personified in Sridama. Still others partook of the bhava embodied in the VrajaGopis. While some most fortunate and intelligent souls actually tasted the sweet nectar of the lotus feet of Srimati Radhika. By the mercy of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, what wealth have they not obtained?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

A superbly attractive feature of Sri Gaura’s incarnation is illustrated in the depiction of His boundless compassion in instilling the wealth of bhava of the Vrajabasis in each and every person. By His mercy what wealth have they not acquired? These rewards have been explained in the following manner: some attained the ecstasy of servitorship, like Raktak, Patrak and others. Some attained the ecstasy of fraternal affection, like the illustrious Sridama and company. The suffix adi (Sridamadi) implies paternal affection as well; some were thus conferred with vatsalya prema. Others obtained the sweet (madhur- conjugal) loving sentiments of the VrajaGopis. Still others were able to relish the lovely charm of the lotus feet of Srimati Radhika. There were even those who, through becoming the devoted follower of one of Sri Radha’s sakhis (accepting that sakhi as their guru), drank the honey of Sri Radhika’s lotus feet in their own eternal form (as that of a manjari).

Karika:

*kalau gauraharau prapte prakatyam ke’pi ke’pi ca*  
*vraja-dasyadikam prapuh рарu radha-padambujam*

**‘With the appearance of Sri GauraHari in this KaliYuga, some devotees attained the devotional sentiments of servitorship (and so on) in Vraja, while others were able to drink the honey from the lotus feet of SrimatiRadhika.’**

**Purport**

The Supreme Lord Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu’s mission, as the maintainer of the universe, is to inundate the globe with the ambrosia of bhakti-rasa. Thus did He appear in the role of a pure devotee. He propagated the chanting of the HolyNames as the most efficacious means to counteract the illusory energy’s (maya ’s) grip on the conditioned souls. By performing sankirtan (congregational chanting), eternally deluded jivas come into contact with devotees. The PadmaPurana attributes the awakening of bhakti, inherent in every jiva, to sat-sanga -association of devotees. Bhakti begins with sravanam (hearing).

The initial stage of bhakti is known as sraddha. However, sraddha, which develops as a result of pious deeds, can also make the living entity bahir-mukh- attracted to the world of the senses, thus turning his back to Krsna. But bhakti utthata sukrti, a result of devotional activities executed unknowingly in the past, will reward the fortunate soul with bhakti sraddha, thus the jiva is convinced that by serving Krsna all his mundane responsibilities are automatically fulfilled.

*satam prasangan mama virya-samvido*  
*bhavanti hrt-karna-rasayanah kathah*  
*taj-josanad asv apavarga-vartmani*  
*sraddha ratir bhaktir anukramisyati*

**‘In the association of pure devotees, discussion of the pastimes and activities of the Supreme Personality of God is very pleasing and satisfying to the heart and ears. By cultivating such knowledge one gradually becomes advanced on the path of liberation, and thereafter he is freed, and his attraction becomes fixed. Then real (pure) devotion and devotional service begin.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**3.25.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.25)**))**

Bhakti-rasa is generated by pure chanting of the HolyNames of Sri Krsna. In the presence of bhakti-rasa all other mundane rasas, even brahmananda-rasa, are negligible and insipid. In truth, all rasas in their purest form are contained within bhakti-rasa. Thus, with the spreading of the Sankirtan movement initiated by SriSri GauraNitai, the entire universe was flooded with the transcendental vibration of the HolyNames.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur comments:

“No rasa other than bhakti-rasa was present. This includes the mundane rasa of the gross sensualists, intellectual and literary rasa, the mundane neutral rasa of philosophers and scholars, the Paramatma rasa of the mystic yogis, the impersonal rasa of the monists, and so on. None of these rasas were even considered rasas in comparison to the non-dual Absolute rasa. This is so because the wondrous bhakti-rasa blooms from the intermingling of sthayi-bhava, or it’s four ingredients: vibhava, anubhava, sattvika and vyabhicari, sthayi-bhava is permanent devotion and loving attraction in the jiva for the Supreme Personality Sri Krsna. Hence, all other rasas are either mundane or incomplete, partial rasas when compared to bhakti-rasa

### Verse 124

*sarvajnairmunipungvaih pravitate tattanmate yuktibhih*  
*purvam naikataratra ko’pi sudrdham visvasta asijjanah*  
*sampratyapratimaprabhava udite gaurangacandre punah*  
*srutyartho haribhaktireva paramah kairva na nirdharyate*

**Erudite thinkers and sages, well-versed in all branches of knowledge, tried to establish their views with logic and argument, but none of them were fully convinced, not even in their own arguments. Recently, however, with the glorious advent of Sri GauraCandra, endowed with immeasurable power, is there anyone who lacks the certainty that loving devotion to Sri Hari is the singular and highest goal propounded in the Vedas? Once again He has come to establish this truth.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The awe-inspiring grandeur of Sri Gauranga’s incarnation is further illustrated by the fact that He has awarded everyone the perception to experience the authentic conclusion of the Vedas - pure devotion to the SupremeLord Sri Hari.

Prior to Sri Gauranga’s advent, sarvajnair muni pungavai...- the principal sages and thinkers tried to establish their individual philosophies and opinions through rhetoric, polemics and dialectics. However, due to the absence of any substantive proof, no philosophy held sway. This means that no one believed in his own opinion, or had faith in another’s. No one was sure of his own philosophy as long as it remained unsupported by others.

Since the appearance of Sri GauraHari, however, who is there who is unable to discern that devotion to Sri Hari is the substantiated, authentic purport and conclusion of the Vedas? Meaning: everyone is able to ascertain this truth. This is possible due to the inconceivable influence of Sri Gauranga.

The reference to Sri GauraHari as Sri GauraCandra, suggests that, just as the brightness of the stars is dimmed by the rising moon, similarly, the many stars of individual opinion dim in the wake of Sri GauraCandra’s appearance. By His cooling rays, the burning fire of material existence is extinguished.

Karika:

*pracina mata karttrnam sraddha tattanmate nahi*  
*gaure tu prakate veda tatparyyartha harau ratih*

**‘Ancient sages did not have faith even in their own opinions. However, after the advent of Sri GauraHari, everyone is able to perceive that attachment (rati- love and affection) to Sri Hari is the authentic purport of the Vedas’**

**Purport**

*yada yada hi dharmasya glanir bhavati bharata*  
*abhyutthanam adharmasya tadatmanam srjamy aham*

**‘Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, О descendant of Bharat, and a predominant rise of irreligion - at that time I descend Myself.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**4.7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.7)**))**

*dharmam tu saksad bhagavat-pranitam*  
*na vai vidur rsayo napi devah*  
*na siddha-mukhya asura manusyah*  
*kuto nu vidyadhara-caranadayah*

**‘Real religious principles are enacted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although fully situated in the mode of goodness, even the great rsis who occupy the topmost planets cannot ascertain real religious principles, nor can the demigods or the leaders of SiddhaLoka, to say nothing of the asuras, ordinary human beings, Vidyadharas and Caranas.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.3.19**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/3.19)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

**“The word muni means one who can agitate his mind in various ways for mental speculation, without coming to a factual conclusion. It is said that every muni has a different angle of vision, and unless a muni differs from other munis, he cannot be called a muni in the strict sense of the term. Nasav rsir yasya matam na bhinnam (MahaBharata VanaParva 313.117). But a sthita-dhir muni, as mentioned herein by the Lord, is different from an ordinary muni. The sthita-dhir muni is always in Krsna consciousness, for he has exhausted all his business of creative speculation. He is called prasanta-nihsesa-mano-rathantara (StotraRatna 43), or one who has surpassed the stage of mental speculations and has come to the conclusion that Lord Sri Krsna, or Vasudeva, is everything (vasudevah sarvam iti sa mahatma sudurlabhah). He is called a muni fixed in mind. Such a fully Krsna conscious person is not at all disturbed by the onslaughts of the threefold miseries, for he accepts all miseries as the mercy of the Lord, thinking himself only worthy of more trouble due to his past misdeeds; and he sees that his miseries, by the grace of the Lord, are minimized to the least extent. Similarly, when he is happy he gives credit to the Lord, thinking himself unworthy of the happiness; he realizes that it is due only to the Lord’s grace that he is in such a comfortable condition and able to render better service to the Lord. For the service of the Lord, he is always daring and active, uninfluenced by attachment or aversion. Attachment means accepting things for one’s own sense gratification, and detachment is the absence of such sensual attachment. One fixed in Krsna consciousness has neither attachment nor detachment because his life is dedicated in the service of the Lord. Consequently he is not at all angry even when his attempts are unsuccessful. Success or no success, a Krsna conscious person is always steady in his determination.”**  
**(Srimad BhagavadGita** [**2.57**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.57) **Purport)**

### Verse 125

*visvam mahapranayasadhusudharasaika-*  
*pathonidhau sakalameva nimajjayantam*  
*gaurangacandranakhacandramanicchatayah*  
*kancidvicitramanubhavamaham smarami*

**I remember the inimitable, incredible influence of the lustre of the moonstone nails of the lotus feet of Sri GauraCandra; an ocean of nectar, the Elixir of Loving Affection, which ocean has bathed the universe, drowning its inhabitants in ecstasy.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Remembering with immense joy how Sri GauraHari inundated the earth with an Ocean of Premamrta, the revered author, Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati describes His glorious incarnation.

‘The toenails of the lotus feet of Sri GauraCandra are like moonstone gems. Their radiance suffuses my heart with the recollection of ineffable ecstasy.’

‘What kind of ecstasy (anubhava)?

The lustre of the nails of His lotus feet liquefies, thus becoming an ocean of nectar; mahapranaya-sadhu-sudharasaika- when intense, affectionate, loving attachment reaches maturity, sublimely sweet nectar is produced therefrom; this nectar inundated the universe, swelling to become a great ocean.

Karika:

*gauracandra padambhoja nakhacandramani prabham*  
*majjayantam jagat premni prabhavam tam smaramyaham*

**‘The splendour from the nails of Sri GauraCandra’s lotus feet have induced a deluge of prema throughout the entire universe. Remembering the influence of His unprecedented love, I have also drowned in this Ocean of Prema.’**

**Purport**

*sancintayed bhagavatas caranaravindam*  
*vajrankusa-dhvaja-saroruha-lanchanadhyam*  
*uttunga-rakta-vilasan-nakha-cakravala-*  
*jyotsnabhir ahata-mahad-dhrdayandhakaram*

**‘The devotee should first concentrate his mind on the Lord’s lotus feet, which are adorned with the marks of a thunderbolt, goad, banner and lotus. The splendour of their beautiful ruby nails resembles the orbit of the moon and dispels the thick gloom of one’s heart.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**3.28.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.21)**))**

*padbhyam nakha-mani-srenya vilasadbhyam samarcatam*  
*hrt-padma-karnika-dhisnyam akramyatmany avasthitam*

**‘One desirous of worshiping the Lord should forcibly catch hold of His lotus feet and situate them on the lotus whorl of his heart, thus bathed in the splendour of the light emanating from the jewellike nails of His lotus feet.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**4.8.50**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.50)**))**

*krpa-sudha-sarid yasya visvarn aplavayanty api*  
*nica-gaiva sada bhati tam caitanya-prabhum bhaje*

**‘I worship Lord Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, whose nectarean mercy flows like a great river, inundating the entire universe. Just as a river flows downstream, Lord Caitanya especially extends Himself to the fallen.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**16.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/16.1)**)**

*krsna-guna-rupa-rasa, gandha, sabda, parasa,*  
*se sudha asvade gopi-gana*  
*ta-sabara grasa-sese, ani’ pancendriya sisye,*  
*se bhiksaya rakhena jivana*

**‘The gopis of VrajaBhumi always taste the nectar of Krsna’s attributes, His beauty. His sweetness. His aroma, the sound of His flute and the touch of His body. My mind’s five disciples, the senses of perception, gather the remnants of that nectar from the gopis and bring them to the yogi of My mind. The senses maintain their lives by eating those remnants.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**14.49**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/14.49)**))**

*unmadera laksana, karaya krsna-sphurana,*  
*bhavavese uthe pranaya mana*  
*solluntha-vacana-riti, mana, garva, vyaja-stuti,*  
*kabhu ninda, kabhu va sammana*

**‘The symptoms of madness serve as an impetus for remembering Krsna. This mood of ecstasy awoke love, disdain, defamation by words, pride, honour and indirect prayer. Thus Sri Krsna was sometimes blasphemed and sometimes honoured.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**2.66**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/2.66)**))**

Pranaya is explained thus: When there is a possibility of receiving direct honour but it is avoided, that love is called pranaya.

Vyaja- pretext, deceit, disguise. On the pretext of insulting their beloved, the gopis actually praise him.

*radha krsna-pranaya-vikrtir hladinl saktir asmad*  
*ekatmanav api bhuvi pura deha-bhedam gatau tau*  
*caitanyakhyarh prakatam adhuna tad-dvayam caikyam aptam*  
*radha-bhava-dyuti-suvalitam naumi krsna-svarupam*

**The loving affairs of Sri Radha and Krsna are transcendental manifestations of the Lord’s internal pleasure-giving potency. Although Radha and Krsna are one in their identity, they have separated themselves eternally. Now these two transcendental identities have again united, in the form of Sri KrsnaCaitanya. I bow down to Him, who has manifest Himself with the sentiment and complexion of Srimati Radharani, although He is Krsna Himself.’**

*sri-radhayah pranaya-mahima kidrso vanayaiva-*  
*svadyo yenadbhuta-madhurima kidrso va madiyah*  
*saukhyam casya mad-anubhavatah kidrsam veti lobhat*  
*tad-bhavadhyah samajani saci-garbha-sindhau harinduh*

**‘Desiring to understand the glory of Radharani’s love, the wonderful qualities in Him that She alone relishes through Her love, and the happiness She feels when She realizes the sweetness of His love, the Supreme Lord Hari, richly endowed with Her emotions, appeared from the womb of Srimati SaciDevi, as the moon appeared from the ocean.’**  
**(Sri Caitanya Caritamrta AdiLila(**[**1.5-6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.5)**))**

### Verse 126

*atipunyairatisukrtaih krtarthlkrtah ko’pi purvvaih*  
*evam kairapi na krtam yat premabdhau nimajjitam visvam*  
*avatirne gauracandre vistirne premasagare*  
*ye na majjanti majjanti te mahanartha sagare*

**Some persons in the past, through the execution of pious activities, became greatly fortunate (attained Vaikuntha). However, it has never before been seen that the entire universe drowned in the Ocean of Prema. With the appearance of Sri GauraCandra, this Ocean of Prema expanded far and wide in all directions. Those who could not immerse themselves in that ocean fell headlong into the ocean of superfluity, meaninglessness and disadvantage.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

The majesty of Sri GauraHari’s incarnation is revealed by portraying Him as the author of a great flood of Premamrta (nectarean love).

In the past, some fortunate souls were made more fortunate (elevated to Vaikuntha), through the execution of pious deeds (sukrti, punya karma).

‘Who were these fortunate souls?’

Noble, high-minded, magnanimous souls, possessed of the capacity to sanctify others; thus are they referred to as ati-punyaih (liberated souls). However, no one had ever before flooded the entire universe with Premamrta (the nectar of DivineLove) as did Sri KrsnaCaitanya.

Karika:

*ko’pi nistaritah, purvaih premambudhi nimajjanam*  
*visvasya na krtam kairapyrte gauraharim kalau*

**‘Previously, some great souls attained salvation. However, no one was ever able to inundate the entire universe in the ocean of Premamrta, as has Sri GauraHari, in this IronAge of Kali.’**

**Purport**

*punyo gandhah prthivyam ca tejas casmi vibhavasau*

**‘I am the original fragrance of the earth, and I am the heat in fire.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**7.9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.9)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“Punya means that which is not decomposed; punya is original. Everything in the material world has a certain flavour or fragrance, as the flavour and fragrance in a flower, or in the earth, in water, in fire, in air, and so on. The uncontaminated flavour, the original flavour, which permeates everything, is Krsna. Similarly, everything has a particular original taste, and this taste can be changed by the mixture of chemicals. So everything original has some smell, some fragrance, and some taste.”

*prapya punya-krtam lokan usitva sasvatih, samah*  
*sucinam srimatam gehe yoga-bhrasto ’bhijayate*

**‘The unsuccessful yogi, after many, many years of enjoyment on the planets of the pious living entities, is born into a family of righteous people, or into a family of rich aristocracy.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**6.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/6.41)**))**

*yesam tv anta-gatam papam jananam punya-karmanam*  
*te dvandva-moha-nirmukta bhajante mam drdha-vratah*

**‘Persons who have acted piously in previous lives and in this life and whose sinful actions are completely eradicated are freed from the dualities of delusion, and they engage themselves in My service with determination.’**  
**(BhagavadGita(**[**7.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.28)**))**

Srila Prabhupad:

“For those who are sinful, atheistic, foolish and deceitful, it is very difficult to transcend the duality of desire and hate. Only those who have passed their lives in practicing the regulative principles of religion, who have acted piously and who have conquered sinful reactions can accept devotional service and gradually rise to the pure knowledge of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Then, gradually, they can meditate in trance on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That is the process of being situated on the spiritual platform.”

*susrusoh sraddadhanasya vasudeva-katha-rucih*  
*syan mahat-sevaya viprah punya-tirtha-nisevanat*

**‘O twice-born sages, by serving those devotees who are completely freed from all vice, great service is done. By such service, one gains affinity for hearing the messages of Vasudeva.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.2.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16)**))**

*srnvatam sva-kathah krsnah punya-sravana-kirtanah*  
*hrdy antah stho hy abhadrani vidhunoti suhrt satam*

**‘Sri Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramatma \[SuperSoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**1.2.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.17)**))**

Srila Prabhupad:

**“As stated in BhagavadGita (**[**7.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.16)**), catur-vidha bhajante mam janah sukrtino “rjuna. Without sukrti, or pious activities, no one can come to the shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord is approached by four kinds of pious men (arto jijnasur artharthi jnani ca), but here we see that Nanda Maharaja and Yasoda surpassed all of them. Therefore Pariksit Maharaja naturally inquired, “What kind of pious activities did they perform in their past lives by which they achieved such a Stage of perfection?”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.8.46**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.46)**)) Purport**

*pancama purusartha—premanandamrta-sindhu*  
*moksadi ananda yarn nahe eka bindu*

**‘For a devotee who has actually developed bhava, the pleasure derived from dharma, artha, kama and moksa appears like a drop in the presence of a nectarean Ocean of Love.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta Adi Lila (**[**7.85**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/7.85)**))**

*krsna-prema sunirmala, yena suddha-ganga-jala,*  
*sei prema—amrtera sindhu*  
*nirmala se anurage, na lukaya anya dage,*  
*sukla-vastre yaiche masi-bindu*

‘Love for Lord Krsna is very pure, just like the waters of the Ganges. That love is an ocean of nectar. That pure attachment to Krsna does not conceal any spot, which would appear just like a spot of ink on a white cloth.’  
(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila ([2.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/2.48)))

*suddha-prema-sukha-sindhu, pai tara eka bindu,*  
*sei bindu jagat dubaya*  
*kahibara yogya naya, tathapi baule kaya,*  
*kahile va keba patiyaya*

**‘Unalloyed love of Krsna is like an ocean of happiness. If someone gets one drop of it, the whole world can drown in that drop. It is not befitting to express such love of Krsna, yet a madman must speak. Yet even though he speaks, no one believes him.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**2.49**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/2.49)**))**

*ei-mata mahaprabhu ratri-divase*  
*prema-sindhu-magna rahe, kabhu dube, bhase*

**‘In this way Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu stayed immersed day and night in an ocean of ecstatic love for Krsna. Sometimes He was submerged, and sometimes He floated.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila (**[**19.77**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/19.77)**))**

\* the second couplet is not present in the SriCaitanya VaniEdition

### Verse 127

*dharme nistham dadhadanupamam visnubhaktim garistham*  
*samvibhrano dadhadiha hi hrttisthativasmasaram*  
*nico goghnadapi jagadaho plavayatyasrupuraih*  
*ко va janatyahaha gahanam hemagaurangarangam*

**Many persons in this world possess religious fervour; even some have taken complete shelter of the most exalted path of bhakti and practice sadhana with incomparable steadfastness, yet their hearts remain adamantine, as though encased in steel frames. Nevertheless, Aho! (Rejoice!) Degenerates more heinous than the slaughterers of cows have completely renounced sinful activities and are inundating the world with incessant tears, by the mercy Sri GauraSundar. Ahaha! (Wonder of wonders!) Who can comprehend the incomprehensible rahga (colour, complexion, dramatic performance, manner, mode, style, fashion, game, sport, fun, frolic) of the golden complexioned (HemaGaura) Sri GauraCandra?**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

Sri Gauranga’s glories are revealed by recounting His inevitable, unhindered compassion as He ignores those who are qualified to receive prema in order to first award prema to the lowest and most unqualified wretches. Who is capable of fathoming the mysterious pastimes of Sri GauraHari?

Some follow strictly the rules and regulations of religion and seriously cultivate devotion to Sri Visnu. but still have hearts as hard as granite, unable to experience ecstatic transformation (sattvik bhava). Their hearts simply will not melt due to the conspicuous absence of DivineLove. Whereas, go ghnad api-those lower than the killers of cows, by receiving the mercy of GauraHari, flood the earth with their tears of ecstatic joy.

Symptoms of ecstasy (sattvik bhava) are ignited by the fire of prema in the heart, causing it to melt. The sannyasis of Kasi, bereft of the mercy of Sri GauraHari, had not one iota of prema, whereas reprobates like Jagai and Madhai experienced exalted levels of DivineLove.

Karika:

*dharme sadhana bhaktau ca nistam prapte jane ’krpa*  
*krpaturyasya nice’bhuttasya ko vetti natakam*  
*tasya gaurangasyeti sesah*

**‘Who can fathom the mysteries of Sri Gauranga’s dramatic lila? He withholds His mercy from those who are attached to religiosity and sadhana bhakti, while bestowing mercy upon the low and wretched.’**

**Purport**

**“Cow slaughter is an act of the grossest type of ignorance. In the Vedic literature (RgVeda 9.4.64) the words gobhih prinita-matsaram- indicate that one who, being fully satisfied by milk, is desirous of killing the cow, is in the grossest ignorance.”**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**14.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.16)**) Purport)**

*nijagrahaujasa virah kalim digvijaye kvacit*  
*nrpa-linga-dharam sudram ghnantam go-mithunam pada*

**‘Once, when Maharaja Pariksit was on his way to conquer the world, he saw the master of KaliYuga, who was lower than a sudra, disguised as a king and hurting the legs of a cow and bull. The King at once caught hold of him to deal sufficient punishment.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.16.4**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/16.4)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“The king, being the representative of the Lord, has to execute the will of the Lord duly. There is no question of self-aggrandizement. Thus, as soon as Maharaja Pariksit saw that a lower-class man in the dress of a king was hurting the legs of a cow and a bull, he at once arrested and punished him. The king cannot tolerate insults to the most important animal, the cow, nor can he tolerate disrespect for the most important man, the brahmana. Human civilization means to advance the cause of brahminical culture, and to maintain it, cow protection is essential. There is a miracle in milk, for it contains all the necessary vitamins to sustain human physiological conditions for higher achievements. Brahminical culture can advance only when man is educated to develop the quality of goodness, and for this there is a prime necessity of food prepared with milk, fruits and grains. Maharaja Pariksit was astonished to see that a black sudra, dressed like a ruler, was mistreating a cow, the most important animal in human society.”

*tad asma-saram hrdayam batedam yad grhyamanair hari-nama-dheyaih*  
*na vikriyetatha yada vikaro netre jalam gatra-ruhesu harsah*

**‘Certainly that heart is steel-framed which, in spite of one’s chanting the HolyNames of the Lord with concentration, does not change when ecstasy takes place, tears fill the eyes and the hairs Stand on end.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**2.3.24**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.24)**))**

Srila Prabhupad:

“The whole process of spiritual culture is aimed at changing the heart of the living being in the matter of his eternal relation with the Supreme Lord as subordinate servant, which is his eternal constitutional position. So with the progress of devotional service, the reaction of change in the heart is exhibited by gradual detachment from the sense of material enjoyment, exhibited by a false sense of lording it over the world, and an increase in the attitude of rendering loving service to the Lord. Vidhi-bhakti, or regulated devotional service by the limbs of the body is stressed herein in relation to the mind, which is the impetus for all activities. It is expected that by discharging regulated devotional service, one must manifest the change of heart. If there is no such change, the heart must be considered steel-framed, for it is not melted even when there is chanting of the HolyNames of the Lord. We must always remember that hearing and chanting are the basic principles of discharging devotional duties, and if they are properly performed there will follow the reaction; ecstasy with signs of tears in the eyes and standing of the hairs on the body. These are natural consequences and are the preliminary symptoms of bhava, which occurs before one reaches the perfectional stage of prema, love of Krsna.  
“If this reaction does not take place, even after continuous hearing and chanting of the HolyNames of the Lord, it may be considered to be due to offenses only. That is the opinion of the Sandarbha. In the beginning of chanting the HolyNames of the Lord, if the devotee is not very careful about avoiding the ten kinds of offenses at the feet of the HolyNames, certainly the reaction of feelings of separation will not be visible as tears in the eyes and standing of the hair on end (horripilation).  
“The bhava stage is manifest by eight transcendental symptoms: inertness, perspiration, goosebumps (bodily hairs standing on end- horripilation), faltering voice, trembling, paleness of the body, tears in the eyes and finally, trance. The Nectar of Devotion, a summary study of Srila Rupa Gosvami’s BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu, explains those symptoms and vividly describes other transcendental developments, both in steady and accelerating manifestations.  
“Srila Visvanath Cakravarti Thakur has very critically discussed bhava in connection with some unscrupulous neophyte’s imitating the above symptoms for cheap appreciation. Sometimes all the above eight symptoms of ecstasy are imitated by the mundane devotees {prakrta-sahajiyas), but the pseudo symptoms are at once detected when one sees the pseudodevotee addicted to so many forbidden things. Even though decorated with the signs of a devotee, a person addicted to smoking, drinking or illegitimate sex with women cannot have all the above-mentioned ecstatic symptoms. Thus it is seen that sometimes these symptoms are wilfully imitated, and for this reason Srila Visvanath Cakravarti accuses the imitators of being stonehearted men. They are sometimes even affected by the reflection of such transcendental symptoms, yet if they still do not give up their forbidden habits, then they are hopeless cases for transcendental realisation.  
“When Lord Caitanya met Srila RamanandaRaya of Kavaur on the bank of the Godavari, the Lord developed all these symptoms, but because of the presence of some nondevotee brahmanas who were attendants of the Raya, the Lord suppressed these symptoms. So sometimes they are not visible even in the body of the first-class devotee, for certain circumstantial reasons. Therefore, we can understand that steady bhava is categorically displayed in the matter of cessation of material desires (ksanti), utilization of every moment in the transcendental loving service of the Lord (avyartha-kalatvam \[Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta. MadhyaLila 23.18-19\]), eagerness for glorifying the Lord constantly (nama-gane sada ruci (MadhyaLila 23.32\]), attraction for living in the land of the Lord (pritis tad vasati sthale), complete detachment from material happiness (virakti), and pridelessness (mana-sunyata). One who has developed all these transcendental qualities is really possessed of bhava, as distinguished from the stonehearted imitator or mundane devotee.  
“The whole process can be summarized as follows: The advanced devotee who chants the HolyNames of the Lord in a perfectly offenseless manner and is friendly to everyone can actually relish the transcendental taste of glorifying the Lord. And the result of such realisation is reflected in the cessation of all material desires, as mentioned above. The neophytes, due to their being in the lower stage of devotional service, are invariably envious, so much so that they invent their own ways and means of devotional regulations without following the acaryas. As such, even if they make a show of constantly chanting the HolyNames of the Lord, they cannot relish the transcendental taste of the HolyNames. Therefore, their show of tears in the eyes, trembling, perspiration or unconsciousness, is condemned. They can, however, get in touch with a pure devotee of the Lord and rectify their bad habits; otherwise they shall continue to be stonehearted and unfit for any treatment. A complete progressive march on the return path home, back to Godhead, will depend on the instructions of the revealed scriptures directed by a realized devotee."

### Verse 128

*kvacit krsnavesannatati bahubhangimabhinayan*  
*kvacidradhavisto hari hari harityarttiruditah*  
*kvacidringan balah kvacidapi ca gopalacarito*  
*jagadgauro vismapayati bahugambhiramahima*

**Sometimes Sri GauraSundar becomes absorbed in the ecstasy of Sri Krsna and thus dances, expressing a variety of dramatic postures and gestures. Sometimes He crawls about on all fours, portraying his lila as BalGopal; on other occasions He exhibits the characteristics of a young cowherd boy. Sometimes He suddenly becomes overwhelmed by the forceful emotions Srimati Radhika feels, due to excruciating pangs of separation from Her beloved Sri Krsna. Crying out “Hari! Hari! Hari!” He sheds profuse tears, deeply afflicted by the anguish of viraha prema, Love-in-Separation. Thus does Sri GauraHari astonish the universe by his profound and unfathomable ecstacies.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

To reveal the super excellence of Sri GauraHari’s incarnation. His various lilas are being described. He astounded the whole world by expressing the bhava (sentiments) of the four rasas of Vraja (dasya, sakhya, vatsalya and madhurya) in three phases of His life (balya, pauganda and kaisora).

Bahu-gambhira-mahima- the magnitude of His unquestionable potency and influence, vismapayati- thoroughly amazes the world. Sometimes overcome by the mood and sentiments of Sri Krsna, little Nimai would crawl on all fours, thus evoking the mood (rasa) of vatsalya prema (parental affection). Kvacidapi gopala-carito- sometimes, Nimai would enact the pastime of pasturing the cows. This boyhood (pauganda) lila evoked the moods (rasas) of dasya (servitorship) and sakhya (fraternal love). Bahubhangim abhinayan- while dancing, he presented many youthful, heroic postures and expressions inducing madhurya-rasa (conjugal mellows). At other times radhavisto- overwhelmed by the sentiments of Srimati Radharani, Sri GauraHari sobbed incessantly, immersed in the agony of separation from Sri Krsna, all the while crying out ‘Hari! Hari!’

Karika:

*balya-pauganda kaisora purvavastham prakasayan*  
*kvacid virahini-bhavam gauro vismapayajjagat*

**‘Sri Gauranga astounds the world, while enacting the pastimes of Sri Krsna; sometimes as a child, sometimes as a boy and sometimes as a youth; sometimes absorbed in the bhava (moods and sentiments) of Srimati Radhika, in the throes of love-in-separation.’**

**Purport**

**‘Krsna manifests His VrindabanLila pastimes just to attract us to meet the Supreme Personality of Godhead, face to face.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**4.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)**), lecture Geneva 1 June 1974)**

**‘Krsna comes down on this planet to exhibit His VrindabanLila just to attract us that anyone can have the same facilities, to play with Krsna, to talk with Krsna.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**16.2-7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/16.1)**), lecture Bombay 8 April 1971)**

*ittham satam brahma-sukhanubhutya dasyam gatanam para-daivatena*  
*mayasritanam nara-darakena sakam vijahruh krta-punya-punjah*

**‘Those who are engaged in self-realisation, appreciating the Brahman effulgence of the Lord, and those engaged in devotional service, accepting the Supreme Personality of Godhead as master, as well as those who are under the clutches of maya, thinking the Lord an ordinary person, cannot understand that certain exalted personalities - after accumulating volumes of pious activities - are now playing with the Lord in friendship as cowherd boys.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam(**[**10.12.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/12.7)**))**

**“Krsna’s lila is nitya-lila. Just to attract us - ‘You are fond of dancing. Why don’t you come back to Me and dance with Me?’ this is Krsna’s business. ‘Why you are rotting in this rotting dance? You want association. You want sporting. Why don’t you come to Me and take part in My sporting with the cowherd boys?’ This is the invitation of Krsna.**  
**“So one who has some intelligence, he will try to enter into the pastimes, transcendental pastimes of the Lord, either as a cowherd boy or as a servant or as a flower, as a tree, or the water of Yamuna, or the land, or a father or mother, or conjugal lover. Or it may be as enemy, as Aghasura, Bakasura, Putana. They are also blessed because they are acting with Krsna. This is the sum and substance of VrindabanLila. Krsna comes, He exhibits His lila in Vrindaban to attract the conditioned souls, who are engaged in false lila, temporary lila, or hellish lila. Krsna wants to save us. The propensity is there. Krsna says, ‘Not here. Not in this material world. This is perverted. You come to Me.’ But the Mayavadis, because they have a poor fund of knowledge, they think that ‘If again there is lila, there is sporting, there is dancing, no, that is here. Then it is maya.’ With their poor fund of knowledge, their brains cannot accommodate that Krsna’s lila and this lila are not the same. Not the same. They think when there is lila (activity), then it must be maya; therefore they are called Mayavadi. Their idea is that liberation means minus this lila, no more lila, simply stop everything. Voidism.”**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**7.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/7.8)**), lecture Vrindaban 15 March 1974)**

“Krsna by His causeless mercy manifests Himself along with His Form, Name, Qualities, Entourage, and Pastimes in order to attract the conditioned souls to the eternal blissful life of knowledge. Thus by understanding Krsna in His manifest lila, one is attracted to His eternal lila, and that is the highest success of life, explained in the latter part of the verse:  
letter to Syamasundar LA 14 May 1970

*yam prapya na nivartante tad dhama paramam mama*

**‘That place from which, having attained it, one never returns - that is My supreme abode.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**8.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/8.21)**))**

**“Since SukadevaGosvami is one of the prominent gata-vyalikas, who are freed from all misconceptions, he therefore expresses his own realized perception of Lord Sri Krsna as being the sum total of all perfection, the Personality of Godhead. Everyone is seeking the favour of the Goddess of Fortune, but people do not know that Lord Sri Krsna is the beloved husband of all Goddesses of Fortune. In the BrahmaSamhita it is said that the Lord, in His transcendental abode GolokaVrndavana, is accustomed to herding the surabhi cows and is served there by hundreds of thousands of Goddesses of Fortune. All these Goddesses of Fortune are manifestations of His transcendental pleasure potency (hladini-sakti), His internal energy. When the Lord manifest His presence on this earth, He partially displayed the activities of His pleasure potency in His RasaLila, just to attract the conditioned souls, who are all after the phantasmagorial pleasure potency in degraded sex enjoyment. The pure devotees of the Lord like SukadevaGosvami, who was completely detached from the abominable sex life of the material world, discussed this act of the Lord’s pleasure potency certainly not in relation to sex, but to relish a transcendental taste inconceivable to the mundaners who are after sex life. Sex life in the mundane world is the root-cause of being conditioned by the shackles of illusion, and certainly SukadevaGosvami was never interested in the sex life of the mundane world. Nor does the manifestation of the Lord’s pleasure potency have any connection with such degraded things. Lord Caitanya was a strict sannyasi, so much so that He did not allow any woman to come near Him, not even to bow down and offer respects. He never even heard the prayers of the deva-dasis offered in the temple of Jagannath because a sannyasi is forbidden to hear songs sung by the fair sex. Yet even in the rigid position of a sannyasi, He recommended the mode of worship preferred by the gopis of Vrindaban as the topmost loving service possible to be rendered to the Lord. Srimati Radharani is the principal head of all such Goddesses of Fortune, and therefore She is the pleasure counterpart of the Lord and is nondifferent from Krsna.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**2.4.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.20)**) Purport)**

*prema-rasa-niryasa karite asvadana*  
*raga-marga bhakti loke karite pracarana*  
*rasika-sekhara krsna parama-karuna*  
*ei dui hetu haite icchara udgama*

**‘The Lord's desire to appear was born from two reasons: the Lord wanted to taste the sweet essence of the mellows of love of God, and He wanted to propagate devotional service in the world on the platform of spontaneous attraction. Thus He is known as supremely jubilant and as the most merciful of all.’**  
**\[Lord Krsna thought:\] “All the universe is filled with the conception of my majesty, but love weakened by that sense of majesty does not satisfy me. If one regards me as the Supreme Lord and himself as a subordinate, I do not become subservient to his love, nor can it control me. In whatever transcendental mellow my devotee worships me, I reciprocate with him. That is my natural behaviour.”**  
**‘In whatever way my devotees surrender unto me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows my path in all respects, О son of Prtha.’**  
**(BhagavadGita (**[**4.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)**))**

‘If one cherishes pure loving devotion to me, thinking of me as his son, his friend or his beloved, regarding himself as great and considering me his equal or inferior, I become subordinate to him. Devotional service rendered to me by the living beings revives their eternal life. “O my dear damsels of Vraja, your affection for me is your good fortune, for it is the only means by which you have obtained my favour.”

“Mother sometimes binds me as her son. She nourishes and protects me, thinking me utterly helpless. My friends climb on my shoulders in pure friendship, saying, ‘What kind of big man are You? You and I are equal.’ If my beloved consort reproaches me in a sulky mood, that steals my mind from the reverent hymns of the Vedas.

“Taking these pure devotees with me, I shall descend and sport in various wonderful ways, unknown even in Vaikuntha. I shall broadcast such pastimes by which even I am amazed.

“The influence of YogaMaya will inspire the gopis with the sentiment that I am their paramour. Neither the gopis nor I shall notice this, for our minds will always be entranced by one another’s beauty and qualities.

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“The acts of YogaMaya make it possible for the Lord and the gopis to sometimes meet and sometimes separate, in loving ecstasy. These transcendental loving affairs of the Lord are unimaginable to empiricists involved in the impersonal feature of the AbsoluteTruth. Therefore the Lord Himself appears before the mundaners to bestow upon them the highest form of spiritual realisation and also personally relish its essence. The Lord is so merciful that He Himself descends to take the fallen souls back home to the kingdom of Godhead, where the erotic principles of Godhead are eternally relished in their real form, distinct from the perverted sexual love so much adored and indulged in by the fallen souls in their diseased condition. The reason the Lord displays the RasaLila is essentially to induce all the fallen souls to give up their diseased morality and religiosity, and to attract them to the kingdom of God to enjoy the reality. A person who actually understands what the RasaLila is will certainly hate to indulge in mundane sex life. For the realized soul, hearing the Lord’s RasaLila through the proper channel will result in complete abstinence from material sexual pleasure.”  
“Pure attachment will unite us even at the expense of moral and religious duties (dharma). Destiny will sometimes bring us together and sometimes separate us. I shall taste the essence of all these rasas, and in this way I shall favour all the devotees. Then, by hearing about the pure love of the residents of Vraja, devotees will worship me on the path of spontaneous love, abandoning all rituals of religiosity and fruitive activity.”
