**‘He Brahman! I will cause the sinful persons of KaliYuga to accept HariBhakti (devotion to Sri Hari), myself having accepted the order of sannyasa.’**

The presiding Deity of the sankirtana yajna mentioned in SrimadBhagavatam is Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu. Deeply enthralled, day and night, by the mellows of RadhaKrsna’s pastimes, he tastes their sweetness through the ecstasy of kirtan. Without waiting for anyone to ask, he goes door to door in every town, country and village, distributing the sumptuous delicacies of the limits of Sri Radha’s love and the resplendent eminence of RasaRaj Sri Krsna’s Names, the sounds of Sri KrsnaSankirtan resounding up into the heavens.

In his Sri CaitanyaBhagavat, Sri Vrndavana das Thakur has described the preaching of sankirtan as the main motive for the appearance of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu-

*kaliyuga dharma hoy harisankirttan \|*  
*etadarthe avatirna srisacinandan \|\|*  
*ei kahe bhagavate sarvatattvasar \|*  
*kirttananimitta gauracandra avatar \|\|*  
*suddho gaurah sudirghangastrisrotastirasambhavah \|*  
*dayapuh kirttanagrahi bhavisyami kalau yuge \|\|*

**‘I will appear on the banks of Ganga in the midst of KaliYuga, having accepted a very tall physique, my fair complexion the colour of cream. I will demonstrate my benevolence to the fallen souls of this age by myself accepting the process of NamaKirttan.’**  
**(VayuPurana)**

*ananadasrukalaromaharsapurnam tapodhan \|*  
*sarvve mameva draksyanti kalau sannyasarupinam \|\|*

**‘He tapodhan! (Oh great hermit, rich in asceticism!) In KaliYuga people will see me in the garb of a sannyasi They will also observe me decorated with the eight ecstatic symptoms-tears of rapture, shivering, my bodily hairs standing on end (horripilation), thrilling with delight.’**  
**(Sri BhavisyaPurana)**

*kalau prathamasandhyayam laksmikanto bhavisyati \| darubrahmasamipasthah sannyasi gauravigrahah \|\|*

**‘During the dawn of KaliYuga the husband of Laksmi, Bhagavan, will accept his form as Sri Gauranga. As a sannyasi he always remains in the presence of DaruBrahma, Lord Jagannath.’**  
**(GaruraPurana)**

*kalau ghoratamaschannan sarvvanacaravarjjitan \|*  
*sacigarbhe sambhuya bhavayisyami narada \|\|*

**‘He Narada! In KaliYuga I will appear in the womb of Sri SaciDevi, to deliver the fallen souls devoid of virtues, from the dense darkness of their lives, overcast with dreadful, frightful nightmares of sinful existence.’**  
**(VamanaPurana)**

Indeed, there is no possibility of estimating the numbers of living entities - from the cultured to the most sinful, vile and mean creatures - whose sinful reactions were eradicated by the incarnation of love, Sri CaitanyaDeva, sprinkling them with the nectar of loving devotion to Krsna. He delivered them from the devouring jaws of their grossly sinful and wayward lives devoid of meaning or purpose, simply by the love that overflowed from his heart, churned by feelings of separation from Krsna. Listening to the freshness of his teachings and the HolyNames of Sri Hari that flowed from his lotus mouth, the grief and lamentation of unlimited numbers of rogues, thieves, atheists, non-believers, uncultured, abominable, immoral debauches and cruel, ferocious barbarians was destroyed. Their lives once again became auspicious, noble and sublime, freed from the putrid, polluting effects of their contaminated lives. To see this young sannyasi -holding his staff and waterpot, dressed in rough silk, his body emaciated by ascetic austerities, handsome, dignified and of unruffled equilibrium, the personification of religious asceticism- the highly-held heads of so many proud, affluent, arrogant and vain-glorious snobs were forced to bow themselves. How many respectable scholars and boasting, bragging philosophers had to relinquish the yoke of their false conceit before becoming his disciples? Charmed by the radiant effulgence of this young ascetic, Sri Gauranga; his humble demeanor filled with so much love and devotion; exalted by the wealth of his renunciation; such a fine example of ideal behavior, dignity and grace - the lives of tens of millions of tens of millions of human beings were made successful, having obtained the inestimably good fortune of the opportunity to serve his lotus feet.

*divija bhuvi jayadhvam bhaktarupinah \|*  
*kalau sankirttanarambhe bhavisyami sacisutah \|\|*

**‘He Svargavasi Devagana! (Oh residents of the heavenly planets! Oh demigods!) You should all now take your birth on the Earth as my devotees. I will appear in KaliYuga as the son of Saci, to introduce the Sankirtan movement.’**  
**(Naradiya Puranam)**

*ahameva dvijasrestha nityam pracchannavigrahah \|*  
*bhagavadbhaktarupena lokam raksami sarvada \|\|*

**‘He DivjaSrestha! (Oh best of the brahmanas!) I will accept my eternally concealed form as that of a devotee and thus always protect this world.’**  
**(Naradiya Puranam)**

Having accepted the mood of a devotee, SvayamBhagavan Sri KrsnaGauranga teaches his devotees the essence of religion, apna acari dharma jivere sikhay, ‘by himself demonstrating the proper behaviour of a human being’.

*antahkrsno bahirgaurah sangopangastraparsadah \|*  
*sacigarbhe samapluyam mayamanusakarmakrt \|\|*

**‘Internally Krsna, externally Gaura, Bhagavan has descended as the son of Mother Saci, along with his plenary portions, his associates and companions who are all his weapons in this incarnation, to teach the religion of love to the living entities, by demonstrating his exemplary character, himself appearing as a human being under the spell of the illusion of this world.’**  
**(SkandaPuranam)**

There is simply no precedent for the pastimes of Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu. Totally immersed in the pastimes of RasikSekhar Sri Krsna, the summit of conviviality, and the mellow flavour of MahaBhavaSvarupa Sri Radhika’s love - stricken ecstasies, Sriman Mahaprabhu has decorated himself with her splendour to establish the ideal life for the living entities of this world; the natural quality of pure love that is our birthright (PremaDharma). His life itself expressed the gradual unfolding and blossoming of the love, anxiety, eagerness and ecstatic separation from Krsna that are the possessions of Srimati Radhika. The rare and unobtainable love of the gopis was established in his life as the ideal, the pattern of excellence, the mellows of which he personally tasted and distributed to the living entities of this world.

In concluding the commentary on this chapter, we should like to emphasise that the ideal example delineated in BhagavadGita- sarvva dharman parityajya mamekam saranam vraja - finds the culmination of its cultivation in the love of the VrajaGopis, devoid of even the slightest tinge of self-interest, their one and only possession, the be-all and end-all of their lives. Indeed, they knew nothing other than their Vrajendra Nandan Sri Krsna, more dear to them than their own lives multiplied tens of millions of times. Religion, irreligion, gain, loss, auspiciousness, inauspiciousness, this life and the next, they felt nothing but contempt for it all as they offered it to their dearmost in the joined palms of their hands, along with their very souls. The vastness of their love and the total surrender of their souls brought forth from the mouth of SvayamBhagavan Sri Krsna these eternal words- na paraye ‘ham... - “I will never be able to repay my debt to you.”

However, since that means that he will never give up trying, BhaktaPremadhin Bhagavan, in his attempt to compensate the love of the gopis and especially that of Srimati Radhika, has become a sannyasi in KaliYuga, the ‘Moon of Gauranga’, to drown himself in the unfathomable ocean of Radha’s devotion and compassion of love-in-separation, while flooding the entire universe in the same.

## Conclusion

### Verse 142

*brahmesadimahascaryamahimapi mahaprabhuh*  
*mugdhabaloditam srutva snigdho’vasyam bhavisyati*

**Sriman Mahaprabhu is unequalled and unsurpassed in Divine power and position, for He is far superior in every respect to MahaVisnu, the source of Lord Brahma and Lord Siva. He will most certainly be affectionately disposed towards me to hear the words of this enchanted child, words that have flourished by witnessing His grandeur.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

One may wonder, ‘if SvayarhBhagavan Sri KrsnaCaitanya, who is endowed with immeasurable, transcendental qualities and whose pastimes (lila) are of the same nature, whose power and glory are not fully comprehended by even Siva, Brahma and the other demigods, will deign to hear your prayers and woeful lamentations. Even if he does hear them, what will he think?’

In reply, our esteemed author offers two concluding verses, in utter humility.

Mahaprabhuh- GreatMaster, SupremeController (isvara). Or, mahan indicates VakresvarPandit and the other devotees, as well as the two Prabhus, Nityananda and Advaita - yasmad yasya va - Mahaprabhu is their Prabhu; and they are proud to have such a Lord as their master. Mahan can also specify Sankarsan and Sankar. the partial expansions of Nityananda and Advaita. These two Prabhus have become inaugurators of bhakti by His influence, thus is He Mahaprabhu. The two Prabhus serve the one Mahaprabhu (dui prabhu mili kare mahaprabhur sevan).

*Eko mahaprabhur jneryo dvau prabhu sammatau satam*

**‘One Mahaprabhu is known by the other two Prabhus who are His two confidential or very obedient servants; satam- of those who are to exist eternally.’**  
**(Sri GauraTattvaNirupan(Sri SvarupDamodarGosvami)**

*Eko mahaprabhur jneyah sri caitanya mahaprabhuh*  
*prabhudvau sriyutau nityanandadvaita mahasayau*

**‘One Mahaprabhu known as Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu, accompanied by two high-souled saintly persons, Sri NityanandaPrabhu and Sri AdvaitaPrabhu.’**  
**(GauraGanoddesaDipika)**

Brahmesadi...- even greater (mahan) than He who is the source of Brahma and Mahesvar (Siva), namely the Lord of Vaikuntha MahaVisnu; endowed with unequaled opulence, Divine grace and charm to the superlative degree - Sri KrsnaCaitanya Mahaprabhu.

‘Although He is so exalted and dignified, the most compassionate Sri Gauranga, hearing the puerile words of this childish, crazy fool, will nevertheless be pleased and thus shower me with paternal affection.’

Impelled by his humility, the best among panditas, Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati has referred to himself as a childish fool - however - the Goddess of Learning, Srimati SarasvatiDevi interprets his words thusly: ‘by hearing the words of Sri Prabodhananda, even ignorant fools become captivating masters of knowledge, crowned with distinction.’ Just as a father feels great satisfaction in relishing the incomplete formulation of words by his child, similarly, Mahaprabhu, the loving guardian of His devotees, is also satisfied to hear the offerings of those who have just entered the path of devotion in adoration (bhakti bhajan), what to speak of those devotees whose hearts are imbued with jataprema- budding prema that has reached the level of bhava.

Karika:

*abodhyamapi bhaktoktam srutva gauraharih kila*  
*vidhyagamyo bhavet prito balarddhoktam pita yatha*

**‘He who is inaccessible through rules, precepts or proper grammar, Sriman GauraHari delights in hearing the offerings of his devotees’ spiritual sentiments, even be they incomprehensible, just as a father affectionately listens to the words of his children.’**

**Purport**

*tad-vag-visargo janatagha-viplavo*  
*jasmin prati-slokam abaddhavaty api*  
*namany anantasya yaso ’nkitani*  
*yat srnvanti gayanti gmanti sadhavah*

**‘On the other hand, that literature which is full of descriptions of the transcendental glories of the Name, Fame, Forms, Pastimes, etc., of the unlimited Supreme Lord is a different creation, full of transcendental words directed toward bringing about a revolution in the impious lives of this world’s misdirected civilisation. Such transcendental literatures, even though imperfectly composed, are heard, sung and accepted by purified men who are thoroughly honest.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.5.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/5.11)**)**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“It is a qualification of the great thinkers to pick up the best even from the worst. It is said that the intelligent man should pick up nectar from a stock of poison, should accept gold even from a filthy place, should accept a good and qualified wife even from an obscure family and should accept a good lesson even from a man or from a teacher who comes from the untouchables. These are some of the ethical instructions for everyone in every place without exception. But a saint is far above the level of an ordinary man. He is always absorbed in glorifying the Supreme Lord because by broadcasting the HolyName and Fame of the Supreme Lord, the polluted atmosphere of the world will change, and as a result of propagating transcendental literatures like SrimadBhagavatam, people will become sane in their transactions.

abaddhavati-irregularly composed.

**One evening, IsvarPuri smilingly requested Nimai, “You are a very learned scholar. I have compiled a short biography about Sri Krsna. I will recite it before you and you can point out to me any mistakes or errors that you notice. I would be very pleased if you would have time to do this.”**

Prabhu replied, “Anyone who sees faults in a devotee’s description of Krsna is nothing but a sinful wretch. However a devotee may express his poetic feelings, Krsna is certainly very much pleased. A fool may say ‘Visnay’, whereas a sober and learned person will say, ‘Visnave’, though the meaning, ‘unto Lord Visnu’, is understood by our Hero in both instances, thus he accepts both the offerings.

*murkho vadati visnay dhiro vadati visnave*  
*ubhayostu samam punyam bhavagrahi janarddanah*

**‘Krsna is BhavagrahiJanardan, he who accepts the mood of the worshipper and not necessarily the articles offered.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaBhagavat AdiLila (**[**11.108**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/11.108)**))**

**“Whoever sees fault, simply sees his own faults. Krsna is very much pleased by whatever a devotee may describe. Therefore, who but some plucky upstart will criticise what has been composed by you under the influence of intense love for Krsna.”**  
**Listening to Nimai’s answer, IsvarPuri felt like he was being sprinkled with drops of nectar. Laughing gently he reassured him, “It will be no fault of yours if you merely point out whatever mistakes might have occurred.” Thus the two of them enjoyed their discussions each day for an hour or two.**  
**One day, while hearing a narration of Sri Puripad’s book, Prabhu smiled while pointing out one mistake, “This verb has not been conjugated properly.” Saying thus he set out for his own house.**  
**IsvarPuri was learned in all the sastras and took great delight in considering all the fine points of philosophy and wisdom. He now began to analyze this grammatical point from various perspectives, and consequently came up with an unlimited number of conclusions.**  
**On another day when NimaiPandit was present there, he explained to him all of these conclusions. The Lord was very pleased to hear his explanation and therefore left it at that, taking great delight in his servant’s victory. It is the conclusion of all the scriptures that the Supreme Lord always acts in such a way that his devotee is glorified.**  
**(Sri CaitanyaBhagavat)**

**“Just like, you are chanting the mantras, but because it is not your language, sometimes it appears broken. Just like guru. Sometimes you say goru. Goru means cow, and guru means spiritual master. So the difference of meaning is vast. The spiritual master is not a cow; or a bull. But sometimes you, mispronounce, because it is not your language; but that doesn’t matter. Because Bhavagrahi Janardana; Krsna is within you. He knows what you want to chant. Therefore He takes the meaning of guru and not goru, even it is spoken as goru. It doesn’t matter. Bhavagrahi Janardana. I know that although you are speaking guru as goru, I don’t take offense, because I know that your desire is something else. I do not protest that you are addressing me as goru. I am not goru. It is not a fault. Similarly, it is said, yasmin prati-slokam abaddhavati. If somebody does not know how to spell, how to pronounce, but his idea is there, abaddhavaty api, because he wants to chant the HolyName of the Supreme Lord, namany anantasya; Ananta means the unlimited; His name is being chanted. Namany anantasya yaso ’nkitani. His glorification is being done. The effect is srnvanti gayanti grnanti sadha... Those who are actually advanced transcendentalists, they’ll appreciate: ‘Oh, how nicely they are doing. How nicely.’ Although there is broken language of goru instead of guru, that will be appreciated.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**1.5.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/5.11)**). Lecture NewVrindaban 10 June 1969)**

### Verse 143

*drstam na sastram guravo na drsta*  
*vivecitam napi budhaih subuddhya*  
*yatha tatha jalpatu balabhavat-*  
*tathaiva me gauraharih prasidatu*

**I have not scrutinized the scriptures, nor have I paid heed to the instructions of a spiritual preceptor. Neither have I engaged my intelligence in deliberation with the wise. Nevertheless, I hope that Sri GauraHari will somehow or other be pleased with my garrulous, rambling prating, the sentimental outbursts of an innocent child.**

**Rasikasvadini Tika**

‘The topics related to Sri GauraHari that I have penned, yathatatha- be they pure or impure; jalpatu- babbling inanities; badatu- incomprehensible - however they may have been spoken, may Sri GauraHari be pleased with me.’

The term yathatatha refers again to balabhavat- ‘like a child (childlike)’. ‘Since I am ignorant, my words may be incoherent.’

The AmaraKosa (dictionary) definition of bala is: one who is murkha- inexperienced, arbhaka- a child. The reason the author calls himself foolish is- drstam па- ‘I have not understood the real import of the scriptures, neither have I taken shelter of a spiritual preceptor (guru), nor have I taken the opportunity to enquire from an advanced devotee, experienced in profound meditation, contemplation and adoration (bhajan). ’ Na vivecitam- ‘I could not use my proper intelligence to discuss spiritual topics with knowledgeable, saintly persons.’

Although Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvatipada has spoken in this humble manner, yet SarasvatiDevi is unable to tolerate this and has thus proffered the real import of this verse: nasa-refers to the termination of material existence (samsara); worship of Sri Caitanya is the astram (weapon) by which this is accomplished; drstam- this I have incontrovertibly established. Guravah na drstah (anadrstah)- I have ascertained that GauraBhaktas are extremely rare and are the real gurus. This I have accomplished with the help of subuddhya vivecitam-deliberation with proper intelligence.

‘With whom have you deliberated on these matters?’

Napi budhaih napitum- with those who are capable of offering transcendental joy to the world through their relevant and penetrating scriptural conclusions. Or, napanam napah-with those who possess ahlad- ecstasy (VrajaPremananda). The use of the verbal root (dhatu)- napa - suggests ecstasy. The expression bala bhavat can also mean- ‘in whichever manner these words are spoken, may Sri GauraHari be pleased with me’.

Setting aside criticism and objection from others, the author boldly declares, na vivecitam- anyone who has not used his proper intelligence to discuss with spiritual preceptors knowledgeable in the philosophy of Sri Caitanya, may make comments, but they are inconsequential to me. My only prayer is that Sri GauraHari will be pleased with my attempts and deliberations.

Sastram (scripture)- signifies the Sruti (Vedas); in particular, the essence of all the Vedic scriptures, beginning with the Sruti and Agamas, namely SrimadBhagavatam. Hence, those who have failed to grasp the real purport of this text are unable to comprehend Sri GauraTattva.

One may post an objection here, ‘how can we accuse others? Those who are learned scholars may study the SrimadBhagavatam. Why shouldn’t they discern its imports?’

In reply- guravo na drstah- those who can directly perceive the AbsoluteTruth are genuine gurus. Without hearing from a realised soul, mere scholarship does not suffice. The associates of SrimanMahaprabhu alone are competent to disclose these profound truths.

In KaliYuga, SvayamBhagavan Sri KrsnaCaitanya and His eternal followers and associates appeared on earth as genuine teachers (the phonetic opposite of ‘cheaters’). At the end of DvaparYuga, during the twenty-eighth divya yuga, the Prince of Vraja, Sri Krsna appeared, his dark complexion shaming the beauty of monsoon clouds. With his eternal entourage he performed his ecstatic pastimes and then disappeared from external vision. Shortly thereafter, in the first part of the following KaliYuga, he appeared again as Sri Gauranga, having again amalgamated the Yugavatar within his person. As Sri Gauranga, Bhagavan Sri Krsna continued to relish His pastimes of DvaparYuga, but from the vantage point of the asraya-tattva (Srimati Radhika). To distribute the taste of this nectar to one and all, Sri KrsnaCaitanya, being the inaugurator of His own sampradaya and the particular system of worship observed in that sampradaya, is therefore naturally a genuine guru, as well as are his followers.

*Prante prataravatiryya saha svaih svayam anusiksayati-*

**‘Appearing in the first quarter of KaliYuga, along with His eternal associates, he will reveal the process of worship to the World.’**  
**(VrajaTapani)**

*Kalau sankirtanarambhe bhavisyami sacisutah-*

**‘In KaliYuga, at the start of the Sankirtan movement, I will appear as the son of MotherSaci.’**  
**(Puranantara)**

There are numerous verses in various scriptures to support this conclusion. They have been mentioned in the first part of this book.

The crest-jewel of learned scholars, the guru of the demigods, Sri Brhaspati appeared as Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya during GauraLila. He has compiled the following verse:

*vairagya vidya nija bhakti-yogah*  
*siksartham ekah purusah puranah*  
*sri krsna caitanya sarira dhare*  
*krpambudhiryyas tam aham prapadye*

*kalan nastarh bhaktiyogam nijdm*  
*yah praduskarttum krsnacaitanya nama*  
*avirbhutas tasya padaravinde*  
*gadham gadham liyatam cittabhrngah*

**‘Let me take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, who has descended in the form of Lord CaitanyaMahaprabhu to teach renunciation through wisdom and devotional service to himself. He has appeared to reestablish the principles of bhakti-yoga that had been almost lost due to the ravages of time. He has descended because He is an ocean of transcendental mercy; I take shelter of this Ocean of Compassion. May the bumblebee of my heart remain always deeply committed at His lotus feet.’**  
**(Sri Caitanyastaka)**

Similarly, Sri Rupa Gosvami has written:

*anarpita-carim cirat karunayavatirnah kalau*  
*samarpayitum unnatojjvala-rasam sva-bhakti-sriyam*  
*harih purata-sundara-dyuti-kadamba-sandipitah*  
*sada hrdaya-kandare sphuratu vah saci-nandanah*

**‘May the Supreme Lord who is known as the son of Srimati SaciDevi be transcendentally situated in the innermost chambers of your heart. Resplendent with the radiance of molten gold, He has appeared in the Age of Kali by His causeless mercy to bestow what no incarnation has ever offered before: the most sublime and radiant mellow of devotional service, the mellow of conjugal love.’**  
**(VidagdhaMadhava(**[**1.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vm-rg/1.2)**))**

So it is that Sri KrsnaCaitanya is the inaugurator of the GauriyaVaisnava Sampradaya and his eternal associates are the Governing Body Commission (the gurus). Will those who do not follow and serve these gurus be able to understand the imports of the scriptures nonetheless? The revered author replies- kakka naiva- ‘no, never.’ Those who are blinded by the darkness of ignorance, having not had the chance to meet and associate with qualified spiritual preceptors, will remain blind, in the absence of the application of the salve of real knowledge to their eyes.

Only due to Sri Gauranga’s advent in KaliYuga has it (KaliYuga) been described in SrimadBhagavatam as the best among the four yugas.

*kalim sabhajayanty arya guna jnah sara-bhaginah*  
*yatra sankirtanenaiva sarva-svartho ’bhilabhyate*

**‘Those who are actually advanced in knowledge are able to appreciate the essential value of this age of Kali. Such enlightened persons worship KaliYuga because in this fallen age all perfection of life can easily be achieved by the performance of Sankirtana.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.36)**))**

*krtadisu praja rajan kalav icchanti sambhavam*  
*kalau khalu bhavisyanti narayana-parayanah*  
*kvacit kvacin maha-raja dravidesu ca bhurisah*

**‘My dear King, the inhabitants of SatyaYuga and other ages eagerly desire to take birth in this age of Kali, since in this age there will be many devotees of the Supreme Lord, Narayana.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.38)**))**

Sri KaviKarnapur writes in Ananda VrndavanCampu- dharmmavikrta krte- krte = SatyaYuga. ‘What was it like in SatyaYuga?’

Dharma was in its pristine state, without aberration; standing on all four legs. The four pillars of dharma (austerity, cleanliness, mercy and truthfulness) were in vogue. In each successive yuga a pillar topples until in KaliYuga only truthfulness remains. Yet this pillar is in a tottering condition as well.

The SupremeLord appears in the four yugas with different complexions in keeping with the general characteristics of the particular age. In KaliYuga, Sri CaitanyaMahaprabhu has appeared with a golden (yellow) complexion, and introduced the sadhana of Sankirtan; fruitive activities recommended in the Vedas have been discarded.

*devarsi-bhutapta-nrnam pitrnam na kinkaro nayam rni ca rajan*  
*sarvatmana yah saranam saranyam goto mukundam parihrtya kartam*

**‘O King, one who has given up all material duties and has taken full shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, who offers shelter to all, is not indebted to the demigods, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives, friends, mankind or even one’s forefathers who have passed away. Since all such classes of living entities are part and parcel of the Supreme Lord, one who has surrendered to the Lord’s service has no need to serve such persons separately.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.41)**))**

*sva-pada-mulam bhajatah priyasya tyaktanya-bhavasya harih paresah*  
*vikarma yac cotpatitam kathancid dhunoti sarvam hrdi sannivistah*

**‘One who has thus given up all other engagements and has taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Hari, the Supreme Personality, is very dear to the Lord. Indeed, if such a surrendered soul accidentally commits some sinful activity, the Supreme Personality, who is seated within everyone’s heart, immediately takes away the reaction to such sin.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**11.5.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.42)**))**

Thus in KaliYuga, Sri GauraHari is the Supreme object of worship. In the shade of the shelter of His lotus feet, the surrendered soul has nothing to fear since He protects His devotees in all circumstances.

One may object that Yamaraj will not easily overlook such accidental deviations. However, Paramesvar (the Supreme Isvar; SupremeController of Brahma and everyone else- paresah) is not under anyone’s control; not even Yamaraja.

A further objection may be raised- ‘according to scriptures, sruti-smrtir mamaivajne- all must obey the instructions and orders of the SupremeLord. If His orders are disobeyed, will He not punish the disobedient?’

The answer to this is: priyasya- those who have offered their souls at the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga with single-minded devotion are very dear to Him. Even if such a beloved devotee of the Lord disobeys Him, the merciful Lord will tolerate it. Furthermore, hrdi sannivistah- the devotee, by practice of bhakti-yoga, enthrones the SupremeLord within his heart and hence any deviations and aberrations are automatically purified by the Lord himself, without separate endeavour on his part. The reason for this being that the SupremePersonality is not under any compunction to act according to the norms of rational thinking.

The essence is- that those who have not read or heard the scriptures, nor associated with preceptors in the disciplic succession of Sri Caitanya will naturally not be able to grasp the accurate, authentic import of the scriptures.

This book has been arrayed in twelve chapters: Stuti (Hymns), Pranam (Obeisance), Asirbad (Benedictions), GaurBhakta Prasamsa (Eulogy of the Devotees of Sri Gauranga), Abhakta Ninda (Vilification of the NonDevotees), Svaninda (SelfCondemnation), UpasyaNisthata (Firm Faith in One’s Worshipful Deity), Loksiksa (General Education), Sri Gauranga Utkarsa (Excellencies of SriGauranga), AvatarMahima (DivineMajesty of this Incarnation), Sri Gauranger Rupa, Ullas, Nrtyadi (The Beauty, Exultation and Dancing of SriGauranga) and ParaTattva Sri GauraHari (The Supreme AbsoluteTruth Sri GauraHari).

Karika:

*nija buddhyapi caitanya priya vijnairapi na vivecitam yena yatha*  
*tatha vadatu mudhatvan mama tu yathantahkarane’sti tathaiva prasidatu*

**‘I have simply relied on my own intelligence, without consulting the wise, beloved devotees of Sri Caitanya; therefore I am nothing more than an infatuated, mentally obsessed fool. I only hope that Sri GauraHari be pleased with whatever music has been vibrated by my heart strings.’**

Thus ends the commentary Rasikasvadinii Tika-compiled by Anandi das on Srila Prabodhananda Sarasvati Gosvami’s Sri CaitanyaCandramrta

**Purport**

*bhrgur uvaca*  
*yan mayaya gahanayapahrtatma-bodh*  
*brahmadayas tanu-bhrtas tamasi svapantah*  
*natman-sritam tava vidanty adhunapi tattvam*  
*so ’yam prasidatu bhavan pranatatma-bandhuh*

**‘Sri Bhrgu said: “My dear Lord, all living entities, beginning from the highest, namely Lord Brahma, down to the ordinary ant, are under the influence of the insurmountable spell of illusory energy, and thus they are ignorant of their constitutional position. Everyone believes in the concept of the body, and all are thus submerged in the darkness of illusion. They are actually unable to understand how You live in every living entity as the SuperSoul, nor can they understand Your absolute position. But You are the eternal friend and protector of all surrendered souls. Therefore, please be kind toward us and forgive all our offenses.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**4.7.30**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.30)**))**

*yo ’nugrahartham bhajatam pada-mulam*  
*anama-rupo bhagavan anantah*  
*namani rupani ca janma-karmabhir*  
*bheje sa mahyam paramah prasidatu*

**‘The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is inconceivably opulent, who is devoid of all material names, forms and pastimes, and who is all-pervading, is especially merciful to the devotees who worship His lotus feet. Thus He exhibits transcendental Forms and Names with His different pastimes. May that Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose Form is eternal and full of knowledge and bliss, be merciful to me.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**6.4.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/4.33)**))**

*sattvadayo na santise yatra na prakrta gunah*  
*sa suddhah sarva-suddhebhyah puman adyah prasidatu*

**‘The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Visnu, is beyond the three qualities goodness, passion and ignorance. No material qualities exist in Him. May that original person, Narayana, who is situated in a completely transcendental position, be pleased with us.’**  
**(VisnuPurana quoted in Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLIla (**[**4.62**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/4.62)**) Purport)**

*sa prasidatu caitanya- devo yasya prasadatah*  
*tal-lila-varnane yogyah sadyah syad adhamo py ayam*

**‘I wish the grace of Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu, by whose mercy even one who is fallen can describe the pastimes of the Lord.’**  
**Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AdiLila (**[**13.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/13.1)**))**

Srila Prabhupad comments:

“To describe Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu or Lord Sri Krsna, one needs supernatural power, which is the grace and mercy of the Lord. Without this grace and mercy, one cannot compose transcendental literature. By dint of the grace of the Lord, however, even one who is unfit for a literary career can describe wonderful transcendental topics. Description of Krsna is possible for one who is empowered. Krsna-sakti vina nahe tara pravartana (Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta AntyaLila 7.11). Unless endowed with the mercy of the Lord, one cannot preach of the Lord’s Name, Fame, Qualities, Form, Entourage and so on. It should be concluded, therefore, that the writing of Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta by Krsnadas Kaviraj Gosvami manifests specific mercy bestowed upon the author, although he thought of himself as the most fallen. We should not consider him fallen because he describes himself as such. Rather, anyone who is able to compose such transcendental literature is our esteemed master.”

*citra-jalpera dasa anga—prajalpadi-nama*  
*‘bhramara-gita ’ra dasa sloka tahate pramana*

**‘Mad emotional talks include ten divisions, called prajalpa and other names. An example of this is the ten verses spoken by Srimati Radharani called ‘The Song to the Bumblebee.’**  
**(Sri CaitanyaCaritamrta MadhyaLila (**[**23.60**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/23.60)**))**

Srila Prabhupad:

“Imaginative mad talks, known as citra-jalpa, can be divided into ten categories -prajalpa, parijalpa, vijalpa, ujjalpa, sanjalpa, avajalpa, abhijalpa, ajalpa. pratijalpa and sujalpa. There are no English equivalents for these different features of jalpa (imaginative talk).”

**“The Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, is always unlimited, and His glories cannot be completely enumerated by anyone, even by a personality like Lord Brahma. It is said that Ananta, a direct incarnation of the Lord, has unlimited mouths, and with each mouth He has been trying to describe the glories of the Lord for an unlimited span of time, yet the glories of the Lord remain unlimited, and He therefore never finishes. It is not possible for any ordinary living entity to understand or to glorify the unlimited Personality of Godhead, but one can offer prayers or service to the Lord according to one’s particular capacity. This capacity is increased by the service spirit. Sevonmukhe hi jihvadau (BhaktiRasamrtaSindhu** [**1.2.234**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.234)**)-means that the service of the Lord begins with the tongue. This refers to chanting. By chanting HareKrsna, one begins the service of the Lord. Another function of the tongue is to taste and accept the Lord’s prasada. We have to begin our service to the Unlimited with the tongue and become perfect in chanting, and accepting the Lord’s prasada. To accept the Lord’s prasada means to control the entire set of senses. Chanting is the medicine, and prasada is the diet. With these processes one can begin his service, and as the service increases, the Lord reveals more and more to the devotee. But there is no limit to His glories, and there is no limit to engaging oneself in the service of the Lord.”**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**4.7.24**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.24)**)) Purport)**

*athapy udara-sravasah prthor hareh kalavatarasya kathamrtadrtah*  
*yathopadesam munibhih pracoditah slaghyani karmani vayam vitanmahi*

**‘Although we are unable to glorify you adequately, we nonetheless have a transcendental taste for glorifying your activities. We shall try to glorify you according to the instructions received from authoritative sages and scholars. Whatever we speak, however, is always inadequate and very insignificant. Dear King, because you are a direct incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, all your activities are liberal and ever laudable.’**  
**(SrimadBhagavatam (**[**4.16.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/16.3)**))**

Srila Prabhupad:

“However expert one may be, he can never describe the glories of the Lord adequately. Nonetheless, those engaged in glorifying the activities of the Lord should try to do so as far as possible. Such an attempt will please the Supreme Personality. By devotional service one can satisfy the Supreme Personality with just a few words. Without devotional service, volumes of books cannot satisfy the Lord. Even though preachers of the Krsna consciousness movement may be unable to describe the glories of the Lord, they can nonetheless go everywhere and request people to chant Hare Krsna.”
